# Ad Angles Checklist

> **Source:** Ad Angles SOP extracted from $100M Money Models Blueprint
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Date:** 2026-02-10
> **Cross-Reference:** ad-angles-sop.md, goated-ads-sop.md, hooks-sop.md
> **Agent:** hormozi-ads

---

## Pre-Work Checklist

### Before Using Any Angle

- [ ] Product/offer clearly defined
- [ ] Target avatar documented with exact language
- [ ] Awareness levels mapped for campaign
- [ ] Proof elements collected (testimonials, case studies, numbers)
- [ ] Read ad-angles-sop.md completely
- [ ] Understand relationship to hooks-sop.md and goated-ads-sop.md
- [ ] Testing infrastructure ready (ad platform, tracking, spreadsheet)

### Red Flags - STOP if:

- [ ] Product still being defined
- [ ] No avatar language documentation
- [ ] No proof elements available
- [ ] Haven't read companion SOPs
- [ ] Expecting to copy angles directly without adaptation

---

## Angle Selection Checklist

### Step 1: Determine Awareness Level

| Level | Description | Check if Targeting |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 - Unaware | Doesn't know they have a problem | [ ] |
| 2 - Problem-Aware | Knows problem, not solutions | [ ] |
| 3 - Solution-Aware | Knows solutions exist, not your product | [ ] |
| 4 - Product-Aware | Knows your product, not convinced | [ ] |
| 5 - Most Aware | Knows product, ready to buy | [ ] |

### Step 2: Select Angle Category

**For Level 1-2 (Cold Traffic):**
- [ ] Rumors Are True (RT-01 to RT-06)
- [ ] Question Hooks (QH-01 to QH-04)
- [ ] Comparison 95% vs 5% (CC-07)

**For Level 3 (Warm Traffic):**
- [ ] Comparison/Contrast (CC-01 to CC-08)
- [ ] Systems/Framework (SF-01 to SF-06)
- [ ] Transformation (TR-01 to TR-06)

**For Level 4 (Warmer Traffic):**
- [ ] Book/Knowledge (BK-01 to BK-05)
- [ ] Transformation with Proof (TR-03, TR-04)

**For Level 5 (Hot Traffic):**
- [ ] Launch/Event (LA-01 to LA-14)
- [ ] Trial/Freemium (TF-01 to TF-14)
- [ ] Retargeting (RT-01 to RT-10)

### Step 3: Apply 70-20-10 Rule

- [ ] 70% of angles from proven winners (your past data)
- [ ] 20% from adjacent categories (same awareness, different angle type)
- [ ] 10% completely new/experimental

---

## Angle Adaptation Checklist

### For Each Angle Selected

**Required Replacements:**
- [ ] [PRODUCT/SERVICE] replaced with your specific offer
- [ ] [AVATAR] replaced with your target persona language
- [ ] [PROBLEM] replaced with your avatar's exact pain
- [ ] [RESULT/OUTCOME] replaced with your specific promise
- [ ] [PROOF/NUMBER] replaced with your evidence
- [ ] [CTA/OFFER] replaced with your call-to-action

**Quality Checks:**
- [ ] All brackets [X] filled with specific content
- [ ] Avatar language used (not generic marketing speak)
- [ ] At least 1 proof element included
- [ ] CTA is single and clear
- [ ] Congruent with landing page/offer

**Variations Created:**
- [ ] Minimum 3 variations per angle
- [ ] Target 5 variations per angle
- [ ] Each variation has meaningful difference

---

## Retargeting Sequence Checklist

### Day 1-3 (Immediate Reminder)
- [ ] RT-01 (Quick Reminder) scheduled
- [ ] RT-02 (Still There For You) scheduled
- [ ] Frequency: 1 per day

### Day 4-7 (Value Reinforcement)
- [ ] RT-06 (The Real Value) scheduled
- [ ] RT-07 (What You Get) scheduled
- [ ] Frequency: 1 per 2 days

### Day 8-14 (Clarification)
- [ ] RT-05 (In Case You Forgot) scheduled
- [ ] RT-08 (Just Clarifying) scheduled
- [ ] Frequency: 1 per 3 days

### Day 15+ (Final Nudge)
- [ ] RT-09 (Your Benefits) scheduled
- [ ] RT-10 (Simple Reminder) scheduled
- [ ] Frequency: 1 per week

### Retargeting Quality Gates
- [ ] All 10 angles adapted for your product
- [ ] Sequence covers full 30-day window
- [ ] No aggressive language (friendly reminders only)
- [ ] Clear value proposition in each angle

---

## Launch Campaign Checklist

### Pre-Launch Phase 1 (T-14 to T-7)
- [ ] LA-04 (Something Big Coming) adapted
- [ ] LA-12 (Record Breaking Event) adapted
- [ ] LA-13 (Few Days Left) adapted
- [ ] Goal: Build anticipation

### Pre-Launch Phase 2 (T-7 to T-1)
- [ ] LA-03 (Final Hours Warning) adapted
- [ ] LA-11 (Last Chance VIP) adapted
- [ ] LA-14 (VIP Access Ending) adapted
- [ ] Goal: Create urgency

### Launch Day (T-0)
- [ ] LA-01 (Free Bonuses) adapted
- [ ] LA-02 (Book Launch Event Today) adapted
- [ ] LA-05 (Launch Day Energy) adapted
- [ ] LA-06 (Limited Time Bonuses) adapted
- [ ] Goal: Event energy

### Final Hours (Last 6 hours of T-0)
- [ ] LA-07 (Exclusive Livestream) adapted
- [ ] LA-08 (The Big Reveal) adapted
- [ ] LA-09 (Don't Miss History) adapted
- [ ] LA-10 (Final Call) adapted
- [ ] Goal: Scarcity close

### Launch Quality Gates
- [ ] All 4 phases planned and scheduled
- [ ] Angles adapted with launch-specific details
- [ ] Bonus/exclusive elements clearly communicated
- [ ] Timing verified with actual launch schedule

---

## Trial/Freemium Offer Checklist

### Value Stack Angles
- [ ] TF-01 (Complete Free Stack) - List all components
- [ ] TF-04 ($70K Value Stack) - Calculate dollar values
- [ ] TF-09 (Free Tech + Training) - Dual offer positioning

### Extended Trial Angles
- [ ] TF-02 (90 Days to Build) - Emphasize timeframe
- [ ] TF-08 (Don't Give Up) - Address persistence
- [ ] TF-13 (7-Day Window) - Create window urgency

### Social Proof Angles
- [ ] TF-06 (25% Make Sales) - Use your success stats
- [ ] TF-07 (Platform Built For) - Feature alignment

### Price Anchor Angles
- [ ] TF-12 (10x Better, Cheaper) - Comparison positioning
- [ ] TF-14 (Price Dropped 10x) - Before/after pricing

### Trial Quality Gates
- [ ] Value stack dollar amount calculated
- [ ] Trial length clearly communicated
- [ ] Locked rate clearly communicated
- [ ] One-time nature emphasized

---

## Testing Checklist

### Before Each Test

- [ ] Angle fully adapted (no brackets remaining)
- [ ] 3-5 variations ready
- [ ] Budget allocated (minimum per goated-ads-sop.md)
- [ ] Success metrics defined (CTR, CPA, ROAS targets)
- [ ] Testing log prepared

### During Test (Daily)

- [ ] Performance data collected
- [ ] CTR checked (threshold: >1%)
- [ ] CPA checked (threshold: within target)
- [ ] Frequency monitored (threshold: <5)
- [ ] Comments/engagement reviewed

### After Test (Day 7)

- [ ] Top 10% performers identified
- [ ] Bottom 10% eliminated
- [ ] Middle performers noted for potential iteration
- [ ] Patterns documented
- [ ] Testing log updated (Appendix C format)

### Scale Decision

**Ready to Scale if:**
- [ ] ROAS >3x for 7 days
- [ ] CPA stable for 100+ conversions
- [ ] Frequency <3 after 14 days
- [ ] CTR maintains >1%

**Do NOT Scale if:**
- [ ] CTR <0.5% (kill)
- [ ] CPA doubled (pause)
- [ ] Frequency >10 (refresh)
- [ ] ROAS <2x for 3 days (analyze)

---

## Weekly Angle Creation Checklist

### Friday Ad Creation Session (3-4 hours)

**Hour 1: Review & Plan (60 min)**
- [ ] Pull last week's performance data
- [ ] Identify top 10% and bottom 10%
- [ ] Document pattern insights
- [ ] Select 15 angles for this week:
  - [ ] 10-11 from proven winners (70%)
  - [ ] 3 from adjacent categories (20%)
  - [ ] 1-2 completely new (10%)

**Hours 2-3: Adapt (90 min)**
- [ ] Adapt selected angles using worksheet
- [ ] Create 3-5 variations per angle
- [ ] Run quality checks on each
- [ ] Total output: 45-75 adapted angles

**Hour 4: Validate & Schedule (60 min)**
- [ ] Quality gate all adaptations
- [ ] Schedule tests in ad platform
- [ ] Update testing log
- [ ] Document this week's angle selections

---

## Angle Quality Gate Checklist

### Gate 1: Adaptation Complete

- [ ] All [BRACKETS] filled with specific content
- [ ] No Hormozi-specific numbers without your equivalent
- [ ] Avatar language verified (80%+ match)
- [ ] Proof element included
- [ ] CTA single and clear

### Gate 2: Ready for Testing

- [ ] Minimum 3 variations exist
- [ ] Each variation meaningfully different
- [ ] Budget allocated
- [ ] Tracking configured
- [ ] Success metrics defined

### Gate 3: Ready for Scale

- [ ] 7+ days of stable performance
- [ ] ROAS >3x achieved
- [ ] 100+ conversions collected
- [ ] Frequency <3
- [ ] CTR >1% maintained

---

## Troubleshooting Checklist

### If All Angles Underperforming

- [ ] Check avatar language match
- [ ] Verify proof elements are strong
- [ ] Test different awareness level
- [ ] Review competitor angles
- [ ] Escalate to marketing lead

### If Specific Category Underperforming

- [ ] Try different angles from same category
- [ ] Try adjacent category for same awareness
- [ ] Review category-specific decision rules
- [ ] Document learnings

### If Angle Suddenly Stops Working

- [ ] Check creative fatigue (>10-14 days?)
- [ ] Check competitor activity
- [ ] Check for platform algorithm changes
- [ ] Create fresh variations
- [ ] Consider pause and restart

### If No Clear Winner After 15 Tests

- [ ] Review testing methodology
- [ ] Ensure sufficient sample size
- [ ] Check for external factors
- [ ] Escalate to strategy review
- [ ] Consider broader angle pivot

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/affiliates-referrals-checklist.md

# Affiliates & Referrals Implementation Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Leads: Section IV "Get People Who Get Leads" - Alex Hormozi
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Created:** 2026-02-10
> **Agent:** hormozi-launch

---

## Pre-Implementation Assessment

### Leverage Scenario Identification
- [ ] **Assess Current State** - Which scenario are you in?
  - [ ] Scenario #1: You alone (High Work, Low Leads, Low Leverage)
  - [ ] Scenario #2: One lead getter (Low Work, Low Leads, High Leverage)
  - [ ] Scenario #3: Many lead getters (High Work, High Leads, Higher Leverage)
  - [ ] Scenario #4: Lead getters who get lead getters (Low Work, High Leads, Highest Leverage)

### Baseline Metrics
- [ ] **Calculate Referral Rate** = Referrals / Total Customers = _____%
- [ ] **Calculate Churn Rate** = Churned Customers / Total Customers = _____%
- [ ] **Referral vs. Churn Assessment**:
  - [ ] Referrals > Churn (Growing without other advertising)
  - [ ] Referrals = Churn (Need advertising to grow)
  - [ ] Referrals < Churn (Advertising just to survive)
- [ ] **Calculate Current LTGP:CAC Ratio** = $_____ : $_____ = _____:1

---

## Section I: Customer Referrals

### Phase 1: Diagnose Why Referrals Aren't Happening

**Problem #1: Product Not Good Enough**
- [ ] Ask yourself: "If my product were exceptional, would people already know about it?"
- [ ] Ask yourself: "Why are my customers too embarrassed to tell everyone they know?"
- [ ] Check NPS score (target: >50)
- [ ] Review customer complaints and common issues
- [ ] If product is the issue: STOP referral tactics, focus on Phase 2

**Problem #2: Not Asking for Referrals**
- [ ] Audit current referral asks (when, how, how often)
- [ ] If no system exists: proceed to Phase 3
- [ ] If system exists but weak: optimize existing before adding new

---

### Phase 2: Build Goodwill (Six Ways to Give More Value)

**Way #1: Sell Better Customers**
- [ ] Identify your most successful customers
- [ ] Find what they have in common (demographics, behaviors, timing)
- [ ] Document the "ideal customer profile"
- [ ] Update targeting to match ideal profile
- [ ] Narrow messaging to speak directly to ideal profile
- [ ] Track: Are new customers getting better results?

**Way #2: Set Better Expectations**
- [ ] List all promises made in marketing/sales
- [ ] For each promise, rate: Can we always exceed it?
- [ ] Lower promises that we sometimes miss
- [ ] Continue lowering until close rates decrease
- [ ] Stop at optimal point (maximum closes + maximum exceed)
- [ ] Document the new promise levels

**Way #3: Get Better Results for More People**
- [ ] Survey customers to identify top performers
- [ ] Interview top 10% - What did they do different?
- [ ] List common actions among top performers
- [ ] Create checklist of "success behaviors"
- [ ] Force new customers to do these behaviors (in onboarding)
- [ ] Match guarantee conditions to success behaviors
- [ ] Measure: Are average results improving?

**Way #4: Make Faster Wins**
- [ ] Map customer journey from purchase to result
- [ ] Identify every possible "win" along the way
- [ ] Break big deliveries into smaller increments
- [ ] Schedule progress updates (never go silent)
- [ ] Force multiple wins in first 48 hours
- [ ] Implement BAMFAM (always schedule next contact)
- [ ] Add 50% buffer to all deadlines
- [ ] Track: Time to first win = _____ hours/days

**Way #5: Keep Improving Your Stuff (Monthly Cycle)**
- [ ] Set recurring monthly meeting for this
- [ ] Collect: Customer service issues, surveys, reviews
- [ ] Identify #1 most common problem
- [ ] Interview customers who succeeded despite problem
- [ ] Design fix based on feedback
- [ ] Test with small group of struggling customers
- [ ] If solved: launch to all customers
- [ ] If not solved: iterate and re-test
- [ ] Move to next problem, repeat

**Way #6: Tell Them What to Buy Next**
- [ ] Audit: What can customers buy after initial purchase?
- [ ] If nothing: design next offer
- [ ] Create system to offer next thing after major wins
- [ ] Track: % of customers who buy second product
- [ ] Ensure customers don't "drop off" with nowhere to go

---

### Phase 3: Ask for Referrals (Seven Methods)

**Method #1: One-Sided Referral Benefit**
- [ ] Calculate your average CAC = $_____
- [ ] Set reward amount (up to CAC)
- [ ] Decide: Reward to referrer OR discount to friend
- [ ] Create tracking system (codes/links)
- [ ] Train team on asking for three-way introductions
- [ ] Script: "If you refer a friend and they sign up, you get $___"
- [ ] Always ask for real introduction (call/text/email), not just name

**Method #2: Two-Sided Referral Benefits**
- [ ] Split CAC between referrer and friend
- [ ] Example: $100 cash to referrer + $100 off for friend
- [ ] Set up tracking for both rewards
- [ ] Communicate benefit to BOTH parties clearly
- [ ] Monitor: Which party is more motivated by their benefit?

**Method #3: Ask Right When They Buy**
- [ ] Add referral ask to sales script/checkout
- [ ] Script: "People who do this with someone else get 3x results. Who would you want to do this with?"
- [ ] Train salespeople to ask and wait for answer
- [ ] If they have someone: get three-way intro immediately
- [ ] Track: Referrals generated at point of sale

**Method #4: Referrals as Negotiation Chip**
- [ ] Prepare script for price objections
- [ ] Script: "I can't lower the price, but if you introduce me to 3 friends right now, I'll waive the initiation fee"
- [ ] Get introductions before giving discount
- [ ] If customer asks about others' discounts: "They got it for referrals. Want $X off? Who are you thinking of?"
- [ ] Track: Referrals from negotiations

**Method #5: Referral Events (Time-Bound)**
- [ ] Plan event (1-4 week duration)
- [ ] Choose reward: Points, credits, cash, or status
- [ ] Create urgency with deadline
- [ ] Promote benefits of doing activity with friends
- [ ] Event name ideas:
  - [ ] "Bring a Friend" promotion
  - [ ] "Spouse Challenge" promotion
  - [ ] "Accountability Partner" promotion
  - [ ] "Coach Challenge" (team competition)
- [ ] Announce and run event
- [ ] Track results and iterate for next event

**Method #6: Ongoing Referral Program**
- [ ] Build referral messaging into regular content
- [ ] Mention in: Social posts, emails, calls, ads
- [ ] Theme: Benefits of doing things with others
- [ ] Make referral program always visible (not just events)
- [ ] Track: % of leads from always-on program

**Method #7: Unlockable Referral Bonuses**
- [ ] List valuable bonuses you can offer
  - [ ] VIP access
  - [ ] Courses/training
  - [ ] Merchandise
  - [ ] Status/titles
  - [ ] Premium support
  - [ ] Additional service hours
- [ ] Set requirements: Referral + testimonial
- [ ] Make offer "so good it's stupid not to"
- [ ] Track: Bonus claim rate

---

### Phase 4: Advanced Referral Tactics

**Gift Card Strategy**
- [ ] Create gift card worth 1/3 of program cost
- [ ] Customer can give to friend
- [ ] Set expiration: 7-14 days
- [ ] Write friend's name on card before photo
- [ ] Use three-way text introduction with card photo
- [ ] Track: Gift card redemption rate

**Gift Card Sale**
- [ ] Sell gift cards at 90% off (for friends of customers only)
- [ ] Referrer looks generous
- [ ] You get paid to acquire new customer
- [ ] Track: Revenue from gift card sales

---

## Section II: Employees

### Phase 1: Mindset Shift

**Belief Transformation Checklist**
- [ ] Acknowledge old belief: "If you want something done right, do it yourself"
- [ ] Adopt new belief: "Get someone to spend all their time doing it"
- [ ] Acknowledge old belief: "Nobody can do it like I do"
- [ ] Adopt new belief: "If I can do it, someone else can do it better"
- [ ] Acknowledge old belief: "No one can replace me"
- [ ] Adopt new belief: "Everyone is replaceable, especially me"

**Wealth Principle Internalization**
- [ ] Understand: "You get rich from what you earn. You become wealthy from what you own."
- [ ] Compare: Business with you vs. without you = asset value difference
- [ ] Commit: Goal is to make yourself unnecessary

---

### Phase 2: Recruit Employees (Internal Core Four)

**Apply Customer Acquisition Methods to Employee Acquisition**
- [ ] Warm Outreach → Ask your network for candidates
- [ ] Cold Outreach → Recruiting outreach to strangers
- [ ] Post Content → Post job openings
- [ ] Paid Ads → Promote job openings
- [ ] Customer Referrals → Employee referral program
- [ ] Affiliates → Associations, guilds, email lists
- [ ] Agencies → Recruiting firms

---

### Phase 3: Train Employees (The 3Ds Method)

**D1: Document**
- [ ] Write out exact steps of your lead generation process
- [ ] Have observer watch you and document what you do
- [ ] Record yourself doing the work multiple ways
- [ ] Create first draft checklist
- [ ] Test: Can YOU get A+ results following only checklist?
- [ ] If yes: proceed. If no: improve checklist.

**D2: Demonstrate**
- [ ] Sit with new employee
- [ ] Walk through checklist step by step
- [ ] Note any confusion or questions
- [ ] Update checklist for each confusion point
- [ ] Create second draft checklist

**D3: Duplicate**
- [ ] Employee follows checklist exactly
- [ ] You observe without interrupting
- [ ] If wrong result + right directions: fix checklist
- [ ] If wrong result + wrong directions: more practice
- [ ] Repeat until consistently correct
- [ ] Celebrate when they get it right

**Clarity Test**
- [ ] Answer honestly: "If I disappeared, could a stranger replicate my results from this checklist alone?"
- [ ] If no: improve checklist until answer is yes

---

### Phase 4: Training Best Practices

- [ ] Remember: If they err, WE erred (fix checklist, not employee)
- [ ] If step needs explanation, step is too complicated (simplify)
- [ ] Competence vs. performance: they may know but need practice
- [ ] Focus on following directions, not just outcomes
- [ ] Praise every success (even if result wrong but directions followed)
- [ ] No punishment during training
- [ ] Give one piece of feedback at a time
- [ ] If performance drops: they stopped doing important step (find and retrain)

---

### Phase 5: Calculate Employee ROI

- [ ] Calculate: Total Payroll for lead generation = $_____
- [ ] Calculate: Total Engaged Leads generated = _____
- [ ] Cost per Engaged Lead = Payroll / Leads = $_____
- [ ] Calculate: Leads needed per customer = _____
- [ ] Employee CAC = Cost per Lead x Leads per Customer = $_____
- [ ] LTGP:CAC Ratio = LTGP / Employee CAC = _____:1
- [ ] Target: At least 3:1 ratio

---

### Phase 6: Diagnose Employee Issues

**If CAC is too high, ask:**
"Do my engaged leads have the problem I solve AND the money to spend?"

| Answer | Problem Type | Action |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| No | Advertising | Fix targeting/messaging, don't fire sales |
| Yes but not buying | Sales | Fix pitch/closing, don't fire advertising |
| Yes but not enough | Advertising | Scale volume |

---

## Section III: Agencies [PARTIAL - Source Limited]

- [ ] Identify which Core Four activities to outsource
- [ ] Interview multiple agencies
- [ ] Set clear KPIs and expectations
- [ ] Start with time-limited engagement
- [ ] Track: Agency CAC vs. internal CAC
- [ ] Goal: Learn from agency, eventually internalize
- [ ] Warning: Don't depend on agencies forever

---

## Section IV: Affiliates [PARTIAL - Source Limited]

- [ ] Define affiliate commission structure (up to CAC)
- [ ] Create affiliate tracking system
- [ ] Recruit affiliates using Core Four
- [ ] Provide affiliates with promotional materials
- [ ] Track: Leads and sales by affiliate
- [ ] Optimize top affiliates, remove non-performers

---

## Leverage Maximization (Scenario #4)

### Building Lead Getters Who Get Lead Getters

**Customer Layer**
- [ ] Create tiered referral rewards (more referrals = better rewards)
- [ ] Build customer advocacy program
- [ ] Create community where customers recruit customers

**Employee Layer**
- [ ] Create employee referral bonus for new hires
- [ ] Train team leaders to recruit and train their own teams
- [ ] Tie career paths to team building

**Agency Layer** [INFERRED]
- [ ] Create agency partner program
- [ ] Incentivize agencies to bring other agencies

**Affiliate Layer**
- [ ] Create tiered affiliate structures
- [ ] Super-affiliate program for top performers
- [ ] Affiliate managers to recruit more affiliates

---

## Quality Gates

| Gate | Condition | Status |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Product Goodwill | NPS > 50 | [ ] Pass [ ] Fail |
| Referral vs. Churn | Referrals > Churn | [ ] Pass [ ] Fail |
| Checklist Clarity | Stranger test passed | [ ] Pass [ ] Fail |
| Employee ROI | LTGP:CAC >= 3:1 | [ ] Pass [ ] Fail |
| Incentive Level | Referral reward <= CAC | [ ] Pass [ ] Fail |
| Scenario Progress | Moving toward #4 | [ ] Pass [ ] Fail |

---

## Monthly Review Checklist

- [ ] Calculate referral rate vs. churn rate
- [ ] Review LTGP:CAC by lead getter type
- [ ] Identify best performing referral method
- [ ] Run product improvement cycle (Phase 2, Way #5)
- [ ] Assess leverage scenario (1-4)
- [ ] Identify next leverage improvement
- [ ] Update training checklists if needed
- [ ] Celebrate top referrers and lead getter employees

---

## The One Question Test

> "You lost all customers but one. The advertising gods banned Core Four. All customers must come from this one customer. How would you treat them?"

Use this thought experiment to guide all referral and leverage decisions.

---

## Key Formulas Reference

```
Goodwill = Value - Price
Referral Net Growth = Referrals - Churn
Employee Lead Cost = Payroll / Leads Generated
LTGP:CAC Ratio = LTGP / CAC (target: >= 3:1)
Leverage = Output / Input
```

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/antipattern-screening.md

# Antipattern Screening Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Offers + prompts-joao KB/v2.0/05_ANTIPATTERN_SHIELDS.md
> **Pattern:** SC-CK-VETO-002 (Veto Checklist - Blocks Execution)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Created:** 2026-02-10
> **Type:** VETO CONDITION - Must PASS before proceeding
> **Agent:** hormozi-chief

---

## CRITICAL: Sistema Imunitario do Negocio

**Este checklist detecta, diagnostica e BLOQUEIA ideias que violam principios fundamentais.**

"Estes antipadroes sao arquiteturas de falha previsiveis que levam a estagnacao, queima de caixa e colapso do negocio."

---

## Arvore de Decisao de Rejeicao

Execute este fluxograma para qualquer oportunidade, oferta ou tatica.
**Um unico REJEITAR em qualquer etapa desqualifica a estrategia.**

---

## GATE 1: Avaliacao de Mercado e Cliente

### 1.1 Churn Estrutural

**Pergunta:** O mercado-alvo tem alta taxa de falencia/desistencia inerente?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Clientes sao iniciantes em algo (alta taxa de desistencia natural)
- [ ] O setor do cliente tem mortalidade > 20% ao ano
- [ ] Clientes frequentemente mudam de carreira/nicho
- [ ] Clientes sao temporarios por natureza (ex: noivas, gravidas)

**Exemplos de Mercados com Churn Estrutural:**
- Personal trainers iniciantes (muitos desistem da profissao)
- Novas academias (1/3 falha no primeiro ano)
- Startups pre-revenue
- Estudantes (se formam e saem)

**Seu Mercado:** ________________________________________________

**Churn Estrutural Detectado?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **VETO: Modelo construido sobre areia movediça**

**Antidoto se SIM:** Pivotar para segmento mais estavel (ex: de "personal trainers iniciantes" para "personal trainers com >3 anos de atuacao")

---

### 1.2 Exploracao de Vulneraveis

**Pergunta:** O modelo explora populacoes vulneraveis atraves de assimetrias de informacao?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Publico tem baixa educacao financeira e estou vendendo produto financeiro complexo
- [ ] Publico esta em estado emocional extremo (luto, divorcio, desespero)
- [ ] Promessas que eu sei que maioria nao conseguira cumprir
- [ ] Uso de taticas de pressao em pessoas em situacao desesperada

**Exploracao Detectada?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **VETO ABSOLUTO: Violacao etica fundamental**

---

## GATE 2: Avaliacao do Modelo de Negocio

### 2.1 Margem Bruta

**Pergunta:** A margem bruta e >= 80% (para servicos)?

**Calculo:**
```
Margem Bruta = (Receita - Custo Direto de Entrega) / Receita
Sua Margem = (_______ - _______) / _______ = _____%
```

**Margem Adequada?**
- [ ] >= 80% - PASS
- [ ] 60-80% - ALERTA (modelo apertado, considerar ajustes)
- [ ] < 60% - **VETO: Sem oxigenio para crescer**

**Antidoto se VETO:** Aumentar preco, reduzir custo de entrega, ou mudar modelo (de DFY para DWY, por exemplo)

---

### 2.2 CAC vs Receita Inicial

**Pergunta:** O negocio exige PERDER dinheiro para adquirir cliente?

**Calculo:**
```
CAC (Custo de Aquisicao de Cliente) = $_______
Receita da Primeira Venda = $_______
FECC (Front End Cash Collected) = $_______
```

**FECC > CAC?**
- [ ] SIM (FECC > CAC) - PASS
- [ ] NAO (CAC > FECC) - **VETO: Ciclo de caixa quebrado**

**Antidoto se VETO:** Criar oferta front-end que liquida CAC, reduzir CAC, ou buscar financiamento se justificavel

---

### 2.3 Key Man Risk (Dependencia do Fundador)

**Pergunta:** O negocio depende CRITICAMENTE do fundador para vendas ou entrega?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] So o fundador consegue fechar vendas
- [ ] So o fundador consegue entregar o servico core
- [ ] Fundador e o "produto" (guru dependency)
- [ ] Sem o fundador, negocio para

**Key Man Risk Detectado?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] PARCIAL - ALERTA (plano de sistematizacao necessario)
- [ ] TOTAL - **VETO: Nao e ativo escalavel, e emprego**

**Antidoto se VETO:** Documentar processos, treinar equipe, criar sistemas que funcionam sem fundador

---

## GATE 3: Avaliacao da Oferta e Taticas

### 3.1 Comoditizacao

**Pergunta:** A oferta e facilmente comparavel com base em PRECO?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Cliente pergunta "quanto custa?" antes de entender valor
- [ ] Competidores oferecem "a mesma coisa" mais barato
- [ ] Nao existe diferenciador claro alem de preco
- [ ] Cliente faz "shopping" de propostas
- [ ] Descrição poderia ser de qualquer concorrente

**Comoditizacao Detectada?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **MODIFICAR: Requer Grand Slam Offer**

**Antidoto:** Engenharia de Grand Slam Offer para criar "categoria de um" (usar create-grand-slam-offer.md)

---

### 3.2 Taticas Enganosas

**Pergunta:** As taticas de marketing erodem confianca a longo prazo?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Escassez FALSA (contador que reseta, vagas que nunca acabam)
- [ ] Urgencia FALSA (deadline que estende automaticamente)
- [ ] Promessas que sei que maioria nao alcancara
- [ ] Depoimentos fabricados ou exagerados
- [ ] Garantias que sei que nao honrarei
- [ ] Precos "originais" inflados artificialmente

**Taticas Enganosas Detectadas?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **VETO DA TATICA: Nao usar**

**Principio:** "Trocar ativo de longo prazo (confianca) por ganho de curto prazo e mau investimento estrategico."

---

## GATE 4: Avaliacao de Lideranca (Para Parcerias)

### 4.1 Reatividade Emocional

**Pergunta:** O fundador/lider toma decisoes baseado em emocoes vs dados?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Muda estrategia baseado em como "se sente" no dia
- [ ] Toma decisoes impulsivas sem analisar dados
- [ ] Nao consegue separar feedback do produto de feedback pessoal
- [ ] Historico de pivotar rapidamente sem dar tempo para validacao

**Reatividade Emocional Detectada?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **VETO DE PARCERIA: Risco de lideranca inaceitavel**

---

## GATE 5: Antipadroes Especificos

### 5.1 Oferta Inchada (Bloated Offer)

**Pergunta:** A oferta tem TANTOS componentes que confunde?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Mais de 10 "bonus" listados
- [ ] Cliente nao consegue explicar o que esta comprando
- [ ] Paralisia de analise reportada em vendas
- [ ] Tempo de apresentacao da oferta > 30 minutos

**Oferta Inchada Detectada?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **MODIFICAR: Simplificar para 3-5 componentes core**

---

### 5.2 Buraco no Modelo (Entrega Desalinhada)

**Pergunta:** Quem vende tem incentivos alinhados com quem entrega?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Vendedor ganha comissao, entregador ganha salario fixo
- [ ] Parceiro de entrega lucra com reembolsos/cancelamentos
- [ ] Franqueado nao tem stake nos resultados do cliente
- [ ] Terceiro pode sabotar entrega sem consequencia

**Desalinhamento Detectado?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **MODIFICAR: Reestruturar incentivos**

---

### 5.3 Niche Slapping Fallacy

**Pergunta:** Voce esta pulando de nicho porque "este nao funciona"?

**Red Flags:**
- [ ] Tentou < 90 dias antes de declarar que "nao funciona"
- [ ] Nao fez "Regra dos 100" antes de desistir
- [ ] Acha que outro nicho sera "mais facil"
- [ ] Ja pivotou 3+ vezes no ultimo ano

**Niche Slapping Detectado?**
- [ ] NAO - PASS
- [ ] SIM - **VETO DO PIVOT: Comprometer-se com validacao completa primeiro**

---

## Resumo de Vetos

### Consolidacao

| Gate | Item | Status |
|------|------|--------|
| 1.1 | Churn Estrutural | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 1.2 | Exploracao de Vulneraveis | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 2.1 | Margem Bruta | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 2.2 | CAC vs Receita | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 2.3 | Key Man Risk | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 3.1 | Comoditizacao | [ ] PASS [ ] MODIFICAR |
| 3.2 | Taticas Enganosas | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 4.1 | Reatividade Emocional | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |
| 5.1 | Oferta Inchada | [ ] PASS [ ] MODIFICAR |
| 5.2 | Buraco no Modelo | [ ] PASS [ ] MODIFICAR |
| 5.3 | Niche Slapping | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |

### Decisao Final

```
SE qualquer VETO → NAO PROSSEGUIR (aplicar antidoto primeiro)
SE MODIFICAR → Ajustar antes de prosseguir
SE todos PASS → Prosseguir para proxima etapa
```

**Status Final:**
- [ ] **PASS** - Nenhum antipattern critico detectado
- [ ] **MODIFICAR** - Ajustes necessarios antes de prosseguir
- [ ] **VETO** - Nao prosseguir ate resolver

---

## Protocolo de Rejeicao Educacional

Se identificou um antipattern, comunique assim:

### Script de Comunicacao

1. **RECONHECIMENTO:** "Compreendo a logica por tras dessa abordagem..."

2. **DIAGNOSTICO:** "No entanto, isso ativa o antipattern de [NOME], porque viola o principio de [PRINCIPIO]."

3. **CONSEQUENCIA:** "A consequencia previsivel de longo prazo e [CONSEQUENCIA]."

4. **ANTIDOTO:** "Uma abordagem mais robusta seria [ANTIDOTO], porque [BENEFICIO]."

---

## Matriz de Referencia Rapida

| Antipattern | Principio Violado | Consequencia | Antidoto |
|-------------|-------------------|--------------|----------|
| Churn Estrutural | Estabilidade da Base | Colapso do modelo | Mudar segmento |
| Comoditizacao | Circulo Virtuoso do Preco | Corrida para o fundo | Grand Slam Offer |
| Falsa Escassez | Preservacao de Confianca | Erosao de marca | Escassez genuina |
| Oferta Inchada | Minimizar Esforco (Eq. Valor) | Paralisia de analise | Simplificar |
| Key Man Risk | Escalabilidade | Teto de crescimento | Sistematizar |

---

## Assinatura de Aprovacao

| Gate | Responsavel | Data | Status |
|------|-------------|------|--------|
| Antipattern Screening | | | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |

**Antipatterns Detectados:**
________________________________________________

**Antidotos Aplicados:**
________________________________________________

---

**Checklist Version:** 1.0.0
**Based on:** $100M Offers + KB Antipattern Shields

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/bonuses-checklist.md

# Bonuses Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Offers - Alex Hormozi (Chapters 10 & 14)
> **Pattern:** SC-CL-001 (SOP Checklist Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Generated:** 2026-02-10
> **Agent:** hormozi-offers

---

## Pre-Bonus Creation Checklist

### Offer Foundation
- [ ] Core offer clearly defined and priced
- [ ] All customer problems/obstacles identified (Chapter 10 exercise)
- [ ] Solution delivery methods mapped (Trim and Stack complete)
- [ ] Target customer profile documented

### Asset Inventory
- [ ] All existing workshop recordings catalogued
- [ ] All existing webinar recordings catalogued
- [ ] All existing event recordings catalogued
- [ ] All existing interviews catalogued
- [ ] All checklists inventoried
- [ ] All templates inventoried
- [ ] All scripts/swipe files inventoried
- [ ] All tools/calculators inventoried

---

## Bonus Creation Checklist

### For Each Bonus Asset

#### Classification
- [ ] Is this HIGH VALUE? (Wow factor - something they shouldn't miss)
- [ ] Is this LOW COST to deliver? (Marginal cost near zero)
- [ ] Can it stand alone as distinct from core offer?
- [ ] Is it short in duration but high in quality?
- [ ] Would it get lost if bundled in main offer?

#### Type Priority (check which applies)
- [ ] TOOL/CALCULATOR - Highest value (lowest customer effort)
- [ ] CHECKLIST - High value
- [ ] TEMPLATE/SCRIPT - High value
- [ ] SWIPE FILE - High value
- [ ] RECORDING (workshop/webinar) - Medium-high value
- [ ] ADDITIONAL TRAINING - Lower value (convert to tool if possible)

#### Obstacle Mapping
- [ ] Maps to specific customer obstacle or limiting belief
- [ ] Proves their limiting belief is incorrect
- [ ] OR solves the next logical problem they'll face
- [ ] Documented which objection this bonus addresses

---

## Bonus Presentation Checklist

### For Each Bonus

#### 1. Name (Benefit in Title)
- [ ] Name includes specific benefit/outcome
- [ ] Name communicates transformation, not just the thing
- [ ] Name is memorable and distinct
- [ ] Name passes the "can you understand the value without explanation?" test

**Name Formula:** [Outcome/Benefit] + [Descriptive Name]

Examples:
- "Foolproof Budget Grocery System" (not "Shopping List")
- "Never-Quit Accountability System" (not "Weekly Check-ins")
- "Live-It-Up-While-You-Slim-Down Eating Out System" (not "Restaurant Guide")

#### 2. Problem Connection
- [ ] Explains how bonus relates to their specific problem
- [ ] Uses their language from the obstacle list
- [ ] Connection is clear and immediate

#### 3. What It Is
- [ ] Clearly describes what they receive
- [ ] Specific and tangible (not abstract)
- [ ] Format is clear (PDF, video, access, etc.)

#### 4. Origin Story
- [ ] Includes how you discovered or created it
- [ ] Authentic and relatable backstory
- [ ] Shows effort/investment that went into creation

#### 5. Future Pacing (Value Equation Aligned)
- [ ] Paints vivid picture of life with bonus benefits
- [ ] At least ONE of these addressed:
  - [ ] FASTER - achieve results in less time
  - [ ] EASIER - simpler process
  - [ ] LESS SACRIFICE - keep what they value
  - [ ] HIGHER LIKELIHOOD - more certain to succeed

#### 6. Proof Element
- [ ] Includes at least ONE of:
  - [ ] Relevant statistic
  - [ ] Client testimonial/case study
  - [ ] Personal experience/result
- [ ] Proof is credible and verifiable

#### 7. Price Anchor
- [ ] Standalone price assigned
- [ ] Price justified (comparison, time savings, cost savings, etc.)
- [ ] Price is believable but impressive

---

## Bonus Enhancement Checklist

### Scarcity Application (When Appropriate)
- [ ] EXCLUSIVE ACCESS: "Only available through this program"
  - Script: "Only people who sign up for [program] will have access to [bonus] that is never for sale or available anywhere else"
- [ ] LIMITED QUANTITY: Physical or practical limits exist
  - Script: "I have [X] remaining [items], if you buy this program, you can get one as a bonus"

### Urgency Application (When Appropriate)
- [ ] TIME-LIMITED: Bonus only available if they act today
  - Script: "If you buy today, I will add [bonus] which normally costs $[X], for free. I do this because I want to reward the action-takers."

**Key Distinction:**
- Scarcity = Not time-limited, but exclusively available through this offer
- Urgency = Time-limited, buy TODAY or lose the bonus

---

## Partner Bonus Checklist

### Partner Identification
- [ ] NOT a direct competitor
- [ ] Serves same customer demographic
- [ ] Solves "the next natural thing they'll want"
- [ ] Has products/services with clear perceived value

### Partner Negotiation

#### Initial Trade
- [ ] Pitched exposure to your best prospects (paying customers)
- [ ] Secured product/service to include as bonus
- [ ] Value of partner bonus documented
- [ ] Agreement confirmed (written)

#### Commission Deal (Advanced)
- [ ] Referral commission discussed
- [ ] Rate agreed ($ per person or % of sale)
- [ ] Tracking mechanism established
- [ ] Agreement confirmed (written)

#### Group Discount (Advanced)
- [ ] Exclusive discount negotiated for your customers
- [ ] Discount they couldn't get on their own
- [ ] Creates triple-win structure

**Triple Win Validation:**
- [ ] Your customers win (exclusive access/discount)
- [ ] Partner wins (free marketing to qualified buyers)
- [ ] You win (better offer + potential commission revenue)

---

## 1-on-1 Sales Bonus Checklist

### Before Presenting Bonuses
- [ ] Full value presentation of core offer completed
- [ ] First close attempt made WITHOUT mentioning bonuses

### If They Say YES
- [ ] Revealed bonuses as surprise AFTER sign-up
- [ ] Created "wow" experience
- [ ] Reinforced their buying decision

### If They Say NO
- [ ] Identified their specific objection
- [ ] Selected bonus that directly addresses that objection
- [ ] Presented bonus with agreement: "Fair enough?"
- [ ] If still no, added another matching bonus
- [ ] NEVER offered a discount (add bonuses instead)

---

## Final Stack Validation Checklist

### Value Ratio
- [ ] Total bonus value EXCEEDS main offer price
- [ ] Target: Bonus value 2x-5x the main offer price
- [ ] Psychology validated: "If these are the bonuses, the main thing must be even MORE valuable"

### Composition
- [ ] Tools and checklists make up >70% of bonuses
- [ ] All major customer obstacles addressed
- [ ] Each bonus has unique purpose (no redundancy)
- [ ] Partner bonuses included where available

### Individual Bonus Validation
For EACH bonus in the stack:
- [ ] Name has benefit in title
- [ ] Maps to specific obstacle
- [ ] Has proof element
- [ ] Price is justified
- [ ] Delivery method is clear

### Presentation Order
- [ ] Sequenced for maximum psychological impact
- [ ] Highest-impact bonuses prominently featured
- [ ] Scarcity/urgency applied to appropriate bonuses
- [ ] Value builds progressively through stack

---

## Quick Reference: Bonus Creation Formula

```
1. INVENTORY existing assets (recordings, tools, templates)
2. MAP to customer obstacles
3. NAME with benefit in title
4. CONNECT to their specific problem
5. DESCRIBE what it is
6. TELL origin story
7. FUTURE PACE the benefits (faster/easier/less sacrifice/more likely)
8. PROVE it works (stat/testimonial/experience)
9. PRICE and justify
10. ENHANCE with scarcity/urgency (where appropriate)
11. STACK until value eclipses main offer
```

---

## Quick Reference: The 11 Bonus Bullets (from source)

1. [ ] Always offer bonuses
2. [ ] Give them a special name with benefit in title
3. [ ] Tell them:
   - a) How it relates to their problem
   - b) What it is
   - c) How you discovered/created it
   - d) How it will improve their life (faster/easier/less sacrifice)
4. [ ] Provide proof (stat, client, or personal experience)
5. [ ] Paint vivid mental picture of life with benefits
6. [ ] Always assign a price and justify it
7. [ ] Tools and checklists > additional trainings
8. [ ] Each bonus addresses specific obstacle/concern
9. [ ] Solve the next problem before they encounter it
10. [ ] Bonus value should eclipse main offer value
11. [ ] Add scarcity and urgency to bonuses (puts technique on steroids)

---

## Quality Gate Checklist

| Gate | Check | Pass/Fail |
|------|-------|-----------|
| Benefit Name | Name includes clear benefit | [ ] |
| Obstacle Mapped | Addresses specific objection | [ ] |
| Proof Present | Has stat, testimonial, or story | [ ] |
| Price Justified | Believable standalone price | [ ] |
| Value Eclipse | Total bonus > main offer price | [ ] |
| Tool Ratio | >70% tools/checklists | [ ] |
| No Discount | Never reduced main offer price | [ ] |

---

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

- [ ] NOT inventing new bonus content (only extract from source)
- [ ] NOT including low-value fillers
- [ ] NOT using generic names without benefits
- [ ] NOT forgetting proof elements
- [ ] NOT leaving any major obstacle unaddressed
- [ ] NOT prioritizing training over tools
- [ ] NOT discounting instead of adding bonuses
- [ ] NOT missing partner bonus opportunities

---

**Checklist Complete:** Ready to create irresistible bonus stack



<\!-- Criado com Squad Creator do AIOXPRO por @oalanicolas e @pedrovalerio | 2026-02-10 -->


## Referência: references/squad/checklists/branding-checklist.md

# Branding Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Branding - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** HO-CL-001 (Hormozi Checklist Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Agent:** hormozi-content

---

## Pre-Flight Checklist

Before starting brand building, verify:

### Strategic Readiness
- [ ] Clear understanding: Branding = deliberate pairing of things
- [ ] Leadership aligned on 5-year minimum commitment
- [ ] Budget allocated for brand building (not just product/economics)
- [ ] Content creation capacity available
- [ ] Distribution channels identified

### Mindset Alignment
- [ ] Understand: Good branding = pairing with things audience LIKES
- [ ] Understand: Bad branding = pairing with things audience DISLIKES
- [ ] Understand: No branding = invisible (normal behavior)
- [ ] Patience commitment: "Wait five years and don't give up"
- [ ] Pricing power goal clear: 2x-10x competitors

### Tracking Systems
- [ ] Reach measurement configured
- [ ] Engagement/influence tracking active
- [ ] Customer feedback loops established
- [ ] Sales attribution to brand activities

---

## Step 1: Figure Out Who Your Ideal Customer Is

### Criterion 1: Growing Market
- [ ] Market size data collected (3-5 year trends)
- [ ] Market is GROWING (not shrinking or maintaining)
- [ ] Growth rate documented
- [ ] "Even if I stay the same size, I'm still going to grow because the market's growing"

### Criterion 2: Have Enough Money
- [ ] Target audience income/revenue levels researched
- [ ] They CAN AFFORD what you sell
- [ ] Premium pricing viable with this audience
- [ ] "If I want to charge a lot of money, they've got to have the money"

### Criterion 3: Easy to Target
- [ ] Advertising platforms assessed for targeting options
- [ ] Community/gathering places identified
- [ ] Reaching them with ads is EASY
- [ ] "If my customers exist, but I can't find them... does it matter?"

### Criterion 4: In Pain
- [ ] Pain points documented
- [ ] Urgency level assessed
- [ ] They DESPERATELY WANT what you sell
- [ ] Competition exists (validates demand)
- [ ] "I'd rather have competition because at least I know people are buying"

### Avatar Validation Score
| Criterion | Met? |
|-----------|------|
| Growing Market | [ ] |
| Have Money | [ ] |
| Easy to Target | [ ] |
| In Pain | [ ] |
| **TOTAL** | __/4 |

**Minimum requirement: 3/4 to proceed**

---

## Step 2: Figure Out What They Like

### Values Inventory
- [ ] Core value #1: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #2: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #3: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #4: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #5: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #6: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #7: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #8: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #9: ___________________
- [ ] Core value #10: ___________________

**Example (Assisted Living Owners):**
- Making more money
- Getting more customers
- Making more profits
- Building a sellable business
- Help recruiting talent
- Retaining talent
- Fewer lawsuits
- Paying fewer taxes

### Admired Figures Inventory
- [ ] Admired figure #1: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #2: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #3: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #4: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #5: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #6: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #7: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #8: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #9: ___________________
- [ ] Admired figure #10: ___________________

**Note:** Verify admiration, not just awareness

### Desired Outcomes Inventory
- [ ] Outcome #1: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #2: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #3: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #4: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #5: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #6: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #7: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #8: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #9: ___________________
- [ ] Outcome #10: ___________________

**Make outcomes concrete and measurable**

### Experience Preferences Inventory
- [ ] Experience #1: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #2: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #3: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #4: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #5: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #6: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #7: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #8: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #9: ___________________
- [ ] Experience #10: ___________________

**Include both aspirational and current**

### Step 2 Validation
| Category | Items Documented | Minimum |
|----------|-----------------|---------|
| Values | ___/10 | 10 |
| Admired Figures | ___/10 | 10 |
| Desired Outcomes | ___/10 | 10 |
| Experience Preferences | ___/10 | 10 |

---

## Step 3: Associate Your Brand With Things They Like

### Content Creation Checklist

**Content Types:**
- [ ] Videos planned and producing
- [ ] Blogs/articles planned and producing
- [ ] Booklets/PDFs planned and producing
- [ ] Podcasts/appearances planned

**Content Quality Gate:**
For EACH piece of content, ask:
- [ ] "Does this genuinely help my audience?"
- [ ] "Is this geared toward my ideal customer?"
- [ ] "Will they think 'this stuff really makes my life better'?"
- [ ] "Who will they think of when it helps them?" (Answer: Your brand)

**Example Content Ideas (from Assisted Living Law Firm):**
- [ ] "Things that helped lower costs and improve quality of life for residents"
- [ ] "How to structure accounting to save more money"
- [ ] "How to set up floor plans for efficiency"

### Distribution Checklist

**Reach Principle:** "A brand can't exist without [reach], so reach is the primary element of a brand"

- [ ] Primary distribution channel #1: ___________________
- [ ] Primary distribution channel #2: ___________________
- [ ] Primary distribution channel #3: ___________________
- [ ] Secondary channel #1: ___________________
- [ ] Secondary channel #2: ___________________
- [ ] Tracking configured for each channel
- [ ] Performance reviewed weekly

### Product Association Checklist
- [ ] Products genuinely serve the audience
- [ ] Products match brand promises
- [ ] Products create positive experience
- [ ] "Your premium brand had better be delivering something special" - Warren Buffett

### People Association Checklist
- [ ] Potential collaborator #1: ___________________ (audience likes? [ ])
- [ ] Potential collaborator #2: ___________________ (audience likes? [ ])
- [ ] Potential collaborator #3: ___________________ (audience likes? [ ])
- [ ] Appearances planned only with people audience admires

### Association Quality Gate
Before EVERY association, ask:
- [ ] "Does the MAJORITY of my ideal audience LIKE this?"
  - YES = Execute
  - NO = Reject
  - UNCERTAIN = Test small first

### Iteration Checklist
- [ ] Audience response monitoring active
- [ ] Behavior change measured (not just sentiment)
- [ ] Content adjusted based on response
- [ ] Failed associations identified and removed

---

## Step 4: Optimize Associations for Maximum Profit

### Market Position Assessment

**Current Position:** ___________________

**Five Directions to Consider:**

| Direction | Definition | Potential Move | Viable? |
|-----------|------------|----------------|---------|
| Up Market | Larger customers | _______________ | [ ] |
| Down Market | Smaller customers | _______________ | [ ] |
| Adjacent | Similar but different | _______________ | [ ] |
| Broader | Entire category | _______________ | [ ] |
| Narrower | Slice of existing | _______________ | [ ] |

### Pivot Planning Checklist

**Before Any Pivot:**
- [ ] Current associations documented ("bouquet inventory")
- [ ] New associations identified (flowers to add)
- [ ] Associations to reduce identified (flowers to trim)
- [ ] Audience impact projected (who gains, who loses)
- [ ] Net change calculated: Gains > Losses?

**Net Change Rule:**
"Losing audience is a part of life. You just wanna make sure you gain more than you lose."

| Metric | Expected Gain | Expected Loss | Net |
|--------|---------------|---------------|-----|
| Audience Size | +___ | -___ | +/- ___ |
| Engagement | +___ | -___ | +/- ___ |
| Revenue | +___ | -___ | +/- ___ |

**Proceed only if NET POSITIVE**

### Pivot Execution Checklist
- [ ] Go decision confirmed (net positive expected)
- [ ] Bouquet adjustment strategy defined
- [ ] Monitoring plan in place
- [ ] Revert criteria established
- [ ] Timeline set

### Post-Pivot Monitoring
- [ ] Actual vs projected tracked daily/weekly
- [ ] Audience feedback monitored
- [ ] Sales impact measured
- [ ] Ready to adjust or revert if needed

---

## Branding Cycle Checklist (Levels of Authority)

### Level 1: What You Say (Least Influential)
- [ ] Content is consistent with brand message
- [ ] Advertising aligns with brand positioning
- [ ] Outreach reflects brand values

### Level 2: What Others Say (More Influential)
- [ ] Affiliates represent brand well
- [ ] Customer testimonials collected
- [ ] Word of mouth monitored
- [ ] Referral programs aligned with brand

### Level 3: What They Experience (MOST Influential)
- [ ] Product delivers on promises
- [ ] Customer experience matches brand
- [ ] Problems resolved quickly
- [ ] Experience reinforces brand associations

**Key Insight:**
"Your advertising has a stronger influence on your brand in the short term. Your product has a stronger influence on your brand in the long term."

## Bouquet Maintenance Checklist

List current associations (flowers in your bouquet):

## Brand Mistake Recovery Checklist

**When Bad Pairing Occurs:**

### Detection
- [ ] Bad pairing identified: ___________________
- [ ] Damage scope assessed
- [ ] Audience impact measured

### Recovery Strategy (NEVER eliminate, only OVERWHELM)
- [ ] Positive associations inventory created
- [ ] Surge content plan developed
- [ ] Additional positive pairings identified
- [ ] Resource allocation for surge

### Surge Execution
- [ ] Content surge launched
- [ ] Multiple positive associations activated
- [ ] All channels utilized
- [ ] Consistency maintained

### Recovery Monitoring
- [ ] Bad pairing shrinking into irrelevance? [ ]
- [ ] Positive associations dominating? [ ]
- [ ] Continue until bad pairing forgotten

**Reference Case:** "Kanye West... has said some things that people don't like, but he also comes out with products that people love... over successive pairings the good stuff minimizes the bad stuff...and people still buy."

## Quality Gate Verification

## Brand Health Metrics

"The single most important decision in evaluating a business is pricing power."

## One Page Branding Checklist (from p.33)

Hormozi's original checklist from the playbook:

- [ ] Figure out who your ideal avatar is:
  - [ ] Growing
  - [ ] In Pain
  - [ ] Can afford your stuff
  - [ ] Easy to find
- [ ] Figure out what they like
- [ ] Associate yourself with the stuff they like through:
  - [ ] Making content they like
  - [ ] Making products they like (both free and paid)
  - [ ] Appearing next to people they like
- [ ] Grow your influence and direction - strategically associate with bigger things that the largest group of your potential customers like. You can go in five directions:
  - [ ] Up market
  - [ ] Down market
  - [ ] Broader market
  - [ ] Narrow market
  - [ ] Adjacent market
- [ ] To grow your reach even more... do more advertising
- [ ] Make your products match your promises, so you create a virtuous cycle of branding:
  - [ ] What you say -> What other people say -> What they say
- [ ] When you make mistakes (which you will), don't shrink away. Double down on what they like.
- [ ] **Wait five years and don't give up.**

---

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference

### Wrong Audience Growing
- [ ] Identify which content attracts wrong people
- [ ] Recenter around ideal customer
- [ ] Accept some audience loss for quality

### High Reach, Low Sales
- [ ] Deepen engagement with target niche
- [ ] Strengthen emotional connection
- [ ] Improve product/promise match

### Competitor Has "Cool Factor"
- [ ] Allocate budget to brand building (not just product)
- [ ] Create associations for intangible value
- [ ] Focus on making people FEEL good

### Bad Publicity Event
- [ ] Don't try to eliminate or hide
- [ ] Launch positive association surge
- [ ] Continue until bad pairing irrelevant

### Pricing Pressure
- [ ] Strengthen unique associations
- [ ] Increase reach + influence
- [ ] Deliver on promises consistently

### Negative Pivot Results
- [ ] Assess if loss is temporary
- [ ] Consider partial revert
- [ ] Test smaller scope next time

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/churn-diagnosis-checklist.md

# Churn Diagnosis Checklist

> Checklist de validação para `diagnose-churn-rate.md` (HZ_RET_001)
> Source: $100M Retention Playbook - Formulas Fundamentais
> Agent: hormozi-retention

---

## Pre-Diagnosis: Data Collection

```yaml
pre_diagnosis:
  required_data:
    - [ ] Número de clientes no início do período
    - [ ] Número de clientes no fim do período
    - [ ] Número de clientes perdidos (churned)
    - [ ] ARPU (Average Revenue Per User)
    - [ ] Gross margin % (margem bruta)
    - [ ] CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost)

  optional_data:
    - [ ] Revenue no início vs fim (para revenue churn)
    - [ ] Avg transactions per customer (se transacional)
    - [ ] NRR (Net Revenue Retention)
    - [ ] Expansion revenue
```

---

## Churn Calculation Validation

```yaml
churn_validation:
  formula_check:
    - [ ] Usou APENAS cohort original (sem novos clientes)
    - [ ] Período definido claramente (mensal/trimestral)
    - [ ] Clientes perdidos = saíram, não pausados

  common_errors:
    - [ ] NÃO incluiu novos clientes no denominador
    - [ ] NÃO confundiu com revenue churn
    - [ ] NÃO misturou períodos diferentes
```

---

## LTV Calculation Validation

```yaml
ltv_validation:
  recurring_business:
    - [ ] Usou fórmula: LTGP = GP Mensal / Churn Rate
    - [ ] Usou Gross Profit (não revenue bruto)
    - [ ] Churn está em decimal (5% = 0.05)

  transactional_business:
    - [ ] Usou fórmula: LTGP = GP/transação × Avg transações
    - [ ] Média de transações baseada em dados reais
```

---

## LTV:CAC Ratio Interpretation

```yaml
ratio_interpretation:
  health_check:
    - [ ] Ratio ≥ 3:1 → Saudável, pode escalar
    - [ ] Ratio 2:1-3:1 → Alerta, otimizar LTV ou reduzir CAC
    - [ ] Ratio < 2:1 → Crítico, PARAR escala

  action_alignment:
    - [ ] Recomendação alinhada com status do ratio
    - [ ] Prioridades corretas (backend antes de acquisition)
```

---

## Red Flags Identified

```yaml
red_flags_check:
  must_flag:
    - [ ] Churn > 10% mensal → PARAR aquisição
    - [ ] LTV:CAC < 2:1 → PARAR escala
    - [ ] Payback > 12 meses → Risco de caixa
    - [ ] NRR < 80% → Hemorrhaging clientes

  green_lights:
    - [ ] Churn < 3% → Produto forte
    - [ ] LTV:CAC > 3:1 → Pode escalar
    - [ ] Payback < 6 meses → Modelo saudável
    - [ ] NRR > 100% → Crescimento orgânico
```

---

## Output Quality

```yaml
output_quality:
  report_complete:
    - [ ] Todas métricas core calculadas
    - [ ] Status de cada métrica definido
    - [ ] Diagnóstico overall claro
    - [ ] Root cause hypothesis documentada
    - [ ] Ações recomendadas priorizadas
    - [ ] Próxima task indicada baseada em dados
```

---

## Decision Rules Applied

```yaml
decision_rules:
  - [ ] DR-001: Churn > 10% = problema de produto, não de crescimento
  - [ ] DR-004: LTV:CAC < 2:1 = parar de escalar
  - [ ] DR-006: LTV:CAC ≥ 3:1 = pode escalar agressivamente
```

---

*Checklist: churn-diagnosis | Version: 1.0*
*Supports: diagnose-churn-rate.md (HZ_RET_001)*

---

## Scoring

| Category | Items | Points Each | Max |
|----------|-------|-------------|-----|
| Critical — Churn Calculation Validation & Red Flags | 11 | 3 | 33 |
| Standard — Required Data, LTV Validation, Ratio Interpretation | 14 | 2 | 28 |
| Bonus — Optional Data, Output Quality, Decision Rules | 13 | 1 | 13 |
| **TOTAL** | **38** | | **74** |

### Thresholds
- **PASS**: >= 60 points (80%)
- **CONDITIONAL**: >= 45 points (60%)
- **FAIL**: < 45 points

### If FAIL
The churn diagnosis is unreliable. Re-collect baseline data ensuring cohort-only calculations (no new customers in denominator), then recalculate LTV using gross profit and verify the LTV:CAC ratio before making any scaling decisions.

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/content-creation-checklist.md

# Content Creation Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Leads: Postar Conteudo Gratuito Parte I & II - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** HO-CL-001 (Hormozi Checklist Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Agent:** hormozi-content

---

## Pre-Flight Checklist

Before starting content creation operations, verify:

### Infrastructure
- [ ] Note-taking system always accessible (phone/watch/notepad)
- [ ] Recording equipment operational (camera, mic, screen capture)
- [ ] Platform accounts created and verified
- [ ] Content calendar system ready
- [ ] Analytics tracking configured per platform
- [ ] Lead capture system ready (if monetizing)

### Knowledge Foundation
- [ ] Five topic categories understood (Distant Past, Recent Past, Present, Trends, Fabricated)
- [ ] Seven headline components memorized (Recency, Relevance, Celebrity, Proximity, Conflict, Unusual, Ongoing)
- [ ] Three retention structures mastered (Lists, Steps, Stories)
- [ ] Give:Ask ratio principles understood

### Content Bank
- [ ] Distant Past lessons documented
- [ ] Recent Past experiences catalogued (last week's calendar reviewed)
- [ ] Idea capture habit established
- [ ] Trending topics monitoring active
- [ ] Fabricated experience ideas listed

---

## Phase I: Hook Checklist

### Topic Selection
**Passado Distante (Distant Past):**
- [ ] Important life lessons identified
- [ ] Connected to product/service value
- [ ] "Story without the scar" approach used
- [ ] Relatable to target audience

**Passado Recente (Recent Past):**
- [ ] Last week's calendar reviewed
- [ ] Meeting insights extracted
- [ ] Conversation lessons captured
- [ ] Client success stories documented
- [ ] Testimonials ready for content

**Presente (Present):**
- [ ] Ideas captured as they come
- [ ] Recording method within arm's reach
- [ ] High-performing ideas marked for expansion
- [ ] Public note-taking active (if applicable)

**Tendencias (Trends):**
- [ ] Current trends identified
- [ ] Personal perspective/experience applied
- [ ] Relevance to expertise established
- [ ] Timing aligned (while still trending)

**Fabricado (Fabricated):**
- [ ] Experience idea documented
- [ ] Effort vs return assessed
- [ ] Content potential evaluated
- [ ] Execution plan ready

### Headline Crafting
**Include at least TWO of these components:**

| Component | Check | Application |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| Recencia (Recency) | [ ] | Most recent possible |
| Relevancia (Relevance) | [ ] | Personally significant to audience |
| Celebridade (Celebrity) | [ ] | Including prominent people |
| Proximidade (Proximity) | [ ] | Close to home geographically |
| Conflito (Conflict) | [ ] | Opposing ideas/people/nature |
| Incomum (Unusual) | [ ] | Strange, unique, rare, bizarre |
| Em andamento (Ongoing) | [ ] | Stories still in progress |

**Headline Validation:**
- [ ] Gives clear reason to consume
- [ ] Stands out from alternatives
- [ ] Promises specific value
- [ ] Appropriate length for platform

### Format Matching
- [ ] Target platform identified
- [ ] Top-performing content in niche studied
- [ ] Visual style matched to platform norms
- [ ] Length appropriate for platform
- [ ] Format familiar to audience expectations

---

## Phase II: Retain Checklist

### Lists
- [ ] Items follow theme
- [ ] Number stated in headline or first seconds
- [ ] Each item provides value
- [ ] Order logical (even if not required)
- [ ] Embedded curiosity: "they want to know all items"

**List Templates:**
- "X Ways I [achieved result]"
- "X [things] That [outcome]"
- "X Mistakes [avatar] Make"
- "X Lessons From [experience]"

### Steps
- [ ] Actions in correct order
- [ ] Clear outcome when completed
- [ ] First steps valuable and clear
- [ ] Each step builds on previous
- [ ] Completion feels achievable

**Steps Templates:**
- "X Steps to [achieve result]"
- "How I [do thing] in X Steps"
- "The [Routine/Process] That [outcome]"

### Stories
- [ ] Clear beginning, middle, end
- [ ] Lesson or conclusion included
- [ ] Relatable characters/situations
- [ ] Tension or conflict present
- [ ] Resolution satisfies curiosity

**Story Types:**
- [ ] Things that happened (real experiences)
- [ ] Things that could happen (scenarios)
- [ ] Things that will never happen (imagination)

### Interweaving
For complex content:
- [ ] Lists within steps considered
- [ ] Stories for each list item considered
- [ ] Stories to reinforce step value
- [ ] Multiple storylines if appropriate
- [ ] Creativity maximized

### Short vs Long Form
- [ ] Length matches platform norms
- [ ] Value per second maintained throughout
- [ ] If long: multiple content units linked together
- [ ] If short: single focused content unit
- [ ] Started smaller, building to longer over time

---

## Phase III: Reward Checklist

### Value Per Second
- [ ] Rewards happen frequently throughout
- [ ] No boring sections (cut or improve)
- [ ] Pacing maintains engagement
- [ ] Information density appropriate
- [ ] "No such thing as too long, only too boring" principle applied

### Promise Fulfillment
- [ ] Hook promise clearly identified
- [ ] Content delivers exactly what was promised
- [ ] Quantity matches (if promised 7, give 7)
- [ ] Quality matches expectations
- [ ] Audience can actually USE the information

**Failure Prevention:**
- [ ] NOT giving fewer items than promised
- [ ] NOT giving bad/known items
- [ ] NOT speaking to wrong audience
- [ ] NOT making unusable promises

### Expectation Exceeding
- [ ] More value than expected delivered
- [ ] Bonus insights included
- [ ] Actionable takeaways clear
- [ ] Reason to share created
- [ ] Reason to come back created

### Success Validation
- [ ] Audience growth tracked
- [ ] If growing: content is rewarding
- [ ] If stagnant: content needs improvement
- [ ] If shrinking: major quality issue to address
- [ ] Continuous improvement mindset active

---

## Phase IV: Monetization Checklist

### Give:Ask Ratio Assessment

| Platform Type | Minimum Ratio | Target Ratio |
|---------------|---------------|--------------|
| Mature (TV, FB) | 3.5:1 | 4:1 |
| Growing | 10:1 | Give until they ask |
| Building Audience | N/A | Pure give |

**Current Ratio Calculation:**
- [ ] Total "give" content counted
- [ ] Total "ask" content counted
- [ ] Ratio calculated
- [ ] Ratio exceeds minimum
- [ ] Audience growth not slowing after asks

### Integration Method Selection

**Integrated (for long-form):**
- [ ] Give:ask ratio maintained within piece
- [ ] Offers placed after valuable moments
- [ ] Offers placed at content end
- [ ] Not over-asking (friend's podcast warning)
- [ ] Growth not slowing after integration

**Example Check:**
- [ ] 60min podcast = max 1.5min total asks
- [ ] 3x 30-second ads = acceptable

**Intermittent (for short-form):**
- [ ] 10 give posts before 1 ask post
- [ ] Ask posts clearly valuable too
- [ ] Pattern sustainable
- [ ] Growth not slowing after asks

### Offer Type Selection

**Lead Magnet (Lower Risk):**
- [ ] Lead magnet created
- [ ] Relevant to content topic
- [ ] Clear value proposition
- [ ] Easy opt-in process
- [ ] Thank you page has main offer

**Lead Magnet Script:**
```
"I have [X] more tips that helped me [result].
Go to [destination] to get a nice visual of them."
```
- [ ] Script adapted to your offer

**Main Offer (Direct Path):**
- [ ] Offer clearly defined
- [ ] Specific avatar called out
- [ ] Dream result stated
- [ ] Time delay mentioned
- [ ] Effort/sacrifice removed
- [ ] Guarantee included
- [ ] Clear CTA

**Main Offer Template:**
```
"I'm looking for [number] [specific avatar] to help achieve
[dream result] in [time delay]. Best part: you don't need
[effort/sacrifice]. If you don't get [dream result]:
1) I'll refund your money
2) I'll work with you until you do.
If that sounds fair, [CTA: DM/schedule/comment/reply]..."
```
- [ ] Template customized to your offer

### Monetization Timing
- [ ] Patience vs urgency assessed
- [ ] Growth priority vs revenue priority decided
- [ ] "Give until they ask" considered first
- [ ] Business needs balanced with growth potential

---

## Phase V: Scaling Checklist

### Current State Assessment
- [ ] Primary platform identified
- [ ] Current posting frequency documented
- [ ] Current growth rate calculated
- [ ] Quality level assessed
- [ ] Resource capacity evaluated

### Strategy Selection

**Depth-First (Profundidade depois largura):**
Best for: Starting out, limited resources

- [ ] Step 1: Post on one relevant platform
- [ ] Step 2: Post regularly on that platform
- [ ] Step 3: Maximize quality AND quantity
  - Short-form: up to 10x/day
  - Long-form: 5x/week
- [ ] Step 4: Add another platform (maintain first)
- [ ] Step 5: Repeat until all platforms maximized

**Breadth-First (Largura depois profundidade):**
Best for: Existing business, resources available

- [ ] Step 1: Post on one relevant platform
- [ ] Step 2: Post regularly
- [ ] Step 3: Move to next platform (maintain previous)
- [ ] Step 4: Continue until on all relevant platforms
- [ ] Step 5: Maximize all platforms together

### Volume Scaling
- [ ] Current posting frequency documented
- [ ] Target posting frequency set
- [ ] Quality maintained at higher volume
- [ ] 10x content = 10x growth principle remembered
- [ ] Sustainable pace established

### Repurposing Strategy
- [ ] Long-form content identified for repurposing
- [ ] Short-form formats mapped
- [ ] Platform-specific adaptations planned
- [ ] Quality maintained across formats
- [ ] Efficiency gained without quality loss

---

## Voice & Authenticity Checklist

### "How I" vs "How To"
- [ ] Speaking from experience, not prescription
- [ ] "I do X" instead of "You should do X"
- [ ] "My favorite ways" instead of "The best ways"
- [ ] Experience-based claims only
- [ ] Unquestionable authenticity

**Good Examples:**
- "I make my oatmeal this way"
- "How I Built My 7-Figure Agency"
- "My favorite way to generate leads"

**Bad Examples to Avoid:**
- "You should make your oatmeal this way"
- "How to Build a 7-Figure Agency"
- "This is the best way to generate leads"

### Differentiation
- [ ] Only I can say this
- [ ] Unique experience included
- [ ] Personal perspective clear
- [ ] Not generic advice anyone could give

### Repetition Permission
- [ ] Repeating important messages
- [ ] Not worried about "already said it"
- [ ] Remembering: 1 in 5 haven't seen it
- [ ] Bored with content before audience is

### Seven Lessons Applied

| # | Lesson | Check |
|---|--------|-------|
| 1 | How I vs How To | [ ] Speaking from experience |
| 2 | Reminded vs Taught | [ ] Repeating important things |
| 3 | Puddles to Oceans | [ ] Starting narrow, expanding over time |
| 4 | Content = Sales Tools | [ ] Greatest hits list for sales team |
| 5 | Free Retains Paid | [ ] Free content is valuable |
| 6 | Higher Standards | [ ] Making content better, not shorter |
| 7 | Avoid Pre-Scheduling | [ ] Manual posting when possible |

---

## Quality Gate Verification

| Gate | Check | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| QG-001 | Headline has 2+ components | [ ] |
| QG-002 | Content uses lists/steps/stories | [ ] |
| QG-003 | Hook promise = content delivery | [ ] |
| QG-004 | Format matches platform norms | [ ] |
| QG-005 | Give:ask ratio >= 3.5:1 | [ ] |
| QG-006 | Audience growing | [ ] |
| QG-007 | Uses "how I" not "how to" | [ ] |

---

## KPI Targets

### Primary Metrics

| Metric | Target | Current | Status |
|--------|--------|---------|--------|
| Audience Size | Growing | _____ | [ ] |
| Monthly Growth Rate | >30% | ___% | [ ] |
| Content Velocity | Match platform max | ___/day | [ ] |

### Growth Benchmarks

| Stage | Monthly Growth Rate | Posting Frequency |
|-------|---------------------|-------------------|
| Starting | >10% | 1x/day |
| Building | >30% | 3x/day |
| Scaling | >50% | Platform max |

### Hormozi Timeline Reference
- Year 1 with regular posting: +200,000 audience
- Months 7-12 with 10x content: +1,200,000 audience
- Podcast to Top 10: 5 years of 2x/week

---

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference

### Audience Not Growing
- [ ] Check share rate (reward quality indicator)
- [ ] Review headline components
- [ ] Compare posting frequency to benchmarks
- [ ] Analyze platform-specific metrics
- [ ] Remember: "If not growing, content not good enough"

### High Views, Low Engagement
- [ ] Compare hook promise to content
- [ ] Check completion rate (retention)
- [ ] Review content structure
- [ ] Ensure promise fulfillment

### Growing But No Leads
- [ ] Check offer frequency
- [ ] Review offer messaging
- [ ] Analyze offer click-through
- [ ] Test lead magnet vs main offer

### Shrinking After Monetization
- [ ] Calculate actual give:ask ratio
- [ ] Compare to pre-monetization growth
- [ ] Reduce ask frequency
- [ ] Return to "give until they ask"

### Content Creation Burnout
- [ ] Use all five topic categories
- [ ] Implement repurposing
- [ ] Consider team/delegation
- [ ] Batch content creation

---

## Daily Operations Checklist

### Morning
- [ ] Check overnight performance
- [ ] Review today's content plan
- [ ] Capture any morning ideas
- [ ] Review trending topics

### Throughout Day
- [ ] Capture ideas as they come
- [ ] Post scheduled content
- [ ] Engage with comments
- [ ] Monitor performance

### Evening
- [ ] Post evening content (if applicable)
- [ ] Review daily metrics
- [ ] Plan tomorrow's content
- [ ] Document new topic ideas

### Weekly
- [ ] Full analytics review
- [ ] Top performing content analysis
- [ ] Content calendar planning
- [ ] Topic bank replenishment
- [ ] Calendar review for Recent Past topics
- [ ] Give:ask ratio calculation

### Monthly
- [ ] Total followers count
- [ ] Growth rate calculation
- [ ] Platform comparison
- [ ] Strategy adjustment
- [ ] Scaling assessment

---

## Content Unit Quick Checklist

For each piece of content:

### HOOK
- [ ] Topic from one of five categories
- [ ] Headline with 2+ components
- [ ] Format matches platform

### RETAIN
- [ ] Uses list, steps, OR story
- [ ] Curiosity created
- [ ] Structure maintains engagement

### REWARD
- [ ] Value per second high
- [ ] Promise fulfilled
- [ ] Expectations exceeded

### VOICE
- [ ] "How I" not "How to"
- [ ] Unique to me
- [ ] Authentic experience

---

**Target: 80%+ for production readiness**

## Content Templates

### List Post Template
```
[Number] [Category] That [Outcome]

[Hook: Why this matters to you]

1. [Item 1]
   [Brief explanation]

2. [Item 2]
   [Brief explanation]

[Continue for all items]

[Reward: Summary + Bonus insight]
```

### Steps Post Template
```
How I [Achieve Result] in [Number] Steps

[Hook: Why you should care]

Step 1: [Action]
[Explanation + Why]

Step 2: [Action]
[Explanation + Why]

[Continue for all steps]

[Reward: What happens when you complete all steps]
```

### Story Post Template
```
[Intriguing opening line]

[Setup: Context and characters]

[Conflict: What went wrong/challenge faced]

[Journey: What happened next]

[Resolution: How it turned out]

[Lesson: What I learned that helps you]
```

### Integrated Offer Template (Long-form)
```
[After valuable section]

Quick note: If you want more on [topic], I put together
[lead magnet description] that shows [specific value].
Grab it at [destination]. Back to what we were talking about...
```

### Intermittent Offer Template (Short-form)
```
[After 10 give posts]

I'm looking for [number] [avatar] who want to [achieve result]
in [timeframe] without [sacrifice].

If that's you, [CTA].
```
