## Referência: references/squad/checklists/lead-nurture-checklist.md

# Lead Nurture Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Lead Nurture - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-CL-001 (Checklist Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10
> **Agent:** hormozi-retention

---

## Pre-Flight Setup

### Infrastructure Requirements
- [ ] CRM system operational and configured
- [ ] Scheduler software installed and tested
- [ ] Auto-dialer system configured (2-3x team efficiency)
- [ ] Multi-channel messaging platform integrated:
  - [ ] Phone/Call system active
  - [ ] SMS/Text platform operational
  - [ ] Email sequences configured
  - [ ] DM channels accessible (Instagram, LinkedIn, etc.)
- [ ] Lead scoring algorithm implemented
- [ ] Call recording enabled for training
- [ ] Rep performance dashboard configured
- [ ] Local area code wrapping enabled

### Calendar Configuration
- [ ] 7-day appointment availability enabled
- [ ] Extended hours configured (6am-6pm PST minimum)
- [ ] 15-minute time slot intervals set
- [ ] Buffer times defined between appointments
- [ ] Staff rotation schedule created
- [ ] Nationwide coverage verified (9am-9pm EST)

### Self-Scheduler Optimization
- [ ] Header confirms right place + next action + why
- [ ] Available dates/times visible immediately
- [ ] Mobile responsiveness verified
- [ ] Desktop view optimized
- [ ] Minimal form fields (no redundant questions)
- [ ] Closer name/photo displayed for human connection
- [ ] Calendar link functional and tested

### Lead Scoring System
- [ ] Scoring criteria defined:
  - [ ] GREEN (Prime) criteria documented
  - [ ] YELLOW (Less qualified) criteria documented
  - [ ] RED (Unqualified) criteria documented
- [ ] Routing rules configured:
  - [ ] Green leads routed to best closers
  - [ ] Yellow leads to standard process
  - [ ] Red leads to resources/downsell path
- [ ] Lead source tracking enabled
- [ ] Demographic data collection configured

### Incentive Inventory
- [ ] Push incentives prepared (gift cards, etc.)
- [ ] Pull incentive options defined (A/B choices):
  - [ ] Quantity options (one or two?)
  - [ ] Type options (product A or B?)
  - [ ] Color options (black or white?)
  - [ ] Time options (morning or afternoon?)
  - [ ] Personnel options (John or Sara?)
- [ ] Incentive budget per lead approved
- [ ] Gift card distribution system ready
- [ ] Inventory stock verified

### Proof Library
- [ ] Testimonials organized by demographic
- [ ] Case studies segmented by industry
- [ ] Video testimonials uploaded and accessible
- [ ] Photo testimonials categorized
- [ ] Results screenshots organized
- [ ] Before/after examples ready

---

## Pillar I: Availability Checklist

### Days Per Week
- [ ] Monday appointments enabled
- [ ] Tuesday appointments enabled
- [ ] Wednesday appointments enabled
- [ ] Thursday appointments enabled
- [ ] Friday appointments enabled
- [ ] Saturday appointments enabled
- [ ] Sunday appointments enabled
- [ ] Staff coverage confirmed for all 7 days
- [ ] "40% more opportunity" baseline achieved (7 days vs 5 days)

### Hours Per Day
- [ ] Early morning slots available (6am-9am PST)
- [ ] Core hours available (9am-5pm PST)
- [ ] Evening slots available (5pm-6pm PST)
- [ ] Extended hours for East Coast (9am-9pm EST)
- [ ] Staff shifts covering all time zones
- [ ] No gaps in calendar coverage

### Time Slot Flexibility
- [ ] 15-minute intervals configured:
  - [ ] :00 slots available
  - [ ] :15 slots available
  - [ ] :30 slots available
  - [ ] :45 slots available
- [ ] Appointment duration standardized
- [ ] Gap time used for lead follow-up activities
- [ ] Calendar efficiency maximized

### Multi-Channel Scheduling
- [ ] Inbound scheduling active (leads call in)
- [ ] Outbound scheduling active (reps call out)
- [ ] Self-scheduling link operational
- [ ] All three channels integrated into CRM
- [ ] Confirmation emails/SMS automated
- [ ] Double-booking prevention enabled

---

## Pillar II: Speed Checklist

### Speed to First Contact
- [ ] Real-time lead notification system active
- [ ] Alert triggers within 60 seconds of opt-in
- [ ] Rep response time tracking enabled
- [ ] 5-minute contact SLA enforced
- [ ] "That was fast!" feedback tracked
- [ ] Contact time logged per lead
- [ ] 391% conversion increase target (60-second contact)
- [ ] 7x qualification increase target (vs 1 hour later)
- [ ] 78% first responder win rate targeted

### Day 1 Contact Cadence
- [ ] Call within 5 minutes of opt-in
- [ ] Double-dial immediately after first call
- [ ] Voicemail script prepared and used
- [ ] Text sent immediately after voicemail
- [ ] Second double-dial + text (hours apart)
- [ ] Third double-dial + text (hours apart)
- [ ] Total 6+ contact attempts on Day 1

### Days 2-3 Cadence
- [ ] Morning call scheduled
- [ ] Evening call scheduled
- [ ] Text after second call each day
- [ ] Total 4+ attempts per day

### Days 4-7 Cadence
- [ ] One call per day scheduled
- [ ] One text per day scheduled
- [ ] Pattern maintained through Day 7
- [ ] Total 7+ attempts days 4-7

### Day 8+ Transition
- [ ] Long-term nurture sequence activated
- [ ] Content soft CTAs configured
- [ ] Re-engagement triggers defined
- [ ] 90-day proof cycle scheduled

### Speed to First Appointment
- [ ] Same-day appointments offered first
- [ ] 72-hour maximum scheduling window enforced
- [ ] >5 day appointments discouraged
- [ ] Pull-forward protocol active

### Five Appointment Outcomes Prioritized
- [ ] Outcome 1: Close them NOW (talking right now = 100% show)
- [ ] Outcome 2: Hot handoff to active closer
- [ ] Outcome 3: Pull appointment forward to today
- [ ] Outcome 4: Confirm within 72h window
- [ ] Outcome 5: Remove unqualified from calendar

### Pull Forward Script Execution
- [ ] Script memorized by reps:
  - [ ] Opening with recorded line disclosure
  - [ ] Confirmation of scheduled time
  - [ ] "Is now a terrible time?" question
  - [ ] Qualification questions (WHO, WHAT, WHAT tried)
  - [ ] "Good news/Better news" transition
  - [ ] Cancellation slot offer
  - [ ] "Unless now is a good time?" always asked
- [ ] Pull forward success rate tracked
- [ ] Calendar gaps used for pull-forward calls

### Hot Handoff Protocol
- [ ] Edification script memorized:
  - [ ] "You're in luck" opening
  - [ ] Expert positioning (years in game, results)
  - [ ] "We're fortunate to have him"
  - [ ] Calendar check pause
  - [ ] "Slide you in" or "Confirmed" transition
  - [ ] Text introduction promise
  - [ ] Phone number confirmation
- [ ] 3-way text group creation enabled
- [ ] Qualification points communicated
- [ ] Handoff success rate tracked

### Response Speed Standards
- [ ] All channels monitored continuously
- [ ] Response time <5 minutes target
- [ ] Rep response times tracked
- [ ] Slow response alerts configured
- [ ] "We prioritize you" messaging reinforced
- [ ] "Slow response = we don't prioritize you" understood

---

## Pillar III: Personalization Checklist

### Multi-Channel Outreach
- [ ] Simultaneous blast protocol active:
  - [ ] Call initiated
  - [ ] Text sent
  - [ ] DM sent (if available)
  - [ ] Email sent
- [ ] "Continue where they respond" rule followed
- [ ] Escalation to richer medium when appropriate
- [ ] "Reach out like you MEAN it" attitude enforced

### Lead Qualification
- [ ] Qualification questions defined
- [ ] Lead scoring performed before appointment
- [ ] Poor fits removed from calendar
- [ ] Resources/downsell offered to unqualified
- [ ] "Canceling bad = more time for good" understood

### Lead Scoring Actions
- [ ] GREEN leads: Priority routing to best closer
- [ ] YELLOW leads: Standard process ("garbage man" opportunity)
- [ ] RED leads: Remove from calendar, offer resources
- [ ] "Yellows are the new gold" culture established

### Lead-Closer Routing Implementation
- [ ] Step 1: Best customers analyzed (demographics + actions)
- [ ] Step 2: Scoring questions in opt-in forms
- [ ] Step 3: 1-5 or Red/Yellow/Green scores assigned
- [ ] Step 4: Best leads routed to best closers
- [ ] Step 5: Conversion by pairing tracked
- [ ] Continuous optimization active

### Segmented Messaging (Easy Version)
- [ ] Lead profile research (5 min minimum for high-value):
  - [ ] Website reviewed
  - [ ] Social profiles checked
  - [ ] Company information gathered
  - [ ] Pain points identified
- [ ] Personalized opening crafted
- [ ] Specific observation included
- [ ] Example: "Hey Greg, I see that your site traffic is down 18%..."

### Segmented Messaging (Hard Version)
- [ ] Different email sequences per lead category
- [ ] Different text sequences per lead category
- [ ] Templates matched to demographics
- [ ] Results examples matched to industry

### Push Incentives (Gifts - Reciprocity)
- [ ] Gift card value appropriate (not insulting)
- [ ] Gift card delivery system ready
- [ ] Script prepared: "make sure you're caffeinated..."
- [ ] Gift delivered regardless of show
- [ ] Reciprocity effect measured
- [ ] Timing: night before appointment

### Pull Incentives (A/B Choice - Commitment)
- [ ] First-time client script ready
- [ ] A/B options defined:
  - [ ] Option A clearly described
  - [ ] Option B clearly described
- [ ] Response triggers commitment tracking
- [ ] Implicit commitment logged
- [ ] "Would you prefer X or Y?" training complete
- [ ] Choice categories available:
  - [ ] Quantity (one bottle or two?)
  - [ ] Start dates (tomorrow or Monday?)
  - [ ] Type (shirt or shorts?)
  - [ ] Colors (black or white?)
  - [ ] Personnel (John or Sara?)
  - [ ] Times (morning or afternoon?)

### Proof Delivery
- [ ] Proof timing configured:
  - [ ] After schedule, before show
  - [ ] Between first and second call
  - [ ] Every 90 days for ghosted leads
- [ ] Demographic matching enforced
- [ ] "Show them what they missed" messaging ready
- [ ] Results of others who signed up when they ghosted prepared

---

## Pillar IV: Volume Checklist

### Contact Attempt Tracking
- [ ] Day 1: 6+ attempts logged
- [ ] Days 2-3: 4+ attempts per day logged
- [ ] Days 4-7: 2+ attempts per day logged
- [ ] Total 15+ attempts in first week
- [ ] Long-term transition after 7 days

### Automated Reminders
- [ ] Immediate confirmation configured:
  - [ ] Time confirmed
  - [ ] Date confirmed
  - [ ] Caller number included
  - [ ] Person meeting with named
- [ ] 24-hour reminder configured
- [ ] 12-hour reminder configured
- [ ] 3-hour reminder configured
- [ ] Transparency about automation maintained
- [ ] Template: "[Auto msg] Hey [Name]! Quick reminder..."
- [ ] Local time zone used

### Manual Reminders
- [ ] Night before personal check-in scheduled
- [ ] Morning of confirmation scheduled
- [ ] 60 minutes before "see you soon" scheduled
- [ ] Real cell phone used (not system number)
- [ ] iPhone preferred (blue messages)
- [ ] Personal touch maintained

### A-C-A Conversation Framework
- [ ] Acknowledge training complete (respond to what they said)
- [ ] Compliment training complete (something genuine)
- [ ] Ask training complete (the next question)
- [ ] Framework applied in all communications
- [ ] Qualify or pull forward through A-C-A

### BAMFAM Protocol
- [ ] "Never end call without scheduling next" rule enforced
- [ ] Script memorized:
  - [ ] "Let me pull up my calendar..."
  - [ ] "[Day A] or [Day B]?" question
  - [ ] "Morning or afternoon?" question
  - [ ] Specific time locked in
  - [ ] Confirmation sent immediately
- [ ] "I'll get back to you" treated as objection
- [ ] "I'll follow up later" = lead goes to no-man's land (avoided)
- [ ] Dodgy about next call = objection to handle
- [ ] BAMFAM success rate tracked
- [ ] "BAMFAM as a way of life" culture established

---

## Decision Rules Validation

### DR-001: Speed Classification
- [ ] Contact time logged for every lead
- [ ] <60 seconds flagged as EXCEPTIONAL (+391% conversion)
- [ ] <5 minutes flagged as STANDARD
- [ ] >5 minutes flagged as SLOW (revenue leak)
- [ ] Speed reports generated daily
- [ ] Immediate contact prioritized

### DR-002: Scheduling Window
- [ ] Same-day slots offered first always (highest show rate)
- [ ] <=72 hours flagged as ACCEPTABLE
- [ ] >72 hours triggers WARNING (increased no-show risk)
- [ ] >5 days triggers DISCOURAGE alert
- [ ] Scheduling window distribution tracked

### DR-003: Lead Score Routing
- [ ] GREEN leads auto-route to top closers
- [ ] YELLOW leads follow standard process
- [ ] RED leads removed + resources offered
- [ ] "Yellows are the new gold" culture maintained
- [ ] Routing effectiveness measured

### DR-004: Ghost Recovery
- [ ] No response AND hours_until_appointment <24h triggers double-book slot
- [ ] No response AND days_since_schedule >3 triggers proof send
- [ ] Complete ghost adds to 90-day nurture
- [ ] "Show them what they missed" campaign active
- [ ] Ghost recovery rate tracked
- [ ] Never give up completely

### DR-005: Incentive Deployment
- [ ] First-time clients receive push incentive (gift card)
- [ ] Qualified leads receive pull incentive (A/B choice)
- [ ] High-value leads receive both
- [ ] Incentive effectiveness measured
- [ ] ROI per incentive type calculated
- [ ] Reciprocity and commitment created

### DR-006: Volume Escalation
- [ ] Day 1 AND attempts <6 continues attempting
- [ ] Day <=3 AND attempts <10 continues attempting
- [ ] Day <=7 AND attempts <15 continues attempting
- [ ] Day >7 transitions to long-term nurture
- [ ] Contact attempt compliance tracked
- [ ] Front-loaded contact attempts enforced

---

## Exception Handling

### Exception 1: Too Many Bad Appointments
- [ ] Calendar quality monitored
- [ ] Trigger: Calendar filled with unqualified leads
- [ ] Friction increase protocol ready:
  - [ ] Video watch requirement before scheduler
  - [ ] Sales letter above scheduler
  - [ ] Price visibility added
  - [ ] Scheduler appearance delayed
- [ ] Bad appointment threshold defined
- [ ] Intervention timeline established

### Exception 2: Lead Can't Schedule Within 72h
- [ ] Treated as objection, not fact
- [ ] Script ready: "What days were you planning on [activity related to offer]?"
- [ ] Response: "This appointment is the first step to that"
- [ ] Alternative scheduling explored
- [ ] Persistence maintained professionally

### Exception 3: High Show Rate, Low Close Rate
- [ ] Rep lead quality distribution reviewed
- [ ] Cherry-picking detection active
- [ ] May be selecting easy leads
- [ ] Fair distribution enforced
- [ ] Close rate by lead type analyzed

### Exception 4: Lead Requests Different Closer
- [ ] Accommodation process defined
- [ ] Pattern investigation triggered
- [ ] Customer preference logged
- [ ] If possible, accommodate
- [ ] Root cause analysis conducted

---

## Quality Gates

### Gate 1: First Contact Speed Gate
- [ ] Target: >50% contacted within 5 minutes
- [ ] If failed: Add capacity or automation
- [ ] Daily measurement active
- [ ] Alert threshold configured
- [ ] Escalation path defined

### Gate 2: Schedule Rate Gate
- [ ] Target: >40% of engaged leads scheduled
- [ ] If failed: Review availability/messaging

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/ltv-checklist.md

# LTV (Lifetime Value) Framework Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Money Models - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 2.0.0
> **Generated:** 2026-02-10
> **Related SOP:** ltv-sop.md
> **Cross-Reference:** upsell-strategy-checklist.md (for detailed upsell validation)
> **Agent:** hormozi-retention

---

## Purpose

Validate that your LTV framework is complete and follows Hormozi's GMMM (Get Money, More Money, Max Money) framework. Use this checklist to maximize Lifetime Value through deliberate offer sequencing across all 4 stages.

**Central Insight:**
> "Voce pode tosquiar uma ovelha por toda a vida, mas so pode esfola-la uma vez." - John, mentor de Alex Hormozi

---

## Pre-Flight Check

Before implementing the LTV framework, verify:

### Business Validation

- [ ] **Product validated** - At least 10 satisfied paying customers
- [ ] **CAC documented** - Cost of Acquisition known and consistent
- [ ] **Delivery capacity** - Can deliver 2x current volume
- [ ] **Payment system ready** - Processor accepts plans and recurring billing
- [ ] **Cash runway** - 3 months of expenses OR credit line available
- [ ] **Tracking installed** - Conversion metrics by stage

### Red Flags - NOT Ready If:

- [ ] **Refund rate > 5%** - Product issues must be fixed first
- [ ] **Can't explain value in 30 seconds** - Messaging needs work
- [ ] **No testimonials/case studies** - Social proof missing
- [ ] **Gross margin < 30%** - Unit economics don't work
- [ ] **Churn > 10% monthly** - Retention crisis

### Scope Validation

**Applies to:**
- [ ] Businesses with recurring products/services
- [ ] Medium to high ticket offers ($500+)
- [ ] Documented CAC
- [ ] B2B and B2C with defined sales cycle

**Does NOT apply to:**
- [ ] Commodities without differentiation
- [ ] Businesses without scalable delivery capacity
- [ ] Gross margin < 30%
- [ ] Refund rate > 5%

---

## SECTION A: Four Pillars of LTV Validation

### A.1: Pillar 1 - 30-Day Profit

- [ ] **Formula understood** - L30 = (P1 x C1) + Sum(Un x Cn x Vn) - CAC - COGS
- [ ] **CAC calculated** - Cost of Acquisition documented
- [ ] **COGS calculated** - Cost of Goods/Services documented
- [ ] **Upsell revenue projected** - Each upsell priced and conversion estimated
- [ ] **30-day profit positive** - Covers CAC + COGS in 30 days
- [ ] **Credit card strategy enabled** - Can use CC as infinite working capital
- [ ] **Consequence understood** - Negative = run out of cash, stop advertising, die slowly

**Formula Calculator:**
```
Initial Price (P1): ____________
Conversion Rate (C1): ____________%
Upsell Revenue Sum: ____________
CAC: ____________
COGS: ____________
30-Day Profit (L30): ____________
[ ] PASS (L30 > 0)
[ ] FAIL (fix offer or add upsells)
```

### A.2: Pillar 2 - Problem-Solution Sequence

- [ ] **Core problem identified** - What your main offer solves
- [ ] **Revealed problems mapped** - Each solution creates new problems
- [ ] **Upsell chain designed** - Each problem has a solution product
- [ ] **Chain is 3+ deep** - Multiple upsell opportunities exist
- [ ] **Problems are genuine** - Not manufactured or forced
- [ ] **Solutions provide real value** - Actually help customers
- [ ] **Consequence understood** - Ignoring = lose 80% of potential profit

**Problem-Solution Examples Validated:**
```
[ ] Rented car -> needs insurance (problem created)
[ ] Fitness challenge -> needs supplements (problem created)
[ ] Software -> needs training (problem created)
```

### A.3: Pillar 3 - Value Anchoring

- [ ] **Anchor price defined** - Premium option 5-10x main price
- [ ] **Premium is genuine** - Would happily fulfill if purchased
- [ ] **Presentation order correct** - Most expensive shown first
- [ ] **Psychological recalibration works** - Other options seem cheap
- [ ] **Consequence understood** - Ignoring = customers always buy cheapest option

**Suit Store Case Study Validated:**
```
[ ] Customer budget: $500
[ ] First suit presented: $16,000
[ ] Second suit presented: $2,200
[ ] Customer bought: $2,200 + $300 accessories = $2,500 (5x budget)
```

### A.4: Pillar 4 - Zero Friction

- [ ] **Card on file enabled** - Can charge without re-asking
- [ ] **No "do you want to buy?"** - Ask "which card?" instead
- [ ] **Payment barriers removed** - Nothing between decision and charge
- [ ] **Multiple payment options** - Credit, debit, financing available
- [ ] **Consequence understood** - 50% of closed sales die in payment friction

---

## SECTION B: GMMM Framework Validation

### B.1: Stage Understanding

| Stage | Objective | Target | KPI | Validated |
|-------|-----------|--------|-----|-----------|
| GET MONEY | Turn strangers into customers | Cover CAC + COGs | 30-day profit > $0 | [ ] |
| MORE MONEY | Maximize profit per customer | 3-5x initial value | LTV 30 days > 3x CAC | [ ] |
| MAX MONEY | Predictable recurring revenue | 80%+ in continuity | Churn < 5% monthly | [ ] |

### B.2: Offer Matrix 4x3 Validation

| Type | Quantity | Quality | Different |
|------|----------|---------|-----------|
| Attraction | [ ] More | [ ] Premium | [ ] New |
| Upsell | [ ] Double | [ ] Better | [ ] Complementary |
| Downsell | [ ] Less | [ ] Inferior | [ ] Alternative |
| Continuity | [ ] Unlimited | [ ] Maintained | [ ] Recurring |

### B.3: 7 Paradigm Shifts Understood

- [ ] Shift 1 documented and applied
- [ ] Shift 2 documented and applied
- [ ] Shift 3 documented and applied
- [ ] Shift 4 documented and applied
- [ ] Shift 5 documented and applied
- [ ] Shift 6 documented and applied
- [ ] Shift 7 documented and applied

---

## SECTION C: Stage I - Attraction Offers (Get Cash) Validation

### C.1: Offer #1 - Get Your Money Back

**Investment Definition:**
- [ ] Value = 3-5x delivery cost
- [ ] B2C sweet spot: $300-$3,000
- [ ] B2B sweet spot: $3,000-$30,000
- [ ] Rule: High enough to filter, low enough to be accessible

**Criteria Model Selection:**
- [ ] Model A (Results-Based) - Lose X in Y weeks
- [ ] Model B (Action-Based) - 100% attendance, 100% tasks
- [ ] Model C (Hybrid - MOST EFFECTIVE) - Actions 70% + Result 30%

**Timeline Selection:**
- [ ] Short (21-28 days) - Maximum urgency
- [ ] Medium (6-8 weeks) - Ideal balance
- [ ] Long (12-16 weeks) - Deep transformations

**Credit Application:**
- [ ] Option A - 100% applied to next purchase immediately
- [ ] Option B - Credit distributed ($600 = $50/month x 12)
- [ ] Option C - Customer chooses A or B

**Scripts & Validation:**
- [ ] Magic script documented - "Whether you hit your goal or not..."
- [ ] Danny's Gym case studied - $500 challenge, 13 referrals from photos
- [ ] Alex's Gym case studied - $600 challenge, 34:1 ROI in 48 hours
- [ ] 70% winner conversion rate understood

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
Investment: $600
Delivery cost: $120
10% refund request: -$60
90% stay (average): $540 revenue
Net first 30 days: $540 - $120 = $420 profit
CAC $100: $420 / $100 = 4.2:1 LTGP:CAC in 30 days
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### C.2: Offer #2 - Giveaways

- [ ] **Main prize chosen** - Exactly what you want to sell next
- [ ] **Perceived value** - 10-20x your average ticket
- [ ] **Partial scholarship** - 30-50% discount presented as 70-90% off
- [ ] **Math example** - $10,000 prize -> "partial scholarship" $7,000 -> customer pays $3,000

**Capture Form:**
- [ ] Name required
- [ ] Email required
- [ ] Phone required
- [ ] Qualifier question required
- [ ] Magic question: "Why do you deserve to win?"

**Timeline (7-14 days):**
- [ ] Days 1-3: Massive promotion
- [ ] Days 4-5: "Last spots"
- [ ] Day 6: "Last day!"
- [ ] Day 7: Announce winner
- [ ] Days 7-14: Convert "losers"

**Execution:**
- [ ] Public: Post celebrating winner
- [ ] Private: Email/SMS "losers" - WHERE THE MONEY IS
- [ ] Master script for "losers" documented

**Hacks:**
- [ ] Double winner hack - "If someone you refer wins, you win too!" = 3-5x participants
- [ ] Economist play in scholarships: A ($59), B ($125), A+B ($125) -> 80% choose combo

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
Prize cost: $5,000 | Marketing: $2,000 | Total: $7,000
500 participants -> 200 buy at $3,000 (40%) = $600,000
ROI: $600,000 / $7,000 = 85.7:1
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### C.3: Offer #3 - Decoy Offer

**Construction:**
- [ ] **Bait defined** - Core function only, no support/guarantees/bonuses
- [ ] **Bait price** - Cost + 10% margin only
- [ ] **Premium defined** - Everything included, 1-on-1, lifetime access, all bonuses
- [ ] **Premium price** - 3-5x bait price

**Presentation Script:**
- [ ] "Are you here for free stuff or lasting results?" [99% say results]
- [ ] BASIC $497: [minimalist] - You're on your own
- [ ] PREMIUM $1,997: [impressive] - We guarantee your success
- [ ] "Which gets you to your goal 10x faster?"

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
100 prospects: 25 bait at $497 = $12,425 | 60 premium at $1,997 = $119,820
Total: $132,245 vs single offer $997: ~30 buyers = $29,910 -> 4.4x lift
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### C.4: Offer #4 - Buy X Get Y Free

**Configuration by Margin:**
- [ ] < 30% margin: Buy 2, Get 1 (physical)
- [ ] 30-60% margin: Buy 1, Get 1 (services)
- [ ] 60-80% margin: Buy 1, Get 2 (digital)
- [ ] > 80% margin: Buy 1, Get 3+ (software)

**Understanding:**
- [ ] Same math, different frame = 5x more sales
- [ ] "Buy 1 pair $600, get 2 free" vs "$200/pair" = same margin, 5x volume
- [ ] Boot Factory Nashville case studied - 5x sales, market dominance for decades

### C.5: Offer #5 - Pay Less Now or More Later

**Structure:**
- [ ] Option A (LATER): $0 today, $497 tomorrow. Zero risk. Card on file.
- [ ] Option B (NOW): $297 today (40% less) + exclusive bonuses
- [ ] 60% choose to pay now

**Pricing Matrix by Ticket:**
- [ ] Low (<$500): Later 100%, Now 60% (40% off)
- [ ] Medium ($500-2k): Later 100%, Now 50% (50% off)
- [ ] High (>$2k): Later 100%, Now 40% (60% off)

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
100 prospects: 60 pay $297 = $17,820 | 40 pay later $497 (80% complete) = $15,904
Total: $33,724 vs single offer $497: ~40 buyers = $19,880 -> 1.7x lift
[ ] VALIDATED
```

---

## SECTION D: Stage II - Upsell Offers (More Cash) Validation

### D.1: Offer #6 - Classic Upsell

**Formula Applied:**
- [ ] "You can't have X without Y" framework documented
- [ ] Problem chain mapped (each solution reveals next problem)

**Case Studies Understood:**
- [ ] Car Rental: Car -> insurance -> gas -> late checkout = 5.2x ($19 -> $100)
- [ ] Hamburger: Burger -> fries -> drink -> supersize = 11.6x ($0.25 -> $3.00 profit)

**9 Key Tactics:**
- [ ] Most profitable upsells first
- [ ] "Say No to Say Yes" - "Voce nao quer mais nada, quer?" (No = Yes)
- [ ] Surprise and delight - Give ALL bonuses even if early yes
- [ ] Hyper-buyer detection - Weddings, babies, new hobbies = embrace upsells
- [ ] Free bonuses CREATE problems that upsells solve
- [ ] Faster access = higher value
- [ ] Bundle upsells and NAME them (transformation package)
- [ ] BAMFAM: Book A Meeting From A Meeting = 5x more opportunities
- [ ] Integrate upsells in delivery of other offers

**Real Numbers Validated:**
- [ ] 19 failed pitches -> "chocolate or vanilla?" -> instant sale -> $5-10k/day
- [ ] Win-back: 200 personalized videos -> $1.9M ARR
- [ ] Average 2-4x LTV increase when well positioned

### D.2: Offer #7 - Menu Upsell

**Formula:** Unsell -> Prescribe -> A/B -> Card on File

**Four Tactics Present:**
- [ ] **UNSELLING** - Cross out what they DON'T need -> builds goodwill -> 25% to 75% conversion
- [ ] **PRESCRIPTION** - Tell what they need, how to use, when, how much
- [ ] **A/B CHOICE** - "Chocolate or vanilla?" removes "yes/no" -> both choices = sale
- [ ] **CARD ON FILE** - "Use the card on file?" -> 40% conversion increase

**Economist Play Ready:**
- [ ] A ($59), B ($125), A+B ($125) -> 80% choose combo

**Real Numbers Validated:**
- [ ] $0 to $5-10k/day supplement sales using menu upsell
- [ ] 80%+ conversion when done correctly
- [ ] Unselling: 25% -> 75% conversion (3x)

### D.3: Offer #8 - Anchor Upsell

**Formula:** Premium first -> Gasp -> Rescue -> Main offer -> Payment

**5 Steps:**
- [ ] Step 1: Present the anchor (5-10x price)
- [ ] Step 2: Wait for the gasp
- [ ] Step 3: Come to rescue: "Voce se importa muito com [premium feature]?"
- [ ] Step 4: Present main offer
- [ ] Step 5: Ask how they want to pay

**CRITICAL:**
- [ ] Treat anchor as REAL offer - If fake, lose trust
- [ ] Quote understood: "The only thing worse than making a $1,000 offer to someone with a $100 budget is making a $100 offer to someone with a $1,000 budget"

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
Without anchor: 30 buy at $2,200 = $66,000
With anchor: 15 premium at $16k + 45 main at $2.2k = $240k + $99k = $339k
Lift: 5.1x revenue
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### D.4: Offer #9 - Rollover Upsell

**Formula:** Credit previous purchase toward larger next purchase

**4 Situations Identified:**
- [ ] RE-ENGAGE dormant clients (6+ months)
- [ ] RESCUE upset clients (instead of refund)
- [ ] STEAL unsatisfied clients from competitors
- [ ] UPSELL current clients (distribute credit)

**Pricing Rule:**
- [ ] Upsell at least 4x the credit = maximum 25% discount

**Gift Card Play Hack:**
- [ ] Sell $200 gift cards for $20
- [ ] Limit to two per customer, can only use on others
- [ ] When they come, roll card to $1,000+ offer
- [ ] Customers PAY YOU to refer friends

**Real Numbers Validated:**
- [ ] 200 personalized videos -> 20% accepted -> $1.9M extra ARR
- [ ] One day recording -> $480k/year net new revenue

---

## SECTION E: Stage III - Downsell Offers (Turn No's into Yes's) Validation

### E.1: Downselling Rules

- [ ] **Rule 1** - "No" means no to THIS offer, not all offers
- [ ] **Rule 2** - Downsells are TRADES - give something, get something
- [ ] **Rule 3** - Personalize, don't pressure
- [ ] **Rule 4** - Same thing in NEW ways
- [ ] **Rule 5** - NEVER lower price on same thing - change offer with price
- [ ] **Rule 6** - Customers talk about price - consistency matters

### E.2: Offer #10 - Payment Plan Downsell

**7-Step Process (stop when they buy):**
- [ ] Step 1: Reward paying in full (price WITH interest -> prepay = discount)
- [ ] Step 2: Third-party financing / credit card / layaway
  - [ ] "Do you prefer that I decide your terms or YOU decide?" -> "I decide" -> card
- [ ] Step 3: Half now, half later (align with pay day)
- [ ] Step 4: CHECK: Scale 1-10. 8+ continue. 7- switch to feature downsell
- [ ] Step 5: Divide into three payments
- [ ] Step 6: Spread evenly (e.g., 16 weeks = 16 payments)
- [ ] Step 7: Free trial (-> Trial with Penalty)

**Seesaw Technique Script:**
- [ ] "Giant or small monthly payments?" -> "Small"
- [ ] "Prepay today: massive discount + zero monthly. Does that work?"
- [ ] If no: "The more you give now = smaller monthly payments"

**Churn by Billing (14,000 companies via ProfitWell):**
```
Monthly:     10.7% churn/month
Quarterly:   5% churn/month
Annual:      2% churn/month
RULE: Double period = half churn. Always start high.
[ ] VALIDATED
```

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
Without plan: 30 buy at $1,000 = $30,000
With plan downsell: 30 full + 20 plans (80% complete) = $30k + $16k = $46,000
Lift: 53% revenue increase
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### E.3: Offer #11 - Trial with Penalty

**Formula:** "If you do X, Y, Z, I'll let you start for free."

**5 Steps:**
- [ ] Step 1: Offer trial LAST (only after main rejected)
- [ ] Step 2: ALWAYS get card ("Which card?" / "How we've always done it")
- [ ] Step 3: Sell staying and paying ("If it works, will you stay long-term?")
- [ ] Step 4: Explain fees AFTER card (not before -> more resistance)
- [ ] Step 5: MANDATORY check-ins (your upsell opportunities)

**Post-Trial Handling:**
- [ ] **Loved it:** Easy upsell to bigger/longer service
- [ ] **Hated it:** "You're right, I'm upset. Your needs match our premium." (50% buy)
- [ ] **Didn't use:** Contact multiple times, waive fee if they show up

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
100 leads: 30 buy main $1,000 + 40 trial
8 fail criteria ($200 penalty) + 24 convert ($500/month)
30 days: $30,000 + $1,600 + $12,000 = $43,600 -> 45% lift
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### E.4: Offer #12 - Feature Downsell

**Formula:** Remove feature -> lower price -> "How about now?"

**The Guarantee Hack:**
```
Full offer $1,000 with guarantee: 25 buy
Remove guarantee, $600: some buy THIS
BUT many reconsider -> buy FULL $1,000 because NOW they see guarantee value
Result: 35 full + 40 without = 75 total (was 25) -> 3x close rate
[ ] VALIDATED
```

**What to Remove (highest value first to trigger re-upsell):**
- [ ] Quantity
- [ ] Quality
- [ ] Service level
- [ ] Availability
- [ ] Speed
- [ ] Ratio
- [ ] Communication
- [ ] Provider
- [ ] Live vs recorded
- [ ] DIY vs DFY
- [ ] Personalization
- [ ] Insurance/Guarantee
- [ ] Entire features

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
Before: 25 x $1,000 = $25,000
After: 35 x $1,000 + 40 x $600 = $59,000 -> 2.36x lift
40% of downsell buyers eventually upgrade
[ ] VALIDATED
```

---

## SECTION F: Stage IV - Continuity Offers (Max Cash) Validation

### F.1: Offer #13 - Continuity Bonus

**Formula:** Incredible bonus to sign up today. Bonus value > first payment.

**Bonus Types:**
- [ ] **Products:** "$800 in free toys with $59/month dog food"
- [ ] **Services:** "$1,000 accelerator free with $100/month membership"
- [ ] **Digital:** "All 40 past newsletters ($15,880) with $399/month subscription"

**Standalone vs Continuity Pricing:**
```
50% continuity: Standalone = 1.33x monthly
60% continuity: Standalone = 1.66x monthly
70% continuity: Standalone = 2.00x monthly
80% continuity: Standalone = 2.33x monthly
90% continuity: Standalone = 2.66x monthly
[ ] Pricing calculated
```

**Post-Entry Upsell:**
- [ ] Pre-paid block (buy 5 get 1 free)
- [ ] 1 in 8 taking = 50% more 30-day profit

**Real Numbers Validated:**
- [ ] Gym: Before 17% effective continuity. After bonus: 40% direct. 2.35x lift.
- [ ] 8 of 40 take annual prepay -> massive cash boost

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
40 enter $99/month (bonus cost $50 each = $2,000)
8 prepay annual $990
Monthly: $3,168 + $660 = $3,828/month -> $45,936/year
vs challenge-only: $20,196/year -> 2.27x lift ARR
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### F.2: Offer #14 - Continuity Discount

**Formula:** Free time with commitment
- [ ] "3 months free with 12-month commit" = 25% off effective
- [ ] "Buy 6 months, get 6 months free" = 50% off, doubles commitment

**4 Announcement Formats:**
- [ ] Percentage: 25% off
- [ ] Dollar: $300 off
- [ ] Free portion: 3 months free
- [ ] Total: 12 months for $900 (crossed out $1,200)

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
Month-to-month $99: average 10 months = $990 LTV
Commit 12 months $75/month: guaranteed $900 + 60% renew = $1,440 average LTV -> 45% lift
[ ] VALIDATED
```

### F.3: Offer #15 - Waived Fee

**Formula:** Setup fee with month-to-month OR waived with annual commit

**Structure:**
- [ ] Option A: $5,000 setup + $1,000/month, cancel anytime
- [ ] Option B: $0 setup, 12-month commit at $1,000/month
- [ ] Early exit = pay waived fee
- [ ] 85% choose commitment. Churn <5%.

**Psychology:**
- [ ] People START to avoid fee
- [ ] People STAY because leaving > staying
- [ ] After commitment: fee disappears forever (equitable)

**Cause-Based Cancellation (Advanced):**
- [ ] "What cause do you absolutely HATE?"
- [ ] "If you cancel early, I'm donating your fee to them"
- [ ] Double aversion = 50% additional churn reduction

**Setup Parameters:**
- [ ] Duration: 12 months minimum
- [ ] Fee: 3-5x monthly
- [ ] Early exit: Pay waived fee
- [ ] If >5% want out early -> investigate product, not pricing

**Base Calculation Validated:**
```
85 annual $1,000/month = $1,020,000
15 month-to-month $5,000 setup + $15,000/month
Year 1: $1,020k + $75k + $120k = $1,215,000
Without fee: 100 x $1,000 x average 6 months = $600,000 -> 2x+ lift
[ ] VALIDATED
```

---

## SECTION G: Health Check System Validation

### G.1: LTGP:CAC Analysis

- [ ] **Ratio calculated** - LTGP / CAC

| Ratio | Status | Action |
|-------|--------|--------|
| > 3:1 | [ ] | Scale aggressively. Model printing money. Invest every cent in acquisition. |
| 2-3:1 | [ ] | Optimize Money Model. Add at least 2 offers to sequence. |
| < 2:1 | [ ] | STOP AND FIX URGENT. Redesign offer sequence BEFORE spending more. |

### G.2: 30-Day CAC Recovery

| Recovery | Status | Action |
|----------|--------|--------|
| < 30 days | [ ] | Healthy business. Can use CC as infinite working capital. |
| > 30 days | [ ] | BANKRUPTCY RISK. 82% of businesses die from cash flow, not customers. |

### G.3: Churn Rate Analysis

| Churn | Status | Action |
|-------|--------|--------|
| < 5% monthly | [ ] | Exceptional. Focus on acquisition and upsells. |
| 5-10% monthly | [ ] | Healthy but improvable. Add waived fee and continuity bonuses. |
| > 10% monthly | [ ] | CRITICAL PROBLEM. Wrong product, bad delivery, or wrong customer. |

### G.4: Performance Benchmarks

| Level | Benchmark | Status |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| BAD | 30-day profit negative | [ ] |
| MEDIUM | 30-day profit = 1x CAC | [ ] |
| GOOD | 30-day profit = 2x CAC | [ ] |
| EXCELLENT | 30-day profit = 3x+ CAC | [ ] |

---

## SECTION H: D.I.E. Framework Validation

### H.1: DIAGNOSE - Where's the problem?

- [ ] **CAC known** - Cost to acquire one customer
- [ ] **Average ticket known** - Revenue per sale
- [ ] **Conversion known** - % who buy
- [ ] **Churn known** - % who leave per month
- [ ] **Billing cycle known** - Monthly, quarterly, annual
- [ ] **LTGP:CAC calculated** - Ratio determined
- [ ] **30-day recovery calculated** - Days to break even
- [ ] **Broken stage identified** - Which of 4 stages failing?

### H.2: IMPLEMENT - Which Money Model fixes it?

| Problem | Solution | Applied |
|---------|----------|---------|
| CAC > 30-day revenue | Fix Attraction Offer | [ ] |
| Low margins | Add Upsells | [ ] |
| Conversion < 20% | Add Downsells | [ ] |
| No predictability | Add Continuity | [ ] |

### H.3: EVALUATE - Numbers in 30 days

- [ ] **30-day cash tracked** - $X -> $Y
- [ ] **CAC payback tracked** - X -> Y days
- [ ] **LTGP:CAC tracked** - X:1 -> Y:1

---

## SECTION I: Cash First Hierarchy Validation

### I.1: Priority Order

- [ ] **Priority 1: Fix Attraction** - If CAC > 30-day revenue (losing money per customer)
- [ ] **Priority 2: Add Upsells** - If covered but low margins (Classic -> Menu -> Anchor -> Rollover)
- [ ] **Priority 3: Add Downsells** - If conversion < 20% (Payment Plan -> Trial Penalty -> Features)
- [ ] **Priority 4: Add Continuity** - If 1-3 work (Bonus -> Waived Fee -> Discount)

### I.2: Sequence Validation

- [ ] **Not skipping steps** - Each priority addressed in order
- [ ] **Each stage profitable** - Before moving to next
- [ ] **One stage per quarter** - Not everything at once

---

## SECTION J: 10 Counter-Intuitive Truths Validation

- [ ] **#1 Free costs more than paid** - Free 40% show-up, $1 = 80%, $10 = 90%
- [ ] **#2 More offers = more sales** - 9 sequential = 3x conversion vs 1
- [ ] **#3 Higher price = less churn** - 14,000 companies prove it
- [ ] **#4 Penalties increase satisfaction** - 80% completion vs 20%
- [ ] **#5 Start expensive = sell more cheap** - $16k anchor -> $2.2k seems like a deal
- [ ] **#6 Harder to leave = easier to stay** - Leaving > staying = retention
- [ ] **#7 Give to receive more** - Zero margin front-end OK if upsells compensate
- [ ] **#8 Sell what they DON'T need** - Unselling: 25% -> 75% conversion
- [ ] **#9 Hide price until end** - Value first = 3x conversion
- [ ] **#10 Less choice = more purchase** - "Chocolate or vanilla?" > "Want to buy?"

---

## SECTION K: 10 Fatal Errors Prevention

- [ ] **#1 Same thing cheaper** - NEVER (destroys trust)
- [ ] **#2 Skipping upsell** - Lose 80% profit
- [ ] **#3 Giving up at first no** - Lose 60% sales
- [ ] **#4 No card on trials** - 90% disappear
- [ ] **#5 Too much time to decide** - Momentum dies
- [ ] **#6 Explaining before anchoring** - Effect lost
- [ ] **#7 Too complex** - Paralysis
- [ ] **#8 No follow-up** - Lose 40%
- [ ] **#9 Accepting "I don't have money"** - Always offer plan
- [ ] **#10 Everything at once** - System breaks (one stage per quarter)

---

## SECTION L: Implementation Timeline Validation

### L.1: Phase 1 - Foundation (Weeks 1-4)

**Week 1: Discovery and Mapping**
- [ ] Mon-Tue: Map current journey (each touchpoint)
- [ ] Wed-Thu: Identify 10 problems created by solution
- [ ] Fri-Sun: Choose 1 attraction offer and create materials

**Week 2: Attraction Test**
- [ ] Mon-Tue: Test offer with 10 prospects
- [ ] Wed-Thu: Adjust based on objections
- [ ] Fri-Sun: Document winning script

**Week 3: First Upsell**
- [ ] Mon-Tue: Create classic upsell "can't have X without Y"
- [ ] Wed-Thu: Test with all buyers
- [ ] Fri-Sun: Measure acceptance rate (target: 30%)

**Week 4: Basic Downsell**
- [ ] Mon-Tue: Implement simple payment plan
- [ ] Wed-Thu: Offer to all "no's"
- [ ] Fri-Sun: Calculate total 30-day profit

### L.2: Phase 2 - Optimization (Weeks 5-8)

**Weeks 5-6: Offer Menu**
- [ ] Create 3 service levels (minimum, standard, premium)
- [ ] Implement unselling for personalization
- [ ] Add A/B upsell in each category

**Weeks 7-8: Conversion Optimization**
- [ ] Anchor with 5x premium price
- [ ] Trial with penalty for hesitants
- [ ] Rollover for old clients

### L.3: Phase 3 - Scale (Weeks 9-12)

**Weeks 9-10: Dominant Continuity**
- [ ] Migrate 60%+ to recurring
- [ ] Implement massive bonuses
- [ ] Waived fee for commitments

**Weeks 11-12: Automation and Scale**
- [ ] CRM with automatic triggers
- [ ] Documented scripts for team
- [ ] Double volume maintaining conversion

---

## SECTION M: Decision Rules Validation

### M.1: Health Check Rules

- [ ] **DR-001** - LTGP:CAC > 3:1 -> Scale aggressively
- [ ] **DR-002** - LTGP:CAC 2-3:1 -> Optimize (add offers)
- [ ] **DR-003** - LTGP:CAC < 2:1 -> STOP and fix

### M.2: 30-Day Cash Rules

- [ ] **DR-004** - CAC recovery < 30 days -> Healthy model
- [ ] **DR-005** - CAC recovery > 30 days -> Bankruptcy risk

### M.3: Churn Rules

- [ ] **DR-006** - Churn < 5% -> Focus acquisition
- [ ] **DR-007** - Churn 5-10% -> Add continuity
- [ ] **DR-008** - Churn > 10% -> Product problem

### M.4: Execution Rules

- [ ] **DR-009** - Always present premium first (anchor)
- [ ] **DR-010** - Offer until you hear yes (7-10 offers normal)
- [ ] **DR-011** - Card first, explanation after
- [ ] **DR-012** - Longer billing = less churn

---

## SECTION N: Troubleshooting Validation

| Symptom | Probable Cause | Solution | Checked |
|---------|----------------|----------|---------|
| Conversion < 10% | Wrong offer | Change to another attraction type | [ ] |
| Upsell < 20% | Timing/relevance | Move to different moment | [ ] |
| Downsell < 30% | Too expensive/complex | Simplify options | [ ] |
| Churn > 10% | Product doesn't deliver | Fix product first | [ ] |
| Negative profit | Too few offers | Add offers or raise prices | [ ] |

---

## SECTION O: Scripts Validation

### O.1: Classic Upsell Script
- [ ] "Great! Now that you have [solution A], you need to solve [problem B created by A]. 90% of our clients who get [result] also get [product B]. You can't have [final result] without [product B]. Want to add for just $[X] instead of the normal $[2X]? ...You don't want anything else, do you?" [No = Yes]

### O.2: Downsell Seesaw Script
- [ ] "Prefer giant or small monthly payments?" [Customer: Small]
- [ ] "Normally costs $[X], but if you prepay today, zero monthly payments. Does that work?"
- [ ] [If no] "The more you give now, the smaller your payments. What amount works today?"

### O.3: Trial with Penalty Script
- [ ] "How about we start you for free? I just need the card to guarantee commitment. If you do everything right, you pay nothing. If you skip something, small fee to keep you on track. It's how we've always done it. Fair?"

### O.4: Anchor Script
- [ ] "We have two options. First, our [premium] for $[5-10x]. Includes [everything]."
- [ ] [Wait for gasp] "Do you care a lot about [premium feature]?"
- [ ] [Customer: No] "Perfect. Then our [main] for $[X] is exactly what you need. Which card do you prefer?"

## Quick Reference: Key Validation Points

### Must-Have Before Launch

1. **30-day profit positive** - Not losing money per customer
2. **LTGP:CAC > 2:1** - Minimum viable ratio
3. **At least 3 offer types** - Attraction + Upsell + Downsell minimum
4. **All scripts documented** - No improvisation
5. **Card on file enabled** - Zero friction payment
6. **Metrics tracking live** - Know what's working

### Common Failures to Avoid

1. **Same thing cheaper** - Destroys trust
2. **Skipping stages** - Losing 80% profit
3. **No card on trials** - 90% disappear
4. **Everything at once** - System breaks
5. **Ignoring churn signals** - Product problem masked as pricing

### Hormozi Reminder

```
"A matematica nao mente. 82% dos negocios morrem por falta de
cash flow, nao de clientes." - Alex Hormozi

"Voce pode tosquiar uma ovelha por toda a vida,
mas so pode esfola-la uma vez." - John, mentor de Hormozi
```

---

## Next Steps After Passing

1. **Implement Phase 1** - Foundation (Weeks 1-4)
2. **Track all metrics** - 30-day profit, LTGP:CAC, churn
3. **Optimize Phase 2** - Add offers based on data
4. **Scale Phase 3** - Automate and grow
5. **Regular audits** - Monthly health checks
6. **Continuous improvement** - Iterate based on metrics

# Market Validation Veto Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Offers - Alex Hormozi (Chapter 4: Finding The Right Market)
> **Pattern:** SC-CK-VETO-001 (Veto Checklist - Blocks Execution)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Created:** 2026-02-10
> **Type:** VETO CONDITION - Must PASS before creating any offer
> **Agent:** hormozi-chief

---

## CRITICAL: This is a BLOCKING checklist

**If ANY indicator scores < 7/10, you MUST NOT proceed with offer creation.**

"Uma otima oferta para um mercado ruim sempre falhara." - Alex Hormozi

---

## The 4 Market Indicators (Starving Crowd Test)

### Indicator 1: DOR MASSIVA (Massive Pain)

**Question:** O publico precisa DESESPERADAMENTE de uma solucao?

| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 10 | Problema ameaca vida/negocio, urgencia extrema |
| 9 | Problema causa perdas financeiras significativas (>$10k/ano) |
| 8 | Problema afeta qualidade de vida diariamente |
| 7 | Problema incomoda muito, ja tentaram resolver antes |
| 6 | Problema reconhecido, mas nao urgente |
| 5 | Problema existe, mas vivem com ele |
| 1-4 | Nice-to-have, nao need-to-have |

**Perguntas de Validacao:**
- [ ] O prospect PERDEU SONO por causa desse problema?
- [ ] O prospect ja GASTOU DINHEIRO tentando resolver?
- [ ] O prospect FALA ATIVAMENTE sobre esse problema?
- [ ] O prospect teria VERGONHA se outros soubessem?

**Your Score: ___ /10**

**Evidencias:**
________________________________________________

**VETO CHECK:** Score >= 7? [ ] PASS [ ] **FAIL - STOP HERE**

---

### Indicator 2: PODER DE COMPRA (Purchasing Power)

**Question:** O publico TEM DINHEIRO (ou acesso) para pagar pela solucao?

| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 10 | Orcamento dedicado, aprovacao facil, B2B com ROI claro |
| 9 | Renda alta, gastos discrecionarios significativos |
| 8 | Classe media alta, historico de compras premium |
| 7 | Capacidade de parcelar, acesso a credito |
| 6 | Renda limitada mas priorizam essa area |
| 5 | Precisariam sacrificar outras coisas |
| 1-4 | Publico sem recursos financeiros |

**Perguntas de Validacao:**
- [ ] O prospect JA PAGA por solucoes similares?
- [ ] O prospect tem RENDA DISPONIVEL apos despesas essenciais?
- [ ] O prospect INVESTE em outras areas (cursos, ferramentas, etc)?
- [ ] O prospect tem ACESSO A CREDITO se necessario?

**Sinais de Poder de Compra:**
- B2B com faturamento > $500k/ano
- Profissionais com renda > $75k/ano
- Empresarios com equipe > 5 pessoas
- Historico de compras high-ticket no nicho

**Your Score: ___ /10**

**Evidencias:**
________________________________________________

**VETO CHECK:** Score >= 7? [ ] PASS [ ] **FAIL - STOP HERE**

---

### Indicator 3: FACIL DE ATINGIR (Easy to Target)

**Question:** O publico esta CONCENTRADO em locais onde posso alcancar?

| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 10 | Lista propria, comunidade ativa, associacao especifica |
| 9 | Grupos de Facebook/LinkedIn com >10k membros ativos |
| 8 | Conferencias/eventos especificos do nicho |
| 7 | Publicacoes/podcasts que eles consomem |
| 6 | Hashtags/keywords com volume razoavel |
| 5 | Dispersos, mas encontraveis com esforco |
| 1-4 | Nao existe congregacao clara |

**Perguntas de Validacao:**
- [ ] Existem ASSOCIACOES PROFISSIONAIS para esse publico?
- [ ] Existem GRUPOS ONLINE ativos com >5k membros?
- [ ] Existem EVENTOS/CONFERENCIAS especificos?
- [ ] Existem INFLUENCIADORES que esse publico segue?
- [ ] Existem PUBLICACOES (revistas, blogs, podcasts) do nicho?

**Canais Identificados:**
1. ________________________________________________
2. ________________________________________________
3. ________________________________________________

**Your Score: ___ /10**

**Evidencias:**
________________________________________________

**VETO CHECK:** Score >= 7? [ ] PASS [ ] **FAIL - STOP HERE**

---

### Indicator 4: CRESCENDO (Growing Market)

**Question:** O mercado esta em EXPANSAO (vento a favor)?

| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 10 | Crescimento > 20% ao ano, tendencia clara |
| 9 | Crescimento 15-20% ao ano |
| 8 | Crescimento 10-15% ao ano |
| 7 | Crescimento 5-10% ao ano, estavel positivo |
| 6 | Mercado estavel, sem crescimento/declinio |
| 5 | Crescimento < 5% ao ano |
| 1-4 | Mercado em declinio |

**Perguntas de Validacao:**
- [ ] Google Trends mostra tendencia POSITIVA nos ultimos 3 anos?
- [ ] Numero de COMPETIDORES esta aumentando? (sinal de demanda)
- [ ] Investimento em STARTUPS no setor esta crescendo?
- [ ] DEMOGRAFICAMENTE o publico-alvo esta expandindo?

**Fontes de Dados:**
- Google Trends: ________________________________________________
- Relatorios de Industria: ________________________________________________
- Numero de competidores novos: ________________________________________________

**Your Score: ___ /10**

**Evidencias:**
________________________________________________

**VETO CHECK:** Score >= 7? [ ] PASS [ ] **FAIL - STOP HERE**

---

## VETO GATE: Decisao Final

### Score Consolidado

| Indicator | Score | Veto Status |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| Dor Massiva | /10 | [ ] PASS [ ] FAIL |
| Poder de Compra | /10 | [ ] PASS [ ] FAIL |
| Facil de Atingir | /10 | [ ] PASS [ ] FAIL |
| Crescendo | /10 | [ ] PASS [ ] FAIL |
| **TOTAL** | **/40** | |

### Veto Rules

```
SE qualquer indicador < 7/10 → VETO (nao prosseguir)
SE total < 28/40 → VETO (nao prosseguir)
SE todos >= 7 E total >= 28 → PASS (pode criar oferta)
```

### Decision

- [ ] **PASS** - Todos indicadores >= 7, Total >= 28. Prosseguir para criacao de oferta.
- [ ] **VETO** - Um ou mais indicadores < 7. Escolher outro mercado ou ajustar avatar.

---

## Se VETO: Proximos Passos

### Opcao 1: Ajustar o Avatar dentro do Mercado
Exemplo: Se "donos de academia" falhou, tentar "donos de academia com >3 anos de operacao" (evita churn estrutural de iniciantes)

**Novo Avatar Proposto:**
________________________________________________

### Opcao 2: Pivotar para Mercado Adjacente
Exemplo: De "coaches iniciantes" para "coaches estabelecidos buscando escalar"

**Mercado Adjacente Proposto:**
________________________________________________

### Opcao 3: Abandonar e Buscar Novo Mercado
Se nenhum ajuste resolve os indicadores fracos.

**Novo Mercado a Explorar:**
________________________________________________

---

## Caso de Estudo: Por Que Este Veto Existe

### O Caso Lloyd (do livro)

"Lloyd era treinador de fitness. Excelente no que fazia. Mas escolheu vender para 'personal trainers' - um mercado com alto churn estrutural (muitos desistem da profissao). Mesmo com habilidades identicas, fracassou nesse mercado. Quando pivotou para 'donos de academia estabelecidos' (mesmo skillset), prosperou."

**Licao:** A mesma pessoa, com a mesma habilidade, FALHA em mercado ruim e PROSPERA em mercado bom. O mercado e a variavel dominante.

---

## Comparacao de Mercados (Use para Decisao)

Se estiver entre dois mercados, use esta matriz:

| Indicador | Mercado A: _______ | Mercado B: _______ |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Dor Massiva | /10 | /10 |
| Poder de Compra | /10 | /10 |
| Facil de Atingir | /10 | /10 |
| Crescendo | /10 | /10 |
| **TOTAL** | /40 | /40 |

**Decisao:** Escolher mercado com maior total, desde que todos indicadores >= 7.

---

## Assinatura de Aprovacao

| Gate | Responsavel | Data | Status |
|------|-------------|------|--------|
| Market Validation Veto | | | [ ] PASS [ ] VETO |

**Observacoes:**
________________________________________________

---

**Este checklist DEVE ser executado ANTES de qualquer trabalho de criacao de oferta.**

**Checklist Version:** 1.0.0
**Based on:** $100M Offers, Chapter 4 - Finding The Right Market

# Marketing Machine Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Marketing Machine - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** HO-CL-001 (Hormozi Checklist Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Agent:** hormozi-leads

---

## Pre-Flight Checklist

Before starting Marketing Machine operations, verify:

### Infrastructure
- [ ] Call recording system active
- [ ] Extra storage purchased (no auto-delete)
- [ ] Social monitoring tools configured
- [ ] Content library/folder structure created
- [ ] Video editing capability available
- [ ] Community platform active
- [ ] Review site accounts verified

### Legal & Compliance
- [ ] Permission language in all customer contracts
- [ ] "Compliance, training, and advertising purposes" covered
- [ ] Process to ask customers if OK with using story
- [ ] Protocol to honor "no" responses

### Team Readiness
- [ ] Sales trained to identify happy customers weekly
- [ ] Support reps know to screenshot wins
- [ ] Community manager knows wins collection process
- [ ] Camera teams identified for events
- [ ] Video editing resources available

Timing: End of day 1 or before lunch day 2

### Professional Testimonials
- [ ] Customers not pulled during keynotes
- [ ] Alternative times: morning, lunch, breaks, end of day
- [ ] Customer bonus for participation offered
- [ ] 6-point script followed:

**The 6-Point Script:**
```
1. (Internal Struggle) What was rock bottom before doing this?
   What did you have to do that you hated?
   What things did you want to do that you couldn't?

2. (External Struggle) What were your objective metrics?

3. (Skepticism) What were your main concerns about buying?

4. (Overcome) What made you do it anyways?

5. (External Victory) What are your objective metrics now?

6. (Internal Victory) What's been the best moment since?
   What can you do now you couldn't do before?
   What things did you hate doing you don't have to do anymore?
```

- [ ] Hook: Multiple versions tested before main story
- [ ] Name stated at beginning of video
- [ ] Videos saved, uploaded, music added

### Man-in-Street Testimonials
- [ ] 10 core questions prepared
- [ ] Target: 10+ responses per question
- [ ] Questions printed for camera team
- [ ] Tally space below each question
- [ ] Ask only one question until target reached

**Example Questions:**
```
- How many new customers have you gained since you started?
- What were you making before X vs now?
- How much extra income has X added?
- How much weight have you lost since you started here?
- How much has your credit score improved?
- What was your old score and what is it now?
```

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/money-model-checklist.md

# Money Model Architecture Checklist

> Checklist de validação para `design-money-model.md` (HZ_MOD_001)
> Source: $100M Money Models - Framework GMMM
> Agent: hormozi-models

---

## Pre-Design Validation

```yaml
pre_validation:
  business_ready:
    - [ ] Produto validado (mín 10 clientes satisfeitos pagantes)
    - [ ] CAC documentado e consistente
    - [ ] Capacidade de entrega (consegue 2x volume atual)
    - [ ] Sistema de cobrança aceita planos e recorrência
    - [ ] Tracking de conversão por estágio instalado

  red_flags_absent:
    - [ ] Taxa de reembolso ≤ 5%
    - [ ] Consegue explicar valor em 30 segundos
    - [ ] Tem depoimentos/casos de sucesso
    - [ ] Margem bruta ≥ 30%
    - [ ] Churn ≤ 10% mensal
```

---

## Pilar 1: Lucro em 30 Dias

```yaml
pilar_1:
  formula_applied:
    - [ ] L30 = (P1 × C1) + Σ(Un × Cn) - CAC - COGS
    - [ ] Todos componentes calculados
    - [ ] Resultado documentado

  health_check:
    - [ ] L30 < 0: Crítico, parar marketing
    - [ ] L30 = 0-1x CAC: Médio, adicionar ofertas
    - [ ] L30 = 1-2x CAC: Bom, otimizar
    - [ ] L30 > 2x CAC: Excelente, escalar
```

---

## Pilar 2: Sequência Problema-Solução

```yaml
pilar_2:
  problems_mapped:
    - [ ] Core offer identificada
    - [ ] Problemas criados pela solução listados
    - [ ] Pelo menos 3 problemas mapeados
    - [ ] Urgência de cada problema avaliada

  solutions_designed:
    - [ ] Solução/upsell para cada problema
    - [ ] Preço e timing definidos
    - [ ] Naturalidade da transição avaliada
```

---

## Pilar 3: Ancoragem de Valor

```yaml
pilar_3:
  anchor_strategy:
    - [ ] Âncora definida (5-10x preço principal)
    - [ ] Âncora é oferta REAL (preparado para entregar)
    - [ ] Script de apresentação documentado
    - [ ] Pergunta de resgate preparada

  expected_split:
    - [ ] % esperado que compra âncora
    - [ ] % esperado que compra principal
```

---

## Pilar 4: Fricção Zero

```yaml
pilar_4:
  friction_removed:
    - [ ] "Qual cartão?" ao invés de "Quer comprar?"
    - [ ] Cartão em arquivo quando possível
    - [ ] Processo de pagamento simplificado
    - [ ] Barreiras identificadas e removidas
```

---

## GMMM Framework

```yaml
stage_1_get_money:
  attraction_offer:
    - [ ] Oferta de atração definida
    - [ ] Preço estabelecido
    - [ ] Conversão target definida
    - [ ] COGS calculado
    - [ ] Meta: Cobrir CAC + COGs

stage_2_more_money:
  upsells:
    - [ ] Pelo menos 2 upsells definidos
    - [ ] Preço de cada upsell
    - [ ] Timing de cada upsell
    - [ ] Conversão esperada

  downsells:
    - [ ] Pelo menos 1 downsell definido
    - [ ] Trigger de quando oferecer
    - [ ] Preço e diferencial do principal

  target:
    - [ ] Meta: 3-5x valor inicial

stage_3_max_money:
  continuity:
    - [ ] Oferta de continuidade definida
    - [ ] Tipo escolhido (bonus, discount, waived fee)
    - [ ] Preço mensal
    - [ ] Churn target < 5%
    - [ ] Meta: 80%+ em continuidade
```

---

## Matriz de Ofertas 4x3

```yaml
offer_matrix:
  attraction:
    - [ ] Quantidade: Opção "mais"
    - [ ] Qualidade: Opção "premium"
    - [ ] Diferente: Opção "novo"

  upsell:
    - [ ] Quantidade: Opção "dobro"
    - [ ] Qualidade: Opção "melhor"
    - [ ] Diferente: Opção "complementar"

  downsell:
    - [ ] Quantidade: Opção "menos"
    - [ ] Qualidade: Opção "inferior"
    - [ ] Diferente: Opção "alternativa"

  continuity:
    - [ ] Quantidade: Opção "ilimitado"
    - [ ] Qualidade: Opção "mantida"
    - [ ] Diferente: Opção "recorrente"
```

---

## Cash First Hierarchy

```yaml
cash_first:
  priority_check:
    - [ ] Se CAC > 30-day revenue → Consertando atração PRIMEIRO
    - [ ] Se cobriu mas margens baixas → Adicionando upsells
    - [ ] Se conversão < 20% → Adicionando downsells
    - [ ] Se 1-3 funcionam → Adicionando continuidade
```

---

## Projections

```yaml
projections:
  calculated:
    - [ ] Novo L30 projetado
    - [ ] Novo LTV projetado
    - [ ] Novo LTV:CAC projetado
    - [ ] Health status esperado

  implementation:
    - [ ] Prioridades de implementação definidas
    - [ ] Timeline realista
```

---

## LTGP:CAC Health

```yaml
health_interpretation:
  status_correct:
    - [ ] > 3:1 → Saudável, escalar agressivamente
    - [ ] 2-3:1 → Alerta, otimizar
    - [ ] < 2:1 → Crítico, PARAR e consertar
```

---

*Checklist: money-model | Version: 1.0*
*Supports: design-money-model.md (HZ_MOD_001)*

---

## Scoring

| Category | Items | Points Each | Max |
|----------|-------|-------------|-----|
| Critical — Pre-Validation Red Flags, GMMM Stages, LTGP:CAC Health | 23 | 3 | 69 |
| Standard — 4 Pillars (L30, Problem-Solution, Anchor, Friction), Offer Matrix | 24 | 2 | 48 |
| Bonus — Cash First Hierarchy, Projections | 6 | 1 | 6 |
| **TOTAL** | **53** | | **123** |

### Thresholds
- **PASS**: >= 99 points (80%)
- **CONDITIONAL**: >= 74 points (60%)
- **FAIL**: < 74 points

### If FAIL
The money model architecture is incomplete and risks negative 30-day cash flow. Validate all pre-design red flags first, then ensure GMMM Stage 1 (Get Money) covers CAC + COGS before designing upsell and continuity stages.

## Referência: references/squad/checklists/naming-framework-checklist.md

# Naming Framework Checklist

> **Source:** $100M Offers (Chapter 16) + Swipefile Master Definitivo
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Purpose:** Quick-reference validation for all naming decisions
> **Agent:** hormozi-offers

---

## Pre-Naming Checklist

### Preconditions Verified
- [ ] Offer deliverable and outcome clearly defined
- [ ] Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) documented
- [ ] Price point established
- [ ] Specific result promise quantified
- [ ] Timeframe for results known
- [ ] Unique mechanism identified (the "how")

---

## MAGICO Framework Checklist

### Components Present (2+ Required)
- [ ] **M** - Mecanismo unico (unique mechanism/method)
- [ ] **A** - Alvo atraente (attractive target/outcome)
- [ ] **G** - Grafia diferente (creative spelling/format)
- [ ] **I** - Ideia que ajuda (solution concept)
- [ ] **C** - Convergencia temporal (time element)
- [ ] **O** - Objetivo final (dream result)

### MAGICO Quality Check
- [ ] Contains 2+ MAGICO components
- [ ] Components work together cohesively
- [ ] Name tells prospect what they get in <10 words

---

## Archetype Selection Checklist

### Context Analysis
- [ ] ICP technical level assessed
- [ ] Category maturity identified
- [ ] Primary barrier to purchase known
- [ ] Competitive landscape mapped

### Archetype Match (Select One)
- [ ] **LITERAL EXTREMO** - Non-technical audience, complex category
- [ ] **VERBO CULTURAL** - Creating new behavior, want dominance
- [ ] **ESTADO DESEJADO** - Emotional transformation product
- [ ] **NUMERICO ESPECIFICO** - Time/quantity as differentiator
- [ ] **PARADOXO INTRIGANTE** - Commodity category, need attention
- [ ] **TRIBAL IDENTIFIER** - Community > product
- [ ] **METAFORA VISUAL** - Visual/physical benefit
- [ ] **STATUS SIGNAL** - Premium pricing, status buyers
- [ ] **INVENTOR FRIENDLY** - New category, no reference
- [ ] **HERITAGE FABRICADO** - Trust is main barrier

---

## Price Tier Alignment Checklist

### Match Language to Price
- [ ] **$0-$10 (Micro)**: Uses "Quick", "Instant", "[Number] Minute"
- [ ] **$10-$97 (Low)**: Uses "Cheatsheet", "Hacks", "[Number] Ways"
- [ ] **$97-$997 (Mid)**: Uses "Accelerator", "System", "Mastery"
- [ ] **$997-$10K (High)**: Uses "Intensive", "Certification", "Authority"
- [ ] **$10K-$100K (Ultra)**: Uses "Inner Circle", "Mastermind", "Partnership"
- [ ] **$100K+ (Extreme)**: Uses "Equity Partner", "Advisory", "Legacy"

---

## 20-Question Validation (15+ to Pass)

### Basic (5 points)
- [ ] 1. Passes drunk test (easy to say/spell)
- [ ] 2. .com domain available for <$10K
- [ ] 3. Trademark free globally
- [ ] 4. Works in 3+ languages
- [ ] 5. Social @handles available

### Strategic (5 points)
- [ ] 6. Communicates category OR creates new one
- [ ] 7. Allows future product expansion
- [ ] 8. Different from everything on Google page 1
- [ ] 9. Potential to become cultural verb
- [ ] 10. Pleasant sound when spoken aloud

### Psychological (5 points)
- [ ] 11. Evokes instant emotion
- [ ] 12. Suggests desired transformation
- [ ] 13. Reduces purchase anxiety
- [ ] 14. Creates immediate curiosity
- [ ] 15. Memorable after single mention

### Commercial (5 points)
- [ ] 16. Enables premium pricing
- [ ] 17. Works on outdoor/audio ads
- [ ] 18. Viral hashtag potential
- [ ] 19. Has interesting story/origin
- [ ] 20. Desire scale rating: 8+/10

### Score Interpretation
| Score | Status | Action |
|-------|--------|--------|
| 20/20 | Unicorn potential | Launch immediately |
| 15-19 | Launch ready | Launch and iterate |
| 10-14 | Needs refinement | Revise before launch |
| <10 | Restart | Back to brainstorm |

**Current Score: ___/20**

---

## 7 Immutable Laws Check

### Laws Compliance
- [ ] **Law 1**: Simplicidade > Criatividade (Simple beats clever)
- [ ] **Law 2**: Beneficio > Feature (Benefit beats feature)
- [ ] **Law 3**: Emocao > Logica (Emotion beats logic)
- [ ] **Law 4**: Especifico > Generico (Specific beats generic)
- [ ] **Law 5**: Curto > Longo (Short beats long - avg 7.3 chars)
- [ ] **Law 6**: Historia > Descricao (Story beats description)
- [ ] **Law 7**: Timing > Perfeicao (80% launched > 100% never)

---

## Specificity Checklist

### Quantified Elements
- [ ] Specific number for outcome (not range)
- [ ] Broken number used if possible (19, 67, 93 > 20, 70, 90)
- [ ] Time element specific (17 weeks > "a few months")
- [ ] Result measurable and verifiable

### Specificity Examples Applied
| Generic | Specific | Applied |
|---------|----------|---------|
| "Lose weight" | "Lose 23.5 lbs in 17 weeks" | [ ] |
| "Get clients" | "5 new $2K/mo clients weekly" | [ ] |
| "Learn marketing" | "52 documented millionaires created" | [ ] |

---

## Bonus Naming Checklist

### All Bonuses Named
- [ ] Bonus 1: ________________________________ (Named with MAGICO)
- [ ] Bonus 2: ________________________________ (Named with MAGICO)
- [ ] Bonus 3: ________________________________ (Named with MAGICO)
- [ ] Bonus 4: ________________________________ (Named with MAGICO)
- [ ] Bonus 5: ________________________________ (Named with MAGICO)

### Bonus Naming Quality
- [ ] Each bonus has specific outcome in name
- [ ] Each bonus uses at least 1 power word
- [ ] Generic terms avoided (not just "Guide" or "Template")
- [ ] Time/quantity elements included where possible

**Bonus Naming Example:**
- WRONG: "Guia de Compras"
- RIGHT: "O Segredo de Compras Economicas de 5 Minutos que Economizara $100s Por Mes"

---

## Power Words Applied

### Conversion Multipliers (2-5X)
- [ ] Blueprint
- [ ] System
- [ ] Formula
- [ ] Framework
- [ ] Accelerator
- [ ] Intensive
- [ ] Revolution
- [ ] Breakthrough

### Price Perception Multipliers (3-10X)
- [ ] Platinum
- [ ] Elite
- [ ] Mastermind
- [ ] Certification
- [ ] Authority
- [ ] Inner Circle
- [ ] Advisory
- [ ] Concierge

### Risk Reducers
- [ ] Proven
- [ ] Guaranteed
- [ ] Certified
- [ ] Scientific
- [ ] Tested
- [ ] Trusted
- [ ] Safe
- [ ] Simple

---

## Market Timing Check

### Current Market Conditions
- [ ] **Bull Market**: Using aspirational names (Millionaire, 10X, Unicorn)
- [ ] **Bear Market**: Using conservative names (Safe, Proven, Guaranteed)
- [ ] **Category Start**: Using educational names (explains what it is)
- [ ] **Category Mature**: Using differentiation names (paradox, controversial)
- [ ] **Disruption Coming**: Using radical simplicity (one word, benefit-focused)

---

## Failure Prevention Checklist

### Avoid These Mistakes
- [ ] NOT using version number (2.0) for rebrand
- [ ] NOT copying competitor naming pattern exactly
- [ ] NOT choosing feature name over benefit name
- [ ] NOT using meaningless invented sounds
- [ ] NOT invalidating existing brand equity
- [ ] NOT ignoring cultural/language connotations

### Documented Failures Reference
| Name | Cost | Mistake |
|------|------|---------|
| Quibi | $1.75B | Feature name, not benefit |
| Google Glass | $1B+ | Negative connotations |
| New Coke | $Billions | Invalidated heritage |
| Microsoft Zune | $289M | Meaningless sound |
| CNN+ | $300M/3wks | Copied without value |

---

## Rebrand Trigger Checklist

### When to Rename (Check if ANY apply)
- [ ] Offer associated with past failure in market
- [ ] Perceived as commodity (competing on price)
- [ ] Market confused by positioning
- [ ] "Version 2.0" approach failed or insufficient
- [ ] Negative word-of-mouth attached to name

**If ANY checked**: Execute full MAGICO rename process

---

## Final Launch Checklist

### Technical Validation
- [ ] Domain secured
- [ ] Social handles secured
- [ ] Trademark search complete
- [ ] No legal conflicts identified

### Strategic Validation
- [ ] Name scores 15+ on 20-question test
- [ ] Passes majority of 7 laws
- [ ] Contains 2+ MAGICO components
- [ ] Aligned with price tier psychology
- [ ] Matched to appropriate archetype

### Documentation Complete
- [ ] MAGICO breakdown documented
- [ ] Archetype classification recorded
- [ ] Power words used noted
- [ ] 20-question scorecard filed
- [ ] Rejected alternatives documented with reasons

---

## Quick Reference: The MAGICO Formula

```
[TIME ELEMENT] + [UNIQUE MECHANISM] + [DREAM RESULT]

Example: "O Sistema de 6 Semanas Six Pack FRAQUEZA-A-RIQUEZA"

- 6 Semanas = Time (C)
- Sistema = Mechanism (M)
- Six Pack = Target (A)
- FRAQUEZA-A-RIQUEZA = Creative spelling (G) + Objective (O)
```

---

## Quick Reference: Archetype Decision Tree

```
Is your audience technical?
├── YES → Is category new?
│         ├── YES → INVENTOR FRIENDLY
│         └── NO → LITERAL EXTREMO
└── NO → Is the benefit emotional?
          ├── YES → ESTADO DESEJADO
          └── NO → Is price premium?
                    ├── YES → STATUS SIGNAL
                    └── NO → NUMERICO ESPECIFICO
```

---

## Validation Summary

| Checkpoint | Status | Notes |
|------------|--------|-------|
| Preconditions | [ ] | |
| MAGICO (2+) | [ ] | |
| Archetype Selected | [ ] | |
| Price Aligned | [ ] | |
| 20-Question (15+) | [ ] | Score: ___/20 |
| 7 Laws | [ ] | |
| Specificity | [ ] | |
| Bonuses Named | [ ] | |
| Power Words | [ ] | |
| Timing Check | [ ] | |
| Failures Avoided | [ ] | |
| Technical Clear | [ ] | |

**READY TO LAUNCH**: [ ] All critical checkpoints passed

---
