# ===============================================================================
# KPIs & SUCCESS METRICS
# ===============================================================================

kpis:
  primary:
    bonus_to_price_ratio:
      formula: "Total Bonus Value / Main Offer Price"
      target: ">2:1"
      excellent: ">5:1"

    close_rate_improvement:
      formula: "(Close Rate with Bonuses - Close Rate without) / Close Rate without"
      target: ">20%"

  secondary:
    obstacle_coverage:
      formula: "Obstacles Addressed / Total Obstacles"
      target: "100%"

    tool_ratio:
      formula: "Tools and Checklists / Total Bonuses"
      target: ">70%"

    partner_commission_revenue:
      formula: "Monthly revenue from partner referrals"
      target: "Incremental profit stream"

  by_phase:
    creation:
      - "Assets inventoried"
      - "Obstacles mapped"
      - "Gaps identified"

    presentation:
      - "All bonuses named with benefits"
      - "All bonuses have proof"
      - "All prices justified"

    optimization:
      - "Value exceeds main offer"
      - "Scarcity/urgency applied"
      - "Optimal sequencing determined"

# ===============================================================================
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ===============================================================================

troubleshooting:
  - symptom: "Bonuses not improving close rate"
    possible_causes:
      - "Bonuses don't address real obstacles"
      - "Names don't communicate value"
      - "Proof elements not credible"
    diagnosis:
      - "Survey lost prospects on objections"
      - "Test name recognition"
      - "Verify proof sources"
    solutions:
      - "Remap bonuses to actual objections"
      - "Rewrite names with benefits"
      - "Add stronger proof elements"

  - symptom: "Prospects only want bonuses"
    possible_causes:
      - "Core offer perceived as weak"
      - "Bonuses eclipsing too much"
      - "Scarcity not properly applied"
    diagnosis:
      - "Compare core offer value perception"
      - "Evaluate bonus prominence"
    solutions:
      - "Strengthen core offer presentation"
      - "Apply exclusive scarcity to bonuses"
      - "Rebalance presentation emphasis"

  - symptom: "Partners not agreeing to deals"
    possible_causes:
      - "Poor value proposition for partner"
      - "Approaching competitors"
      - "Customer quality concerns"
    diagnosis:
      - "Review pitch effectiveness"
      - "Verify non-competing status"
      - "Share customer demographics"
    solutions:
      - "Lead with exposure value"
      - "Target truly adjacent businesses"
      - "Provide customer quality proof"

  - symptom: "Too many bonuses overwhelming presentation"
    possible_causes:
      - "No prioritization of bonuses"
      - "Including low-value items"
      - "Poor sequencing"
    diagnosis:
      - "Rank bonuses by impact"
      - "Evaluate value of each"
    solutions:
      - "Lead with highest-impact bonuses"
      - "Save extras for post-purchase surprise"
      - "Remove low-impact bonuses"

# ===============================================================================
# GAPS TO RESOLVE
# ===============================================================================

gaps_to_resolve:

    description: "Specific price justification formulas"
    severity: Medium

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/branding-sop.md

# Branding SOP

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Branding - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Build a brand that commands premium prices, attracts customers at lower costs, and creates lifelong loyalty. Branding is the deliberate pairing of your business with things your ideal customer likes.

**Core Definition:**
```
Branding = Deliberate pairing of things
Good Branding = Pairing with things your ideal audience LIKES
Bad Branding = Pairing with things your audience DISLIKES
No Branding = Exposure results in normal behavior (invisible)
```

**Business Impact:**
```
Brand enables:
1) Lower CAC - Convert higher % from advertising at lower cost
2) Higher LTV - Charge 2x, 5x, or 10x more for the same thing
3) Lower Risk - Customers buy repeatedly without considering competition

"The only way to make all three happen, for the lowest cost,
over the longest time horizon is one word: branding." (p.3)
```

**Brand Measurement Variables:**
```
Advertising = REACH (how many people know about you)
Branding = INFLUENCE (chance it changes behavior) + DIRECTION (towards or away)

Good advertising = Everyone knows about your stuff
Good branding = Audience likes and BUYS
```

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Building a brand from scratch (new business, new product)
- Growing an existing brand (expanding reach and influence)
- Pivoting a damaged or misaligned brand
- Repositioning for a new market segment (up/down/adjacent/broader/narrower)

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- Direct response advertising tactics (covered in separate playbook)
- Product development (separate from brand positioning)
- Pricing strategy (brand enables pricing, doesn't set it)

### Business Types
- Personal brands (entrepreneurs, thought leaders)
- Company brands (products, services)
- Any business wanting premium pricing power
- B2B and B2C

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Ideal Customer Profile | Avatar defined and documented | Demographics + psychographics clear |
| Product/Service | Something to sell | Offering exists and works |
| Distribution Channel | Way to reach audience | Advertising or content mechanism |
| Patience Commitment | 5-year minimum horizon | Leadership aligned on timeframe |
| Content Capacity | Ability to create pairings | Team/resources for content creation |
| Tracking System | Way to measure results | Sales, engagement, feedback loops |

---

## Part 4: The Four-Step Brand Framework

### Framework Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              FOUR STEPS TO BUILD, GROW, OR PIVOT A BRAND                │
├──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────────┤
│   STEP 1     │    STEP 2    │     STEP 3       │        STEP 4         │
│   WHO        │    WHAT      │     ASSOCIATE    │       OPTIMIZE        │
├──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ Define ideal │ Figure out   │ Associate with   │ Optimize for          │
│ customer     │ what they    │ those things     │ max profit            │
│              │ like         │                  │                       │
├──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ Growing      │ Values       │ Content          │ Up market             │
│ Money        │ People       │ Products         │ Down market           │
│ Easy to find │ Outcomes     │ Appearances      │ Adjacent              │
│ In pain      │ Experiences  │                  │ Broader/Narrower      │
└──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────────┘
```

### The Branding Cycle (Levels of Authority)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LEVELS OF AUTHORITY (BRANDING CYCLE)                  │
├────────────────────┬────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┤
│  1. WHAT YOU SAY   │ 2. WHAT OTHERS SAY │ 3. WHAT THEY EXPERIENCE      │
├────────────────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤
│ Least influential  │ More influential   │ MOST influential              │
│ Content, Ads,      │ Affiliates,        │ Product experience,           │
│ Outreach           │ Customers          │ Personal opinion              │
├────────────────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┤
│ Short-term impact  │ Medium-term impact │ Long-term impact              │
│ on brand           │ on brand           │ on brand                      │
└────────────────────┴────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┘

"Your advertising has stronger influence on your brand in the short term.
Your product has stronger influence on your brand in the long term." (p.24)
```

### The Bouquet Metaphor

```
Brand = Bouquet of Flowers

Individual elements (products, values, experiences, people) = individual flowers
Assembled together = brand bouquet

Narrow brand = Single type of flowers (e.g., only red roses)
Broad brand = Many types of flowers
Adjacent move = Shift from red roses to yellow roses
Bad pairing = Sticks and weeds in bouquet (distorts clarity)
```

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### STEP 1: FIGURE OUT WHO YOUR IDEAL CUSTOMER IS

#### Step 1.1: Identify Growing Market
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Select an audience that is growing, not shrinking or maintaining |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis (market research) |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Data gathering automatable, selection requires judgment |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Access to market data |
| **Output** | Market growth assessment |
| **Guardrails** | "If I have to pick between shrinking, maintaining, or growing - I'd rather go after one that's bigger" (p.20) |
| **Decision Rule** | Growing market > Stable market > Shrinking market |

**Rationale:** "Even if I stay the same size, I'm still going to grow because the market's growing." (p.20)

#### Step 1.2: Verify Financial Capacity
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Ensure target audience can afford what you sell |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Income data accessible |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Pricing range defined |
| **Output** | Audience affordability assessment |
| **Guardrails** | "If I want to charge a lot of money, they've got to have the money so I can charge it" (p.20) |
| **Decision Rule** | Rich people > Medium people > Poor people (for premium offerings) |

#### Step 1.3: Assess Targeting Ease
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Determine how easily you can reach this audience with advertising |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Platform targeting data accessible |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Advertising platforms identified |
| **Output** | Targeting feasibility score |
| **Guardrails** | "If my customers exist, but I can't find them... does it matter?" (p.20) |
| **Decision Rule** | Easy to target > Hard to target |

#### Step 1.4: Evaluate Pain Level
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Confirm audience desperately wants what you sell |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment + Perception |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires qualitative research |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Offer defined |
| **Output** | Pain intensity assessment |
| **Guardrails** | "I'd rather have competition because at least I know people are buying that thing" (p.20) |
| **Decision Rule** | Desperate pain > Moderate discomfort > Mild inconvenience |

**Four Criteria Summary:**
```
Ideal Avatar Checklist:
[ ] Growing market
[ ] Can afford your stuff
[ ] Easy to find/target
[ ] In significant pain
```

---

### STEP 2: FIGURE OUT WHAT THEY LIKE

#### Step 2.1: Identify Values They Hold
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Research and document core values your audience prizes |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Perception |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Survey data automatable, interpretation human |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Avatar defined (Step 1) |
| **Output** | Values inventory |
| **Guardrails** | Focus on values that differentiate, not universal ones |
| **Decision Rule** | Prioritize values that connect to your offering |

**Example (Assisted Living Owners):**
- Making more money
- Getting more customers
- Making more profits
- Building a sellable business
- Fewer lawsuits
- Paying fewer taxes (p.21)

#### Step 2.2: Identify People They Admire
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Document people, figures, and authorities your audience respects |
| **Cognitive Type** | Research + Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Avatar defined |
| **Output** | Admired figures inventory |
| **Guardrails** | Verify admiration, not just awareness |
| **Decision Rule** | Strong positive association > Mild positive > Neutral |

**Example:**
- "We'll pair Elon and Warren Buffet, a couple of the richest people in the world. People who like investing, entrepreneurship, and money would probably respond favorably." (p.14)

#### Step 2.3: Identify Outcomes They Desire
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Document the specific results and transformations they want |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires deep customer understanding |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Avatar in pain (Step 1.4) |
| **Output** | Desired outcomes inventory |
| **Guardrails** | Outcomes must be concrete and measurable |
| **Decision Rule** | Specific outcomes > Vague aspirations |

#### Step 2.4: Identify Experiences They Value
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Document experiences, activities, and consumption preferences |
| **Cognitive Type** | Research |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Avatar defined |
| **Output** | Experience preferences inventory |
| **Guardrails** | Include both aspirational and current experiences |
| **Decision Rule** | Experiences that connect to brand message |

---

### STEP 3: ASSOCIATE YOUR BRAND WITH THINGS THEY LIKE

#### Step 3.1: Create Content They Value
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Make videos, blogs, articles, booklets, PDFs geared toward audience |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Creative work requires human |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Values and interests documented (Step 2) |
| **Output** | Content library |
| **Guardrails** | Content must genuinely help audience; no filler |
| **Decision Rule** | "When I start doing this, people are like, 'Wow, this stuff really makes my life better'" (p.22) |

**Content Examples (Assisted Living Law Firm):**
- "Here are some things that we see across our firm for Assisted Living facilities that have helped lower costs and improve quality of life for residents." (p.22)
- "They can structure their accounting to depreciate their investments this way so they can save more money." (p.22)
- "Here's how people set up their floor plans to make it more efficient." (p.22)

#### Step 3.2: Distribute Content Widely
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Get content in front of target audience through multiple channels |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution + Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Distribution automatable |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Content created (Step 3.1) |
| **Output** | Reach metrics |
| **Guardrails** | Track which channels resonate with avatar |
| **Decision Rule** | More reach = more brand building (reach is primary brand element) |

**Key Insight:** "A brand can't exist without [reach], so reach is the primary element of a brand." (p.8)

#### Step 3.3: Create Products They Like
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Develop both free and paid offerings that serve the audience |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Values documented |
| **Output** | Product/offering suite |
| **Guardrails** | Products must match brand promises |
| **Decision Rule** | "Your premium brand had better be delivering something special" - Warren Buffett (p.24) |

#### Step 3.4: Appear Next to People They Like
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Associate with admired figures, participate in valued communities |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment + Negotiation |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Admired figures identified (Step 2.2) |
| **Output** | Association portfolio |
| **Guardrails** | Associations must be authentic; forced pairings backfire |
| **Decision Rule** | Strong positive associations > Weak positive > None |

**Association Transfer Mechanism:**
```
1) Start with brand that means nothing (just a logo)
2) Pair it with stuff your customers like
3) Brand starts to mean "thing customer likes" to them
4) Add brand to generic product → transforms to premium branded product
5) Customers want to associate with that positive branded product
6) They exchange money for premium product
7) They get product AND association
8) You get higher profits from those associations (p.16-17)
```

#### Step 3.5: Iterate Based on Response
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Monitor audience response and adjust associations accordingly |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Data automatable, decisions human |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Content distributed, feedback loop exists |
| **Output** | Optimized association strategy |
| **Guardrails** | Measure behavior change, not just sentiment |
| **Decision Rule** | What changes buying behavior = good; what doesn't = adjust |

---

### STEP 4: OPTIMIZE ASSOCIATIONS FOR MAXIMUM PROFIT

#### Step 4.1: Assess Market Position Options
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Evaluate five directions for expanding addressable market |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategic Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Current brand established |
| **Output** | Market positioning recommendation |
| **Guardrails** | Each direction requires different associations |
| **Decision Rule** | Choose direction that maximizes profit potential |

**Five Positioning Options:**
```
1) UP MARKET - Larger customers
   Example: Multi-location assisted living owners

2) DOWN MARKET - Smaller customers
   Example: At-home care and mobile assisted living owners

3) ADJACENT - Similar but slightly different market
   Example: Rehab facilities

4) BROADER - Entire category
   Example: All senior living centers (hospice, end of life, retirement)

5) NARROWER - Slice of existing market
   Example: Assisted living with 100-500 residents (p.25)
```

#### Step 4.2: Execute Brand Pivot (If Needed)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Shift associations to match new target market |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategic Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | New direction chosen (Step 4.1) |
| **Output** | Pivoted brand positioning |
| **Guardrails** | Must gain more than you lose |
| **Decision Rule** | "Net positive on all moves we make" (p.27) |

**Bouquet Adjustment Strategy:**
- Narrow: "Only bouquet of red roses" - talk only about specific things
- Broader: "All sorts of flowers" - expand topic range
- Adjacent: "Red roses to yellow roses" - still roses, different type
- Up market: Focus on problems larger players have
- Down market: Focus on problems smaller players have (p.25-26)

#### Step 4.3: Monitor Net Audience Changes
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Track whether moves gain more audience than they lose |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Metrics automatable |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Pivot executed |
| **Output** | Net change assessment |
| **Guardrails** | "Losing audience is a part of life. You just wanna make sure you gain more than you lose" (p.27) |
| **Decision Rule** | Positive net change = continue; Negative = revert |

**Case Study (Hormozi Personal Brand):**
"When I started branding, I only made business content. As I got bigger I started touching on other topics. Views followed. But, I realized it was the wrong views. So, I recentered my content around only business. And unsurprisingly, more business owners paid attention." (p.26)

#### Step 4.4: Recover from Branding Mistakes
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Overwhelm bad pairings with good ones rather than trying to eliminate |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Bad pairing identified |
| **Output** | Recovered brand perception |
| **Guardrails** | "We don't try and eliminate the DUI... But what we try to do is overwhelm it with way more of the stuff that the majority of our people actually like" (p.29) |
| **Decision Rule** | More good associations > Hiding/eliminating bad |

**Recovery Mechanism:**
"Just like one ugly flower messes up the whole bouquet... To recover from something like that, you just have to overwhelm customers with the stuff they like until eventually the bad pairing shrinks into irrelevance." (p.29)

---

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Avatar Selection
```yaml
rule: AVATAR_QUALIFICATION
trigger: Selecting target audience
condition:
  - IF market_growing AND has_money AND easy_to_target AND in_pain THEN "IDEAL"
  - IF 3_of_4_criteria THEN "ACCEPTABLE"
  - IF <3_of_4_criteria THEN "RECONSIDER"
action: Prioritize ideal avatars
confidence: HIGH (p.19-21)
```

### DR-002: Association Quality
```yaml
rule: PAIRING_EVALUATION
trigger: Considering new brand association
condition:
  - IF majority_of_audience_likes THEN "GOOD_PAIRING"
  - IF majority_of_audience_dislikes THEN "BAD_PAIRING"
  - IF neutral_response THEN "NO_BRANDING" (invisible)
action: Only execute good pairings
confidence: HIGH (p.6)
```

### DR-003: Pivot Execution
```yaml
rule: BRAND_PIVOT_DECISION
trigger: Considering market repositioning
condition:
  - IF expected_gains > expected_losses THEN "EXECUTE_PIVOT"
  - IF expected_losses > expected_gains THEN "ABORT_PIVOT"
  - IF uncertain THEN "TEST_SMALL_FIRST"
action: Never make negative net changes
confidence: HIGH (p.27)
```

### DR-004: Mistake Recovery
```yaml
rule: BAD_PAIRING_RECOVERY
trigger: Brand damaged by bad association
condition:
  - IF bad_pairing_identified THEN overwhelm_with_good()
  - NEVER try_to_eliminate() or hide()
action: Double down on positive associations
confidence: HIGH (p.29)
```

### DR-005: Pricing Power Check
```yaml
rule: BRAND_STRENGTH_INDICATOR
trigger: Evaluating brand effectiveness
condition:
  - IF can_raise_prices_without_losing_business THEN "STRONG_BRAND"
  - IF need_prayer_session_before_10%_increase THEN "WEAK_BRAND"
action: Use as diagnostic for brand health
confidence: HIGH (Warren Buffett quote, p.17)
```

### DR-006: Channel Authority Weighting
```yaml
rule: INFLUENCE_SOURCE_PRIORITY
trigger: Allocating brand-building resources
condition:
  - experience_weight: HIGHEST (long-term impact)
  - others_say_weight: MEDIUM (referrals, affiliates)
  - you_say_weight: LOWEST (your advertising)
action: Invest most in product experience
confidence: HIGH (p.23-24)
```

---

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: High Reach, Low Influence
**Trigger:** Many people know about you but don't change behavior
**Example:** Taylor Swift brand for Hormozi - "I think she's good but probably won't buy much of her stuff" (p.9)
**Response:** Focus on deepening engagement with target niche rather than broader reach

### Exception 2: Polar vs Non-Polar Brand Decision
**Trigger:** Questioning whether to deliberately polarize
**Analysis:** "You don't have to be polar to build a strong brand... Just look at brands like Taylor Swift, Mother Teresa, Apple" (p.13)
**Response:** "Selling polarizes people. Deliberately trying to 'polarize' interferes with doing business - Just focus on getting people to buy your stuff" (p.13)

### Exception 3: Bad Publicity Management
**Trigger:** Negative publicity event
**Analysis:** "Good beats bad. Bad beats none. Lots of good beats everything." (p.12)
**Response:** Don't shrink away; double down on positive associations

### Exception 4: Misaligned Audience Growth
**Trigger:** Growing audience but wrong type of people
**Example:** Hormozi's content "started attracting more wantrepreneurs. This was not my goal" (p.21)
**Response:** Recenter content around ideal customer; accept some audience loss

### Exception 5: Cool Factor vs. Economics
**Trigger:** Superior economics but losing to "cooler" competitor
**Example:** Hormozi supplement company - "I had put my entire budget into commissions and product, but none into building a brand people would think was cool" (p.2)
**Response:** Allocate budget specifically to brand building, not just product/economics

## Part 8: Outputs

| Output | Format | Destination | Frequency |
|--------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Avatar Profile | Document | Strategy Team | Once, update quarterly |
| Likes Inventory | Matrix | Content Team | Once, update monthly |
| Association Map | Visual Diagram | Leadership | Monthly review |
| Reach Metrics | Dashboard | Marketing | Weekly |
| Influence/Direction Assessment | Survey Analysis | Strategy | Quarterly |
| Net Audience Change | Report | Leadership | Per pivot/campaign |

### Key Metrics to Track
```
BRAND HEALTH:
├── Reach (advertising metric)
│   └── How many people know about your stuff
├── Influence (branding metric #1)
│   └── Likelihood of changing behavior
└── Direction (branding metric #2)
    └── Towards or away from purchase

BUSINESS IMPACT:
├── CAC change over time (should decrease)
├── LTV change over time (should increase)
├── Pricing power (can you raise prices?)
├── Retention rate (do they come back?)
└── Referral rate (do others recommend?)
```

---

## Part 9: Validation

### Brand Strength Quality Gates

| Gate | Threshold | Action if Failed |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| Avatar Clarity | All 4 criteria defined | Revisit Step 1 |
| Likes Inventory | 10+ items per category | Deepen research |
| Content Volume | Publishing consistently | Increase cadence |
| Reach Growth | Month-over-month increase | Increase distribution |
| Conversion Rate | Above industry baseline | Check association quality |
| Pricing Power | Can raise without losing | Strengthen associations |

### Brand Building Milestones

| Milestone | Indicator | Timeline |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Brand Recognition | Audience can identify you | 6-12 months |
| Brand Association | "They're the [X] company" | 12-24 months |
| Premium Pricing | 2x+ competitor pricing | 24-36 months |
| Loyalty | Repeat purchase without shopping | 36-48 months |
| Advocacy | Unprompted recommendations | 48-60 months |

## Appendix A: The Economics of Brand

### Branded vs Unbranded Comparison

| Metric | Unbranded | Branded | Difference |
|--------|-----------|---------|------------|
| Price | $2,500 | $5,500 | +120% |
| Cost of Goods | $500 | $500 | Same |
| Gross Profit | $2,000 | $5,000 | +150% |
| Ad Spend | $2,000 | $2,000 | Same |
| CTR | 1% | 3% | +200% |
| Clicks | 100 | 300 | +200% |
| Conversion Rate | 4% | 6% | +50% |
| Sales | 2 | 18 | +800% |
| Gross Profit Total | $8,000 | $90,000 | +1,025% |
| ROAS | 4:1 | 45:1 | +1,025% |

Source: Table on p.17

**Key Insight:** "Branded returns on advertising are absurd. They just take time. And that's why no one does it." (p.18)

---

## Appendix B: What Branding Enables

### When You Do This Right (p.30)
- Get higher click through rates on all advertising
- Get higher closing rates
- Close at higher prices
- Get people to keep buying again and again
- Get cheaper customers than everyone else
- Get increasingly large customers over time
- Get new customers from compounding word of mouth
- Attract the best talent (they want to work for the best)
- Build an asset that itself has value

### When You Do This Wrong (p.30-31)
- Ward off good customers
- Attract bad ones
- Pay more for customers than you should
- Negative word of mouth compounds faster than any marketing
- Lose customers on the back end
- Need crazy new offers constantly to get customers
- Struggle to get good talent
- Constantly consider changing businesses

# AGENT DEFINITIONS

agents:
  brand-coordinator:
    id: brand-coordinator
    title: "Brand Strategy Orchestrator"
    tier: orchestrator
    icon: "crown"

    purpose: |
      Orchestrate the Four-Step Brand Framework to build a premium brand
      that commands higher prices and creates customer loyalty.

    core_frameworks:
      - name: "Four-Step Brand Framework"
        steps: ["Define Who", "Research What They Like", "Associate", "Optimize"]
      - name: "Brand Measurement"
        variables: ["Reach", "Influence", "Direction"]
      - name: "Branding Cycle"
        levels: ["What You Say", "What Others Say", "What They Experience"]

    decision_authority:
      - "Avatar validation and selection"
      - "Association approval/rejection"
      - "Pivot go/no-go decisions"
      - "Recovery strategy activation"

    inputs:
      - "Market research data"
      - "Customer feedback"
      - "Competitor analysis"
      - "Performance metrics"

    outputs:
      - "Brand strategy direction"
      - "Association recommendations"
      - "Pivot decisions"
      - "Resource allocation"

    success_metrics:
      primary:
        - name: "Pricing Power"
          indicator: "Can raise prices without losing business"
        - name: "Net Audience Change"
          target: "Positive on all pivots"
      secondary:
        - "Reach growth month-over-month"
        - "Conversion rate above baseline"
        - "Repeat purchase rate"

  avatar-analyst:
    id: avatar-analyst
    title: "Ideal Customer Profile Specialist"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "user-search"

    purpose: |
      Define and validate ideal customer profile using the four criteria:
      Growing, Have Money, Easy to Target, In Pain.

    four_criteria:
      growing:
        question: "Is the market growing, not shrinking or maintaining?"
        assessment: "Compare market size trends over 3-5 years"
        preference: "Growing > Stable > Shrinking"

      have_money:
        question: "Can they afford what you're selling?"
        assessment: "Income levels, business revenue, budget availability"
        preference: "Rich > Medium > Poor (for premium)"

      easy_to_target:
        question: "Can you put ads in front of them easily?"
        assessment: "Platform targeting options, community presence"
        preference: "Easy > Moderate > Hard"

      in_pain:
        question: "Do they desperately want what you sell?"
        assessment: "Pain intensity, urgency, competition presence"
        preference: "Desperate > Uncomfortable > Mild"

    outputs:
      - "4-criteria scorecard"
      - "Avatar qualification decision"
      - "Targeting feasibility report"
      - "Market size estimate"

    validation_rule: |
      "If I could choose between hard and easy, I'd rather make it easy."
      - All 4 criteria = IDEAL
      - 3 of 4 criteria = ACCEPTABLE
      - <3 criteria = RECONSIDER

  likes-researcher:
    id: likes-researcher
    title: "Audience Preferences Researcher"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "heart"

    purpose: |
      Research and document everything the target audience likes:
      values, people, outcomes, and experiences.

    research_categories:
      values:
        description: "Core values the audience prizes"
        examples:
          - "Making more money"
          - "Getting more customers"
          - "Building sellable business"
          - "Fewer lawsuits"
          - "Paying fewer taxes"

      people:
        description: "Figures and authorities they admire"
        examples:
          - "Industry leaders"
          - "Successful peers"
          - "Thought leaders"
          - "Celebrities in their space"

      outcomes:
        description: "Specific results they want"
        examples:
          - "Revenue growth"
          - "Time freedom"
          - "Market leadership"
          - "Lifestyle improvements"

      experiences:
        description: "Activities and consumption preferences"
        examples:
          - "Events they attend"
          - "Content they consume"
          - "Communities they belong to"
          - "Products they buy"

    research_methods:
      - "Customer interviews"
      - "Survey analysis"
      - "Social media monitoring"
      - "Competitor customer research"
      - "Community observation"

    outputs:
      - "Values inventory (10+ items)"
      - "Admired figures list"
      - "Desired outcomes inventory"
      - "Experience preferences map"
      - "Association opportunity matrix"

  content-creator:
    id: content-creator
    title: "Brand Content Strategist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "file-text"

    purpose: |
      Create content geared toward target audience that genuinely helps them
      and creates positive brand associations.

    content_philosophy: |
      "When I start doing this, people are like, 'Wow, this stuff
      really makes my life better.'...and who do they think of when
      that happens? Our business." (p.22)

    content_types:
      - type: "Videos"
        purpose: "Visual demonstration of expertise"
        cadence: "Weekly minimum"

      - type: "Blogs/Articles"
        purpose: "Written thought leadership"
        cadence: "2-3x weekly"

      - type: "Booklets/PDFs"
        purpose: "Deep-dive value delivery"
        cadence: "Monthly"

      - type: "Podcasts"
        purpose: "Long-form relationship building"
        cadence: "Weekly"

    content_rules:
      - "Content must genuinely help audience"
      - "Focus on their problems, not your products"
      - "Take their perspective always"
      - "Give away the best stuff for free"

    quality_check: |
      Before publishing, ask: "Does this make their life better?"
      If no, don't publish.

  distribution-engine:
    id: distribution-engine
    title: "Reach Maximization Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "share-2"

    purpose: |
      Maximize reach through multi-channel distribution.
      "A brand can't exist without [reach], so reach is the primary
      element of a brand." (p.8)

    reach_principle: |
      Advertising = Letting people know about your stuff
      Good advertising = Everyone knows about your stuff
      Reach = Primary brand element

    distribution_strategy:
      channels:
        - "Social media platforms"
        - "Email list"
        - "Podcast appearances"
        - "Speaking engagements"
        - "Partnerships/collaborations"
        - "Paid advertising"

      optimization:
        - "Track channel performance"
        - "Double down on what works"
        - "Test new channels"
        - "Consistent presence across channels"

    metrics:
      primary: "Total reach (unique people)"
      secondary:
        - "Channel-specific reach"
        - "Growth rate"
        - "Engagement rate"
        - "Cost per reach"

  association-builder:
    id: association-builder
    title: "Strategic Association Architect"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "link"

    purpose: |
      Create deliberate pairings between your brand and things
      your ideal audience likes.

    association_transfer_mechanism:
      step_1: "Start with brand that means nothing (just a logo)"
      step_2: "Pair it with stuff your customers like"
      step_3: "Brand starts to mean 'thing customer likes' to them"
      step_4: "Add brand to generic product = premium branded product"
      step_5: "Customers want to associate with positively branded product"
      step_6: "They exchange money for premium product"
      step_7: "They get product AND association"
      step_8: "You get higher profits from those associations"

    association_types:
      content_associations:
        description: "Topics and themes you cover"
        execution: "Create content around what they care about"

      people_associations:
        description: "Who you appear with"
        execution: "Strategic collaborations, appearances, endorsements"

      product_associations:
        description: "What you sell"
        execution: "Products aligned with audience values"

      experience_associations:
        description: "How they interact with you"
        execution: "Customer experience design"

    quality_gate: |
      Before any association, ask:
      "Does the majority of my ideal audience LIKE this?"
      - YES = Execute
      - NO = Reject
      - UNCERTAIN = Test small first

  positioning-strategist:
    id: positioning-strategist
    title: "Market Positioning Specialist"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "compass"

    purpose: |
      Determine and execute market positioning moves to expand
      addressable market while maintaining brand coherence.

    five_directions:
      up_market:
        definition: "Target larger customers"
        example: "Multi-location assisted living owners"
        bouquet_shift: "Focus on problems larger players have"

      down_market:
        definition: "Target smaller customers"
        example: "At-home care and mobile assisted living"
        bouquet_shift: "Focus on problems smaller players have"

      adjacent:
        definition: "Similar but slightly different market"
        example: "Rehab facilities instead of assisted living"
        bouquet_shift: "Red roses to yellow roses"

      broader:
        definition: "Entire category"
        example: "All senior living (hospice, end of life, retirement)"
        bouquet_shift: "Add all types of flowers"

      narrower:
        definition: "Slice of existing market"
        example: "Only assisted living with 100-500 residents"
        bouquet_shift: "Only red roses, nothing else"

    decision_framework: |
      1. Identify current market position
      2. Assess potential in each direction
      3. Evaluate required association changes
      4. Project net audience change
      5. Recommend direction with highest profit potential

  pivot-executor:
    id: pivot-executor
    title: "Brand Pivot Specialist"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "refresh-cw"

    purpose: |
      Execute brand pivots while ensuring positive net outcomes.
      "Only two things can happen: gain more than you lose,
      or lose more than you gain." (p.27)

    pivot_philosophy: |
      Bouquet Metaphor:
      - Individual elements = individual flowers
      - Assembled together = brand bouquet
      - What we include, from where, and how much = brand we create
      - Bad pairings = sticks and weeds (distort clarity)

    pivot_process:
      step_1: "Document current associations (bouquet inventory)"
      step_2: "Identify associations to add (new flowers)"
      step_3: "Identify associations to reduce (trim existing)"
      step_4: "Project audience impact (who gains, who loses)"
      step_5: "Execute if net positive expected"
      step_6: "Monitor actual results"
      step_7: "Adjust or revert based on data"

    net_change_rule: |
      "Losing audience is a part of life. You just wanna make sure
      you gain more than you lose. Don't let the five mean comments
      stop you from gaining the 500 new people who like the new thing." (p.28)

    case_studies:
      positive_pivot:
        example: "Small town band goes big"
        outcome: "Lost some locals, gained much larger audience"

      negative_pivot:
        example: "Pepsi Kendall Jenner ad"
        outcome: "More people hated it than liked it"

  recovery-specialist:
    id: recovery-specialist
    title: "Brand Recovery Specialist"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "shield"

    purpose: |
      Recover from branding mistakes by overwhelming bad pairings
      with good ones, never by elimination.

    recovery_philosophy: |
      "Most people's brands happen by accident... They take every podcast.
      They sell any customer. They talk about whatever's trending.
      And, surprisingly to them, no one has any idea what they're about." (p.28)

    mistake_impact: |
      "One bad pairing can absolutely hurt a brand. Just like one ugly
      flower messes up the whole bouquet." (p.29)

    recovery_strategy:
      principle: |
        "We don't try and eliminate the DUI, we don't try and eliminate
        the dead rose. It happened; there's nothing we can do about it.
        But what we try to do is to just overwhelm it with way more of
        the stuff that the majority of our people actually like." (p.29)

      execution:
        step_1: "Identify the bad pairing"
        step_2: "Assess damage scope"
        step_3: "Inventory positive associations available"
        step_4: "Create surge of positive content/associations"
        step_5: "Continue until bad pairing shrinks to irrelevance"

    case_study:
      name: "Kanye West"
      description: |
        "Kanye West... has said some things that people don't like,
        but he also comes out with products that people love. He made
        a Super Bowl ad, he sold shoes, he just came out with an album...
        over successive pairings the good stuff minimizes the bad stuff
        ...and people still buy." (p.30)

  brand-auditor:
    id: brand-auditor
    title: "Brand Health Monitor"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "activity"

    purpose: |
      Monitor brand health across reach, influence, and direction.
      Evaluate pricing power as ultimate brand strength indicator.

    measurement_framework:
      reach:
        definition: "How many people know about your stuff"
        measurement: "Audience size, impressions, recognition surveys"
        good: "Everyone in target market knows"
        bad: "No one knows"

      influence:
        definition: "Chance it changes behavior when they see it"
        measurement: "Engagement rates, action rates, conversion"
        good: "High likelihood of behavior change"
        bad: "No behavior change"

      direction:
        definition: "How behavior changes - towards or away"
        measurement: "Sentiment analysis, purchase intent, referrals"
        good: "Towards (they like and buy)"
        bad: "Away (they hate and don't)"

    pricing_power_test: |
      Warren Buffett: "The single most important decision in evaluating
      a business is pricing power. If you've got the power to raise prices
      without losing business to a competitor, you've got a very good
      business. And if you have to have a prayer session before raising
      the price by 10%, then you've got a terrible business." (p.17)

    health_indicators:
      strong_brand:
        - "Can raise prices without losing business"
        - "Higher conversion than competitors"
        - "Customers don't consider competition"
        - "Word of mouth growing"
        - "Best talent wants to work for you"

      weak_brand:
        - "Need prayer session before price increase"
        - "Must compete on price"
        - "High churn to competitors"
        - "Negative word of mouth"
        - "Struggle to attract talent"

# ==============================================================================
# EXECUTOR MATRIX
# ==============================================================================

executor_matrix:
  # Step 1: Avatar Definition
  - task: "Research market growth trends"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Use reliable data sources"

  - task: "Assess target audience financial capacity"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Verify with actual customer data"

  - task: "Evaluate targeting ease on platforms"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Check all major platforms"

  - task: "Qualify pain level of audience"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Requires qualitative research"

  - task: "Final avatar selection decision"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "All 4 criteria must be assessed"

  # Step 2: Likes Research
  - task: "Survey audience values"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Large sample size required"

  - task: "Identify admired figures"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Verify admiration vs awareness"

  - task: "Document desired outcomes"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must be specific and measurable"

  - task: "Map experience preferences"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Include both aspirational and current"

  # Step 3: Association Building
  - task: "Create content for audience"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must genuinely help them"

  - task: "Distribute content across channels"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Track performance by channel"

  - task: "Develop aligned products"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Match brand promises"

  - task: "Plan strategic appearances"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Only with people audience likes"

  - task: "Monitor audience response"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Measure behavior change, not sentiment"

  # Step 4: Optimization
  - task: "Assess market positioning options"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Evaluate all 5 directions"

  - task: "Project net audience change"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Must be positive to proceed"

  - task: "Execute brand pivot"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Monitor closely, ready to revert"

  - task: "Track reach metrics"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Real-time dashboard"

  - task: "Evaluate pricing power"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Test with actual price changes"

  # Recovery
  - task: "Detect bad pairings"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Monitor sentiment and sales"

  - task: "Execute recovery surge"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Overwhelm, don't eliminate"

  - task: "Track recovery progress"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Until bad pairing irrelevant"

# ==============================================================================
# QUALITY GATES
# ==============================================================================

quality_gates:
  QG-001:
    name: "Avatar Validation Gate"
    transition: "Research -> Avatar Definition"
    condition: "all_four_criteria_assessed == true"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Complete missing criteria assessment"

  QG-002:
    name: "Likes Inventory Gate"
    transition: "Avatar -> Association Planning"
    condition: "likes_inventory_items >= 10_per_category"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Deepen research"

  QG-003:
    name: "Association Quality Gate"
    transition: "Planning -> Execution"
    condition: "majority_of_audience_likes == true"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Reject association, find alternative"

  QG-004:
    name: "Net Change Gate"
    transition: "Current -> Pivot"
    condition: "expected_gains > expected_losses"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Abort pivot or adjust scope"

  QG-005:
    name: "Pricing Power Gate"
    transition: "Brand Building -> Premium Pricing"
    condition: "can_raise_prices_without_losing_business == true"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Strengthen associations before pricing"

  QG-006:
    name: "Content Quality Gate"
    transition: "Creation -> Distribution"
    condition: "content_genuinely_helps_audience == true"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Revise or reject content"

# ==============================================================================
# WORKFLOWS
# ==============================================================================

workflows:
  brand_from_scratch_workflow:
    trigger: "New brand initiative"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: avatar-analyst
        action: "Assess market against 4 criteria"
        output: "Avatar qualification score"

      - step: 2
        agent: avatar-analyst
        action: "Select and document ideal customer"
        output: "Avatar profile"

      - step: 3
        agent: likes-researcher
        action: "Research values they hold"
        output: "Values inventory"

      - step: 4
        agent: likes-researcher
        action: "Identify people they admire"
        output: "Admired figures list"

      - step: 5
        agent: likes-researcher
        action: "Document desired outcomes"
        output: "Outcomes inventory"

      - step: 6
        agent: likes-researcher
        action: "Map experience preferences"
        output: "Experience map"

      - step: 7
        agent: association-builder
        action: "Plan association strategy"
        output: "Association roadmap"

      - step: 8
        agent: content-creator
        action: "Create content geared to audience"
        output: "Content library"

      - step: 9
        agent: distribution-engine
        action: "Distribute widely"
        output: "Reach metrics"

      - step: 10
        agent: brand-auditor
        action: "Monitor and iterate"
        output: "Brand health report"

  brand_pivot_workflow:
    trigger: "Market repositioning decision"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: positioning-strategist
        action: "Assess 5 positioning options"
        output: "Options analysis"

      - step: 2
        agent: positioning-strategist
        action: "Select direction"
        output: "Direction recommendation"

      - step: 3
        agent: pivot-executor
        action: "Project net audience change"
        output: "Net change projection"

      - step: 4
        agent: brand-coordinator
        action: "Go/no-go decision"
        gate: "QG-004"

      - step: 5
        agent: pivot-executor
        action: "Execute bouquet adjustment"
        output: "Pivot execution"

      - step: 6
        agent: brand-auditor
        action: "Monitor results"
        output: "Actual vs projected"

      - step: 7
        agent: pivot-executor
        action: "Adjust or revert based on data"
        condition: "If net change negative"

  brand_recovery_workflow:
    trigger: "Bad pairing detected"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: brand-auditor
        action: "Assess damage scope"
        output: "Damage assessment"

      - step: 2
        agent: recovery-specialist
        action: "Inventory positive associations"
        output: "Available positive pairings"

      - step: 3
        agent: recovery-specialist
        action: "Plan positive surge"
        output: "Surge strategy"

      - step: 4
        agent: content-creator
        action: "Create surge content"
        output: "Positive content batch"

      - step: 5
        agent: distribution-engine
        action: "Execute surge distribution"
        output: "Reach metrics"

      - step: 6
        agent: brand-auditor
        action: "Monitor recovery"
        output: "Recovery progress"

      - step: 7
        agent: recovery-specialist
        action: "Continue until irrelevance"
        condition: "Until bad pairing forgotten"

  content_creation_workflow:
    trigger: "Content needed for association"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: likes-researcher
        action: "Confirm topic alignment with audience likes"
        output: "Topic validation"

      - step: 2
        agent: content-creator
        action: "Create content draft"
        output: "Draft content"

      - step: 3
        agent: content-creator
        action: "Quality check: Does this help them?"
        gate: "QG-006"

      - step: 4
        agent: distribution-engine
        action: "Distribute across channels"
        output: "Published content"

      - step: 5
        agent: brand-auditor
        action: "Monitor response"
        output: "Engagement metrics"

      - step: 6
        agent: content-creator
        action: "Iterate based on response"
        output: "Content optimization"

# ==============================================================================
# KPIs & SUCCESS METRICS
# ==============================================================================

kpis:
  primary:
    pricing_power:
      test: "Can you raise prices without losing business?"
      strong: "Yes, easily"
      weak: "Need prayer session first"
      source: "Warren Buffett quote, p.17"

    net_audience_change:
      formula: "New audience gained - Existing audience lost"
      target: "Positive on every pivot"
      impact: "Brand grows vs shrinks"

  secondary:
    reach:
      definition: "How many people know about your stuff"
      measurement: "Audience size, impressions"
      target: "Growing month-over-month"

    influence:
      definition: "Likelihood of behavior change"
      measurement: "Engagement, conversion rates"
      target: "Above industry baseline"

    direction:
      definition: "Behavior change towards or away"
      measurement: "Purchase intent, sentiment"
      target: "Strongly towards"

  business_impact:
    cac_reduction:
      benefit: "Convert higher % from advertising"
      example: "Dwayne Johnson launches product, millions buy day one"

    ltv_increase:
      benefit: "Charge 2x-10x more for same thing"
      example: "Starbucks $5 vs competitor $1 for coffee"

    risk_reduction:
      benefit: "Customers buy repeatedly without considering competition"
      example: "Mac users only buy Apple for life"

  by_step:
    step_1:
      - "Avatar meets all 4 criteria"
      - "Market size validated"
      - "Targeting feasibility confirmed"

    step_2:
      - "10+ items per likes category"
      - "Values match brand capability"
      - "Association opportunities identified"

    step_3:
      - "Content publishing consistency"
      - "Reach growth rate"
      - "Engagement metrics"
      - "Association quality scores"

    step_4:
      - "Net positive on all pivots"
      - "Pricing power maintained/improved"
      - "Brand coherence preserved"

# ==============================================================================
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ==============================================================================

troubleshooting:
  - symptom: "Audience growth but wrong type of people"
    cause: "Content/associations attracting non-ideal customers"
    example: "Hormozi attracting wantrepreneurs instead of business owners"
    solution:
      - "Recenter content around ideal customer"
      - "Prune associations that attract wrong audience"
      - "Accept some audience loss for quality"

  - symptom: "High reach, low influence"
    cause: "People know you but don't change behavior"
    solution:
      - "Deepen engagement with target niche"
      - "Strengthen emotional connection"
      - "Increase product quality/promise match"

  - symptom: "Competitor has 'cool factor' despite worse economics"
    cause: "Brand not delivering intangible value"
    example: "Hormozi supplements vs cool competitor"
    solution:
      - "Allocate budget specifically to brand building"
      - "Not just product/economics"
      - "Create associations that make people feel good"

  - symptom: "Bad publicity event"
    cause: "Single bad pairing damaging overall bouquet"
    solution:
      - "Don't try to eliminate or hide"
      - "Overwhelm with positive associations"
      - "Continue until bad pairing shrinks to irrelevance"

  - symptom: "Pricing pressure from competitors"
    cause: "Weak brand, commodity positioning"
    solution:
      - "Strengthen unique associations"
      - "Increase reach + influence"
      - "Deliver on promises consistently"

  - symptom: "Pivot resulted in net audience loss"
    cause: "Lost more than gained in repositioning"
    solution:
      - "Assess if loss is temporary vs permanent"
      - "Consider partial revert"
      - "Test smaller scope next time"

# ==============================================================================
# TIME REQUIREMENTS
# ==============================================================================

time_requirements:
  patience_mandate: |
    "Wait five years and don't give up." (One Page Checklist, p.33)

    "Branding has higher returns than direct response advertising
    if you measure over a longer period of time." (p.30)

  milestones:
    month_1_6: "Foundation building, avatar clarity, initial content"
    month_6_12: "Reach building, association establishment"
    year_1_2: "Brand recognition, 'they're the [X] company'"
    year_2_3: "Premium pricing power emerging"
    year_3_4: "Loyalty development, repeat purchase without shopping"
    year_4_5: "Advocacy stage, unprompted recommendations"

  realistic_expectations: |
    "There is no magic here. It's teaching people what you are about.
    And repeating it every day until the end of time. Because every day,
    you'll have people who just found you and have no idea who you are.
    And you have to serve them the same way you did your 'OGs.'" (p.31)

# ==============================================================================
# GAPS TO RESOLVE
# ==============================================================================

gaps_to_resolve:
  - id: GAP-001
    description: "Specific budget allocation between product vs brand"
    severity: Medium
    clarification_needed: "What percentage should go to brand building?"

  - id: GAP-002
    description: "Quantitative thresholds for influence measurement"
    severity: Medium
    clarification_needed: "What engagement rates indicate strong influence?"

  - id: GAP-003
    description: "Detailed content calendar framework"
    severity: Low
    note: "May be covered in content playbooks"

  - id: GAP-004
    description: "Specific criteria for 'majority of audience likes'"
    severity: Medium
    clarification_needed: "What percentage constitutes majority?"

  - id: GAP-005
    description: "Recovery timeline expectations"
    severity: Medium
    clarification_needed: "How long until bad pairing becomes irrelevant?"

# ==============================================================================
# VALIDATION
# ==============================================================================

validation:
  sop_parts_complete: 11/11
  task_anatomy_fields: 8/8
  decision_rules_documented: 6
  executor_matrix_complete: true
  quality_gates_defined: 6
  workflows_documented: 4

  blueprint_status: "READY FOR SQUAD CREATION"

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/content-creation-sop.md

# Content Creation SOP

> **Source:** $100M Leads: Postar Conteudo Gratuito Parte I & II - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Build a growing audience of warm leads through free content that hooks, retains, and rewards attention. The Content Creation process creates an **accumulating asset** - the audience itself - that compounds over time and makes all other advertising more effective.

**Core Equation:**
```
Audience Growth = Content Units x Volume x Consistency

Example:
- 1 piece/day x 30 days = 30 content units
- Each unit hooks, retains, rewards audience
- Audience grows → More leads → More money
```

**Business Impact:** "Construir uma audiencia e a coisa mais valiosa que ja fiz." (Building an audience is the most valuable thing I've ever done.) - Alex Hormozi, p.67

**Key Insight:** "O conteudo que voce cria nao e o ativo que se acumula - a audiencia e. Entao, mesmo que o conteudo possa desaparecer com o tempo, sua audiencia continua crescendo." (The content you create isn't the asset that accumulates - the audience is. So even though content may disappear over time, your audience keeps growing.) - p.65

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Building audience through free content (social media, podcasts, videos, blogs)
- Creating content units that hook, retain, and reward attention
- Scaling content production across platforms
- Monetizing audience through integrated or intermittent offers

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- Warm outreach (direct personal contact) - covered in other playbook
- Cold outreach (direct advertising) - covered in other playbook
- Paid ads (covered separately)
- Sales calls/closing (covered in Lead Nurture SOP)

### Business Types
- Any business wanting to build an audience
- Creators, coaches, consultants, agencies
- B2B and B2C
- Product and service businesses

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Platform Access | Active accounts on target platforms | Profiles created and verified |
| Content Creation Tools | Recording, editing, publishing capabilities | Tools operational |
| Topic Expertise | Knowledge/experience to share | Stories and lessons documented |
| Time Commitment | Consistent posting schedule | Calendar blocked |
| Lead Magnet/Offer | Something to offer when asking | Lead magnet or main offer ready |
| Note-Taking System | Way to capture ideas always | System accessible at all times |

## Part 4: The Content Unit Framework

### Framework Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       THE CONTENT UNIT                                  │
├──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┤
│       HOOK           │       RETAIN         │       REWARD              │
├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ Make them notice     │ Make them consume    │ Satisfy their reason      │
│ Give reason to       │ Keep them curious    │ Exceed expectations       │
│ redirect attention   │ wanting more         │ Make them share           │
├──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ COMPONENTS:          │ COMPONENTS:          │ COMPONENTS:               │
│ - Topic              │ - Lists              │ - Value per second        │
│ - Headline           │ - Steps              │ - Promise fulfillment     │
│ - Format             │ - Stories            │ - Exceed expectations     │
└──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘
```

**Source:** "A menor quantidade de material necessaria para fisgar, reter e recompensar atencao e uma unidade de conteudo." (The smallest amount of material necessary to hook, retain, and reward attention is a content unit.) - p.111

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### PHASE I: HOOK - GETTING ATTENTION

#### Step 1.1: Choose Your Topic
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Select topic from five categories based on your experience |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis (connecting experience to audience needs) |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires personal experience and judgment |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Personal experiences documented |
| **Output** | Topic selected for content creation |
| **Guardrails** | "So existe um de voce. A maneira mais facil de se diferenciar e dizer algo que ninguem mais pode dizer." (There's only one of you. The easiest way to differentiate is to say something no one else can say.) - p.121 |
| **Decision Rule** | Use personal experiences; speak from what YOU did, not what others should do |

**Five Topic Categories:**

**a) Passado Distante (Distant Past):**
- Important life lessons from your past
- Connect wisdom to your product/service
- "De a eles a historia sem a cicatriz." (Give them the story without the scar.) - p.123

**b) Passado Recente (Recent Past):**
- Talk about what you just did or what happened
- Review your calendar from last week
- Meetings, social interactions, conversations with clients
- Testimonials and case studies fit here - p.134-136

**c) Presente (Present):**
- Ideas as they come to you in the moment
- "Sempre tenha uma maneira de gravar suas ideias ao alcance dos bracos." (Always have a way to record your ideas within arm's reach.) - p.137
- "Eu anoto minhas ideias publicamente." (I note my ideas publicly.) - p.139

**d) Tendencias (Trends):**
- What's trending now
- Apply your experience to current events
- "Falar sobre coisas da moda e muito eficaz para ganhar a atencao de uma audiencia mais ampla." (Talking about trending things is very effective for gaining attention from a wider audience.) - p.141

**e) Fabricado (Fabricated):**
- Create experiences specifically for content
- Example: "Vivi com $100 por um mes. Eis como." (I lived on $100 for a month. Here's how.) - p.145
- Costs more time but can have biggest returns - p.143

#### Step 1.2: Morpheus Your Headline
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create headline using news-proven components to capture attention |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Templates help, but creativity needed |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Topic selected |
| **Output** | Headline that gives reason to consume |
| **Guardrails** | Include at least two components from the seven proven elements |
| **Decision Rule** | "Eles a usam para pesar a probabilidade de obterem uma recompensa por consumir seu conteudo versus outro." (They use it to weigh the probability of getting a reward from consuming your content versus another.) - p.149 |

**Seven Headline Components (from meta-analysis of news):**

| Component | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Recencia** (Recency) | Most recent possible | "Aconteceu ha uma hora" vs "ha um ano" - p.155 |
| **Relevancia** (Relevance) | Personally significant to audience | "Enfermeiras prestam mais atencao a coisas que afetam enfermeiras" - p.157 |
| **Celebridade** (Celebrity) | Including prominent people | "Normalmente, nao nos importariamos com o que outro humano come... Mas se for Jeff Bezos, nos importamos." - p.159 |
| **Proximidade** (Proximity) | Close to home geographically | "Uma casa pegando fogo do outro lado do pais nao chama sua atencao. Se for seu vizinho, certamente chama." - p.161 |
| **Conflito** (Conflict) | Opposing ideas, people, nature | "Abacaxi vs sem abacaxi na pizza? Conflito!" - p.163 |
| **Incomum** (Unusual) | Strange, unique, rare, bizarre | "Se esta fora da norma, as pessoas prestam mais atencao." - p.165 |
| **Em andamento** (Ongoing) | Stories still in progress | "Se alguem entra em trabalho de parto, as pessoas querem atualizacoes a cada dez minutos" - p.167 |

#### Step 1.3: Match Your Format
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Format content to match platform expectations and audience preferences |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception (reading platform norms) |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Templates and repurposing tools |
| **Executor** | Worker (formatting) + Human (creative decisions) |
| **Precondition** | Topic and headline defined |
| **Output** | Content formatted for target platform |
| **Guardrails** | "Voce tem que fazer seu conteudo parecer com o que eles esperam que os recompense." (You have to make your content look like what they expect will reward them.) - p.179 |
| **Decision Rule** | Study the best content on the platform targeting your market; match that format |

**Format Matching Process:**
1. Identify target platform
2. Study top-performing content in your niche
3. Note visual style, length, structure
4. Adapt your content to match expectations
5. "Formate seu conteudo para a plataforma primeiro. Entao, ajuste-o para fisgar sua audiencia ideal." - p.181

---

### PHASE II: RETAIN - KEEPING ATTENTION

#### Step 2.1: Use Lists
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Present information as numbered lists to create curiosity |
| **Cognitive Type** | Organization + Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Structure is formulaic |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Content topic defined |
| **Output** | List-structured content |
| **Guardrails** | "Dar o numero de itens listados em sua manchete, ou nos primeiros segundos do seu conteudo, diz as pessoas o que esperar." - p.191 |
| **Decision Rule** | Use lists for flexible collections; more flexible but less explicit reward |

**List Examples:**
- "7 Maneiras Que Investi $1000 nos Meus 20 Anos Que Valeram a Pena" - p.193
- "28 Maneiras de Ficar Pobre" - p.193
- "Uma unidade de conteudo tem tres pecas..." - p.193

#### Step 2.2: Use Steps
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Present information as sequential steps that achieve an outcome |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Organization |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Structure is formulaic |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Process or outcome to teach |
| **Output** | Step-structured content |
| **Guardrails** | "Passos sao acoes que devem ser feitas em uma ordem especifica para obter um resultado." - p.199 |
| **Decision Rule** | Use steps when order matters; less flexible but more explicit reward |

**Steps Examples:**
- "3 Passos para Criar um Otimo Hook" - p.197
- "Como Crio uma Manchete em 7 Passos" - p.197
- "A Rotina Matinal Que Aumenta Minha Produtividade" - p.197

#### Step 2.3: Use Stories
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Describe events (real or imagined) with lessons or conclusions |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Narrative |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires human storytelling |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Experience or scenario to share |
| **Output** | Story-structured content |
| **Guardrails** | "Historias que valem a pena contar geralmente tem alguma licao ou conclusao para o ouvinte." - p.201 |
| **Decision Rule** | Stories generate curiosity because people want to know what happens next |

**Story Examples:**
- "Quase todo capitulo deste livro tem uma historia." - p.203
- "Meu editor me fez fazer 19 rascunhos deste livro - aqui esta o que fiz com ele." - p.203
- "Minha jornada de dormir no andar de baixo de uma academia ate o andar de cima de um hotel 5 estrelas." - p.203

#### Step 2.4: Interweave Structures
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Combine lists, steps, and stories for complex content |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires creative judgment |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Multiple retention structures identified |
| **Output** | Complex, engaging content |
| **Guardrails** | "Voce pode usar listas, passos e historias sozinhos ou entrelaca-los." - p.205 |
| **Decision Rule** | Your creativity is the only limit; great content weaves all three together |

**Interweaving Examples:**
- Lists within steps with a story for each item
- Stories to reinforce the value of a step
- A list of stories
- Multiple ongoing storylines

---

### PHASE III: REWARD - SATISFYING ATTENTION

#### Step 3.1: Maximize Value Per Second
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Deliver rewards frequently throughout content consumption |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment + Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires quality judgment |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Content draft created |
| **Output** | High-density value content |
| **Guardrails** | "Pense em valor por segundo... nao existe tal coisa como muito longo, apenas muito chato." - p.211 |
| **Decision Rule** | Same person who gets bored 3 seconds into 10-second video can marathon 900-page book |

**Key Insight:** "A mesma pessoa que fica entediada tres segundos em um video de dez segundos tambem pode maratonar um livro de 900 paginas. E essa mesma pessoa pode maratonar uma serie de televisao por oito horas seguidas." - p.211

#### Step 3.2: Fulfill Your Promise
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Clearly satisfy the reason that hooked them in the first place |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires content quality check |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Content completed |
| **Output** | Promise-fulfilling content |
| **Guardrails** | If hook promises "7 ways" deliver 7 good ways they haven't heard before |
| **Decision Rule** | "Responda completamente as perguntas nao resolvidas que voce incorporou em suas mentes." - p.225 |

**Failure Examples:**
- Hook: "7 Maneiras de Se Reconciliar com Seu Conjuge"
  - FAIL: Giving only 4 ways
  - FAIL: Giving 7 bad ways
  - FAIL: Speaking to single people without spouses - p.219

- Hook: "4 Estrategias de Marketing que Dentistas Podem Usar"
  - FAIL: If dentists can't actually use them - p.221

#### Step 3.3: Validate with Audience Growth
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Measure success by whether audience grows |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Analytics tools |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Content published |
| **Output** | Growth metrics |
| **Guardrails** | "Recompensar sua audiencia significa igualar ou exceder suas expectativas quando decidem consumir seu conteudo." - p.223 |
| **Decision Rule** | "Se nao esta crescendo, suas coisas nao sao tao boas. Pratique e voce melhorara." - p.223 |

---

### PHASE IV: MONETIZATION

#### Step 4.1: Master the Give:Ask Ratio
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Maintain high give ratio to build goodwill before asking |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategic judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires strategic decision |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Audience established |
| **Output** | Sustainable monetization strategy |
| **Guardrails** | Television: 47min give, 13min ask (3.5:1). Growing platforms give much more. |
| **Decision Rule** | "O momento em que voce comeca a pedir dinheiro e o momento em que decide desacelerar seu crescimento." - p.271 |

**Ratios:**
- Television: ~3.5:1 (give:ask) - mature, monetizing platform
- Facebook: ~4:1 (content:ads) - mature platform
- Growing platforms: "dão dão dão... dão dão dão... talvez peçam" - p.259

**Best Strategy:** "De ate que eles pecam." (Give until they ask.) - p.263

#### Step 4.2: Choose Offer Integration Method
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Decide between integrated offers or intermittent offers |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategic judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Can template the approach |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Offer ready (lead magnet or main offer) |
| **Output** | Offer integration plan |
| **Guardrails** | Monitor if audience growth slows after introducing asks |
| **Decision Rule** | Long-form = integrated; Short-form = intermittent - p.295 |

**Integrated Offers:**
- Announce in every piece of content
- Keep give:ask ratio high within each piece
- Example: 3 x 30-second ads in 1-hour podcast = 58.5min give : 1.5min ask - p.285
- Place CTAs after valuable moments or at end - p.289

**Intermittent Offers:**
- Many pure "give" pieces
- Occasional "ask" piece
- Example: 10 give posts, 1 ask post - p.293

#### Step 4.3: Morpheus Your Ask
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create compelling offer announcement |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Persuasion |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Templates available |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Offer defined |
| **Output** | Offer script/copy |
| **Guardrails** | Can promote lead magnet (lower risk) or main offer (direct path) |
| **Decision Rule** | If unsure, start with lead magnet - p.309 |

**Lead Magnet Script:**
"Tenho mais 11 dicas que me ajudaram a fazer isso. Va ao meu site para pegar um visual bonito delas." - p.299

**Main Offer Script Template:**
```
"Estou procurando 5 (avatar especifico) para ajudar a alcancar
(resultado dos sonhos) em (atraso de tempo). A melhor parte e que
voce nao precisa (esforco e sacrificio). E se voce nao conseguir
(resultado dos sonhos), faremos duas coisas:
1) Devolverei seu dinheiro
2) Trabalharei com voce ate conseguir.
Faco isso porque quero que todos tenham uma experiencia incrivel
conosco e porque estou confiante de que posso cumprir minha promessa.
Se isso parece justo, mande DM/agende uma ligacao/comente abaixo..."
- p.303
```

---

### PHASE V: SCALING

#### Step 5.1: Choose Scaling Strategy
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Select depth-first or breadth-first scaling approach |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategic judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Business decision |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | One platform working |
| **Output** | Scaling roadmap |
| **Guardrails** | Both approaches are valid; choose based on resources and goals |
| **Decision Rule** | Existing business with resources = breadth-first; Starting out = depth-first |

**Depth-First (Profundidade depois largura):**
1. Post on one relevant platform
2. Post regularly on that platform
3. Maximize quality AND quantity on that platform
4. Add another platform while maintaining the first
5. Repeat until all platforms maximized - p.319

*Advantages:* Leverage accumulation, less resources needed
*Disadvantages:* Single channel risk, no omnipresence effect

**Breadth-First (Largura depois profundidade):**
1. Post on one relevant platform
2. Post regularly
3. Move to next platform (maintaining previous)
4. Continue until on all relevant platforms
5. Now maximize all platforms together - p.327

*Advantages:* Wider reach faster, content repurposing efficiency
*Disadvantages:* More work, risk of bad content everywhere - p.331

#### Step 5.2: Maximize Volume
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Increase posting frequency to accelerate growth |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Scheduling tools help |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Quality maintained |
| **Output** | Increased content output |
| **Guardrails** | "Quando coloquei dez vezes mais conteudo, minha audiencia cresceu dez vezes mais rapido." - p.77 |
| **Decision Rule** | "Voce so precisa fazer mais, cara." - Influencer mentor, p.76 |

**Volume Targets:**
- Short-form: up to 10x per day per platform - p.319
- Long-form: daily (like soap operas) - p.319
- Podcast example: "duas vezes por semana por quatro anos antes mesmo de ser escolhido na lista Top 100" - p.387
