## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Topic Selection
```yaml
rule: TOPIC_SELECTION
trigger: Need to create content
condition:
  - IF has_recent_experience THEN use "Passado Recente"
  - IF has_trending_relevance THEN use "Tendencias"
  - IF has_important_lesson THEN use "Passado Distante"
  - IF capturing_live_idea THEN use "Presente"
  - IF willing_to_invest_time THEN use "Fabricado"
action: Select topic category that fits current situation
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-002: Headline Components
```yaml
rule: HEADLINE_STRENGTH
trigger: Writing headline
condition:
  - IF components >= 2 THEN "STRONG" headline
  - IF components == 1 THEN "ACCEPTABLE" headline
  - IF components == 0 THEN "WEAK" - add components
action: Include at least 2 of 7 components
confidence: HIGH (meta-analysis data)
```

### DR-003: Content Length
```yaml
rule: CONTENT_LENGTH
trigger: Determining content length
condition:
  - IF can_maintain_value_per_second THEN length_is_fine
  - IF boring_sections_exist THEN "TOO_LONG" - cut or improve
action: "Nao existe tal coisa como muito longo, apenas muito chato"
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-004: Give:Ask Ratio
```yaml
rule: GIVE_ASK_RATIO
trigger: Planning monetization
condition:
  - IF growing_priority THEN give_until_they_ask
  - IF monetizing_priority THEN maintain_minimum_3.5:1
  - IF audience_growth_slowing THEN reduce_asks
action: Prioritize growth over short-term revenue
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-005: Platform Strategy
```yaml
rule: PLATFORM_SCALING
trigger: Adding new platform
condition:
  - IF current_platform_maximized THEN depth_first_ready
  - IF resources_abundant THEN breadth_first_viable
  - IF single_channel_risk_high THEN prioritize_diversification
action: Choose strategy based on resources and risk tolerance
confidence: MEDIUM
```

### DR-006: Content Quality Validation
```yaml
rule: QUALITY_CHECK
trigger: Content published
condition:
  - IF audience_growing THEN quality_sufficient
  - IF audience_stagnant THEN quality_needs_improvement
  - IF audience_shrinking THEN major_quality_issue
action: "Se nao esta crescendo, suas coisas nao sao tao boas"
confidence: HIGH
```

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: Personal Brand Resistance
**Trigger:** Fear of fame, privacy concerns, hate messages
**Response:** Hormozi's transformation story - p.53-59
**Key Quote:** "Se receber mensagens estranhas e odio de pessoas que nao conheco e o preco que tenho que pagar para causar o impacto que quero ter, eu pagaria esse preco qualquer dia da semana." - p.57

### Exception 2: Competitor Copying
**Trigger:** Others copying your successful content
**Response:** Expected; requires constant innovation - p.93
**Action:** Stay ahead through volume and personal experience

### Exception 3: Content Not Performing
**Trigger:** Individual piece underperforms
**Response:** Normal; not every piece will win
**Action:** "Pratique e voce melhorara." Keep posting, analyze patterns

### Exception 4: Podcast Pre-Scheduling
**Trigger:** Temptation to schedule posts in advance
**Response:** Manual posting performs better
**Rationale:** "Quando voce posta manualmente, sabe que em segundos sera recompensado ou punido pela qualidade do conteudo. Por causa desse loop de feedback proximo, voce tenta muito mais para torna-lo melhor." - p.371

### Exception 5: Audience Already Knows Information
**Trigger:** Worried about repeating yourself
**Response:** "Precisamos Ser Lembrados Mais Do Que Precisamos Ser Ensinados"
**Data:** "Pesquisei minha audiencia e perguntei se sabiam que eu tinha um livro. Um em cada cinco que viu o post disse que nao sabia." - p.361

## Part 9: Validation

### Content Unit Quality Gates

| Gate | Check | Action if Failed |
|------|-------|------------------|
| Hook Presence | Does content have clear hook? | Add topic + headline + format |
| Retention Structure | Does content use lists/steps/stories? | Restructure with curiosity elements |
| Reward Fulfillment | Does content deliver on hook promise? | Revise to fulfill promise completely |
| Audience Fit | Is content for your target audience? | Adjust topic/angle |
| Platform Fit | Does format match platform norms? | Reformat for platform |

### Growth Benchmarks

| Metric | Starting | Building | Scaling |
|--------|----------|----------|---------|
| Posting Frequency | 1x/day | 3x/day | 10x/day (short) |
| Monthly Growth Rate | >10% | >30% | >50% |
| Time to Results | 12 months | 18 months | 5+ years |

**Hormozi's Timeline:**
- Year 1: +200,000 audience - p.71
- Months 7-12: +1,200,000 audience (10x content = 10x growth) - p.77

## Appendix A: The Seven Lessons

### Hormozi's Content Creation Lessons - p.353-371

| # | Lesson | Application |
|---|--------|-------------|
| 1 | "Mude de 'Como fazer' para 'Como eu'" | Speak from experience, not prescription. "Eu faco minha aveia desta forma" vs "Voce deve fazer sua aveia desta forma" - p.355-359 |
| 2 | "Precisamos Ser Lembrados Mais Do Que Precisamos Ser Ensinados" | Repeat yourself. 1 in 5 didn't know about the book despite daily posts - p.361 |
| 3 | "Pocas, Lagoas, Lagos, Oceanos" | Start narrow (local niche), expand over time. King of puddle → pond → lake → ocean - p.363 |
| 4 | "Conteudo Cria Ferramentas Para Vendedores" | Create "greatest hits" list for sales team to use before/after calls - p.365 |
| 5 | "Conteudo Gratuito Retem Clientes Pagantes" | Customers include free content value in their ROI calculation - p.367 |
| 6 | "As pessoas nao tem periodos de atencao mais curtos, elas tem padroes mais altos" | No such thing as too long, only too boring - p.369 |
| 7 | "Evite Pre-Agendar Posts" | Manual posting creates pressure to make it better - p.371 |

## Appendix B: Content Synergy with Other Advertising

### Why Content Makes Everything Work Better

**Discovery:** "78% de todos os clientes tinham consumido pelo menos DUAS pecas de conteudo de forma longa antes de agendar uma ligacao." - p.347

**Implication:** Free content nurtures demand even when you don't know it. Paid ads get the credit, but content warms the audience.

**Integration Strategy:**
1. Continue warm outreach alongside content
2. Content provides material for warm outreach posts
3. Content warms people who see cold outreach
4. "Conteudo gratuito da aos estranhos uma oportunidade de encontrar, obter valor e compartilhar suas coisas." - p.349

## Appendix C: First Post Psychology

**Hormozi's Advice:** "Nao tenha medo do que outras pessoas pensam. Se alguem nao vai falar no seu funeral, voce nao deveria se importar com a opiniao deles enquanto esta vivo." - p.395

**Permission to Start:** You've been providing value to humans for a while. Your first post can include an ask. If it doesn't work, give more first.

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/content-creation-squad-blueprint.yaml

```yaml
# Content Creation Squad Blueprint
# Pattern: HO-SB-001 (Hormozi Squad Blueprint Standard)
# Source: $100M Leads: Postar Conteudo Gratuito Parte I & II - Alex Hormozi
# Version: 1.0.0
# Generated: 2026-02-10

squad:
  name: content-creation
  purpose: "Build growing audience through free content that hooks, retains, and rewards attention"
  domain: content-marketing
  source_playbook: "$100M Leads: Postar Conteudo Gratuito"

  core_equation: |
    Audience Growth = Content Units x Volume x Consistency
    The content is not the asset - the AUDIENCE is the asset
    More content = faster audience growth (10x content = 10x growth)

# ===============================================================================
# TIER STRUCTURE
# ===============================================================================

tier_structure:
  orchestrator:
    - agent: content-coordinator
      role: "Orchestrate content creation pipeline and optimize for audience growth"
      decisions:
        - "Content calendar priorities"
        - "Platform strategy (depth vs breadth)"
        - "Give:Ask ratio timing"
        - "Performance analysis and adaptation"
      kpis:
        - "Audience growth rate"
        - "Content velocity"
        - "Engagement metrics"

  tier_0_diagnosis:
    - agent: topic-miner
      role: "Extract content topics from experience categories"
      inputs:
        - "Calendar/meeting notes (Passado Recente)"
        - "Life lessons (Passado Distante)"
        - "Real-time ideas (Presente)"
        - "Trending topics (Tendencias)"
        - "Planned experiments (Fabricado)"
      outputs:
        - "Topic bank with category tags"
        - "Topic-to-audience match score"
        - "Differentiation assessment"

    - agent: audience-analyst
      role: "Monitor audience growth and content performance"
      inputs:
        - "Platform analytics"
        - "Follower/reach data"
        - "Engagement metrics"
        - "Content-to-lead conversion"
      outputs:
        - "Growth rate reports"
        - "Top performing content analysis"
        - "Platform-specific insights"
        - "Audience feedback synthesis"

  tier_1_execution:
    - agent: hook-crafter
      role: "Create attention-grabbing hooks using proven components"
      specialization: "Phase I: Hook"
      techniques:
        topics:
          - distant_past: "Important life lessons"
          - recent_past: "What you just did/experienced"
          - present: "Ideas as they happen"
          - trends: "Current events + your perspective"
          - fabricated: "Created experiences for content"
        headlines:
          - recency: "Most recent possible"
          - relevance: "Personally significant to audience"
          - celebrity: "Including prominent people"
          - proximity: "Close to home geographically"
          - conflict: "Opposing ideas/people/nature"
          - unusual: "Strange, unique, rare, bizarre"
          - ongoing: "Stories still in progress"
        format: "Match platform expectations"

    - agent: retention-architect
      role: "Structure content to maintain curiosity and engagement"
      specialization: "Phase II: Retain"
      structures:
        lists:
          description: "Things, facts, tips, opinions in sequence"
          rule: "Give number in headline or first seconds"
          flexibility: "High - can contain anything in any order"
          examples:
            - "7 Ways I Invested $1000..."
            - "28 Ways to Stay Poor"
        steps:
          description: "Actions in order that achieve an outcome"
          rule: "Clear first steps make them want all steps"
          flexibility: "Low - order matters"
          examples:
            - "3 Steps to Create a Great Hook"
            - "How I Create a Headline in 7 Steps"
        stories:
          description: "Events (real or imagined) with lessons"
          rule: "Stories generate curiosity about what happens next"
          flexibility: "Medium - needs arc and payoff"
          examples:
            - "My journey from sleeping under a gym to a 5-star hotel"
            - "My editor made me do 19 drafts"
        interweaving: "Combine all three for complex content"

    - agent: reward-validator
      role: "Ensure content delivers value and fulfills promises"
      specialization: "Phase III: Reward"
      principles:
        value_per_second: "Reward frequently throughout consumption"
        promise_fulfillment: "Deliver exactly what hook promised"
        exceed_expectations: "Give more than they expected"
      validation_rules:
        - "If promised 7 ways, give 7 GOOD ways"
        - "If audience can't use it, you failed"
        - "If they don't share, reward was weak"
      success_metric: "Audience growth = proof of reward"

    - agent: format-adapter
      role: "Adapt content for different platforms and formats"
      specialization: "Multi-platform distribution"
      capabilities:
        - "Format content for platform norms"
        - "Repurpose long-form to short-form"
        - "Adapt visual style per platform"
        - "Maintain quality across formats"

  tier_2_judgment:
    - agent: monetization-strategist
      role: "Plan and execute audience monetization without killing growth"
      responsibilities:
        give_ask_ratio:
          tv_standard: "3.5:1 (47min give, 13min ask)"
          facebook_standard: "4:1 content:ads"
          growth_priority: "Give give give give... maybe ask"
          hormozi_method: "Give until they ask"
        integration_methods:
          integrated:
            description: "Offers within each content piece"
            placement: "After valuable moments or at end"
            example: "3x30sec ads in 60min podcast = 58.5min give : 1.5min ask"
          intermittent:
            description: "Many give pieces, occasional ask piece"
            example: "10 give posts, then 1 ask post"
            platform_fit: "Short-form platforms"
        offer_types:
          lead_magnet: "Lower risk, builds list"
          main_offer: "Direct path to revenue"

    - agent: scaling-strategist
      role: "Plan and execute platform expansion strategy"
      strategies:
        depth_first:
          description: "Maximize one platform, then add next"
          steps:
            - "Post on one relevant platform"
            - "Post regularly"
            - "Maximize quality AND quantity"
            - "Add another platform while maintaining first"
            - "Repeat until all platforms maximized"
          advantages:
            - "Leverage accumulation"
            - "Less resources needed"
          disadvantages:
            - "Single channel risk"
            - "No omnipresence effect"
        breadth_first:
          description: "Enter all platforms early, maximize together"
          steps:
            - "Post on one relevant platform"
            - "Post regularly"
            - "Move to next platform (maintaining previous)"
            - "Continue until on all platforms"
            - "Maximize all platforms together"
          advantages:
            - "Wider reach faster"
            - "Content repurposing efficiency"
          disadvantages:
            - "More work required"
            - "Risk of bad content everywhere"
      decision_rule: "Resources abundant = breadth; Starting out = depth"

    - agent: voice-guardian
      role: "Ensure authentic personal voice in all content"
      principles:
        how_i_not_how_to:
          good: "How I do X"
          bad: "How you should do X"
          rationale: "When you speak from experience, no one can question you"
        personal_differentiation:
          rule: "Only one of you exists"
          application: "Say things only you can say"
        repetition_permission:
          insight: "1 in 5 audience members don't know about your book despite daily posts"
          rule: "You'll be bored before your audience sees it all"

# ===============================================================================
# AGENT DEFINITIONS
# ===============================================================================

agents:
  content-coordinator:
    id: content-coordinator
    title: "Content Creation Orchestrator"
    tier: orchestrator
    icon: "🎬"

    purpose: |
      Coordinate the Content Creation pipeline to maximize audience growth.
      Ensure consistent output of content units that hook, retain, and reward.

    core_frameworks:
      - name: "Content Unit"
        components: ["Hook", "Retain", "Reward"]
      - name: "Give:Ask Ratio"
        default: "Give until they ask"
      - name: "Volume Principle"
        rule: "10x content = 10x growth"

    decision_authority:
      - "Content calendar prioritization"
      - "Platform strategy selection"
      - "Monetization timing"
      - "Quality standards"

    inputs:
      - "Topic bank from topic-miner"
      - "Performance data from audience-analyst"
      - "Content drafts from execution agents"
      - "Business goals and constraints"

    outputs:
      - "Weekly content plan"
      - "Platform priority rankings"
      - "Performance feedback to agents"
      - "Scaling recommendations"

    success_metrics:
      primary:
        - name: "Audience Growth Rate"
          target: ">30% monthly"
          calculation: "(New followers / Starting followers) x 100"
        - name: "Content Velocity"
          target: "Match platform maximums"
      secondary:
        - "Engagement rate by platform"
        - "Content-to-lead conversion"
        - "Share/repost rate"

  topic-miner:
    id: topic-miner
    title: "Topic Discovery Specialist"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "⛏️"

    purpose: |
      Extract valuable content topics from all five source categories.
      Build a topic bank that only YOU can speak about.

    topic_categories:
      distant_past:
        definition: "Important life lessons from your past"
        source: "Your experiences, mistakes, transformations"
        connection: "Link wisdom to product/service value"
        mantra: "Give them the story without the scar"
        example:
          hook: "I complained to a friend about not having enough time while glued to my phone"
          retain: "They grabbed it, checked screen time - 3 hours/day on social media"
          reward: "They said 'Hey, found some time for you'"

      recent_past:
        definition: "What you did or what happened recently"
        source: "Last week's calendar - meetings, conversations, interactions"
        connection: "Real-time lessons from real activities"
        gold_mines:
          - "Client conversations"
          - "Meetings with team"
          - "Social interactions"
          - "Testimonials and case studies"

      present:
        definition: "Ideas in the moment they come to you"
        source: "Real-time thoughts, observations, insights"
        practice: "Always have recording method within arm's reach"
        approach: "Pause meetings to note ideas - people don't mind"
        evolution: "Post ideas publicly; if performs well, create more on that topic"

      trends:
        definition: "What's trending now + your perspective"
        source: "Current events, viral topics, industry news"
        application: "Apply your experience to trending topics"
        benefit: "Effective for gaining wider audience attention"

      fabricated:
        definition: "Created experiences specifically for content"
        source: "Your imagination + willingness to execute"
        cost: "More time and effort"
        benefit: "Can have biggest returns"
        example: "I lived on $100 for a month. Here's how."

    data_collection:
      - "Weekly calendar review"
      - "Idea capture system always accessible"
      - "Trending topic monitoring"
      - "Client conversation notes"
      - "Personal reflection/journaling"

    outputs:
      - "Topic bank with category tags"
      - "Differentiation score (uniqueness)"
      - "Audience relevance score"
      - "Content type recommendations"

  audience-analyst:
    id: audience-analyst
    title: "Audience Growth Analyst"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "📊"

    purpose: |
      Track audience growth and content performance to inform strategy.
      "If audience isn't growing, content isn't good enough."

    primary_metrics:
      total_followers:
        description: "Audience size across platforms"
        measurement: "Sum of followers on all platforms"
        frequency: "Monthly"
        example: "1000 to 1500 = +500 growth"

      growth_rate:
        description: "Speed of audience growth"
        calculation: "(New followers / Starting followers) x 100"
        frequency: "Monthly"
        example: "500 new / 1000 start = 50% growth rate"

      total_reach:
        description: "People seeing content"
        measurement: "Platform-provided reach metrics"
        frequency: "Monthly"

      reach_growth_rate:
        description: "Speed of reach expansion"
        calculation: "(New reach / Starting reach) x 100"
        frequency: "Monthly"

    secondary_metrics:
      - "Engagement rate by platform"
      - "Share/repost rate (reward indicator)"
      - "Content-to-lead conversion"
      - "Top performing content types"
      - "Posting frequency vs growth correlation"

    philosophy: |
      "The more ways you measure, the more ways you can win."
      - Dr. Kashey (cited by Hormozi)

    reporting:
      - "Weekly performance summary"
      - "Monthly growth report"
      - "Content performance rankings"
      - "Platform comparison analysis"

  hook-crafter:
    id: hook-crafter
    title: "Hook Creation Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "🪝"

    purpose: |
      Create hooks that capture attention and give reasons to consume.
      "Hook effectiveness = percentage of people who start consuming."

    topic_framework:
      rule: "Use personal experience - only one of you exists"
      categories:
        - distant_past
        - recent_past
        - present
        - trends
        - fabricated

    headline_components:
      # From meta-analysis of news
      recency:
        description: "Most recent possible"
        example: "What happened an hour ago > what happened a year ago"

      relevance:
        description: "Personally significant to audience"
        example: "Nurses pay more attention to nurse-related content"

      celebrity:
        description: "Including prominent people"
        example: "We don't care what random person eats for breakfast. Jeff Bezos? We care."

      proximity:
        description: "Close to home geographically"
        example: "House fire across the country? Meh. Your neighbor's house? Attention."

      conflict:
        description: "Opposing ideas, people, nature"
        examples:
          - "Pineapple on pizza - yes or no?"
          - "Good vs Evil"
          - "Freedom vs Security"

      unusual:
        description: "Strange, unique, rare, bizarre"
        example: "Six-fingered man in old circuses - outside the norm = attention"

      ongoing:
        description: "Stories still in progress"
        example: "Someone in labor - people want updates every 10 minutes"

    headline_rule: "Include at least TWO components for strong headline"

    format_matching:
      rule: "Make content look like what they expect will reward them"
      process:
        - "Identify target platform"
        - "Study top-performing content in your niche"
        - "Note visual style, length, structure"
        - "Adapt your content to match"

  retention-architect:
    id: retention-architect
    title: "Content Retention Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "🏗️"

    purpose: |
      Structure content to maintain curiosity and keep audience engaged.
      "My favorite retention engine is curiosity."

    retention_structures:
      lists:
        definition: "Things, facts, tips, opinions presented one after another"
        rule: "Give number in headline or first seconds"
        psychological_mechanism: "Embedded questions - they want to know all items"
        examples:
          - "7 Ways I Invested $1000 in My 20s That Paid Off"
          - "28 Ways to Stay Poor"
        characteristics:
          flexibility: "High"
          reward_explicitness: "Low"

      steps:
        definition: "Actions in order that achieve an outcome"
        rule: "Clear, valuable first steps make them want all steps"
        psychological_mechanism: "Promise of achievable outcome"
        examples:
          - "3 Steps to Create a Great Hook"
          - "How I Create a Headline in 7 Steps"
          - "The Morning Routine That Increases My Productivity"
        characteristics:
          flexibility: "Low (order matters)"
          reward_explicitness: "High"

      stories:
        definition: "Events (real or imagined) with lessons"
        rule: "Worth-telling stories have lesson or conclusion"
        psychological_mechanism: "People want to know what happens next"
        examples:
          - "My editor made me do 19 drafts of this book - here's what I did with him"
          - "My journey from sleeping under a gym to a 5-star hotel"
        types: ["Things that happened", "Things that could happen", "Things that will never happen"]

    interweaving:
      description: "Combine structures for complex content"
      examples:
        - "Lists within steps with a story for each item"
        - "Stories to reinforce value of a step"
        - "A list of stories"
        - "Multiple ongoing storylines"
      limit: "Your creativity is the only limit"

    short_vs_long:
      insight: "Not much difference"
      explanation: "Short = hook-retain-reward few times. Long = hook-retain-reward many times"
      skill_progression: "Longer content = more skill (chaining more 'good' units)"
      advice: "Start small, build from there"

  reward-validator:
    id: reward-validator
    title: "Content Reward Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "🎁"

    purpose: |
      Ensure content delivers value and fulfills promises made in hooks.
      "The audience decides if content is good, not you."

    core_principles:
      value_per_second:
        concept: "How often content rewards during consumption"
        insight: "Same person bored 3 seconds into 10-sec video can marathon 900-page book"
        rule: "No such thing as too long, only too boring"

      promise_fulfillment:
        concept: "Clearly satisfy the reason that hooked them"
        rule: "Answer all unresolved questions you embedded in their minds"

      expectation_exceeding:
        concept: "Give more than they expected"
        result: "They share, come back, trust more"

    failure_patterns:
      quantity_fail:
        example: "Promised 7 ways, gave 4"
        result: "Betrayed trust"

      quality_fail:
        example: "Gave 7 ways but they were bad or already known"
        result: "Wasted their time"

      audience_fail:
        example: "Reconciliation advice to room of single people"
        result: "Wrong audience for content"

      usability_fail:
        example: "Marketing strategies dentists 'can use' but actually can't"
        result: "Broke promise of utility"

    success_validation:
      metric: "Audience growth"
      interpretation:
        growing: "Content is rewarding audience"
        stagnant: "Content needs improvement"
        shrinking: "Content is actively bad"
      advice: "Practice and you'll improve"

  format-adapter:
    id: format-adapter
    title: "Multi-Platform Format Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "🔄"

    purpose: |
      Adapt content for different platforms while maintaining quality.
      "Format for platform first, then adjust for your ideal audience."

    adaptation_principles:
      platform_first:
        rule: "Match what succeeds on each platform"
        research: "Study top content in your niche on each platform"

      audience_second:
        rule: "Adjust for your specific audience within platform norms"

      quality_maintained:
        rule: "Repurposing ≠ quality reduction"
        warning: "Many end up with bad content everywhere"

    repurposing_strategies:
      long_to_short:
        source: "Podcast, video, blog post"
        outputs:
          - "Short clips"
          - "Quote graphics"
          - "Tweet threads"
          - "Stories/Reels"

      cross_platform:
        source: "One piece of content"
        outputs:
          - "Same video, different format per platform"
          - "Same message, platform-native presentation"

    efficiency_principle: |
      "With a little extra work, you can capture tons of efficiency.
      With minimal format changes, same content fits multiple platforms."

  monetization-strategist:
    id: monetization-strategist
    title: "Audience Monetization Specialist"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "💰"

    purpose: |
      Plan and execute monetization without killing audience growth.
      "The moment you start asking for money is the moment you decide to slow growth."

    core_philosophy:
      hormozi_method: "Give until they ask"
      psychology: "Makes people uncomfortable to keep receiving without giving back"
      benefit: "Gets the best customers - the givers"

    give_ask_ratios:
      mature_platforms:
        television: "47min give : 13min ask (3.5:1)"
        facebook: "4 content posts : 1 ad"
        interpretation: "Minimum sustainable ratio"

      growth_platforms:
        pattern: "Give give give... give give give... maybe ask"
        interpretation: "Dramatically over-give, under-ask"

      recommended:
        strategy: "Give in public, ask in private"
        practice: "Let audience self-select when ready to buy"

    integration_methods:
      integrated:
        description: "Announce in every piece while keeping ratio high"
        placement: "After valuable moments or at content end"
        example: "3x 30-sec ads in 60min podcast = 58.5min give : 1.5min ask"
        platform_fit: "Long-form content"
        warning: "Friend's podcast shrank from over-asking"

      intermittent:
        description: "Many pure give pieces, occasional ask piece"
        pattern: "10 give posts → 1 ask post"
        platform_fit: "Short-form platforms"

    offer_types:
      lead_magnet:
        description: "Free value in exchange for contact info"
        risk: "Low"
        example: '"I have 11 more tips that helped me do this. Go to my site for a nice visual."'
        next_step: "Thank you page shows paid offer"

      main_offer:
        description: "Direct pitch of paid offering"
        risk: "Higher"
        template: |
          "I'm looking for 5 [specific avatar] to help achieve
          [dream result] in [time delay]. Best part: you don't need
          [effort/sacrifice]. If you don't get [dream result], I'll:
          1) Refund your money
          2) Work with you until you do.
          If that sounds fair, DM/schedule/comment/reply..."

    monetization_timing:
      patience_benefit: "The longer you wait, the more you get when you ask"
      growth_tradeoff: "Every ask slows growth"
      decision: "Business needs vs growth potential"

  scaling-strategist:
    id: scaling-strategist
    title: "Platform Scaling Specialist"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "📈"

    purpose: |
      Plan and execute platform expansion for maximum audience growth.
      "The best day to start posting was the day you were born. Second best is today."

    depth_first_strategy:
      name: "Depth before Breadth"
      description: "Maximize one platform, then add next"

      steps:
        - step: 1
          action: "Post on one relevant platform"
        - step: 2
          action: "Post regularly on that platform"
        - step: 3
          action: "Maximize quality AND quantity"
          targets:
            short_form: "Up to 10x per day"
            long_form: "5x per week (like soap operas)"
        - step: 4
          action: "Add another platform while maintaining first"
        - step: 5
          action: "Repeat until all platforms maximized"

      advantages:
        - "Leverage audience accumulation"
        - "Less resources needed"
        - "Deep platform expertise"

      disadvantages:
        - "Single channel risk (bans happen)"
        - "No omnipresence effect"
        - "Slower initial reach"

    breadth_first_strategy:
      name: "Breadth before Depth"
      description: "Enter all platforms early, maximize together"

      steps:
        - step: 1
          action: "Post on one relevant platform"
        - step: 2
          action: "Post regularly on that platform"
        - step: 3
          action: "Move to next platform (maintain previous)"
        - step: 4
          action: "Continue until on all relevant platforms"
        - step: 5
          action: "Maximize all platforms together"

      advantages:
        - "Wider reach faster"
        - "Content repurposing efficiency"
        - "Platform risk diversification"
        - "Omnipresence effect"

      disadvantages:
        - "More work, attention, time required"
        - "Risk of bad content everywhere"

    decision_criteria:
      depth_first_when:
        - "Just starting out"
        - "Limited resources"
        - "Learning content creation"

      breadth_first_when:
        - "Existing business with resources"
        - "Team to support production"
        - "Proven content formula"

    volume_principle:
      insight: "10x more content = 10x faster growth"
      source: "Influencer mentor to Hormozi"
      hormozi_result: "12 months = 200K audience. Next 6 months with 10x content = 1.2M audience"

  voice-guardian:
    id: voice-guardian
    title: "Authentic Voice Specialist"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "🎤"

    purpose: |
      Ensure all content maintains authentic personal voice.
      "The easiest way to differentiate is to say something no one else can say."

    core_principles:
      how_i_vs_how_to:
        wrong: "How you should do X"
        right: "How I do X"
        wrong: "This is the best way"
        right: "These are my favorite ways"
        rationale: "When you speak from experience, no one can question you"
        examples:
          good:
            - "I make my oatmeal this way"
            - "How I Built My 7-Figure Agency"
            - "My favorite way to generate leads"
          bad:
            - "You should make your oatmeal this way"
            - "How to Build a 7-Figure Agency"
            - "This is the best way to generate leads"

      differentiation:
        rule: "Only one of you exists"
        application: "Say things only you can say"
        source: "Your unique experiences"

      repetition_permission:
        myth: "Audience has seen everything"
        reality: "1 in 5 didn't know about Hormozi's book despite daily posts"
        permission: "Keep repeating - you'll be bored before audience sees it all"

    seven_lessons:
      lesson_1:
        title: "How I vs How To"
        application: "Share experience, not prescription"

      lesson_2:
        title: "Reminded vs Taught"
        application: "Repeat yourself constantly"

      lesson_3:
        title: "Puddles to Oceans"
        application: "Start narrow, expand over time"
        progression: "King of puddle → pond → lake → ocean"

      lesson_4:
        title: "Content Creates Sales Tools"
        application: "Greatest hits list for sales team"

      lesson_5:
        title: "Free Content Retains Paid Customers"
        application: "Customers include free content in ROI calculation"

      lesson_6:
        title: "Higher Standards, Not Shorter Attention"
        application: "No too long, only too boring"

      lesson_7:
        title: "Avoid Pre-Scheduling"
        application: "Manual posting creates pressure for quality"

# ===============================================================================
# EXECUTOR MATRIX
# ===============================================================================

executor_matrix:
  # Phase I: Hook
  - task: "Mine topics from calendar/meetings"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Review past week's interactions"

  - task: "Capture real-time ideas"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Always have recording method accessible"

  - task: "Monitor trending topics"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Filter for relevance to expertise"

  - task: "Research fabricated experience topics"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Assess effort vs potential return"

  - task: "Morpheus headline with 2+ components"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Must include recency, relevance, celebrity, proximity, conflict, unusual, or ongoing"

  - task: "Format content for platform"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Match top-performing content style"

  # Phase II: Retain
  - task: "Structure content as list"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "State number in headline or first seconds"

  - task: "Structure content as steps"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Ensure order matters and outcome is clear"

  - task: "Morpheus story arc"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must have lesson or conclusion"

  - task: "Interweave retention structures"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Creativity required"

  # Phase III: Reward
  - task: "Validate value per second"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Cut or improve boring sections"

  - task: "Verify promise fulfillment"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Hook promise = content delivery"

  - task: "Track audience growth metrics"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Monthly total + growth rate"

  # Phase IV: Monetization
  - task: "Calculate give:ask ratio"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Minimum 3.5:1, prefer give-until-they-ask"

  - task: "Place integrated offers"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "After valuable moments or at end"

  - task: "Schedule intermittent offers"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "10 give : 1 ask pattern"

  - task: "Morpheus lead magnet offer"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Relevant to content topic"

  - task: "Morpheus main offer pitch"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Use proven template"

  # Phase V: Scaling
  - task: "Analyze platform performance"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Compare growth rates"

  - task: "Decide depth vs breadth strategy"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Based on resources and goals"

  - task: "Repurpose content for new platform"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Maintain quality, match format"

  - task: "Increase posting frequency"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Track quality vs quantity tradeoff"

  # Voice & Quality
  - task: "Review for 'how I' vs 'how to' language"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Experience, not prescription"

  - task: "Check for authentic differentiation"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Only you can say this"

  - task: "Manual post publishing"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Avoid pre-scheduling when possible"

# ===============================================================================
# QUALITY GATES
# ===============================================================================

quality_gates:
  QG-001:
    name: "Hook Strength Gate"
    transition: "Topic → Published Content"
    condition: "headline_components >= 2"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Add more headline components"

  QG-002:
    name: "Retention Structure Gate"
    transition: "Draft → Final Content"
    condition: "has_list OR has_steps OR has_story"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Restructure with curiosity elements"

  QG-003:
    name: "Promise Fulfillment Gate"
    transition: "Content Complete → Publish"
    condition: "hook_promise == content_delivery"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Revise to fulfill promise"

  QG-004:
    name: "Platform Format Gate"
    transition: "Content → Platform"
    condition: "format_matches_platform_norms"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Reformat for platform"

  QG-005:
    name: "Give:Ask Ratio Gate"
    transition: "Monetization Planning"
    condition: "give_ask_ratio >= 3.5"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Add more give content before ask"

  QG-006:
    name: "Audience Growth Gate"
    transition: "Monthly Review"
    condition: "growth_rate > 0"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Content quality review - 'If not growing, content not good enough'"

  QG-007:
    name: "Voice Authenticity Gate"
    transition: "Draft → Publish"
    condition: "uses_how_i_not_how_to"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Rewrite from experience perspective"

# ===============================================================================
# WORKFLOWS
# ===============================================================================

workflows:
  content_unit_creation:
    trigger: "Content creation needed"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: topic-miner
        action: "Select topic from five categories"
        output: "Topic with category tag"

      - step: 2
        agent: hook-crafter
        action: "Create headline with 2+ components"
        output: "Attention-grabbing headline"

      - step: 3
        agent: hook-crafter
        action: "Match format to platform"
        output: "Platform-appropriate format spec"

      - step: 4
        agent: retention-architect
        action: "Structure with lists/steps/stories"
        output: "Retention-optimized structure"

      - step: 5
        agent: reward-validator
        action: "Validate value delivery"
        output: "Quality-checked content"

      - step: 6
        agent: voice-guardian
        action: "Review for authentic voice"
        output: "Voice-validated content"

      - step: 7
        agent: format-adapter
        action: "Final platform formatting"
        output: "Publish-ready content"

      - step: 8
        agent: content-coordinator
        action: "Approve and schedule/publish"
        output: "Published content"

  monetization_planning:
    trigger: "Ready to monetize audience"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: audience-analyst
        action: "Assess audience size and engagement"
        output: "Audience readiness report"

      - step: 2
        agent: monetization-strategist
        action: "Calculate current give:ask ratio"
        output: "Ratio assessment"

      - step: 3
        agent: monetization-strategist
        action: "Choose integration method (integrated vs intermittent)"
        output: "Monetization method"

      - step: 4
        agent: monetization-strategist
        action: "Select offer type (lead magnet vs main offer)"
        output: "Offer selection"

      - step: 5
        agent: hook-crafter
        action: "Morpheus offer messaging"
        output: "Offer script/copy"

      - step: 6
        agent: content-coordinator
        action: "Integrate into content calendar"
        output: "Monetized content plan"

  platform_expansion:
    trigger: "Ready to add new platform"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: audience-analyst
        action: "Assess current platform performance"
        output: "Platform health report"

      - step: 2
        agent: scaling-strategist
        action: "Recommend depth vs breadth approach"
        output: "Scaling recommendation"

      - step: 3
        agent: scaling-strategist
        action: "Identify next platform"
        output: "Platform selection"

      - step: 4
        agent: format-adapter
        action: "Research new platform norms"
        output: "Platform format guide"

      - step: 5
        agent: format-adapter
        action: "Adapt existing content for new platform"
        output: "Platform-ready content"

      - step: 6
        agent: content-coordinator
        action: "Update content calendar for multi-platform"
        output: "Expanded content plan"

  performance_review:
    trigger: "Monthly review cycle"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: audience-analyst
        action: "Calculate total followers and growth rate"
        output: "Growth metrics"

      - step: 2
        agent: audience-analyst
        action: "Identify top performing content"
        output: "Top content analysis"

      - step: 3
        agent: audience-analyst
        action: "Identify underperforming content"
        output: "Content improvement opportunities"

      - step: 4
        agent: content-coordinator
        action: "Adjust content strategy"
        output: "Updated content priorities"

      - step: 5
        agent: scaling-strategist
        action: "Recommend volume changes"
        output: "Volume recommendations"

# ===============================================================================
# KPIs & SUCCESS METRICS
# ===============================================================================

kpis:
  primary:
    audience_size:
      formula: "Total followers across platforms"
      target: "Continuous growth"
      measurement: "Monthly snapshot"

    audience_growth_rate:
      formula: "(New followers / Starting followers) x 100"
      target: ">30% monthly"
      benchmarks:
        starting: ">10%"
        building: ">30%"
        scaling: ">50%"

    content_velocity:
      formula: "Content units published per day"
      targets:
        short_form: "Up to 10x/day"
        long_form: "5x/week"
        minimum: "1x/day"

  secondary:
    reach_growth:
      formula: "(New reach / Starting reach) x 100"
      target: "Match or exceed follower growth"

    engagement_rate:
      formula: "Engagements / Reach"
      target: "Platform-dependent"

    share_rate:
      formula: "Shares / Views"
      target: "Increasing over time"
      significance: "Indicates reward quality"

    content_to_lead_conversion:
      formula: "Leads / Content views"
      target: "Track and improve"

  by_phase:
    hook:
      - "Click-through rate on headlines"
      - "Initial view/impression count"
      - "Stop rate (for video)"

    retain:
      - "Watch time / read time"
      - "Completion rate"
      - "Drop-off points"

    reward:
      - "Share/repost rate"
      - "Save/bookmark rate"
      - "Comment sentiment"
      - "Follower conversion"

    monetize:
      - "Click rate on offers"
      - "Lead magnet opt-in rate"
      - "Direct sales from content"

# ===============================================================================
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ===============================================================================

troubleshooting:
  - symptom: "Audience not growing"
    possible_causes:
      - "Content not rewarding enough"
      - "Hooks not strong enough"
      - "Not enough volume"
      - "Wrong platform"
    diagnosis:
      - "Review share rate (reward indicator)"
      - "Check headline components used"
      - "Compare posting frequency to benchmarks"
      - "Analyze platform-specific metrics"
    solutions:
      - "Improve value per second"
      - "Add more headline components"
      - "Increase posting frequency"
      - "Test different platforms"
    hormozi_quote: "If it's not growing, your stuff isn't that good. Practice and you'll improve."

  - symptom: "High views but low engagement"
    possible_causes:
      - "Hook strong but content doesn't deliver"
      - "Promise not fulfilled"
      - "Retention weak"
    diagnosis:
      - "Compare hook promise to content"
      - "Check retention metrics (completion rate)"
      - "Review content structure"
    solutions:
      - "Ensure content delivers on headline promise"
      - "Add lists, steps, or stories for retention"
      - "Cut boring sections"

  - symptom: "Audience growing but no leads"
    possible_causes:
      - "No offer integration"
      - "Give:ask ratio too high (never asking)"
      - "Offer not compelling"
    diagnosis:
      - "Check offer frequency"
      - "Review offer messaging"
      - "Analyze offer click-through"
    solutions:
      - "Add occasional offers"
      - "Test lead magnet vs main offer"
      - "Improve offer copy"

  - symptom: "Audience shrinking after monetization"
    possible_causes:
      - "Give:ask ratio too low"
      - "Asking too frequently"
      - "Offers not matching audience needs"
    diagnosis:
      - "Calculate actual give:ask ratio"
      - "Compare to pre-monetization growth"
    solutions:
      - "Reduce ask frequency"
      - "Improve give quality"
      - "Return to 'give until they ask' approach"

  - symptom: "Content creation burnout"
    possible_causes:
      - "Unsustainable posting schedule"
      - "Not using all topic categories"
      - "Not repurposing content"
    diagnosis:
      - "Review content calendar sustainability"
      - "Check topic source diversity"
      - "Assess repurposing usage"
    solutions:
      - "Use all five topic categories"
      - "Implement repurposing workflow"
      - "Build team/delegate"
      - "Batch content creation"

# ===============================================================================
# TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENTS
# ===============================================================================

technology:
  required:
    - tool: "Note-Taking System"
      purpose: "Capture ideas in the moment"
      requirements:
        - "Always accessible (phone/watch)"
        - "Quick capture capability"
```

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/core-four-sop.md

# Core Four Lead Acquisition SOP

> **Source:** $100M Leads - Alex Hormozi (Sections II-III)
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

The Core Four are the **only four ways** a single person can advertise - let other people know about the things they sell. Master any one of these methods and you will never starve. Master all four and you build a $100M lead machine.

**Core Equation:**
```
Advertising = Making Known
Leads = People You Can Contact
Engaged Leads = People Who Show Interest In Your Stuff

More Advertising → More Engaged Leads → More Customers → More Money
```

**The Core Four Matrix:**

| | Warm (Know You) | Cold (Strangers) |
|---|-----------------|------------------|
| **1-to-1 (Private)** | #1 Warm Outreach | #3 Cold Outreach |
| **1-to-many (Public)** | #2 Post Free Content | #4 Run Paid Ads |

**Business Impact:** "If you're not getting as many leads as you want, you are not doing the core four with enough skill or enough volume."

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Starting a business from zero
- Launching new products or services
- Need more leads than you currently get
- Building predictable lead flow
- Scaling existing lead acquisition

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- Post-sale customer success (covered in delivery playbooks)
- Leveraging other people to do the core four (covered in Section IV: Lead Getters)
- Building offers and lead magnets (covered in $100M Offers and Section II)

### Business Types
- Every business that needs customers
- B2B and B2C
- Local and online
- High-ticket and low-ticket
- Product and service

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Lead Magnet OR Offer | Something valuable to promote | Passes Grand Slam Offer test |
| Contact List (Warm) | Phone, email, social contacts | List exported and counted |
| Communication Channels | Phone, email, social media accounts | All channels operational |
| Tracking System | Way to measure leads and results | CRM or spreadsheet ready |
| Time OR Money | Resource to trade for leads | Budget/hours allocated |
| Value Proposition | Clear articulation of benefit | Can state in <30 seconds |

---

## Part 4: The Core Four Framework

### Framework Overview

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                           THE CORE FOUR MATRIX                                  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                         WARM AUDIENCE        COLD AUDIENCE                      │
│                        (Know You)            (Strangers)                        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1-to-1 (Private)    │ #1 WARM OUTREACH     │ #3 COLD OUTREACH                 │
│                      │ • Calls              │ • Cold calls                     │
│                      │ • Texts              │ • Cold emails                    │
│                      │ • DMs                │ • Cold DMs                       │
│                      │ • Emails             │ • Flyers/mailers                 │
│                      │ COST: Time           │ COST: Time + Automation          │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1-to-many (Public)  │ #2 POST CONTENT      │ #4 PAID ADS                      │
│                      │ • Videos             │ • Social ads                     │
│                      │ • Podcasts           │ • Search ads                     │
│                      │ • Articles           │ • Display ads                    │
│                      │ • Social posts       │ • Direct mail                    │
│                      │ COST: Time           │ COST: Money                      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### When To Use Each Method

| Situation | Recommended Method | Rationale |
|-----------|-------------------|-----------|
| Just starting, no money | Warm Outreach | Free, reliable, immediate |
| More time than money | Warm Outreach → Post Content | Time-based methods |
| More money than time | Cold Outreach → Paid Ads | Scale faster with money |
| Want compound growth | Post Content | Audience grows over time |
| Need immediate leads | Warm Outreach + Paid Ads | Fastest results |
| Already doing one well | Add another Core Four | Compound effects |

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### #1 WARM OUTREACH

#### Purpose
Reach out one-on-one to people who already know you. The cheapest and easiest way to find people interested in what you sell.

#### Why It Works
- High trust (they know you)
- No cost (just time)
- Reliable (works every time)
- 20% response rate typical
- Can build $100k+ business with this alone

#### Step 1.1: Build Your List
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Export contacts from ALL sources: phone, email, social media |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception (data gathering) |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Export tools available |
| **Executor** | Human (initial) → Worker (automation) |
| **Precondition** | Access to all contact platforms |
| **Output** | Master contact list with count |
| **Guardrails** | Include ALL contacts - don't pre-judge |
| **Decision Rule** | "Everyone knows someone. Your contacts are your first 1000 leads." |

**Sources to Export:**
- Phone contacts
- All email accounts (personal, work, old)
- Facebook friends
- Instagram followers
- LinkedIn connections
- Twitter/X followers
- Any other social platform
- Old Christmas card lists
- Business cards collected

#### Step 1.2: Choose a Platform
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Start with platform where you have most contacts |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Contact list counted by platform |
| **Output** | Priority platform selected |
| **Guardrails** | Will hit all platforms eventually |
| **Decision Rule** | "Start with most contacts, then move to second most, and so on" |

#### Step 1.3: Personalize Your Message
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Use something you know about the contact as reason to reach out |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Perception |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Must feel personal |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Contact info available |
| **Output** | Personalized opening message |
| **Guardrails** | Check social profiles for recent life events |
| **Decision Rule** | "Don't be weird. Pay your social dues." |

**Example Personalization:**
```
"I saw you just had a baby! Congratulations! How's the baby? How are you?"
```

#### Step 1.4: Reach Out - 100 Per Day
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Contact 100 people per day with personalized messages |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Personal touch required |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Messages personalized |
| **Output** | 100 outreaches completed |
| **Guardrails** | Three attempts per contact max (1/day for 3 days) |
| **Decision Rule** | "To get what you want, you have to deserve what you want." - Charlie Munger |

**Rule of 100:**
- Warm Outreach: 100 reach outs per day
- Do this for 100 days straight
- "Commit to the rule of 100 and you'll never go hungry again"

#### Step 1.5: Warm Them Up (A-C-A Framework)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | When they respond, build rapport using Acknowledge-Compliment-Ask |
| **Cognitive Type** | Social Intelligence |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Contact responded |
| **Output** | Rapport established, conversation guided |
| **Guardrails** | 3-4 exchanges before making offer |
| **Decision Rule** | "People love talking about themselves. Let them." |

**A-C-A Framework:**
- **A**cknowledge: Rephrase what they said in your own words (shows listening)
- **C**ompliment: Tie to a positive character trait
- **A**sk: Guide conversation toward your offer topic

**Example:**
```
"Two kids and you're an accountant... Wow! Supermom! So hardworking!
Managing a full-time career and two kids... Do you have time for yourself?"
```

#### Step 1.6: Invite Their Friends
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Ask if they know anyone who needs help (not if THEY need help) |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment + Negotiation |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Rapport established |
| **Output** | Referral or self-identification |
| **Guardrails** | Don't ask them to buy - ask who they know |
| **Decision Rule** | "When you ask about someone else, they often identify themselves" |

**The Ask Script (Value Equation):**
```
"By the way, do you know anyone who is (describe their struggles)
looking for (dream outcome) in (time delay)?

I'm taking on five case studies for free because it's all I can
handle. I just want to get some testimonials for my service/product.

I help them (dream outcome) without (effort and sacrifice). It works.
I even guarantee people get (dream outcome) or I work with them until
they do.

I just had a girl named XXX work with me who (dream outcome) even
though she (describe the same struggle your contact has). I also
had another guy who (dream outcome) and it was his first time.

I'd just like more testimonials to show it works in different
scenarios. Does anyone you like come to mind?

...and if they say no... Haha, well... does anyone you hate come
to mind? (ha)"
```

#### Step 1.7: Make the Easiest Offer - FREE
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | First five clients should be free to build testimonials |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | N/A |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Someone shows interest |
| **Output** | Free client enrolled |
| **Guardrails** | Get commitments: use it, give feedback, leave review |
| **Decision Rule** | "Free clients make you money three ways: convert to paid, send referrals, give testimonials" |

**Free Client Script:**
```
"As I'm taking only five people, I can give all the attention you need
to get brag-worthy results. And I'll give everything for free, as long
as you promise:

1) Use it
2) Give me feedback and
3) Leave a killer review if you think it deserves it.

Does that sound fair?"
```

**Why Free First Five Works:**
1. Get reps and become comfortable making offers
2. You're probably terrible at first - people are more tolerant when free
3. Learn and improve from real feedback
4. Get reviews and testimonials for future marketing

#### Step 1.8: Start Over From the Top
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | After exhausting one platform, move to the next largest |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Current platform exhausted |
| **Output** | Next platform started |
| **Guardrails** | Track which contacts on which platform |
| **Decision Rule** | "1000 leads = 10 solid days of work = minimum 5 free clients" |

#### Step 1.9: Start Charging
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | When people start referring, start charging |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | N/A |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Referrals begin coming |
| **Output** | Paid clients |
| **Guardrails** | Increase price by 20% every five clients |
| **Decision Rule** | "Litmus test: Once people start referring, start charging" |

**Price Escalation:**
- First 5: Free
- Next 5: 80% off
- Next 5: 60% off
- Next 5: 40% off
- Next 5: 20% off
- Then: Full price
- Continue: Raise 20% every 5 until you find sweet spot

#### Step 1.10: Keep Your List Warm
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Give regular value to your list to keep them warm for future outreach |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Initial outreach complete |
| **Output** | Warm list maintained |
| **Guardrails** | Use "9-word email" to probe for interest |
| **Decision Rule** | "A warm list is a valuable asset - treat them well" |

**Dean Jackson's 9-Word Email:**
```
"Are you still looking for [4-word desire]?"

Examples:
- Are you still looking for... to buy your dream home?
- Are you still looking for... to get more sales leads?
- Are you still looking for... to tone your arms?
- Are you still looking for... to open an online store?
```

No images. No frills. No links. Just a question.

---

### #2 POST FREE CONTENT

#### Purpose
Say it once and reach everyone. Build a growing warm audience that compounds over time.

#### Why It Works
- One effort reaches many people
- Audience grows over time (compounds)
- Makes all other advertising more effective
- Free (just time)
- Shared content = free distribution

#### Key Insight
"What I didn't understand was - the content you create is not the asset that compounds - the audience is. So even though content may disappear over time, your audience keeps growing."

#### Step 2.1: Understand the Unit of Content
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Every piece of content must Hook, Retain, and Reward |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Topic selected |
| **Output** | Content unit created |
| **Guardrails** | Must satisfy the reason they started consuming |
| **Decision Rule** | "There's no such thing as too long, only too boring" |

**The Unit of Content:**
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              THE UNIT OF CONTENT                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. HOOK      → Give them reason to notice          │
│                  (What % start consuming?)          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  2. RETAIN    → Keep them consuming                 │
│                  (What % keep going?)               │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  3. REWARD    → Satisfy the reason they started     │
│                  (Did they get what was promised?)  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Step 2.2: Create Great Hooks
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Choose topics, craft headlines, match format to platform |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Understand platform norms |
| **Output** | Attention-grabbing hook |
| **Guardrails** | Include 2+ headline elements |
| **Decision Rule** | "80 cents of your advertising dollar is in the headline" - David Ogilvy |

**Topic Sources (5 Categories):**
1. **Distant Past:** Important life lessons
2. **Recent Past:** Things you did/happened recently
3. **Present:** Ideas as they come to you
4. **Trends:** What's trending now
5. **Manufactured:** Create an experience, then share it

**Headline Elements (Include 2+):**
- **Recency:** As recent as possible
- **Relevance:** Personally significant to audience
- **Celebrity:** Includes prominent people
- **Proximity:** Close to home (geographically)
- **Conflict:** Opposing ideas or people
- **Unusual:** Weird, unique, rare, bizarre
- **Ongoing:** Stories still in progress

**Format Rule:** Match what performs well on the specific platform

#### Step 2.3: Retain With Curiosity
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Use lists, steps, and stories to embed unanswered questions |
| **Cognitive Type** | Structure |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Hook created |
| **Output** | Structured content that retains |
| **Guardrails** | Use cliffhangers and loops |
| **Decision Rule** | "People want to know what happens... next" |

**Three Retention Engines:**
1. **Lists:** Items presented one after another with a theme
   - "7 Ways I Invested $1000 That Paid Off"
   - "28 Ways to Go Broke"

2. **Steps:** Actions that occur in order to achieve a goal
   - "3 Steps to Create a Great Hook"
   - "The Morning Routine That Doubled My Productivity"

3. **Stories:** Events (real or imagined) with lessons/conclusions
   - "My journey from sleeping under a gym to a 5-star penthouse"

#### Step 2.4: Reward Completely
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Fully satisfy the promise made in the hook |
| **Cognitive Type** | Quality Control |
| **Automation Potential** | N/A |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Content retained audience |
| **Output** | Satisfied audience who shares |
| **Guardrails** | If they don't share, it wasn't good enough |
| **Decision Rule** | "The audience decides. If audience grows, you're doing well." |

**Test Questions:**
- Did you deliver on the hook's promise?
- Would someone share this?
- Would someone want more?

#### Step 2.5: Master the Give:Ask Ratio
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Give far more than you ask; let them ask first |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | N/A |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Creating regular content |
| **Output** | Growing audience with high trust |
| **Guardrails** | Minimum 3:1 give:ask ratio; ideally "give until they ask" |
| **Decision Rule** | "The moment you start asking for money is the moment you decide to slow your growth" |

**Ratio Benchmarks:**
- Mature platforms (TV, Facebook): ~4:1 give:ask (monetizing)
- Growing platforms: Much higher give ratio
- Recommended strategy: "Give give give... give give give... maybe ask"
- Best strategy: "Give until they ask"

#### Step 2.6: Make CTAs When Needed
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | If you must ask, use integrated or intermittent CTAs |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Enough goodwill deposited |
| **Output** | Leads generated without killing growth |
| **Guardrails** | Don't kill your golden goose |
| **Decision Rule** | "Give in public, ask in private" |

**Two CTA Strategies:**
1. **Integrated:** Brief ads within content (like podcast spots)
   - Keep ratio high (58 min value : 2 min ask)
   - Place after valuable moments or at end

2. **Intermittent:** Mostly pure give content, occasional ask content
   - 10 posts of give, 1 post of ask
   - Better for short-form platforms

#### Step 2.7: Scale Production
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Choose depth-first or breadth-first scaling approach |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Human → Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Consistent posting established |
| **Output** | Expanded reach |
| **Guardrails** | Don't sacrifice quality for quantity |
| **Decision Rule** | "The best day to start posting was the day you were born. The second best day is today." |

**Depth-First (Recommended for starters):**
1. Post on one platform
2. Post regularly
3. Maximize quality AND quantity on that platform
4. Add another platform while maintaining first
5. Repeat until all platforms maximized

**Breadth-First (For established businesses):**
1. Post on one platform
2. Post regularly
3. Add another platform (before maximizing first)
4. Continue until on all platforms
5. Then maximize all at once

---

### #3 COLD OUTREACH

#### Purpose
Reach out one-on-one to complete strangers. Scale warm outreach to people who don't know you yet.

#### Why It Works
- Unlimited pool of prospects
- Can be automated at scale
- Works while you sleep
- Lower response rate but higher volume compensates
- Combined with content = powerful

#### Key Differences From Warm Outreach
- Expect LOWER response rates (5-10% vs 20%)
- MUST use automation to scale
- Need stronger hooks (no existing relationship)
- Compliance/legal considerations
- Volume makes up for lower conversion

#### Step 3.1: Build Your Target List
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create lists of people who fit your ideal customer profile |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Research |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker → Human validation |
| **Precondition** | Ideal customer profile defined |
| **Output** | Targeted contact list |
| **Guardrails** | Quality > quantity; verify accuracy |
| **Decision Rule** | "The right list is more important than the perfect message" |

**List Building Methods:**
- Purchased lists
- Scraped data (LinkedIn, directories)
- Industry databases
- Conference attendee lists
- Association member lists
- Social media searches

#### Step 3.2: Morpheus Your Cold Message
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create message that earns attention from strangers |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW (template creation) → HIGH (sending) |
| **Executor** | Human (create) → Worker (send) |
| **Precondition** | Target list ready |
| **Output** | Message template |
| **Guardrails** | Test multiple variations; track responses |
| **Decision Rule** | "Lead with value, not with pitch" |

**Cold Message Elements:**
- Relevance: Why you're contacting THEM specifically
- Value: What's in it for them
- Credibility: Why they should believe you
- CTA: Clear, low-friction next step

#### Step 3.3: Execute 100 Per Day With Automation
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Use automation tools to reach 100+ strangers daily |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker (automation) + Human (responses) |
| **Precondition** | Message and list ready |
| **Output** | 100+ outreaches per day |
| **Guardrails** | Follow platform rules; don't get banned |
| **Decision Rule** | "Expect lower response rates; use automation to compensate" |

**Rule of 100 - Cold Version:**
- 100 cold reach outs per day
- Email, text, DM, cold call, flyers
- Automation is essential at this volume
- Track response rates obsessively

#### Step 3.4: Convert Responses
| Field | Value |

| **Cognitive Type** | Social Intelligence |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |

### #4 PAID ADS

#### Purpose
Trade money for leads at scale. The fastest way to scale lead acquisition.

#### Why It Works
- Unlimited scale (limited only by budget)
- Speed (immediate leads)
- Predictable (know your CAC)
- Skills from content transfer here
- Can test rapidly

#### Key Insight
"Paid ads are all about ROI. You put in X dollars and get Y dollars back. Good enough is good enough - you just need to make it profitable enough to scale."

#### Step 4.1: Set Up Tracking First
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Configure tracking before spending a single dollar |
| **Cognitive Type** | Technical Setup |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Ad platform access |
| **Output** | Complete tracking setup |
| **Guardrails** | Cannot optimize what you cannot measure |
| **Decision Rule** | "Phase 1 is Track Money. If you don't track, you'll get cleaned out." |

**Three Phases of Paid Ads:**
1. **Track Money:** Set up tracking before spending
2. **Lose Money:** Test and learn (expect to lose more than you win)
3. **Print Money:** Scale winners aggressively

#### Step 4.2: Create Your Ads
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Apply content principles to paid format |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW (creation) → HIGH (distribution) |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Tracking configured |
| **Output** | Multiple ad variations |
| **Guardrails** | Best free content often makes best paid ads |
| **Decision Rule** | "Test 10 ads expecting 9 to fail. Scale the 1 that wins." |

**Ad Creation Checklist:**
- [ ] Platform selected (where audience is)
- [ ] Audience defined (who sees it)
- [ ] Messaging ready (Hook + Retain + Reward)
- [ ] Call to action (what to do next)
- [ ] Budget set (what you're willing to lose)

#### Step 4.3: Budget Strategically
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Budget 2x your 30-day customer value per test |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Know customer value |
| **Output** | Testing budget set |
| **Guardrails** | If no leads at 1x 30-day value, turn off |
| **Decision Rule** | "2x 30-day profit to test; 1x 30-day profit cutoff if zero leads" |

**Budget Examples:**
- $100 profit in 30 days → Allow $200 per ad test
- Getting leads but losing? → Let it run to $200
- Zero leads? → Turn off at $100

#### Step 4.4: Measure LTGP:CAC
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Compare lifetime gross profit to customer acquisition cost |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Ads running, customers acquired |
| **Output** | LTGP:CAC ratio |
| **Guardrails** | Target >3:1; struggling companies usually <3:1 |
| **Decision Rule** | "If LTGP:CAC < 3:1, fix model or ads. If CAC > 3x industry average, fix ads. Otherwise, fix model." |

**LTGP (Lifetime Gross Profit):**
```
LTGP = Total Revenue from Customer - Total Cost to Deliver

Example:
- Customer pays $15/month
- Costs $5/month to deliver
- Gross profit = $10/month
- Customer stays 10 months
- LTGP = $100
```

#### Step 4.5: Achieve Customer-Financed Acquisition
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Structure offers so customers pay you back within 30 days |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | N/A |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Know your unit economics |
| **Output** | Breakeven in <30 days |
| **Guardrails** | Use upsells, cross-sells to accelerate payback |
| **Decision Rule** | "Cover CAC + delivery cost in first 30 days = infinite scale" |

**Customer-Financed Acquisition Example:**
```
Problem:
- CAC = $30
- First month profit = $10
- Breakeven = 3 months (cash flow problem)

Solution - Add Upsell:
- CAC = $30
- First month profit = $10
- Upsell ($100, 100% margin) accepted by 20% = $20 avg
- Total 30-day profit = $30
- Breakeven = Day 1 (unlimited scale)
```

#### Step 4.6: Scale Winners Aggressively
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | When ad is profitable, increase budget significantly |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Profitable ads identified |
| **Output** | Scaled ad spend |
| **Guardrails** | Add 20% to budget for efficiency loss at scale |
| **Decision Rule** | "If you had a machine that gave $10 for every $1, what would your budget be? All of it." |

**Scaling Budget Calculation:**
```
Budget = (Desired Customers × CAC) × 1.2

Example:
- Want 100 customers next month
- CAC = $100
- Base budget = $10,000
- Add 20% buffer = $12,000
- Daily budget = $400
```

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Method Selection
```yaml
rule: CORE_FOUR_SELECTION
trigger: Need more leads
condition:
  - IF more_time_than_money THEN start_with_warm_outreach()
  - IF more_money_than_time THEN start_with_cold_outreach_or_ads()
  - IF want_compound_growth THEN add_content()
  - IF already_doing_one_well THEN add_another_core_four()
action: Start with one, master it, then add more
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-002: Warm Outreach Volume
```yaml
rule: WARM_OUTREACH_VOLUME
trigger: Daily warm outreach execution
condition:
  - IF daily_outreach < 100 THEN "INCREASE VOLUME"
  - IF daily_outreach >= 100 THEN "MAINTAIN"
action: Reach 100 people per day for 100 days
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-003: Content Give:Ask Ratio
```yaml
rule: CONTENT_GIVE_ASK
trigger: Making CTAs in content
condition:
  - IF ratio < 3:1 THEN "SLOW DOWN ASKING"
  - IF ratio >= 4:1 THEN "SUSTAINABLE"
  - IF ratio == "give_until_they_ask" THEN "OPTIMAL GROWTH"
action: Default to giving; ask sparingly
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-004: Paid Ads Budget
```yaml
rule: AD_BUDGET_TESTING
trigger: Testing new ad
condition:
  - IF zero_leads AND spend >= 1x_30day_profit THEN turn_off()
  - IF getting_leads AND spend < 2x_30day_profit THEN continue_testing()
  - IF profitable THEN scale_10x()
action: Kill losers fast, scale winners hard
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-005: LTGP:CAC Health
```yaml
rule: LTGP_CAC_RATIO
trigger: Measuring ad efficiency
condition:
  - IF ratio < 3:1 THEN "WARNING - Fix model or ads"
  - IF ratio >= 3:1 THEN "SCALABLE"
  - IF cac > 3x_industry_average THEN "Fix ads first"
  - IF cac < 3x_industry_average THEN "Fix model first"
action: Diagnose root cause, then optimize
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-006: Charging Threshold
```yaml
rule: START_CHARGING
trigger: Deciding when to charge
condition:
  - IF referrals_starting == true THEN start_charging()
  - IF no_referrals == true THEN keep_giving_free()
action: Referrals = permission to charge
confidence: HIGH
```

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: No Contacts for Warm Outreach
**Trigger:** Claim to have zero contacts
**Response:** This is almost never true
**Actions:**
- Check ALL email accounts ever used
- Export phone contacts
- Review all social media platforms
- Look for old lists, business cards
**Minimum Expected:** 100-500 contacts minimum

### Exception 2: Can't Give Away Free
**Trigger:** People won't accept free offer
**Analysis:** Hidden costs are too high (time, effort, sacrifice)
**Response:** Ask "What would I have to do for it to be worth your while?"
**Lesson:** Use feedback to improve offer

### Exception 3: Ads Aren't Working
**Trigger:** Losing money on ads consistently
**Analysis:** Could be ads OR model
**Diagnostic:**
- If CAC > 3x industry average → Fix ads
- If CAC < 3x industry average → Fix model (LTGP too low)
**Key Insight:** "The cost to acquire customers is much closer between competitors than you'd think. The difference is how much they make from each customer."

### Exception 4: Content Isn't Growing Audience
**Trigger:** Posting but no growth
**Analysis:** Content not rewarding enough
**Response:**
- Review hook quality
- Check retention mechanics
- Ensure promise is being satisfied
- Look at what's working for others on platform
**Rule:** "If audience grows, you're doing well. If not, your stuff isn't that good yet."
