## Appendix B: More Better New Framework

### How to 10x Any Core Four Method

When you plateau with any method, apply this framework:

**1. MORE**
- Do more of what's already working
- Double your inputs → More outputs
- "Volume negates luck"

**2. BETTER**
- Test one thing per week per platform
- Focus on constraints (biggest drop-off points)
- Track results in a testing log

**3. NEW**
- New placements on same platform
- New platform with same approach
- New Core Four method entirely

**Priority Order:**
```
MORE (maximize volume)
→ BETTER (improve efficiency)
  → NEW PLACEMENTS (same platform, new spots)
    → NEW PLATFORMS (same method, new platform)
      → NEW CORE FOUR (add another method)
```

**Decision Point:** Only move to "new" when returns from "more" and "better" are lower than returns from "new"

        - "Lead magnet assets"
      outputs:
        - "Offer readiness score"
        - "Value equation assessment"
        - "Improvement recommendations"

  tier_1_execution:
    - agent: warm-outreach-engine
      role: "Execute systematic warm outreach to known contacts"
      specialization: "Core Four #1: Warm Outreach"
      targets:
        daily_outreach: "100 per day"
        duration: "100 days"
        response_rate: ">20%"
      techniques:
        - "A-C-A Framework (Acknowledge-Compliment-Ask)"
        - "Value Equation offer structure"
        - "9-word re-engagement emails"
        - "Price escalation strategy"

    - agent: content-engine
      role: "Create and distribute content that builds audience"
      specialization: "Core Four #2: Post Free Content"
      capabilities:
        - "Hook-Retain-Reward content creation"
        - "Platform format matching"
        - "Give:Ask ratio management"
        - "Depth-first or breadth-first scaling"
      content_unit:
        hook: "Topics, Headlines, Format"
        retain: "Lists, Steps, Stories"
        reward: "Satisfy the promise"

    - agent: cold-outreach-engine
      role: "Execute automated outreach to strangers at scale"
      specialization: "Core Four #3: Cold Outreach"
      targets:
        daily_outreach: "100+ per day (automated)"
        response_rate: ">5%"
      techniques:
        - "List building and verification"
        - "Message template optimization"
        - "Multi-channel automation"
        - "Response handling workflow"

    - agent: paid-ads-engine
      role: "Run profitable paid advertising campaigns"
      specialization: "Core Four #4: Paid Ads"
      phases:
        phase_1: "Track Money - Set up tracking"
        phase_2: "Lose Money - Test and learn"
        phase_3: "Print Money - Scale winners"
      metrics:
        - "LTGP:CAC ratio (target >3:1)"
        - "30-day payback"
        - "Cost per lead"
        - "Cost per customer"

  tier_2_judgment:
    - agent: method-optimizer
      role: "Apply More-Better-New framework to improve results"
      framework:
        more: "Increase volume of what's working"
        better: "Test one thing per week per platform"
        new: "New placements → New platforms → New Core Four"
      priorities:
        - "Exhaust MORE and BETTER before NEW"
        - "Focus on constraints (biggest drop-off points)"
        - "Track all tests in testing log"

    - agent: conversion-analyst
      role: "Analyze lead quality and conversion patterns"
      inputs:
        - "Lead source data"
        - "Conversion rates by method"
        - "Customer lifetime value"
        - "Response patterns"
      outputs:
        - "Method ROI comparison"
        - "Quality score by source"
        - "Optimization recommendations"

    - agent: scaling-strategist
      role: "Determine when and how to scale winning methods"
      decisions:
        - "When to add staff/automation"
        - "Budget allocation adjustments"
        - "Platform expansion timing"
        - "Method stacking strategy"

# ===============================================================================
# AGENT DEFINITIONS
# ===============================================================================

agents:
  core-four-coordinator:
    id: core-four-coordinator
    title: "Core Four Orchestrator"
    tier: orchestrator
    icon: "4"

    purpose: |
      Coordinate the four fundamental advertising methods to maximize lead generation.
      Ensure consistent execution while optimizing resource allocation.

    core_frameworks:
      - name: "Core Four Matrix"
        components: ["Warm Outreach", "Post Content", "Cold Outreach", "Paid Ads"]
      - name: "More Better New"
        sequence: ["More", "Better", "New Placements", "New Platforms", "New Core Four"]
      - name: "Rule of 100"
        commitment: "100 primary actions per day for 100 days"

    decision_authority:
      - "Method prioritization"
      - "Resource allocation"
      - "Scaling decisions"
      - "Testing cadence"

    inputs:
      - "Current lead metrics"
      - "Resource availability"
      - "Method performance data"
      - "Business goals"

    outputs:
      - "Method priority matrix"
      - "Resource allocation plan"
      - "Scaling recommendations"
      - "Optimization roadmap"

    success_metrics:
      primary:
        - name: "Total Engaged Leads"
          target: "Growing month-over-month"
        - name: "Lead Cost"
          target: "Decreasing over time"
      secondary:
        - "Method diversity (using 2+ methods)"
        - "Consistency (Rule of 100 adherence)"

  warm-outreach-engine:
    id: warm-outreach-engine
    title: "Warm Outreach Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "W"

    purpose: |
      Execute systematic outreach to people who already know you.
      The cheapest and most reliable way to get your first leads.

    core_mantra: |
      "To get what you want, you have to deserve what you want." - Charlie Munger

    process_steps:
      step_1:
        name: "Build Your List"
        action: "Export contacts from ALL sources"
        sources:
          - "Phone contacts"
          - "All email accounts"
          - "Facebook friends"
          - "Instagram followers"
          - "LinkedIn connections"
          - "Twitter/X followers"
          - "Any other platform"
        output: "Total contact count"

      step_2:
        name: "Choose Platform"
        action: "Start with most contacts, then move to next"
        rule: "Will hit all platforms eventually"

      step_3:
        name: "Personalize Messages"
        action: "Use something you know about them"
        technique: "Check social profiles for recent life events"
        example: "I saw you just had a baby! Congratulations!"

      step_4:
        name: "Execute 100/Day"
        action: "Reach 100 people per day"
        follow_up: "Three attempts max (1/day for 3 days)"
        duration: "100 days straight"

      step_5:
        name: "Warm Them Up"
        action: "Use A-C-A Framework when they respond"
        framework:
          acknowledge: "Rephrase what they said"
          compliment: "Tie to positive character trait"
          ask: "Guide toward your offer topic"
        exchanges: "3-4 before making offer"

      step_6:
        name: "Invite Friends"
        action: "Ask who they KNOW, not if THEY need help"
        psychology: "Most people identify themselves"

      step_7:
        name: "Make Free Offer"
        action: "First 5 clients are free"
        commitments:
          - "Use it"
          - "Give feedback"
          - "Leave killer review if deserved"

      step_8:
        name: "Start Over"
        action: "Move to next platform"
        cycle: "Continue until all exhausted"

      step_9:
        name: "Start Charging"
        trigger: "When referrals start coming"
        escalation: "80% off → 60% off → 40% off → 20% off → Full price"
        rule: "Increase by 20% every 5 clients"

      step_10:
        name: "Keep List Warm"
        action: "Regular value delivery"
        technique: "9-word email to probe interest"
        template: "Are you still looking for [4-word desire]?"

    scripts:
      value_equation_offer: |
        "By the way, do you know anyone who is (describe struggles)
        looking for (dream outcome) in (time delay)?

        I'm taking on five case studies for free because it's all I can
        handle. I just want to get some testimonials.

        I help them (dream outcome) without (effort and sacrifice). It works.
        I even guarantee people get (dream outcome) or I work with them
        until they do.

        I just had a girl named XXX who (dream outcome) even though she
        (describe the same struggle). I also had another guy who
        (dream outcome) and it was his first time.

        I'd just like more testimonials. Does anyone you like come to mind?
        ...Haha, well... does anyone you hate come to mind?"

      free_acceptance: |
        "As I'm taking only five people, I can give all the attention
        you need to get brag-worthy results. And I'll give everything
        for free, as long as you promise:
        1) Use it
        2) Give me feedback
        3) Leave a killer review if you think it deserves it
        Does that sound fair?"

      nine_word_email: |
        "Are you still looking for [4-word desire]?"

    benchmarks:
      response_rate: "~20%"
      free_acceptance_rate: "20% of respondents"
      free_to_paid_conversion: "25%"
      leads_per_100_outreaches: "20 responses → 4 free → 1 paid"

    math_example: |
      500 reach outs/week = 5 customers/week
      $400 product × 5 customers = $2000/week
      $2000/week × 52 weeks = $104,000/year

  content-engine:
    id: content-engine
    title: "Content Creation Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "C"

    purpose: |
      Create content that builds a growing warm audience.
      The content you create is not the asset that compounds - the AUDIENCE is.

    core_insight: |
      "It wasn't about the content - it was about the audience.
      Even though content may disappear, your audience keeps growing."

    unit_of_content:
      hook:
        goal: "Give them a reason to notice"
        measure: "% who start consuming"
        components:
          topics:
            - name: "Distant Past"
              description: "Important life lessons"
            - name: "Recent Past"
              description: "Things that happened recently"
            - name: "Present"
              description: "Ideas as they come"
            - name: "Trends"
              description: "What's trending now"
            - name: "Manufactured"
              description: "Create experience, then share"

          headlines:
            elements:
              - "Recency (as recent as possible)"
              - "Relevance (personally significant)"
              - "Celebrity (prominent people)"
              - "Proximity (close to home)"
              - "Conflict (opposing ideas/people)"
              - "Unusual (weird, unique, rare)"
              - "Ongoing (stories still in progress)"
            rule: "Include 2+ elements"

          format:
            rule: "Match what performs well on the platform"
            insight: "Make content LOOK like things they've liked before"

      retain:
        goal: "Keep them consuming"
        measure: "% who keep going"
        engines:
          lists:
            description: "Items presented one after another with a theme"
            examples:
              - "7 Ways I Invested $1000 That Paid Off"
              - "28 Ways to Go Broke"
          steps:
            description: "Actions in order to achieve a goal"
            examples:
              - "3 Steps to Create a Great Hook"
              - "The Morning Routine That Doubled My Productivity"
          stories:
            description: "Events with lessons/conclusions"
            examples:
              - "My journey from sleeping under a gym to a 5-star penthouse"

      reward:
        goal: "Satisfy the reason they started"
        measure: "Do they share? Do they want more?"
        test: "Fully satisfy the promise made in the hook"
        truth: "The audience decides. If audience grows, you're doing well."

    give_ask_ratio:
      minimum: "3:1 (like TV/Facebook)"
      growing_platforms: "Much higher give ratio"
      recommended: "Give give give... give give give... maybe ask"
      optimal: "Give until they ask"

      cta_strategies:
        integrated:
          description: "Brief ads within content"
          example: "58 min value : 2 min ask in 60 min podcast"
          placement: "After valuable moments or at end"

        intermittent:
          description: "Mostly pure give, occasional ask"
          example: "10 posts of give, 1 post of ask"
          best_for: "Short-form platforms"

    scaling_approaches:
      depth_first:
        description: "Maximize one platform, then add next"
        steps:
          - "Post on one platform"
          - "Post regularly"
          - "Maximize quality AND quantity"
          - "Add another platform"
          - "Repeat"
        advantages:
          - "Leverage compound growth"
          - "Less resources needed"
        disadvantages:
          - "Platform dependency risk"
          - "Slower initial breadth"

      breadth_first:
        description: "Get on all platforms, then maximize together"
        steps:
          - "Post on one platform"
          - "Post regularly"
          - "Add another platform (before maximizing)"
          - "Continue until on all platforms"
          - "Then maximize all at once"
        advantages:
          - "Repurpose content across platforms"
          - "Omnipresence feeling"
        disadvantages:
          - "Risk of mediocre content everywhere"
          - "More resources required"

    lessons:
      - lesson: "Change 'How to' to 'How I'"
        example: "How I Built My Agency vs How to Build an Agency"
      - lesson: "Need to be reminded more than taught"
        action: "Keep repeating - most haven't seen it"
      - lesson: "Pools, Ponds, Lakes, Oceans"
        action: "Narrow focus first, expand over time"
      - lesson: "Content creates sales tools"
        action: "Build 'greatest hits' library for sales team"
      - lesson: "Free content retains paid customers"
        insight: "They include free content in their ROI calculation"
      - lesson: "Shorter attention = higher standards"
        truth: "No such thing as too long, only too boring"
      - lesson: "Avoid pre-scheduling"
        insight: "Manual posting performs better (more care)"

    benchmarks:
      audience_growth: "Month-over-month increase"
      engagement_rate: "Platform-specific benchmarks"
      content_consumed_before_purchase: "78% consume 2+ pieces before buying"

  cold-outreach-engine:
    id: cold-outreach-engine
    title: "Cold Outreach Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "CO"

    purpose: |
      Execute scaled outreach to strangers using automation.
      Lower response rate than warm, but unlimited pool of prospects.

    key_differences_from_warm:
      - "Lower response rate (5-10% vs 20%)"
      - "MUST use automation"
      - "Need stronger hooks"
      - "Compliance considerations"
      - "Volume compensates for lower conversion"

    process_steps:
      step_1:
        name: "Build Target List"
        methods:
          - "Purchased lists"
          - "Scraped data (LinkedIn, directories)"
          - "Industry databases"
          - "Conference attendee lists"
          - "Association member lists"
          - "Social media searches"
        rule: "Quality > quantity; verify accuracy"

      step_2:
        name: "Morpheus Cold Message"
        elements:
          - "Relevance: Why contacting THEM specifically"
          - "Value: What's in it for them"
          - "Credibility: Why they should believe you"
          - "CTA: Clear, low-friction next step"
        rule: "Lead with value, not with pitch"

      step_3:
        name: "Execute 100+/Day"
        requirement: "Use automation tools"
        channels:
          - "Cold email"
          - "Cold text"
          - "Cold DM"
          - "Cold call"
          - "Flyers"
        tracking: "Track response rates obsessively"

      step_4:
        name: "Convert Responses"
        action: "Use A-C-A framework from warm outreach"
        rule: "Response from stranger = treat like gold"

    rule_of_100: "100 cold reach outs per day (automated)"

    benchmarks:
      response_rate: "5-10%"
      conversion_rate: "Varies by offer"

  paid-ads-engine:
    id: paid-ads-engine
    title: "Paid Advertising Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "PA"

    purpose: |
      Trade money for leads at scale. Fastest way to scale lead acquisition.
      Efficiency matters more than creativity.

    core_insight: |
      "Paid ads are all about ROI. You put in X dollars and get Y dollars back.
      Good enough is good enough - you just need to make it profitable enough to scale."

    three_phases:
      phase_1_track:
        name: "Track Money"
        action: "Set up tracking before spending a single dollar"
        rule: "If you don't track, you'll get cleaned out"

      phase_2_lose:
        name: "Lose Money (Invest)"
        action: "Test and learn"
        expectation: "Lose more times than win"
        budget_rule: "2x 30-day profit per test"
        cutoff_rule: "If zero leads at 1x 30-day profit, turn off"
        insight: "Lose nine times, win once - but win BIG"

      phase_3_print:
        name: "Print Money"
        action: "Scale winners aggressively"
        question: "If machine gave $10 for every $1, what's your budget?"
        answer: "All of it"
        scaling_formula: "(Desired Customers × CAC) × 1.2"

    metrics:
      ltgp:
        name: "Lifetime Gross Profit"
        formula: "Total Revenue - Total Delivery Cost"
        example: |
          Customer pays $15/month, costs $5 to deliver
          Gross profit = $10/month
          Stays 10 months
          LTGP = $100

      cac:
        name: "Customer Acquisition Cost"
        formula: "Total Ad Spend / Customers Acquired"

      ltgp_cac_ratio:
        name: "LTGP:CAC Ratio"
        target: ">3:1"
        insight: "Every struggling portfolio company had ratio <3:1"

      diagnostic:
        if_cac_high: "Fix ads (CAC > 3x industry average)"
        if_cac_normal: "Fix model (LTGP too low)"
        insight: "CAC between competitors is closer than you'd think. Difference is LTGP."

    customer_financed_acquisition:
      definition: "Customer pays you back within 30 days"
      why_30_days: "Any business can get interest-free money for 30 days (credit card)"
      result: "Zero debt + new customer + unlimited scale"

      example:
        problem: |
          CAC = $30
          First month profit = $10
          Breakeven = 3 months (cash flow problem)

        solution: |
          Add $100 upsell (100% margin), 20% accept
          Average upsell = $20
          30-day profit = $10 + $20 = $30
          Breakeven = Day 1 (unlimited scale)

    lessons:
      - lesson: "Don't confuse sales problems with ad problems"
        insight: "If qualified leads aren't buying, it's sales, not ads"
      - lesson: "Best free content makes best paid ads"
        action: "Turn high-performing content into ads"
      - lesson: "UGC (User Generated Content) is powerful"
        action: "System to encourage customer testimonials"

    scaling_budget: |
      Budget = (Desired Customers × CAC) × 1.2

      Example:
      - Want 100 customers
      - CAC = $100
      - Base budget = $10,000
      - Add 20% buffer = $12,000
      - Daily = $400

  method-optimizer:
    id: method-optimizer
    title: "More-Better-New Optimizer"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "MBN"

    purpose: |
      Apply the More-Better-New framework to continuously improve results.
      "What's stopping them from doing 10x what they're currently doing?"

    framework:
      more:
        definition: "Do more of what's already working"
        action: "Double your inputs"
        insight: "Even without improvements, 2x inputs = more leads"
        rule_of_100: |
          Warm: 100 reach outs/day
          Content: 100 minutes/day
          Cold: 100 reach outs/day
          Ads: 100 minutes/day working on ads
          Duration: 100 days straight

      better:
        definition: "Improve efficiency through testing"
        action: "Test one thing per week per platform"
        focus: "Constraints (biggest drop-off points)"

        testing_cadence:
          monday: "Start new split test per platform"
          week: "Let test run"
          next_monday:
            - "Pick winner"
            - "Log results in test register"
            - "Create next test to beat current best"

        constraint_example: |
          30% Optin
          5% Sign Up ← Biggest drop-off = constraint
          50% Schedule

          5% improvement to constraint = 100% more leads
          5% improvement elsewhere = 10-16% more leads

        rule: "If can't beat current version in 4 tries, move to next constraint"

      new:
        definition: "New placements, platforms, or Core Four methods"
        when: "Only when MORE and BETTER returns are lower than NEW returns"

        priority_order:
          1: "New placements on same platform"
          2: "Same approach on new platform"
          3: "New Core Four method entirely"

        pie_size_fallacy: |
          Small business thinks they "saturated the market"
          But they're only using 1 method, 1 platform, 1 approach
          The market is MUCH bigger than their small slice

    decision_tree: |
      Q: What's stopping 10x current activity?

      IF nothing → Just do MORE
      IF something → Fix constraint first (BETTER)
      IF MORE+BETTER exhausted → Try NEW

      Priority: MORE → BETTER → NEW PLACEMENTS → NEW PLATFORMS → NEW CORE FOUR

# ===============================================================================
# EXECUTOR MATRIX
# ===============================================================================

executor_matrix:
  # Lead Audit
  - task: "Export contact lists"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Include ALL platforms"

  - task: "Count contacts by platform"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Use as priority ranking"

  - task: "Assess resource availability"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Honest time vs money assessment"

  # Warm Outreach
  - task: "Personalize outreach messages"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Check social for recent events"

  - task: "Execute 100 daily outreaches"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must feel personal"

  - task: "A-C-A conversation flow"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "3-4 exchanges before offer"

  - task: "Track responses and conversions"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Log in CRM"

  - task: "Send 9-word emails"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Template + personalization"

  # Content
  - task: "Create hooks (topics/headlines)"
    executor: Human

    guardrails: "Include 2+ headline elements"

  - task: "Create retention structure"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Use lists, steps, or stories"

  - task: "Format for platform"
    executor: Hybrid

    guardrails: "Match top performers"

  - task: "Post content"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Manual posting may perform better"

  - task: "Track audience growth"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Monthly reporting"

  # Cold Outreach
  - task: "Build target lists"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Quality verification required"

  - task: "Morpheus cold message templates"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Test multiple variations"

  - task: "Send cold outreach"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Follow platform rules"

  - task: "Handle responses"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Use A-C-A framework"

  # Paid Ads
  - task: "Set up tracking"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Before spending any money"

  - task: "Create ad variations"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Multiple versions for testing"

  - task: "Set budget parameters"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "2x 30-day profit per test"

  - task: "Monitor ad performance"
    executor: Worker

    guardrails: "Cutoff at 1x if zero leads"

  - task: "Calculate LTGP:CAC"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH

  - task: "Scale winning ads"
    executor: Hybrid

  # Optimization
  - task: "Identify constraints"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM

  - task: "Design tests"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "One test per week per platform"

  - task: "Analyze test results"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Log in test register"

  - task: "Decide MORE vs BETTER vs NEW"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Follow priority order"

# ===============================================================================
# QUALITY GATES
# ===============================================================================

quality_gates:
  QG-001:
    name: "Offer Ready Gate"
    transition: "Start → Advertising"
    condition: "lead_magnet_or_offer_validated == true"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Create/improve offer first"

  QG-002:
    name: "Rule of 100 Gate"
    transition: "Daily Execution"
    condition: "daily_actions >= 100"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Increase effort until hitting 100"

  QG-003:
    name: "Response Rate Gate - Warm"
    transition: "Outreach → Response"
    condition: "warm_response_rate >= 15%"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Improve personalization"

  QG-004:
    name: "Response Rate Gate - Cold"
    transition: "Outreach → Response"
    condition: "cold_response_rate >= 5%"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Improve targeting/message"

  QG-005:
    name: "Audience Growth Gate"
    transition: "Content → Audience"
    condition: "month_over_month_growth > 0"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Improve content quality"

  QG-006:
    name: "Paid Ads Efficiency Gate"
    transition: "Spending → Returns"
    condition: "ltgp_cac_ratio >= 3.0"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Fix model or ads before scaling"

  QG-007:
    name: "Testing Cadence Gate"
    transition: "Weekly Optimization"
    condition: "one_test_per_week_per_platform == true"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Design and launch test"

# ===============================================================================
# WORKFLOWS
# ===============================================================================

workflows:
  method_selection_workflow:
    trigger: "Starting lead generation"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: lead-auditor
        action: "Assess current state"
        output: "Contact counts, resources available"

      - step: 2
        agent: offer-validator
        action: "Validate offer/lead magnet"
        output: "Readiness score"

      - step: 3
        agent: core-four-coordinator
        action: "Select priority method"
        logic:
          more_time_than_money: "Start with warm outreach"
          more_money_than_time: "Start with cold outreach or paid ads"
          want_compound_growth: "Add content"

      - step: 4
        agent: "[selected-method-engine]"
        action: "Begin execution"
        commitment: "Rule of 100"

  warm_outreach_workflow:
    trigger: "Warm outreach selected"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: warm-outreach-engine
        action: "Build master contact list"
        output: "Total count by platform"

      - step: 2
        agent: warm-outreach-engine
        action: "Select highest-count platform"
        output: "Priority platform"

      - step: 3
        agent: warm-outreach-engine
        action: "Execute 100 personalized outreaches"
        daily: true
        duration: "100 days"

      - step: 4
        agent: warm-outreach-engine
        action: "Apply A-C-A to responses"
        output: "Qualified prospects"

      - step: 5
        agent: warm-outreach-engine

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/downsell-strategy-sop.md

# Downsell Strategy SOP

> **Source:** $100M Modelos: Seção 4 Ofertas de Downsell - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Capture revenue from customers who said NO to your main offer by adjusting offers to find the solution of highest value for their budget. Downselling transforms rejections into opportunities.

**Core Principle:**
```
"Any offer you make after someone says no is a downsell."
— Alex Hormozi, Seção 4

Downsells adjust the original offer to find the best value-budget match.
Two levers:
1. HOW they pay (payment plans, trials)
2. WHAT they get (quantity, quality, features)
```

**Business Impact:** Downsells can DOUBLE your closing rate. Example: 3/10 closes become 6/10 with proper downselling (35 on main offer + 40 on downsell from 100 leads).

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Customer has said NO to main offer
- Customer has objection about price
- Customer wants the result but not at current terms
- Retention conversations before cancellation

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- First offer presentation (that's your core offer)
- Upselling (covered in Seção 3)
- Customer hasn't seen main offer yet

### Business Types
- Any business with tiered offerings
- Service businesses with variable components
- Product businesses with payment flexibility
- Recurring revenue models (subscription/membership)

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Main Offer Presented | Customer must have seen and rejected main offer | Rejection documented |
| Payment Options Ready | Payment plan structures pre-defined | Terms approved |
| Feature Menu Defined | Know which features can be removed | Value-price matrix complete |
| Trial Terms Set | Trial criteria and penalties defined | Legal review done |
| CRM Tracking | System to track downsell conversions | Reports configured |
| Credit Card Processing | Ability to store and charge cards | Payment system active |

---

## Part 4: The Three Downsell Frameworks

### Framework Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    THREE DOWNSELL PROCESSES                             │
├───────────────────────┬─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┤
│ PAYMENT PLAN DOWNSELL │ TRIAL COM PENALIDADE│ DOWNSELL DE RECURSOS      │
├───────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ Changes HOW they pay  │ Changes WHEN they   │ Changes WHAT they get     │
│                       │ pay                 │                           │
├───────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ Same total price      │ Pay later IF fail   │ Lower price, less value   │
│ Spread over time      │ Free if complete    │ Remove features           │
├───────────────────────┼─────────────────────┼───────────────────────────┤
│ Up to 7 steps         │ 5 step process      │ Quantity/Quality/Removal  │
│ Works for any price   │ Recurring services  │ Any product/service       │
└───────────────────────┴─────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┘
```

### The 6 Rules of Downselling

| Rule | Description | Source |
|------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | "They said no to THIS offer, not ALL offers" | p.17 - "Don't hide your head in the sand" |
| 2 | "Downsells are trades - if you give, you get" | p.19 - "Work with customer on give/take combinations" |
| 3 | "Personalize, don't pressure" | p.21 - "Discover what they like/dislike" |
| 4 | "Offer same thing in new ways" | p.23 - "100 ways to offer what you already have" |
| 5 | "Never lower price just to make someone buy" | p.25 - "That's discounting, not downselling" |
| 6 | "Customers talk about price" | p.27-28 - "If others got same thing cheaper, you'll upset people" |

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### PROCESS I: PAYMENT PLAN DOWNSELLS

> "How much can you put down today?"

#### Step 1.1: Reward for Paying in Full
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Present full price with interest included, offer discount for prepay |
| **Cognitive Type** | Framing (anchor high, discount down) |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Price presentation templates |
| **Executor** | Human (sales conversation) |
| **Precondition** | Customer said no to main offer |
| **Output** | Either full payment or move to step 2 |
| **Guardrails** | Never present lower price first |
| **Decision Rule** | "It's $15, but it's $10 if you prepay. You save $5." Not "It's $10, but $15 if you pay over time." |

**Rationale:** Same math, better feel. Anchors at higher price, makes prepay feel like winning.

#### Step 1.2: Offer Third-Party Options
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Offer financing, credit card, or layaway options |
| **Cognitive Type** | Option presentation |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Can automate application |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Customer declined prepay discount |
| **Output** | Payment method selected or move to step 3 |
| **Guardrails** | Must have financing partner configured |
| **Decision Rule** | "Do you prefer I decide your payment terms or you decide?" |

**Three Options:**
- **Third-party financing:** Company pays you today, customer pays them over time (like car dealerships)
- **Credit card:** "Use a card, you get it today, pay the card company over time"
- **Layaway:** Pay before receiving - flexible terms, zero risk for you

#### Step 1.3: Offer Half Now, Half Later
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Split payment aligned with paycheck timing |
| **Cognitive Type** | Negotiation |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires conversation |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Third-party options declined |
| **Output** | Payment scheduled or move to step 4 |
| **Guardrails** | Align with customer's pay schedule |
| **Decision Rule** | "When do you get paid? Let's put half today, half then." |

**Script:**
```
"When is the next time you get paid?"
"Do you want to put half today and the rest when you get paid?"
"What's the most you can put down today?"
"Great. Let's put that today and the rest when you get paid. Fair?"
```

#### Step 1.4: Check If They Still Want It
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Confirm desire before offering more payment options |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Half payment declined |
| **Output** | Continue or pivot to different offer |
| **Guardrails** | If <8/10 desire, offer something else |
| **Decision Rule** | "On a scale of 1-10, how much do you want to do this?" |

**Decision Tree:**
- 8-10: Continue to step 5
- 7 or below: "You're right. We might have something more suitable for you." → Feature downsell

#### Step 1.5: Offer Three-Payment Split
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | One-third now, one-third each of next two paychecks |
| **Cognitive Type** | Arithmetic presentation |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Calculator |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Customer scored 8-10 desire |
| **Output** | Three-payment plan accepted or move to step 6 |
| **Guardrails** | Align with pay schedule (biweekly vs monthly) |
| **Decision Rule** | "Let's do a third now and a third on your next two paydays" |

#### Step 1.6: Offer Spread Payments Evenly
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Divide total across service duration |
| **Cognitive Type** | Math presentation |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Payment calculator |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Three-payment split declined |
| **Output** | Weekly/monthly payments accepted or move to step 7 |
| **Guardrails** | Match payment frequency to service delivery |
| **Decision Rule** | "16-week program? 16 weekly payments." |

**Example:** Gym Launch was 16 weeks, so offered 16 weekly payments.

#### Step 1.7: Offer Free Trial
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Transition to trial with penalty (Process II) |
| **Cognitive Type** | Offer pivot |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | All payment plans declined |
| **Output** | Trial enrollment or sale ends here |
| **Guardrails** | Must have trial structure ready |
| **Decision Rule** | "The sale ends here, at least for now." |

---

### PROCESS II: TRIAL COM PENALIDADE (PENALTY TRIAL)

> "If you do X, Y, Z, I'll let you start for free."

#### Step 2.1: Offer Trial Last
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Only offer trial after customer clearly rejected main offer |
| **Cognitive Type** | Strategic sequencing |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Clear rejection of main and payment plan offers |
| **Output** | Trial offer presented |
| **Guardrails** | Never lead with trial |
| **Decision Rule** | "How about we start you for free? Would that work?" |

**Script:**
```
"Hmm, that's really a problem. Tell you what, how about we start you
for free? Would you be okay with that? We can just help you out and
if you like it, you can stay. Let me get your ID and we can start
the process. Fair? Great."
```

#### Step 2.2: Always Get a Card
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Capture credit card even for free trial |
| **Cognitive Type** | Process enforcement |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Form capture |
| **Executor** | Worker (form) + Human (conversation) |
| **Precondition** | Customer agrees to trial |
| **Output** | Card on file |
| **Guardrails** | If they refuse card = walk away |
| **Decision Rule** | "It's just how we've always done it." |

**Pro Tip:** If someone won't put a card down and commit to the work, don't sell to them. They complain more and convert less.

#### Step 2.3: Sell Staying and Paying
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Get commitment to continue after trial IF results |
| **Cognitive Type** | Future pacing |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Card captured |
| **Output** | Verbal commitment to continue |
| **Guardrails** | If they won't commit to staying, no point in trial |
| **Decision Rule** | "If this gets you results, will you stay long-term?" |

**Script:**
```
"I don't want you to just try, I want you to get results. And being
honest, you won't reach your long-term goals during this trial, but
you'll establish the habits to help you achieve them. And we'll help
you do that for free. But if you want your long-term results, you'll
have to continue after. I just want to make sure you're not looking
for a quick fix because ethically I can't promise that."
```

#### Step 2.4: Explain Fees After Getting Card
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Present penalty structure after card is secured |
| **Cognitive Type** | Terms presentation |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Document |
| **Executor** | Human (explain) + Worker (document) |
| **Precondition** | Card on file |
| **Output** | Terms acknowledged |
| **Guardrails** | Have customer initial fee clause separately |
| **Decision Rule** | Explain fees AFTER card, not before |

**Script:**
```
"We'll do our part as long as you do yours. That's fair, right? So
now I just ask you to bet on yourself. If you miss or skip anything,
your results will suffer. We charge to keep you on track. If you
mess up, no problem. You get charged a small fee, but it puts you
back on track. If you comply, you get all of this for free. So this
is the best way to get amazing results and keep it free for you.
Best of both worlds."
```

#### Step 2.5: Make Check-Ins Mandatory
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Build upsell opportunities into trial requirements |
| **Cognitive Type** | Structure design |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Calendar rules |
| **Executor** | Worker (scheduling) + Human (delivery) |
| **Precondition** | Terms acknowledged |
| **Output** | Check-ins scheduled |
| **Guardrails** | Charge fees for missed check-ins |
| **Decision Rule** | "Obviously, we charge if you miss these because it's the only way to get results." |

**Check-In Structure:**
```
"Yes, and you agree to attend each of these three check-ins:
First, we do X so that you can...
Second, we do Y so that you can...
Third, we do Z so that you can...
Obviously, we charge if you miss these because it's the only way
to get results."
```

---

### PROCESS III: FEATURE DOWNSELLS

> "Why don't we try this instead?"

#### Step 3.1: Downsell Quantity
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Offer less of the same product/service |
| **Cognitive Type** | Option reduction |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Pre-built packages |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Price objection identified |
| **Output** | Reduced quantity accepted or move to next step |
| **Guardrails** | Ensure reduced quantity still delivers value |
| **Decision Rule** | "Instead of 3-month supply, start with just 1?" |

**Examples:**
- Product: "Instead of three-month supply, how about we start with just one?"
- Service: "Instead of four sessions per month, why not start with two?"

#### Step 3.2: Downsell Quality
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Offer lower-tier version of product/service |
| **Cognitive Type** | Tier selection |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Tier menu |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Quantity downsell declined |
| **Output** | Lower tier accepted or move to next step |
| **Guardrails** | Maintain core value proposition |
| **Decision Rule** | "Instead of leather, we can do vinyl. Sound good?" |

**Quality Dimensions:**
- Time availability: Specific hours vs anytime
- Days: Mon/Wed/Fri vs any day
- Response speed: Overnight vs 5 minutes
- Delivery speed: Next week vs same day
- Ratio: 1-to-many vs 1-to-1
- Method: Text vs video call
- Provider: New employee vs owner
- Live vs recorded
- DIY vs Done-With-You vs Done-For-You
- Expiration: Limited time vs forever
- Customization: Generic vs personalized

#### Step 3.3: Remove Features Entirely
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Remove specific features to lower price |
| **Cognitive Type** | Subtraction presentation |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Feature menu |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Quality downsell declined |
| **Output** | Feature-reduced package accepted or continue |
| **Guardrails** | Remove high-value features to highlight their worth |
| **Decision Rule** | "Instead of chat, email, AND calls, let's keep just chat and email, drop the calls." |

**Strategic Feature Removal (Guarantee Example):**
```
Before downsell: 25% close rate
After adding "remove guarantee" downsell: 75% close rate
- 35 buy main offer (with guarantee)
- 40 buy downsell (without guarantee)
Total: 3x the customers
```

**Key Insight:** Removing high-value features makes customers SEE the value and often choose to keep it at full price.

#### Step 3.4: Offer DIY Alternative
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Offer product/tools if they won't buy service |
| **Cognitive Type** | Category shift |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Product menu |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | All service downsells declined |
| **Output** | DIY product sold |
| **Guardrails** | Products should support same outcome |
| **Decision Rule** | "Can't afford chiropractic? Let me set you up with some home massage tools." |

**Examples:**
- Chiropractor → Foam rollers, massage tools, mats
- Painter → Rent spray machine, sell paint
- Alex Hormozi → "Instead of us buying your company, join a workshop"

---

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Downsell Sequencing
```yaml
rule: DOWNSELL_ORDER
trigger: Customer says NO
condition:
  - IF objection == "price_too_high" THEN start_payment_plan_downsell()
  - IF objection == "not_sure_value" THEN start_feature_downsell()
  - IF objection == "not_ready" THEN start_trial_downsell()
action: Match downsell type to objection type
confidence: HIGH
source: "Seção 4, p.30"
```

### DR-002: Payment Plan Progression
```yaml
rule: PAYMENT_PLAN_STEPS
trigger: Customer declines payment option
sequence:
  1. Prepay discount
  2. Third-party financing / Credit card / Layaway
  3. Half now, half later
  4. Check desire (1-10 scale)
  5. Three payments
  6. Spread payments evenly
  7. Free trial (Process II)
action: Progress through steps, stop when they buy
confidence: HIGH
source: "Seção 4, p.73-102"
```

### DR-003: Desire Check Gate
```yaml
rule: DESIRE_CHECK
trigger: Customer declines half-payment option
condition:
  - IF desire_score >= 8 THEN continue_payment_downsells()
  - IF desire_score < 8 THEN ask_why_not_10() AND offer_different_product()
action: Pivot to feature downsell if desire is low
confidence: HIGH
source: "Seção 4, p.96-97"
```

### DR-004: Trial Card Rule
```yaml
rule: TRIAL_CARD_MANDATORY
trigger: Customer accepts trial offer
condition:
  - IF customer_provides_card THEN continue_trial_process()
  - IF customer_refuses_card THEN end_conversation_politely()
action: No card = no trial, period
confidence: HIGH
source: "Seção 4, p.176-177"
```

### DR-005: Feature Removal Strategy
```yaml
rule: FEATURE_REMOVAL_ORDER
trigger: Feature downsell initiated
sequence:
  - FIRST remove highest-value features (makes customer re-upsell themselves)
  - THEN remove features they don't care about (better deal for them)
action: Remove high value first to demonstrate worth
confidence: HIGH
source: "Seção 4, p.253-254"
```

### DR-006: Never Discount Rule
```yaml
rule: NO_DISCOUNTING
trigger: Temptation to lower price without changing offer
condition:
  - IF lowering_price_for_same_offer THEN BLOCK
  - IF lowering_price_AND_removing_feature THEN ALLOW
action: Every price reduction must have corresponding value reduction
confidence: HIGH
source: "Seção 4, p.13-14 (Car salesman story)"
```

---

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: Customer Who Really Can't Pay
**Trigger:** Customer has genuine financial hardship
**Action:** Layaway option (pay before receiving)
**Rationale:** "They can take as long as they reasonably want to pay. But they only get the product after they've paid in full." (p.93)

### Exception 2: Customer Who Doesn't Do the Trial Work
**Trigger:** Trial customer not engaging
**Options:**
1. Charge penalty fees (as agreed)
2. Offer makeup opportunity
3. For non-starters: "A small fee isn't worth a one-star review. But hey, your choice." (p.186)

### Exception 3: Customers Talk About Prices
**Trigger:** Concern about different customers getting different prices
**Rule:** "Test prices with a specific number of people ahead of time. Don't charge less in the moment because you felt scared." (p.27-28)
**Action:** Set fixed prices and terms, don't negotiate in the moment

### Exception 4: Trial Customer Who Hates Experience
**Trigger:** Negative trial feedback
**Script:**
```
"Ask what they'd like different. Say you're right and you're
annoyed you missed that. Don't blame them. Only one person can
be angry and it needs to be you. Ask if they'll give you a chance
to make it right. Offer your higher-tier thing."
```
**Close rate on unhappy trials:** ~50% (p.185)

---

## Part 8: Outputs

| Output | Format | Destination | Frequency |
|--------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Downsell Conversion Report | Dashboard | Sales Manager | Daily |
| Payment Plan Performance | Metrics | Finance | Weekly |
| Trial Completion Rate | Report | Operations | Weekly |
| Feature Downsell Mix | Analysis | Product Team | Monthly |
| Charge/Cancelation Rate | Financial | Executive | Monthly |

### Key Metrics to Track
```
PRIMARY:
├── Downsell Conversion Rate = Downsells Closed / Total Rejections
├── 30-Day Cash Collected (payment plans)
├── Trial-to-Paid Conversion Rate
└── Feature Downsell Revenue

SECONDARY:
├── Payment Plan Completion Rate
├── Trial Penalty Collection Rate
├── Average Steps to Close
├── Upsell Rate from Downsell Customers
└── Churn Rate by Acquisition Method
```

---

## Part 9: Validation

### Quality Gates

| Gate | Threshold | Action if Failed |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| Full Payment Ratio | Maintain % of full payments | Review if payment plans are cannibalizing |
| Trial Completion | >70% complete requirements | Adjust trial criteria |
| 30-Day Collection | Track cash vs projected | Optimize payment timing |
| Churn by Entry Point | Compare across entry methods | Investigate higher-churn sources |

### Payment Plan Health Check
```
RULE: Payment plans make money when:
- Total closes increase
- Full payment percentage stays same
- New downsell customers ADDED to full-pay customers

BAD SIGN:
- Full payment customers moving to payment plans
- Payment plans failing before profit point
```
Source: "Seção 4, p.113-114"

## Part 10: Escalation Paths

| Situation | Escalate To | Timeline |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Payment plan failure rate >30% | Finance Manager | Weekly review |
| Trial completion <50% | Operations Lead | Immediately |
| Customer complaints about fees | Manager | Same day |
| Feature removal causing value concerns | Product Owner | Before implementation |
| Churn spike from downsell customers | Executive | Weekly |

## Appendix A: Cultural Elements (Downsell Mindset)

### Core Mantras
| Mantra | Meaning | Application |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| "No to this offer, not all offers" | Rejection is opportunity | Keep offering alternatives |
| "Downsells are trades" | Every give needs a get | Match value to price |
| "Personalize, don't pressure" | Find their fit | Discover preferences first |
| "100 offers, not 100 products" | Same thing, different ways | Maximize existing offerings |
| "Never just lower price" | Discounting kills trust | Always remove value too |
| "Customers talk" | Consistency matters | Same rules for everyone |

### The Car Salesman Anti-Pattern
```
WRONG: $5,000 → $3,000 → $1,000 → $400 for same insurance
RESULT: Customer said no to all AND questioned the car price

RIGHT: Different insurance at different prices
RESULT: Maintain trust, might close a sale
```
Source: "Seção 4, p.11-14"

## Appendix B: Trial With Penalty Criteria Examples

### B2C Example: 28-Day Blueprint to Quit the Habit
```
To get trial free and avoid penalty fee:
- Attend all consultation calls
- Post progress photos weekly in group
- Journal daily in our app
- Attend feedback sessions
- Attend transformation sessions (upsell opportunities)
```

### B2B Example: 5-Day Challenge to Get First 5 Clients
```
To get trial free and avoid penalty fee:
- Send 100 outbound messages per day
- Report statistics on those messages
- Attend daily training
- Post in group after homework
- Attend graduation call (upsell opportunity)
```

### Software Example: $500 Onboarding + $99/month
```
To avoid $500 onboarding fee:
- Attend onboarding (3 x 60-min Zoom calls)
- Complete homework
- Activate employer profile
- Set up employees by end of third call
```

## Appendix C: Seesaw Downselling Script (Simplified Process)

For simpler situations or less experienced salespeople:

**Step 1: Frame payment plan as negative**
```
"Would you rather have giant monthly payments or small ones?"
[They say small]
"Normally it's X, and if you prepay today, you get a huge discount
and zero monthly payments. Does that work?"
```

**Step 2: If they can't prepay**
```
"The more you can put down now, the smaller your monthly payments.
If you can't pay upfront, I totally understand. Let's just adjust
the down payment until you get a monthly rate you like."
```

**Step 3: Make it collaborative**
```
"Pull your chair to their side of the table. Show them the options.
The sale becomes a team effort."
```

Source: "Seção 4, p.107-108"
