## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/fast-cash-sop.md

# Fast Cash SOP

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Fast Cash - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Generate maximum cash in the shortest period possible from your warmest audiences. Fast Cash Plays are "winning lottery tickets you cash in once a quarter" - limited time offers designed to extract premium revenue from existing customers, previous customers, and engaged leads.

**Core Equation:**
```
Fast Cash Revenue = Number Sold x Premium Price
Example:
- 10 customers buy at $6,000 = $60,000
- 90% gross margins = $54,000 profit
- Quarterly execution = $200k+ annual profit boost
```

**10x The 10% Rule:**
```
If 10% of customers pay 10x the price = You double your revenue
- Already spent money to acquire them
- Extra revenue (minus delivery) = straight profit
- Sometimes 2x, 3x, 4x revenue from single customer segment
```

**Business Impact:**
- "Despite Cash Plays only being ~15% of my annual revenue, they were nearly half my profit"
- "Running even one Cash Play per year will pay for itself many years over"
- ROI Example: $300k/year business -> $529k/year with Fast Cash = 76% revenue increase, 4x net income

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Business needs immediate cash injection (unexpected expenses, tax bills, investment opportunities)
- Quarterly promotion calendar (recommended: every 90 days)
- Launch of ultra-premium tier for existing offer
- Year-end prepay campaigns

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- New customer acquisition (different playbooks)
- Long-term lead nurturing (covered in Lead Nurture SOP)
- Reactivation of dormant leads with no purchase history
- Price reductions or discounting strategies

### Business Types
- B2B and B2C ("this works for both business-to-business offers and business-to-consumer offers")
- Any business with existing customers, previous customers, or engaged leads
- Subscription and one-time purchase models
- Service and product businesses

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Warm List | Existing customers, past customers, engaged leads | List segmented and contactable |
| Contact Permission | "All people who've given you explicit permission to contact them" | Permission documented |
| Email/SMS System | Ability to send sequences | CRM configured |
| Premium Offer | Ultra-premium value stack defined | Bonuses separated out |
| Delivery Capacity | Ability to fulfill 5-10% of customer base | Capacity confirmed |
| Payment Processing | Can collect card-on-file or new payments | Systems tested |
| Sales Capacity | For consult path: calendar availability | Slots blocked |

---

## Part 4: Core Framework

### Fast Cash Play Architecture

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                     FAST CASH PLAY ANATOMY                       |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                   |
|   WHO TO ADVERTISE TO:                                            |
|   +-----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+                    |
|   | Existing  |  | Previous  |  | Engaged   |                    |
|   | Customers |  | Customers |  | Leads     |                    |
|   +-----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+                    |
|                                                                   |
|   OFFER CHARACTERISTICS:                                          |
|   +----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+      |
|   | Scarcity |  | Urgency   |  | Exclusivity|  | Premium  |      |
|   | Limited  |  | 7 days    |  | High touch |  | 10x-50x  |      |
|   | spots    |  | or less   |  | unscalable |  | price    |      |
|   +----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+  +-----------+      |
|                                                                   |
|   DELIVERY PATHS:                                                 |
|   +--------------------+    +------------------------+            |
|   | Push to Consult    |    | Push to Auto Checkout  |            |
|   | (7 days, spread    |    | (5 days, stampede      |            |
|   |  appointments)     |    |  first-come-first-serve)|           |
|   +--------------------+    +------------------------+            |
|                                                                   |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Ultra-Premium Value Categories

| Category | Description | Source Examples |
|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Attention** | "1 on 1 attention from you, or senior persons in the company" | Many-on-1: team supports one customer |
| **Personalization** | "Personalized, customized versions of your standard solutions" | Tailored plans |
| **Convenience** | "24/7 support, extended hours, exclusive times" | Personal cell access |
| **Status** | "Special parking, perks, badges, public recognition" | VIP treatment |
| **Duration** | "Longer duration than standard solutions" | 6 months to a year |
| **Speed** | "First in line. Priority. Fast response time promises (<10 min or less)" | Priority queue |
| **Experience** | "White Glove service. Personal cell phone access. A concierge line" | Nice dinners, gifts |
| **Access** | "In-person experiences. Retreats. Normally restricted areas" | Behind the scenes |
| **Network** | "Connection with other top customers (where applicable)" | Peer introductions |
| **Secrets** | "Exclusive bonuses. Trade secrets. Access to vendors you have vetted" | Secret menu, black book |

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### PHASE I: PREPARATION

#### Step 1.1: Assemble Target List
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Pick and assemble the list you plan to send your offer to (past and present customers)" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Segmentation |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - CRM query |
| **Executor** | Worker (list pull) + Human (validation) |
| **Precondition** | Contact database with customer history |
| **Output** | Segmented list: existing customers, past customers, engaged leads |
| **Guardrails** | "Exclude Cooled-Off Leads... if your list has neglected leads - aka - you haven't sent them anything for six months or more, consider excluding them" |
| **Decision Rule** | Include only warm audiences with explicit contact permission |

#### Step 1.2: Design Ultra-Premium Offer
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Pick the offer you will send. Max out unscalable value. Model the examples." |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Strategic decision |
| **Executor** | Human (leadership) |
| **Precondition** | Know what customers find "crazy valuable" |
| **Output** | 1-3 core components + 3 bonuses separated |
| **Guardrails** | "Think of all the most valuable things you can do that are 'unscalable'" |
| **Decision Rule** | "You will want to have one to three core components of your offer, and three bonuses" |

**Offer Structure:**
```
CORE COMPONENTS (1-3):
- Main unscalable value proposition
- Differentiator from standard offer
- Ultimate outcome promise

BONUSES (3, layered in sequence):
- Bonus 1: Added value (Day 5 or Day 4 release)
- Bonus 2: Enhanced feature (Day 2 release)
- Bonus 3: Best bonus - "worth more than entire price tag" (24h release)
```

#### Step 1.3: Set Premium Price
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Pick a price to match it. 10x to 50x for maximum cash. Be bold!" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires market understanding |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Know current average transaction value |
| **Output** | Premium price point (10x-50x current price) |
| **Guardrails** | "The only thing that should shock them as much as the price is the value that goes with it" |
| **Decision Rule** | "Take whatever your average cart value... and add a zero. And if you want to get frisky, multiply it by five" |

**Pricing Examples:**
| Business Type | Standard Price | Fast Cash Price | Multiple |
|---------------|----------------|-----------------|----------|
| Fitness B2C | $150/month | $10,000/year | ~56x monthly |
| Marketing Agency B2B | ~$5,000/year | $50,000/year | 10x |
| Subscription | Monthly price | Monthly x 12 | 12x |

#### Step 1.4: Set Quantity Cap
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "We want to cap how many people can buy it" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Calculation |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Know customer count and fulfillment capacity |
| **Output** | Limited spots number (5-10% of customers) |
| **Guardrails** | "Cap it to a number where you will absolutely sell out" |
| **Decision Rule** | "If you had 100 customers, you'd limit it to 5-10. If you have 1000 or more, then fulfillment may constrain you" |

#### Step 1.5: Choose Selling Method
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Determine if selling via consults or automated checkout |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | N/A - One-time decision |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Know sales team capacity and price point |
| **Output** | Path selection: Consult vs. Auto Checkout |
| **Guardrails** | "For most businesses, high price points deserve a one-on-one consultation" |
| **Decision Rule** | Consult = spread appointments over 7 days. Auto = stampede, first-come-first-serve |

#### Step 1.6: Prep All Materials
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Prep your emails and texts ahead of time" + "Have your bonuses ready before you tell people about them" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Template-based |
| **Executor** | Worker (production) + Human (approval) |
| **Precondition** | Offer, price, quantity all defined |
| **Output** | Complete email + text sequence loaded in CRM |
| **Guardrails** | All messages drafted before campaign start |
| **Decision Rule** | "Send your announcement" only after ALL materials ready |

---

### PHASE II: EXECUTION - PUSH TO CONSULT SEQUENCE (7 Days)

#### Step 2.1: Day 7 - Primer
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Let them know something big is coming via email tomorrow" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | List assembled, materials ready |
| **Output** | Primer text sent |
| **Guardrails** | Text only, no details yet |
| **Decision Rule** | Build anticipation without revealing offer |

**Text Template:**
```
"Hey [CLIENT NAME] would it be cool if I got you [TO THEIR GOAL] and
saved you a ton of money? Give me a thumbs up if that sounds cool.
I'm sending you something you're gonna like tomorrow."
```

#### Step 2.2: Day 6 - Announcement
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Announcement email. List the one to three core components of your offer" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Primer sent day before |
| **Output** | Announcement email + text to draw attention |
| **Guardrails** | Include price range if "you suck at sales or have a hot list" |
| **Decision Rule** | CTA = schedule a consult |

**Include in Announcement:**
- Core offer components (1-3)
- Price indication: "four-figure investment" or "must be willing to invest at least $2000" or "costs more than a year of service"
- Limited spots
- Deadline (Saturday midnight)
- CTA to book consult

#### Step 2.3: Day 5 - Recap + Bonus 1
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Recap offer. Just send bullets of everything you sent the day before for people who missed it" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Announcement sent |
| **Output** | Recap email with first bonus |
| **Guardrails** | "Add your first additional bonus if you have it" |
| **Decision Rule** | Example bonus category: Status (better parking) |

#### Step 2.4: Day 3 - Sales Update
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Let everyone know how many sold already, how many you have left" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Requires live data |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Some sales completed |
| **Output** | Sales update email + text reminder |
| **Guardrails** | "Remind them it's first come first serve" |
| **Decision Rule** | Include "good stuff it helps them get, bad stuff it helps them avoid" |

#### Step 2.5: Day 2 - X Spots Left + Bonus 2
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Let them know spots are running out. Add your second bonus" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Day 3 sent |
| **Output** | Scarcity email + second bonus |
| **Guardrails** | "Make sure to explain the benefits" |
| **Decision Rule** | Example bonus category: Secrets (special training) |

#### Step 2.6: Day 1 AM - Warning + Best Bonus
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Warning: A few hours out or X spots left. Add your best bonus here" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Day 2 sent |
| **Output** | Final warning email with best bonus |
| **Guardrails** | "This should be worth more than the entire price tag and should get you to sell out" |
| **Decision Rule** | Example: "In-Person two-day retreat at a luxury location" |

#### Step 2.7: Day 1 PM - Sold Out
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Sold out. Send a text letting them know" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | All spots filled |
| **Output** | Sold out notification |
| **Guardrails** | Validates scarcity was real |
| **Decision Rule** | If not sold out, consider adding more value or extending briefly |

#### Step 2.8: Post - Back Out (Optional)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "If you have someone back out" - one spot left notification |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Customer backs out |
| **Output** | Re-opening notification via text |
| **Guardrails** | Only send if genuine back-out |
| **Decision Rule** | Creates additional urgency moment |

---

### PHASE III: EXECUTION - PUSH TO AUTOMATED CHECKOUT SEQUENCE (5 Days)

#### Step 3.1: Day 5 - Primer
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Primer Text: Let them know something big is coming via email tomorrow. That's it." |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Materials ready |
| **Output** | Primer text |
| **Guardrails** | Text only |
| **Decision Rule** | Build anticipation |

#### Step 3.2: Day 4 - Announcement
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Announcement email. Say the one to three core components of your offer. Include price" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Primer sent |
| **Output** | Announcement + text |
| **Guardrails** | "Include price if you suck at sales and have a hot list" |
| **Decision Rule** | "Give a price range in 'figures' aka - 'four-figure investment'" |

#### Step 3.3: Day 2 - Cart Opens in 48h + Bonus 1
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Tell them the cart opens in 48 hours. Remind them it's first come, first serve" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Announcement sent |
| **Output** | 48h warning + first bonus |
| **Guardrails** | Add bonus: "Ex= Personalization - extra customization" |
| **Decision Rule** | "Tell them to set an alarm so they don't miss it because you expect it to sell out in minutes" |

#### Step 3.4: Day 1 - 60 Min Out
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Text to remind them to set an alarm and have their payment method ready" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | 24h email sent |
| **Output** | Final prep text |
| **Guardrails** | Immediate, actionable |
| **Decision Rule** | Create stampede conditions |

#### Step 3.5: Cart Open - 5 Min + Best Bonus
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Add the best bonus here the moment you tell them the cart is open" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Cart time reached |
| **Output** | Cart open email + text with best bonus |
| **Guardrails** | "You want this bonus to be the most immediate benefit. So that the moment they respond they get an instant benefit" |
| **Decision Rule** | Example: "Experience - your personal cell" |

#### Step 3.6: Cart Open + 60 Min - Sales Update
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "How many sold already. How many left." |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Live data needed |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Cart opened |
| **Output** | Sales update + text |
| **Guardrails** | Real numbers only |
| **Decision Rule** | Intensify urgency |

#### Step 3.7: Cart Open + 6h - X Spots Left + Bonus
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Add one bonus you didn't mention... And, the benefits of that bonus" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | 60min update sent |
| **Output** | Scarcity + additional bonus |
| **Guardrails** | "This should close out the offer" |
| **Decision Rule** | Example: "Convenience - extended hours" |

#### Step 3.8: Cart Open + 12h - Sold Out
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "You let everyone know. It shows the promo was justified" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Sold out |
| **Output** | Sold out notification |
| **Guardrails** | Validates scarcity |
| **Decision Rule** | Sets stage for next Fast Cash Play |

#### Step 3.9: Next Day - Back Out (Optional)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "If you have someone back out" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Customer backs out |
| **Output** | One spot left text |
| **Guardrails** | Genuine back-out only |
| **Decision Rule** | "If they had payment ready and just got there a little too late, get permission to notify them if a spot opens up" |

---

### PHASE IV: FULFILLMENT & FOLLOW-UP

#### Step 4.1: Deliver The Stuff
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Deliver the stuff" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Unscalable by design |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Sales completed |

| **Guardrails** | "You. Will. Work. More. For. These. Customers. You will earn that money" |

#### Step 4.2: Collect 4Rs
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | "Collect the 4Rs at the end: Reviews, Results, Referrals, and Resells" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution + Relationship |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |

| **Precondition** | Delivery completed |
| **Output** | 4Rs captured |
| **Guardrails** | Systematize collection |

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Audience Selection
```yaml
rule: AUDIENCE_INCLUSION
trigger: Building Fast Cash list
condition:
  - IF customer_status == "current" THEN INCLUDE
  - IF customer_status == "past_good_standing" THEN INCLUDE
  - IF lead_status == "engaged" AND has_permission THEN INCLUDE
  - IF no_contact_6_months == true THEN EXCLUDE
action: "Exclude Cooled-Off Leads... consider excluding them from this offer but start warming them up for the next one"
confidence: HIGH (source: Important Points, p.13)
```

### DR-002: Price Setting
```yaml
rule: PREMIUM_PRICING
trigger: Setting Fast Cash price
condition:
  - IF goal == "max_cash" THEN price = avg_cart_value * 10 TO 50
  - IF goal == "volume" THEN price = lower_multiple + scale_features
action: "Take whatever your average cart value... and add a zero. And if you want to get frisky, multiply it by five"
confidence: HIGH (source: What to charge, p.8)
```

### DR-003: Quantity Cap
```yaml
rule: SCARCITY_LIMIT
trigger: Setting Fast Cash quantity
condition:
  - IF customer_count < 100 THEN limit = "handful" (private, personal appeal)
  - IF customer_count >= 100 THEN limit = 5-10% of customers
  - IF fulfillment_constrains THEN limit = fulfillment_capacity
action: "Cap it to a number where you will absolutely sell out"
confidence: HIGH (source: How many to sell, p.8)
```

### DR-004: Selling Method Selection
```yaml
rule: SALES_PATH
trigger: Choosing consult vs auto checkout
condition:
  - IF price == "high" AND sales_team_capacity == true THEN use_consult_path
  - IF price == "high" AND brand_strength == "very_strong" THEN allow_auto_checkout
  - IF sales_team == "limited" THEN spread_consults_over_7_days
action: "For most businesses, high price points deserve a one-on-one consultation"
confidence: HIGH (source: How to sell it, p.8)
```

### DR-005: Bonus Deployment
```yaml
rule: BONUS_TIMING
trigger: Releasing bonuses in sequence
condition:
  - Bonus 1: Release Day 5 (consult) or Day 2 (auto) - "first additional bonus"
  - Bonus 2: Release Day 2 (consult) or +6h (auto) - "second bonus"
  - Bonus 3: Release 24h out (consult) or cart open (auto) - "best bonus"
action: "Layer in these bonuses one at a time to increase the likelihood people buy"
confidence: HIGH (source: Description, p.7-8)
```

### DR-006: Quarterly Cadence
```yaml
rule: FAST_CASH_FREQUENCY
trigger: Scheduling next Fast Cash Play
condition:
  - IF quarter_elapsed THEN schedule_next_fast_cash
  - IF list_fatigue_concerns THEN extend_to_6_months
action: "Once a quarter is the sweet spot"
confidence: HIGH (source: 5 Reasons, p.15)
```

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: Not Selling Out Fast Enough
**Trigger:** "If you haven't sold out, or at least a substantial percentage" by midpoint
**Action:** "Consider adding things to the offer to make it more compelling before sending the remaining emails and texts"
**Source:** p.19 Sample Email section

### Exception 2: Too Many Bad Leads on List
**Trigger:** Cold leads who haven't been contacted in 6+ months
**Action:** "Consider excluding them from this offer but start warming them up for the next one. For now, just stick with existing customers and past customers in good standing."
**Source:** p.13 Important Points

### Exception 3: Limited Sales Staff
**Trigger:** Cannot handle all consults in compressed timeframe
**Action:** "Make your thing available for purchase day one, but drive people to book appointments. This way you can spread out the consults and see everyone, even with a limited sales staff (which is sometimes just you)"
**Source:** p.8 How to sell it

### Exception 4: No Cards on File
**Trigger:** Need to collect payment but don't have card info
**Action:** "Just call them up to collect their card immediately after they respond"
**Source:** p.8 How to sell it

### Exception 5: Customer Backs Out After Purchase
**Trigger:** Paid customer cancels
**Action:** Send "one spot left" notification to waitlist: "If they had payment ready and just got there a little too late, get permission to notify them if a spot opens up - and charge them if it does"
**Source:** p.10-11 Both sequences

### Exception 6: Over-Demand (Waitlist Management)
**Trigger:** More buyers than spots
**Action:** "I'd rather you sell out and then waitlist people who already tried to buy"
**Source:** p.10 Note

## Part 9: Validation

### Fast Cash Quality Gates

| Gate | Threshold | Action if Failed |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| List Warmth | No contacts >6 months cold | Exclude cold leads |
| Offer Value | 10x+ unscalable value | Add more premium elements |
| Price Premium | 10x-50x current price | Increase price or add value |
| Scarcity Reality | 5-10% of customer base | Adjust limit to ensure sellout |
| Material Readiness | All emails/texts prepped | Complete before launch |
| Capacity Verification | Can deliver to all buyers | Confirm or reduce limit |

### Campaign Performance Standards

| Metric | Minimum | Target | Exceptional |
|--------|---------|--------|-------------|
| Sell-out | Yes (all spots) | <50% time | <25% time |
| Customer Take Rate | 5% | 10% | 15%+ |
| Gross Margin | 80% | 90% | 95% |
| Email Open Rate | 30% | 50% | 70% |
| 4Rs Collection | 50% | 75% | 90% |

```yaml
# Fast Cash Squad Blueprint
# Pattern: HO-SB-001 (Hormozi Squad Blueprint Standard)
# Source: $100M Playbook: Fast Cash - Alex Hormozi
# Version: 1.0.0
# Generated: 2026-02-10

squad:
  name: fast-cash
  purpose: "Generate maximum cash in shortest time from warmest audiences via premium limited-time offers"
  domain: revenue-acceleration
  source_playbook: "$100M Playbook: Fast Cash"

  core_equation: |
    Fast Cash Revenue = Number Sold x Premium Price
    10x The 10% Rule: If 10% of customers pay 10x price = 2x revenue
    Impact: "~15% of annual revenue = nearly half my profit"

# ===============================================================================
# TIER STRUCTURE
# ===============================================================================

tier_structure:
  orchestrator:
    - agent: fast-cash-coordinator
      role: "Orchestrate end-to-end Fast Cash Play execution"
      decisions:
        - "Timing of quarterly Fast Cash Plays"
        - "Target audience selection and exclusions"
        - "Escalation when sales velocity insufficient"
      kpis:
        - "Campaign revenue"
        - "Sell-out velocity"
        - "Gross margin (target: 90%+)"

  tier_0_diagnosis:
    - agent: list-curator
      role: "Assemble and validate warm audience lists"
      inputs:
        - "Customer database"
        - "Purchase history"
        - "Contact permissions"
      outputs:
        - "Segmented target list"
        - "Exclusion list (cold leads)"
        - "List warmth score"

    - agent: offer-architect
      role: "Design ultra-premium unscalable value stacks"
      inputs:
        - "Current offer catalog"
        - "Customer value preferences"
        - "Fulfillment capacity"
      outputs:
        - "Core offer components (1-3)"
        - "Three layered bonuses"
        - "Price point recommendation (10x-50x)"

  tier_1_execution:
    - agent: sequence-engine
      role: "Execute email/text campaign sequences"
      specialization: "Push to Consult & Push to Auto Checkout paths"
      capabilities:
        - "7-day consult sequence execution"
        - "5-day auto checkout sequence execution"
        - "Bonus layering at specified intervals"
        - "Real-time sales update messaging"

    - agent: scarcity-manager
      role: "Monitor and communicate scarcity authentically"
      responsibilities:
        - "Track spots remaining in real-time"
        - "Trigger scarcity messages at thresholds"
        - "Manage waitlist for sold-out offers"
        - "Handle back-out notifications"

  tier_2_judgment:
    - agent: offer-optimizer
      role: "Adjust offer mid-campaign if velocity insufficient"
      triggers:
        - "Less than 50% sold by midpoint"
        - "Open rates below threshold"
        - "Low consult booking rate"
      techniques:
        - "Add additional bonuses"
        - "Enhance value proposition"
        - "Extend deadline strategically"

    - agent: fulfillment-coordinator
      role: "Ensure premium delivery capacity and execution"
      responsibilities:
        - "Verify fulfillment capacity pre-campaign"
        - "Schedule premium service delivery"
        - "Coordinate 4Rs collection post-delivery"
        - "Maintain premium experience standards"

    - agent: cadence-keeper
      role: "Maintain quarterly rhythm and cooldown periods"
      responsibilities:
        - "Schedule next Fast Cash 90 days out"
        - "Monitor list fatigue indicators"
        - "Coordinate warmup for next campaign"
        - "Track annual Fast Cash performance"

# ===============================================================================
# AGENT DEFINITIONS
# ===============================================================================

agents:
  fast-cash-coordinator:
    id: fast-cash-coordinator
    title: "Fast Cash Play Orchestrator"
    tier: orchestrator
    icon: "💰"

    purpose: |
      Orchestrate quarterly Fast Cash Plays to extract maximum revenue from
      warm audiences. "Cash is reality" - ensure the business always has
      get-out-of-jail-free cards ready.

    core_principles:
      - name: "Revenue vs Profit vs Cash"
        quote: "Revenue is vanity. Profit is sanity. Cash is reality."
        source: "p.1"
      - name: "10x The 10%"
        quote: "If you get 10% of your customers to pay 10x the price...you double your revenue"
        source: "p.5"
      - name: "Quarterly Cadence"
        quote: "I've found that once a quarter is the sweet spot"
        source: "p.15"

    decision_authority:
      - "Campaign launch timing"
      - "Target audience composition"
      - "Price point approval"
      - "Offer structure validation"
      - "Mid-campaign adjustments"

    inputs:
      - "Customer database metrics"
      - "Quarterly revenue goals"
      - "Fulfillment capacity"
      - "Previous campaign performance"

    outputs:
      - "Campaign launch decision"
      - "Resource allocation"
      - "Performance reports"
      - "Next campaign scheduling"

    success_metrics:
      primary:
        - name: "Campaign Revenue"
          target: "$30,000-$60,000 per campaign"
          source: "Story: 'The average business collected an extra $30,000 in cash'"
        - name: "Sell-Out"
          target: "100% of spots filled"
        - name: "Gross Margin"
          target: "90%+"
          source: "'My Fast Cash Plays run at least 90% gross margins'"
      secondary:
        - "Sell-out velocity (<50% campaign duration)"
        - "Customer take rate (5-15%)"
        - "4Rs collection rate"

  list-curator:
    id: list-curator
    title: "Warm Audience Curator"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "📋"

    purpose: |
      Assemble the highest-quality warm audience list for Fast Cash campaigns.
      Exclude cooled-off leads to maintain campaign effectiveness.

    audience_segments:
      existing_customers:
        definition: "Currently paying customers"
        priority: 1
        action: "Always include"
        source: "p.4, p.7"

      previous_customers:
        definition: "Past customers in good standing"
        priority: 2
        action: "Include if relationship warm"
        source: "p.4, p.7"

      engaged_leads:
        definition: "Leads who've given explicit permission to contact"
        priority: 3
        action: "Include if recently engaged"
        source: "p.4"

      cooled_off_leads:
        definition: "No contact in 6+ months"
        priority: "EXCLUDE"
        action: "Exclude from this campaign, warm up for next"
        source: "p.13 - 'if your list has neglected leads - aka - you haven't sent them anything for six months or more, consider excluding them'"

    outputs:
      - "Primary target list"
      - "Exclusion list with reasons"
      - "Warmth score per segment"
      - "Estimated take rate"

    guardrails:
      - "Only include those with explicit contact permission"
      - "Verify contact information accuracy"
      - "Segment by customer value for personalization"

  offer-architect:
    id: offer-architect
    title: "Ultra-Premium Offer Designer"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "🎨"

    purpose: |
      Design offers that make customers think "holy sh*t" - ultra-premium
      value stacks using unscalable elements that justify 10x-50x pricing.

    value_categories:
      attention:
        description: "1 on 1 attention from you, or senior persons in the company"
        variant: "Many on 1: team supports one customer"
        premium_level: HIGH
        source: "p.7"

      personalization:
        description: "Personalized, customized versions of your standard solutions"
        premium_level: HIGH
        source: "p.7"

      convenience:
        description: "24/7 support, extended hours, exclusive times"
        premium_level: MEDIUM
        source: "p.7"

      status:
        description: "Special parking, perks, badges, public recognition"
        premium_level: MEDIUM
        source: "p.7"

      duration:
        description: "Longer duration than standard solutions. Think six months to a year"
        premium_level: HIGH
        source: "p.7"

      speed:
        description: "First in line. Priority. Fast response time promises (<10 min or less)"
        premium_level: HIGH
        source: "p.7"

      experience:
        description: "'White Glove' service. Personal cell phone access. A concierge line. Nice dinners. Nice drinks. Gifts"
        premium_level: VERY_HIGH
        source: "p.7"

      access:
        description: "In-person experiences. Retreats. Normally restricted areas. Behind the scenes"
        premium_level: VERY_HIGH
        source: "p.8"

      network:
        description: "Connection with other top customers (where applicable)"
        premium_level: HIGH
        source: "p.8"

      secrets:
        description: "Exclusive bonuses. Trade secrets. Access to vendors you have vetted. Think 'Secret menu' 'Black book'"
        premium_level: HIGH
        source: "p.8"

    offer_structure:
      core_components:
        count: "1-3"
        description: "Main unscalable value propositions"
        source: "p.8 - 'You will want to have one to three core components of your offer'"

      bonuses:
        count: 3
        strategy: "Layer in one at a time"
        timing:
          bonus_1: "Day 5 (consult) or Day 2 (auto)"
          bonus_2: "Day 2 (consult) or +6h (auto)"
          bonus_3: "24h out (consult) or cart open (auto)"
        source: "p.8 - 'we'll layer in these bonuses one at a time to increase the likelihood people buy'"

      best_bonus_rule: "This should be worth more than the entire price tag"
      source: "p.10"

    pricing_framework:
      base_calculation: "Current average cart value"
      multiplier_range: "10x to 50x"
      quote: "Take whatever your average cart value... and add a zero. And if you want to get frisky, multiply it by five"
      source: "p.8"
      validation: "The only thing that should shock them as much as the price is the value that goes with it"

    examples:
      b2c_fitness:
        price: "$10,000"
        offer: "1 on 1 Year Long 'Total Transformation' Package"
        core: "Tailored Supplements. Meals. Workouts. Photoshoot. The works."
        bonuses:
          - "Nutrition plan designed for a year + meal prep company intro"
          - "Workouts with you 1 on 1 three times per week"
          - "24/7 personal cell phone access"
        source: "p.12"

      b2b_agency:
        price: "$50,000/year"
        offer: "1 Year Personal Brand Explosion. Aka 'Get Famous' Package"
        core: "Script. Film. Edit. Post. All content. 4x per year."
        bonuses:
          - "Additional Social Media Platform"
          - "Lead Magnet creation"
          - "Organic funnel built with video sales letters"
        source: "p.12"

      recurring_max:
        price: "Monthly Price x 12"
        offer: "1 Year to [ULTIMATE RESULT]"
        bonuses:
          - "Custom work on the thing they struggle with"
          - "Thing that makes it faster for them"
          - "Thing that makes it virtually guaranteed they achieve it"
        note: "Typically you need to offer little else beyond the bonuses to get 10% to say yes"
        source: "p.12"

  sequence-engine:
    id: sequence-engine
    title: "Campaign Sequence Executor"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "📧"

    purpose: |
      Execute email and text sequences that build tension, release bonuses
      strategically, and drive urgency. "The texts draw attention to the emails."

    philosophy: |
      "I use a seven-day campaign so I meet with everyone to close them.
      Any longer and it loses urgency. Any shorter and I miss out on sales."

    sequence_paths:
      push_to_consult:
        duration: "7 days"
        use_case: "High price points, limited sales staff"
        strategy: "Spread appointments over campaign window"

        timeline:
          day_7:
            action: "Primer text"
            content: "Let them know something big is coming"
            source: "p.9"

          day_6:
            action: "Announcement email + text"
            content: "1-3 core components, price indication, deadline"
            cta: "Schedule consult"
            source: "p.9"

          day_5:
            action: "Recap email"
            bonus_release: "Bonus 1 (Status type)"
            source: "p.9"

          day_3:
            action: "Sales update email + text"
            content: "How many sold, how many left, first-come-first-serve"
            source: "p.9"

          day_2:
            action: "X Spots Left email + text"
            bonus_release: "Bonus 2 (Secrets type)"
            source: "p.10"

          day_1_am:
            action: "Warning email + text"
            bonus_release: "Bonus 3 (Best - Access type)"
            source: "p.10"

          day_1_pm:
            action: "Sold out notification"
            source: "p.10"

          optional:
            action: "Back-out notification"
            trigger: "Customer cancels"
            source: "p.10"

      push_to_auto_checkout:
        duration: "5 days"
        use_case: "Very strong brand, can create stampede"
        strategy: "Build tension, stampede at cart open"

        timeline:
          day_5:
            action: "Primer text"
            content: "Something big coming"
            source: "p.10"

          day_4:
            action: "Announcement email + text"
            content: "Core components, price"
            source: "p.10"

          day_2:
            action: "48h warning email + text"
            bonus_release: "Bonus 1 (Personalization type)"
            content: "Set alarm, first-come-first-serve"
            source: "p.10"

          day_1_60min:
            action: "Final prep text"
            content: "Have payment ready"
            source: "p.10"

          cart_open:
            action: "Cart open email + text"
            bonus_release: "Bonus 3 (Best - Experience type, immediate benefit)"
            source: "p.10-11"

          cart_60min:
            action: "Sales update"
            content: "How many sold, how many left"
            source: "p.11"

          cart_6h:
            action: "X Spots Left + surprise bonus"
            bonus_release: "Unlisted bonus (Convenience type)"
            content: "This should close out the offer"
            source: "p.11"

          cart_12h:
            action: "Sold out notification"
            source: "p.11"

          next_day:
            action: "Back-out notification"
            trigger: "Customer cancels"
            source: "p.11"

    email_subjects:
      - "We need to talk"
      - "best. deal. ever. [for 10 people only]"
      - "how to [get dream result] and save money doing it"
      - "2 spots left + game changer"
      - "Saving $XXX ends tonight. Don't kick yourself tomorrow."
      - "RE: your goals we set"
      source: "p.21-26"

    text_pairing: |
      "I like pairing texts with emails. The texts draw attention to the emails.
      The emails give the details. Pretty simple."
      source: "p.19"

  scarcity-manager:
    id: scarcity-manager
    title: "Scarcity & Urgency Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "⏰"

    purpose: |
      Manage authentic scarcity and urgency throughout the campaign.
      "You want to sell out fast. This makes your Fast Cash offer even more
      compelling the next time you make it...selling out even faster."

    scarcity_elements:
      spots_limit:
        calculation: "5-10% of customer base"
        rationale: "Cap it to a number where you will absolutely sell out"
        source: "p.8"

      time_limit:
        consult_path: "7 days or until sold out"
        auto_path: "~12 hours from cart open"
        source: "p.9-11"

    communication_triggers:
      sales_update:
        trigger: "After first 2-3 sales"
        content: "How many sold already, how many left"
        source: "p.9, p.11"

      x_spots_left:
        trigger: "2-3 spots remaining"
        content: "Spots running out"
        source: "p.10, p.11"

      sold_out:
        trigger: "All spots filled"
        content: "Shows the promo was justified"
        source: "p.10, p.11"

      back_out:
        trigger: "Customer cancels"
        content: "One spot opened up"
        source: "p.10, p.11"

    waitlist_management:
      rule: "I'd rather you sell out and then waitlist people who already tried to buy"
      process: "If they had payment ready and just got there a little too late, get permission to notify them if a spot opens up"
      action: "charge them if it does"
      source: "p.11"

  offer-optimizer:
    id: offer-optimizer
    title: "Mid-Campaign Offer Optimizer"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "🔧"

    purpose: |
      Monitor campaign velocity and adjust offer if not selling fast enough.
      "Consider adding things to the offer to make it more compelling."

    intervention_triggers:
      - trigger: "Less than 50% sold by campaign midpoint"
        source: "p.19 - 'If you haven't sold out, or at least a substantial percentage'"
        action: "Add value to offer"

      - trigger: "Low open rates"
        action: "Adjust subject lines or send times"

      - trigger: "High opens, low clicks"

quality_gates:
  QG-001:
    name: "List Warmth Gate"
    transition: "Pre-launch → Launch"
    condition: "No leads with >6 months no contact"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Exclude cold leads, start warming for next campaign"
    source: "p.13"

  QG-002:
    name: "Offer Value Gate"
    transition: "Design → Launch"
    condition: "offer_includes_unscalable_elements AND price >= 10x_current"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Add premium elements or reduce quantity"
    source: "p.7-8"

  QG-003:
    name: "Material Readiness Gate"
    transition: "Prep → Launch"
    condition: "all_emails_ready AND all_texts_ready AND bonuses_defined"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Complete all materials"
    source: "p.13"

  QG-004:
    name: "Capacity Gate"
    transition: "Pre-launch → Launch"
    condition: "fulfillment_capacity >= spots_offered"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Reduce spots or add capacity"
    source: "p.8"

  QG-005:
    name: "Velocity Gate"
    transition: "Midpoint → Continuation"
    condition: "sold_percentage >= 50%"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Add value to offer"
    source: "p.19"

  QG-006:
    name: "Cooldown Gate"
    transition: "Post-campaign → Next campaign"
    condition: "days_since_last_campaign >= 90"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Wait for cooldown period"
    source: "p.15"

            output: "Enhanced offer"

      - phase: "Fulfillment"

            output: "Service delivered"

      - phase: "Cooldown"

      - "List too cold"
      - "Messaging not resonating"
    diagnosis:

    solutions:

      - "Enhance messaging urgency"
    source: "p.19"

  - symptom: "High opens, low conversions"
    possible_causes:
      - "Offer unclear"
      - "Price shock without value shock"
      - "CTA friction"

      - "Test different CTAs"
    solutions:
      - "Clarify value proposition"
      - "Add payment flexibility (card on file)"
      - "Simplify booking process"

  - symptom: "Customers backing out"
    possible_causes:

      - "Delivery concerns"
      - "Financial overextension"
    diagnosis:
      - "Review back-out reasons"
      - "Check delivery communication"
    solutions:
      - "Improve onboarding"
      - "Send reassurance content"
      - "Offer payment plan (if appropriate)"

  - symptom: "List fatigue"
    possible_causes:
      - "Too frequent campaigns"
      - "Insufficient value content between campaigns"
      - "Scarcity credibility damaged"
    diagnosis:
      - "Review campaign frequency"
      - "Check engagement trends"
    solutions:

      - "Increase value content"
      - "Rebuild scarcity credibility"
    source: "p.15"
```

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/goated-ads-sop.md

# SOP: GOATed Ads Framework

> Extraído de: $100M GOATed Ads Playbook + Checklist de Ads ($50M testados)
> Versão: 1.0
> Data: 2026-02-10
> Extrator: SOP Extractor Agent

---

## 1. Propósito

Criar 150-750 anúncios por semana usando o processo de montagem de ads que permite escalar campanhas além do "teto de saturação" através de volume e qualidade de criativos.

**Insight Central:**
> "You haven't saturated Facebook. But you have gotten all the low hanging fruit. You've hit a wall with your ad quality, not with the market."

---

## 2. Escopo

**Aplica-se a:**
- Facebook/Meta Ads
- YouTube Ads
- TikTok Ads
- LinkedIn Ads
- Qualquer plataforma de paid media com video/imagem

**NÃO aplica-se a:**
- Google Search Ads (texto puro)
- Ads sem capacidade de teste A/B
- Orçamentos <$50/dia por conjunto

---

## 3. Pré-condições

### Matemática Fundamental
- [ ] CAC máximo calculado (LTGP ÷ 3)
- [ ] Break-even em dias definido (ideal: <30)
- [ ] Budget teste = 10x CPA esperado
- [ ] Margem mínima: 30% após ads

### Pesquisa de Mercado
- [ ] 10 concorrentes analisados no Ad Library
- [ ] 5 ângulos funcionando identificados
- [ ] 3 ofertas dominantes mapeadas
- [ ] Gaps no mercado documentados

### Avatar Cirúrgico
- [ ] Dor #1 identificada (a que tira sono)
- [ ] Linguagem exata coletada (prints de comentários)
- [ ] Nível de awareness medido (1-5)
- [ ] Poder de compra validado

---

## 4. O Processo de Montagem de Ads (Ad Assembly)

### Visão Geral

```
50 Hooks × 3-5 Meats × 1-3 CTAs = 150-750 Ads/semana
```

### Distribuição de Tempo

| Componente | % do Tempo | Justificativa |
|------------|------------|---------------|
| Hooks | 80% | Se não passa do hook, nada mais importa |
| Meat | 20% | Menos pessoas veem, rotaciona menos |
| CTAs | ~0% | Uma vez definido, reutiliza |

### Frequência

- **Sexta-feira:** Dia dedicado a advertising
- **Cadência:** Semanal (mínimo)
- **Output:** 150+ ads/semana

---

## 5. STEP 1: Criar 50 Hooks (80% do esforço)

### 5.1 Níveis de Awareness (Eugene Schwartz)

| Nível | Descrição | Tipo de Hook | Tamanho Audiência |
|-------|-----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 5 | Most Aware | Oferta | Menor (quente) |
| 4 | Product-Aware | Prova | ↓ |
| 3 | Solution-Aware | Promessa | ↓ |
| 2 | Problem-Aware | Dor | ↓ |
| 1 | Unaware | Curiosidade | Maior (frio) |

### 5.2 Templates por Nível

**Nível 5 - Most Aware (Oferta):**
```
"50% off nosso [PRODUTO] mais vendido até [DATA]"
"[PRODUTO]: Nova fórmula com 25% mais [BENEFÍCIO]"
```

**Nível 4 - Product-Aware (Prova):**
```
"Descubra por que 10.000 pessoas escolheram [PRODUTO] no último mês"
"Veja como [PRODUTO] aumentou ROI em 150% para 5 indústrias"
```

**Nível 3 - Solution-Aware (Promessa):**
```
"O jeito mais rápido de [RESULTADO] - apresentando [PRODUTO]"
"Dobre suas vendas em 6 meses com nossa estratégia"
```

**Nível 2 - Problem-Aware (Dor):**
```
"Cansado de [PROBLEMA ESPECÍFICO]? Existe um jeito melhor"
"Seu site não está vendendo? Você pode estar perdendo esses elementos"
```

**Nível 1 - Unaware (Curiosidade):**
```
"O perigo escondido na sua rotina que está custando [$/tempo/saúde]"
"O jeito inesperado que seu negócio está perdendo $1000s/mês"
```

### 5.3 Fontes de Hooks (Ordem de Prioridade)

1. **Hooks vencedores de ads anteriores** — Reutilize winners
2. **Hooks de conteúdo orgânico próprio** — Longs, shorts, tweets, emails
3. **Hooks de ads de outros** — Salve em álbum no celular
4. **Hooks de conteúdo viral de outros** — Views = validação
5. **Ad Libraries** — Último recurso (difícil saber o que funciona)

### 5.4 Regras de Distribuição

```yaml
DR-001:
  rule: "Se 90% dos hooks estão em 'Most Aware', espalhe para capturar fatia maior"
  action: "Na dúvida, vá um pouco mais broad"
  reason: "Você ainda pega audiência quente + atrai audiência fria"
```

### 5.5 Pro Tip: Memes

> "Memes or meme-like content attract the largest percentage of your audience."

Para nichos específicos, use memes culture-specific como moth to a flame.

---

## 6. STEP 2: Criar 3-5 Meats (20% do esforço)

### 6.1 Os 5 Formatos de Ad Meat

| # | Formato | Exemplos | Quando Usar |
|---|---------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | **Demonstration** | Unboxing, before/after, hero ads | Produto físico, resultado visual |
| 2 | **Testimonial** | UGC, podcast, parade of proof | Prova social forte |
| 3 | **Education** | Whiteboard, how-to, explainer | Solução complexa |
| 4 | **Story** | Lifestyle, documentary, manifesto | Conexão emocional |
| 5 | **Faceless** | Screenshots, text, animations | Sem apresentador, baixo custo |

### 6.2 Detalhamento dos Formatos

**1. Demonstration Ads:**
- Live use ou reactions
- Unboxing
- Comparisons (before/after)
- High production hero ads (Dollar Shave Club, Old Spice)
- Service demonstration (mostrar resultado)

**2. Testimonial Ads:**
- User-generated content (UGC)
- Direct to camera
- Podcast style (clipes de entrevistas)
- Professional testimonials
- Raw iPhone style
- Walk 'n talk rants
- Group testimonials (muitas pessoas no frame)
- Lifecycle ads
- Man-on-the-street interviews
- Influencer collabs
- **Parade of Proof** — Múltiplos depoimentos em sequência

**3. Education Ads:**
- Explainer videos
- How-to listicles
- Whiteboard explainer
- High performing organic content repurposed

**4. Story Ads:**
- Storytelling/narrative
- Lifestyle
- Warnings and opportunities
- Documentary style
- Skits
- Brand manifestos
- Problem-solution

**5. Faceless Ads:**
- Screenshots de comentários/textos de clientes
- Text only
- Slide shows
- Animations
- Cartoon ads
- Visual effect based ads

---

## 7. STEP 3: Criar 1-3 CTAs (~0% do esforço)

### 7.1 Anatomia de um CTA Completo

| Elemento | Descrição | Exemplo |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| **O que fazer** | Ação específica | "Aproveite essa oferta" |
| **Como fazer** | Instrução clara | "tocando no botão abaixo" |
| **Quando fazer** | Urgência | "antes que expire" |
| **O que ganha** | Benefício | "e receba $1000 em bônus grátis" |
| **O que acontece** | Próximo passo | "entregue direto no seu email" |

### 7.2 Exemplos de CTAs

```
"Start free on the next page"
"Grab your 14-day free trial on the next page"
"Get started on the next page free"
```

### 7.3 Regra de Ouro

> **Clear > Clever**

- S-P-E-L-L it out: Click, Call, Reply, Go, Scan
- **Show AND Tell:** Demonstre visualmente o que acontece ao clicar

### 7.4 Demonstração Visual

- Mostre a tela que aparece quando clicam
- Mostre onde preenchem informação
- Mostre o processo de submit
- Crie congruência total entre ad e landing page

---

## 8. Estrutura de Vídeo (Timing)

```
0-3s:   HOOK (Pattern interrupt)
3-10s:  Agitar problema
10-20s: Apresentar solução
20-27s: Prova social
27-30s: CTA claro
```

### Elementos do Hook (Primeiros 3 Segundos)

- [ ] Problema específico mencionado
- [ ] Número na primeira linha
- [ ] Pattern interrupt visual
- [ ] Avatar falando com avatar

---

## 9. Regras de Decisão

```yaml
# Hooks
DR-001: "90% hooks em Most Aware → espalhar para níveis mais frios"
DR-002: "Na dúvida, vá um pouco mais broad"
DR-003: "Hooks vencedores podem ser reutilizados indefinidamente"

# Testing
DR-004: "Testar 3 meats idênticos com hooks diferentes para isolar variável"
DR-005: "Testar 3 CTAs idênticos com mesmo hook+meat para otimizar"
DR-006: "80% resultado vem de 20% dos ads"

# Scale
DR-007: "Creative fatigue = 10-14 dias"
DR-008: "Nunca scale sem 100 conversões"
DR-009: "Regra 20%: Aumenta budget 20% a cada 48h"

# Kill Signals
DR-010: "CTR <0.5% = MATA"
DR-011: "CPA dobrou = PAUSA"
DR-012: "Frequência >10 = REFRESH"
DR-013: "ROAS <2x por 3 dias = ANÁLISE"
```

---

## 10. Métricas e KPIs

### KPIs Dia 1 (Primeiras 24h)

| Métrica | Threshold | Se Não Bater |
|---------|-----------|--------------|
| CTR | >1% | Hook ruim |
| CPM | <$30 | Criativo ruim |
| CPC | <$3 | Relevância baixa |
| Link CTR | >0.8% | Copy fraca |

### KPIs Dia 2

| Métrica | Threshold | Se Não Bater |
|---------|-----------|--------------|
| Frequência | <2 | Saturação |
| CPL | <50% do target | Mata e recomeça |
| Add to Cart | >5% | Página quebrada |
| Video Views 3s | >30% | Hook fraco |

### Regra de Decisão Rápida

> "Não bateu? Mata e recomeça. Sem ego."

---

## 11. Fluxo de Otimização Semanal

### Semana 1
- [ ] Matar ads com CPA >150% do target
- [ ] Duplicar budget dos vencedores
- [ ] Testar 3 novos criativos
- [ ] Ajustar bid cap se necessário

### Semana 2
- [ ] Criar lookalike dos compradores
- [ ] Testar novo ângulo de copy
- [ ] Adicionar retargeting
- [ ] Implementar exclusões de audiência

### Semana 3-4
- [ ] Scale vertical (aumentar budget 20%/dia)
- [ ] Scale horizontal (novas audiências)
- [ ] Testar novos formatos (carousel, collection)
- [ ] Adicionar novos geos/demos

---

## 12. Scale Matrix

### Sinais de Ready to Scale

- [ ] ROAS >3x por 7 dias seguidos
- [ ] CPA estável por 500+ conversões
- [ ] Frequência <3 após 14 dias
- [ ] CTR mantém >1%

### Como Escalar

| Método | Descrição |
|--------|-----------|
| **Regra 20%** | Aumenta budget 20% a cada 48h |
| **Novos conjuntos** | Mesma copy, nova audiência |
| **Surfing** | Pausa sexta, reativa segunda |
| **Day-parting** | Desliga madrugada se B2B |

---

## 13. Troubleshooting

### CPM Alto
- [ ] Criativo cansou (frequência >7)
- [ ] Relevance score <6
- [ ] Competição aumentou (Q4, Black Friday)
- [ ] Conta com penalidade

### CPA Subindo
- [ ] Página convertendo menos
- [ ] Oferta perdeu força
- [ ] Competidor com oferta melhor
- [ ] Mudança no algoritmo

### CTR Baixo
- [ ] Hook fraco
- [ ] Visual genérico
- [ ] Copy não ressoa
- [ ] Saturação de mercado

---

## 14. Budget Allocation Framework

```
70% = Campanhas provadas (winners)
20% = Testes novos (exploration)
10% = Retargeting
```

---

## 15. Red Flags Imediatos

| Sinal | Ação |
|-------|------|
| CPA dobrou | **PAUSA** |
| CTR <0.5% | **MATA** |
| Frequência >10 | **REFRESH** |
| ROAS <2x por 3 dias | **ANÁLISE** |
| Relevance score <4 | **NOVO CRIATIVO** |

---

## 16. Checklist de Campanha

### Configuração
- [ ] CBO ligado (deixa algoritmo trabalhar)
- [ ] 3-5 conjuntos de anúncios máximo
- [ ] Budget mínimo: $50/dia por conjunto
- [ ] Pixel instalado e eventos configurados

### Segmentação
- [ ] Broad targeting (3-10% da população)
- [ ] SEM interesses empilhados
- [ ] Idade: range de 10 anos mínimo
- [ ] Lookalike 1% da lista de clientes

### Copy
- [ ] Headline: Resultado específico + tempo
- [ ] Primary text: <125 caracteres
- [ ] Descrição: Benefício principal
- [ ] CTA: Verbos de ação (Garantir, Começar, Acessar)

### Landing Page
- [ ] Headline match com ad (exata)
- [ ] CTA em <3 segundos de scroll
- [ ] Prova social visível
- [ ] Tempo de carregamento <2s
- [ ] Taxa de conversão mínima: 2%

---

## 17. Checklist Diário (5 min)

- [ ] CPA ontem vs hoje
- [ ] Frequência <5
- [ ] Comentários respondidos
- [ ] Competidores checados
- [ ] Budget utilization >90%

---

## 18. Regras de Ouro

1. **Nunca scale sem 100 conversões**
2. **Creative fatigue = 10-14 dias**
3. **80% do resultado vem de 20% dos ads**
4. **Teste preço antes de mudar tudo**
5. **iOS mata 30% do tracking (calcule isso)**

---

## 19. Output do Processo

### Por Sessão de Gravação (Sexta-feira)

| Componente | Quantidade | Tempo |
|------------|------------|-------|
| Hooks | 50 | 1-2 horas |
| Meats | 3-5 | ~1 hora |
| CTAs | 1-3 | ~5 minutos |
| **Total Ads** | **150-750** | **~3 horas** |

### Resultado Anual

```
600 ads/mês × 12 meses = 7.200 ads/ano
(vs. 60 ads/ano do método tradicional = 120x mais)
```

---

## 20. Histórico e Validação

**Caso de Referência:**
- Portfolio company: $200K/mês em ads
- Problema: "Saturação de mercado" com 5 ads/mês
- Solução: 500 ads/mês (100x mais)
- Resultado: Dobrou em 2 quarters

**Base de Dados:**
- $50M+ gastos em ads
- 5 anos de otimização
- 13 anos de desenvolvimento do processo

```yaml
# Squad Blueprint: GOATed Ads Framework
# Extracted from: $100M GOATed Ads Playbook
# Version: 1.0
# Date: 2026-02-10

squad:
  name: hormozi-ads
  purpose: "Create 150-750 ads per week using the GOATed Ads assembly process to scale paid advertising beyond the 'saturation ceiling'"
  extracted_from: "goated-ads-sop.md"

  philosophy: |
    "Six-Pack-Abs are made in the kitchen, not in the gym. And like six-packs,
    ads are made in research, not in recording."
    - 80% time on hooks, 20% on meat, ~0% on CTAs
    - Volume is the secret to finding winners
    - Better ads = bigger audience converted

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# TIER STRUCTURE
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

tier_structure:
  orchestrator:
    - ads-strategist
    # Coordinates weekly ad creation and optimization

  tier_0_research:
    - market-researcher
    - hook-hunter
    # Pre-production research and hook collection

  tier_1_creation:
    - hook-writer
    - meat-scripter
    - cta-crafter
    # Core creative production

  tier_2_execution:
    - campaign-launcher
    - performance-optimizer
    # Campaign setup and optimization

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# AGENT DEFINITIONS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

agents:
  ads-strategist:
    role: "Orchestrator"
    description: "Coordinates the GOATed Ads assembly process"
    cognitive_type: "Judgment + Synthesis"
    executor_type: "Hybrid"

    responsibilities:
      - "Define weekly ad production targets"
      - "Allocate hooks across awareness levels"
      - "Approve final ad combinations"
      - "Decide kill/scale based on metrics"

    weekly_cadence:
      friday: "Ad production day"
      daily: "5-minute performance check"
      weekly: "Optimization decisions"

    decision_rules:
      - "DR-001: 90% hooks em Most Aware → espalhar"
      - "DR-006: 80% resultado vem de 20% dos ads"
      - "DR-009: Regra 20% para scale"

  market-researcher:
    role: "Tier 0 - Research"
    description: "Analyzes competitors and market landscape"
    cognitive_type: "Analysis"
    executor_type: "Agent"

    inputs:
      - "Industry/niche"
      - "Competitor list"
      - "Ad libraries access"

    outputs:
      - "10 competitor ad analyses"
      - "5 working angles identified"
      - "3 dominant offers mapped"
      - "Market gaps documented"

    tools:
      - "Facebook Ad Library"
      - "TikTok Creative Center"
      - "YouTube Ad Transparency"

    deliverables:
      competitor_analysis:
        fields:
          - "Brand name"
          - "Hook used"
          - "Meat format"
          - "CTA style"
          - "Estimated performance"

  hook-hunter:
    role: "Tier 0 - Research"
    description: "Collects winning hooks from multiple sources"
    cognitive_type: "Perception + Analysis"
    executor_type: "Agent"

    sources_priority:
      1: "Previous winning ads (own)"
      2: "Own organic content winners"
      3: "Competitor ads"
      4: "Viral content in niche"
      5: "Ad libraries (last resort)"

    outputs:
      - "Hook swipe file (50+ per week)"
      - "Hook categorization by awareness level"
      - "Performance notes where available"

    collection_rules:
      - "Save all ads you like in phone album"
      - "Note the hook separately from the ad"
      - "Cross-industry hooks often work"

  hook-writer:
    role: "Tier 1 - Creation"
    description: "Writes 50 hooks per week across awareness levels"
    cognitive_type: "Creativity + Synthesis"
    executor_type: "Agent"

    inputs:
      - "Hook swipe file from hook-hunter"
      - "Awareness level distribution targets"
      - "Avatar language/pain points"

    outputs:
      - "50 hooks minimum per session"
      - "Distribution across 5 awareness levels"
      - "Variations of proven winners"

    frameworks:
      awareness_templates:
        most_aware: "Offer-driven hooks"
        product_aware: "Proof-driven hooks"
        solution_aware: "Promise-driven hooks"
        problem_aware: "Pain-driven hooks"
        unaware: "Curiosity-driven hooks"

    distribution_rule: |
      If 90% of hooks are in "Most Aware" bucket,
      spread them out to capture bigger slice.
      When in doubt, go a little broader.

  meat-scripter:
    role: "Tier 1 - Creation"
    description: "Creates 3-5 ad meat scripts per session"
    cognitive_type: "Creativity + Synthesis"
    executor_type: "Agent"

    inputs:
      - "Product/service details"
      - "Available assets (testimonials, demos)"
      - "Proof points"

    outputs:
      - "3-5 meat scripts"
      - "Format specification for each"
      - "Asset requirements list"

    formats:
      demonstration:
        types: ["unboxing", "before/after", "hero ad", "live use"]
        when: "Physical product, visual result"

      testimonial:
        types: ["UGC", "podcast clip", "parade of proof", "walk n talk"]
        when: "Strong social proof available"

      education:
        types: ["whiteboard", "how-to", "explainer"]
        when: "Complex solution needs explanation"

      story:
        types: ["lifestyle", "documentary", "manifesto"]
        when: "Emotional connection needed"

      faceless:
        types: ["screenshots", "text only", "animation"]
        when: "No presenter, low budget"

    video_structure:
      - "0-3s: Hook"
      - "3-10s: Agitate problem"
      - "10-20s: Present solution"
      - "20-27s: Social proof"
      - "27-30s: Clear CTA"

  cta-crafter:
    role: "Tier 1 - Creation"
    description: "Creates 1-3 CTAs per session"
    cognitive_type: "Synthesis"
    executor_type: "Worker"

    inputs:
      - "Offer details"
      - "Landing page URL"
      - "Conversion goal"

    outputs:
      - "1-3 CTA variations"
      - "Visual demonstration script"

    cta_anatomy:
      what_to_do: "Action verb"
      how_to_do: "Specific instruction"
      when_to_do: "Urgency element"
      what_they_get: "Benefit"
      what_happens_next: "Next step preview"

    principle: "Clear > Clever"

    demonstration_rule: |
      Show AND tell them what to do next.
      Demonstrate visually what happens when they click.
      Show the landing page, the form, the submit button.

  campaign-launcher:
    role: "Tier 2 - Execution"
    description: "Sets up and launches ad campaigns"
    cognitive_type: "Execution"
    executor_type: "Worker"

    inputs:
      - "Approved hook+meat+CTA combinations"
      - "Budget allocation"
      - "Audience targeting specs"

    outputs:
      - "Live campaigns"
      - "Proper tracking setup"
      - "Initial performance baseline"

    setup_checklist:
      - "CBO enabled"
      - "3-5 ad sets maximum"
      - "Budget min $50/day per ad set"
      - "Pixel + events configured"

    targeting_rules:
      - "Broad targeting (3-10% of population)"
      - "NO stacked interests"
      - "Age range: 10 years minimum"
      - "Lookalike 1% from customer list"

    math: "Broad audiences = 40% lower CPM"

  performance-optimizer:
    role: "Tier 2 - Execution"
    description: "Monitors and optimizes campaign performance"
    cognitive_type: "Analysis + Judgment"
    executor_type: "Hybrid"

    inputs:
      - "Campaign performance data"
      - "KPI thresholds"
      - "Budget constraints"

    outputs:
      - "Kill/scale decisions"
      - "Optimization recommendations"
      - "Winner identification"

    kpis_day_1:
      CTR: ">1% (else hook ruim)"
      CPM: "<$30 (else criativo ruim)"
      CPC: "<$3 (else relevância baixa)"
      link_CTR: ">0.8%"

    kpis_day_2:
      frequency: "<2"
      CPL: "<50% of target"
      add_to_cart: ">5%"
      video_views_3s: ">30%"

    decision_rules:
      kill:
        - "CTR <0.5%"
        - "CPA doubled"
        - "ROAS <2x for 3 days"
        - "Relevance score <4"

      scale:
        - "ROAS >3x for 7 days"
        - "CPA stable for 500+ conversions"
        - "Frequency <3 after 14 days"
        - "CTR maintains >1%"

      refresh:
        - "Frequency >10"
        - "Creative fatigue (10-14 days)"

    scale_methods:
      rule_20: "Increase budget 20% every 48h"
      horizontal: "Same copy, new audiences"
      surfing: "Pause Friday, reactivate Monday"
      day_parting: "Turn off overnight if B2B"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXECUTOR MATRIX
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# QUALITY GATES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

quality_gates:
  QG-001:
    name: "Pre-Launch Math Gate"
    transition: "Start → Research"
    conditions:
      - "CAC máximo calculado"
      - "Break-even definido"
      - "Budget teste = 10x CPA"
    type: "blocking"

  QG-002:
    name: "Research Completeness Gate"
    transition: "Research → Creation"
    conditions:
      - "10 competitors analyzed"
      - "Avatar language collected"
      - "Awareness level mapped"
    type: "blocking"

  QG-003:
    name: "Hook Volume Gate"
    transition: "Creation → Assembly"
    conditions:
      - "50+ hooks written"
      - "Distribution across 5 levels"
    type: "blocking"

  QG-004:
    name: "Assembly Completeness Gate"
    transition: "Assembly → Launch"
    conditions:
      - "150+ ad combinations ready"
      - "Landing page match verified"
      - "Tracking configured"
    type: "blocking"

  QG-005:
    name: "Day 1 Performance Gate"
    transition: "Launch → Continue"
    conditions:
      - "CTR >1%"
      - "CPM <$30"
    type: "warning"
    action_if_fail: "Kill and restart"

  QG-006:
    name: "Scale Readiness Gate"
    transition: "Optimize → Scale"
    conditions:
      - "ROAS >3x for 7 days"
      - "100+ conversions"
      - "CPA stable"
    type: "blocking"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# WORKFLOWS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

workflows:
  weekly_ad_production:
    trigger: "Every Friday"
    duration: "~3 hours"

    steps:
      - agent: "market-researcher"
        action: "Update competitive landscape"
        duration: "30 min"
        parallel: true

      - agent: "hook-hunter"
        action: "Collect new winning hooks"
        duration: "30 min"
        parallel: true

      - agent: "hook-writer"
        action: "Write 50 hooks"
        duration: "1-2 hours"
        gate: "QG-003"

      - agent: "meat-scripter"
        action: "Create 3-5 meat scripts"
        duration: "1 hour"

      - agent: "cta-crafter"
        action: "Create 1-3 CTAs"
        duration: "5 min"

      - agent: "ads-strategist"
        action: "Approve combinations"
        gate: "QG-004"

      - agent: "campaign-launcher"
        action: "Launch campaigns"

    output: "150-750 new ads live"

  daily_optimization:
    trigger: "Daily (5 min)"

    steps:
      - agent: "performance-optimizer"
        action: "Check KPIs"
        checks:
          - "CPA today vs yesterday"
          - "Frequency <5"
          - "Budget utilization >90%"

      - agent: "performance-optimizer"
        action: "Execute kill decisions"
        conditions:
          - "CTR <0.5% → KILL"
          - "CPA doubled → PAUSE"
          - "Frequency >10 → REFRESH"

      - agent: "ads-strategist"
        action: "Note winners for next week"

  scale_workflow:
    trigger: "When QG-006 passes"

    steps:
      - agent: "performance-optimizer"
        action: "Confirm scale readiness"
        gate: "QG-006"

      - agent: "ads-strategist"
        action: "Approve scale approach"
        options:
          - "Vertical: +20% budget every 48h"
          - "Horizontal: New audiences"
          - "Both: Combined approach"

      - agent: "campaign-launcher"
        action: "Execute scale"
        monitoring: "Daily for 2 weeks"
```
