## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/hooks-sop.md

# SOP: $100M Hooks Framework

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Hooks + FRAMEWORK HOOKS - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10
> **Cross-Reference:** See `goated-ads-sop.md` for ad creation process (hooks = 80% of ad effort)

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Double marketing results by mastering the first 5 seconds of any content, ad, or outreach. Hooks are the single variable that can instantly 5x, 10x, or 100x marketing performance without changing anything else.

**Core Insight:**
> "After you've written your headline, you've spent eighty cents of your advertising dollar." - David Ogilvy

**Business Impact:**
- Same content, same offer, same price - different hook = millions in difference (Dean Graziosi case)
- If 10 hours available for advertising, 8 hours should go to hooks
- The hook determines whether everything else matters or not

**The Dean Graziosi Proof:**
Larry King infomercial with ego-driven hook ("Tonight on Larry King, I'm here with my guest Dean Graziosi, a multi New York Times best seller...") = BOMBED. Same infomercial with audience-focused hook ("Have you ever in your adult life looked at yourself in the mirror and thought 'I should be further ahead by now?'") = Sold millions of books.

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Creating any content, ad, email, or outreach
- Optimizing existing content performance
- Testing and iterating on marketing assets
- Building hook libraries and swipe files

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- Post-hook content creation (body/meat) - see `goated-ads-sop.md` Part 6
- Landing page optimization (different discipline)
- Product/offer design (hooks sell attention, not products)

### Relationship to GOATed Ads SOP
```
GOATed Ads SOP = WHAT to do (full ad creation process)
Hooks SOP = HOW to do the 80% (deep dive into hook mastery)

Use Together:
1. This SOP for hook research, creation, testing
2. GOATed Ads SOP for assembling hooks into complete ads
```

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Spreadsheet System | Master tracker with platform tabs | Name/Hook/Views/Link columns configured |
| Performance Data | Access to analytics on at least one platform | Can see views/engagement metrics |
| Competitor Access | Can view competitor content/ads | Ad Library access, social platforms |
| Recording Capability | Can produce content to test hooks | Camera, editing, or text platform |
| Testing Mindset | Willing to test 10x more than current | "Let the data do the teaching" committed |
| Time Allocation | 80% of content creation time for hooks | Calendar blocked |

### Red Flags - NOT Ready If:
- [ ] Believes creativity is more important than data
- [ ] Not willing to "copy" what works
- [ ] Only tests 1-2 variations per piece
- [ ] No system for tracking performance
- [ ] Emotionally attached to original ideas
- [ ] Thinks hooks are "just titles"

---

## Part 4: The Hook Framework

### Core Components

```
HOOK = Call Out + Condition for Value

Call Out = Makes prospect say "This is for me"
Condition for Value = Promise of reward IF they consume
```

### The Cocktail Party Effect

> "Imagine you're at a club. Lots of people are hooting and hollering. Loud music thumping. In all that noise, a single sound pierces through it all and you turn around. Wanna know the sound? Your name."

Hooks harness this neurological mechanism. Goal: cut through noise and grab involuntary attention.

### Two Hook Types

**1. Verbal Hooks (Words)**

| Type | Description | Example |
|------|-------------|---------|
| Labels | Words your avatar identifies with | "Local business owners, I have a gift for you" |
| Questions (Yes) | Questions with obvious "yes" answer | "Would you pay $1,000 to have the business of your dreams in 30 days?" |
| Questions (Open) | Questions that create curiosity | "Which would you rather be?" |
| Conditionals | Scenarios leading to result/command | "If you're working all the time and your business isn't growing, you're working on the wrong sh*t" |
| Commands | Direct instructions | "Read this if you're tired of being broke" |
| Statements | Declarative assertions | "The smartest thing you can do today..." |
| Lists/Steps | Numbered items | "In this video I'm going to talk to you about the 28 ways to stay poor" |
| Narratives | Stories and anecdotes | "One day I was in the back and this old lady comes in and she was piss angry" |
| Exclamations | Strong emotion expressions | "Ahhhhh... This is the blueprint to becoming a millionaire" |

**2. Nonverbal Hooks (Visuals/Sounds)**

| Type | Mechanism | Example |
|------|-----------|---------|
| Pattern Interrupt | Unexpected visual | Catching a banana, unusual setting |
| Sound Cue | Attention-grabbing audio | Dropped tray (embarrassment signal), champagne clink (announcement signal) |
| Movement | Kinetic attention grab | Fast action, sudden change |

**Best Practice:** Combine verbal + nonverbal hooks for maximum impact.

### Hook Distribution by Type (Based on 121 Best Performers)

| Type | Percentage |
|------|------------|
| Statements | 35% |
| Conditionals | 20% |
| Questions | 15% |
| Commands | 10% |
| Narratives | 10% |
| Lists | 5% |
| Labels | 3% |
| Exclamations | 2% |

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### Phase 1: Hook Research (70-20-10 Framework)

#### Step 1.1: Core Winners Collection (70% of Effort)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Document and organize proven winning hooks from your own content and competitors |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Pattern Recognition |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Can automate data collection, human judges quality |
| **Executor** | Hybrid (Worker collects, Human curates) |
| **Precondition** | Spreadsheet system configured |
| **Output** | Core hooks library (50+ proven winners) |
| **Guardrails** | Only include hooks with verified performance data |
| **Decision Rule** | "70% of your effort goes to 'more of what works'" |

**Implementation:**
1. Create new spreadsheet with tabs for each platform
2. Add columns: Name, Hook, Views, Link, Type, Date
3. Review your top 10% performing content
4. Extract the exact hook (first sentence/visual)
5. Document with metrics
6. Review before every content creation session

**Sources (Priority Order):**
1. Your own winning hooks (highest priority)
2. Your high-performing organic content
3. Competitor ads saved in swipe album
4. Viral content in your space
5. Ad Libraries (lowest - can't verify performance)

#### Step 1.2: Emerging Hooks Research (20% of Effort)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Find promising hooks from adjacent niches to adapt |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires creative judgment |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Core library exists |
| **Output** | Adapted hooks from other niches (10-20) |
| **Guardrails** | Must have evidence of performance in original niche |
| **Decision Rule** | "Winner Adjacent - if it works there, test here" |

**Implementation:**
1. Subscribe to software tools showing outliers by platform
2. Search topics adjacent to yours
3. Screenshot outliers with high engagement
4. Create slide deck with screenshot + adaptation idea
5. Test adapted versions in your niche

#### Step 1.3: Experimental Hooks Creation (10% of Effort)

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create completely new, untested hook concepts |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Risk-Taking |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | 70% and 20% buckets filled |
| **Output** | Experimental hooks (5-10) |
| **Guardrails** | Accept 90% failure rate; looking for breakthroughs |
| **Decision Rule** | "Big new ideas - risky but could lead to huge wins" |

---

### Phase 2: Hook Creation by Awareness Level

#### Step 2.1: Map Audience Awareness

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Determine which awareness levels to target |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires market judgment |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Know your audience segments |
| **Output** | Awareness level distribution plan |
| **Guardrails** | Don't concentrate 90% in "Most Aware" - spread out |
| **Decision Rule** | "When in doubt, go a little broader" |

**The 5 Awareness Levels (Eugene Schwartz):**

| Level | Name | Hook Type | Audience Size |
|-------|------|-----------|---------------|
| 5 | Most Aware | Offer-driven | Smallest (hottest) |
| 4 | Product-Aware | Proof-driven | Small |
| 3 | Solution-Aware | Promise-driven | Medium |
| 2 | Problem-Aware | Pain-driven | Large |
| 1 | Unaware | Curiosity-driven | Largest (coldest) |

#### Step 2.2: Create Hooks for Each Level

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Write hooks targeting each awareness level |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Writing |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - AI can draft, human refines |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Awareness distribution decided |
| **Output** | 50 hooks across awareness levels |
| **Guardrails** | Use templates, don't invent from scratch |
| **Decision Rule** | "The hook determines the content, not the other way around" |

**Templates by Level:**

**Level 5 - Most Aware (Offer):**
```
"50% off our best-selling [PRODUCT] until [DATE]"
"[PRODUCT]: New formula with 25% more [BENEFIT]"
"The best offer I've ever made"
"At last! It's finally here."
```

**Level 4 - Product-Aware (Proof):**
```
"Discover why 10,000 people chose [PRODUCT] last month"
"See how [PRODUCT] increased ROI 150% for 5 industries"
"$4,664 per month in recurring revenue... That's what Kyle... The last person on the leaderboard... Was able to build..."
"The rumors are true..."
```

**Level 3 - Solution-Aware (Promise):**
```
"The fastest way to [RESULT] - introducing [PRODUCT]"
"Double your sales in 6 months with our strategy"
"How to get ahead of 99% of people"
"How I made my first $100M"
```

**Level 2 - Problem-Aware (Pain):**
```
"Tired of [SPECIFIC PROBLEM]? There's a better way"
"Your site isn't selling? You might be missing these elements"
"If you're working all the time and your business isn't growing, you're working on the wrong sh*t"
"Business owners: Do you ever wonder if you're working on the wrong stuff?"
```

**Level 1 - Unaware (Curiosity):**
```
"The hidden danger in your routine costing you [$/time/health]"
"The unexpected way your business is losing $1000s/month"
"You guys want to hear something completely insane"
"On November 30th, 2022, the world changed forever."
```

---

### Phase 3: Hook Testing

#### Step 3.1: Volume Testing Setup

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Configure testing infrastructure for high volume |
| **Cognitive Type** | Technical Setup |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Platform access, tracking configured |
| **Output** | Testing system ready for 10x volume |
| **Guardrails** | Budget minimum: enough for statistically significant data |
| **Decision Rule** | "Record 10 hooks for every 1 piece of ad content" |

**Testing Ratios by Content Type:**
| Content Type | Hooks per Piece | Reason |
|--------------|-----------------|--------|
| Paid Ads | 10 | Highest stakes, need most data |
| Short Content | Reuse winning tweets as shorts | Cross-platform validation |
| Long Content | 3-4 | Team picks best in post |
| Emails | Active split tests | Document winners separately |

#### Step 3.2: Execute Tests

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Run hooks through content/ads and collect data |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH (ad platforms automate distribution) |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Content created with hook variations |
| **Output** | Performance data for each hook |
| **Guardrails** | Same meat/CTA across hook tests to isolate variable |
| **Decision Rule** | "Let the data do the teaching" |

#### Step 3.3: Analyze and Iterate

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Rank hooks, identify patterns, update libraries |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Pattern Recognition |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Sufficient data collected |
| **Output** | Updated hook rankings, pattern insights |
| **Guardrails** | Top 10% replicate, Bottom 10% eliminate |
| **Decision Rule** | "No matter how bad your content is, some will be in the top 10%. Make more like that." |

**Weekly Iteration Cycle:**
```
1. Look at top 10% performers (top 5 hooks)
2. 70% of next batch: variations of those top 5
3. 20% of next batch: permutations (visual + word changes)
4. 10% of next batch: completely different hooks (new research)
```

---

### Phase 4: Hook Organization & Swipe File

#### Step 4.1: Maintain Swipe File

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Continuously collect and organize winning hooks |
| **Cognitive Type** | Curation |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Can auto-save, human organizes |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Phone album created, spreadsheet active |
| **Output** | Growing swipe file of proven hooks |
| **Guardrails** | Save immediately when you see good hooks - don't rely on memory |
| **Decision Rule** | "I have an album on my phone where I save them all" |

**Organization System:**
1. Phone: Album for screenshots of ads/content
2. Spreadsheet: Categorized by type, awareness level, performance
3. Review: Before every content creation session

---

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Time Allocation
```yaml
rule: HOOK_TIME_PRIORITY
trigger: Starting any content creation
condition:
  - IF creating_ads THEN allocate_80%_to_hooks()
  - IF creating_content THEN allocate_majority_to_hook_selection()
action: "If you have ten hours to advertise, focus your first eight hours on the hooks"
confidence: HIGH (Dean Graziosi case, Ogilvy principle)
source: "Section: What Makes Hooks So Important?"
```

### DR-002: Testing Volume
```yaml
rule: TESTING_RATIO
trigger: Creating new ad
condition:
  - IF paid_ad THEN create_10_hook_variations()
  - IF long_content THEN create_3_4_hook_variations()
  - IF email THEN run_split_test()
action: Always test significantly more than feels necessary
confidence: HIGH
source: "Section: Testing The Hooks"
```

### DR-003: Hook Source Priority
```yaml
rule: HOOK_SOURCE_HIERARCHY
trigger: Researching new hooks
condition:
  - PRIORITY_1: Own winning hooks
  - PRIORITY_2: Own organic content hooks
  - PRIORITY_3: Competitor ad hooks (saved in album)
  - PRIORITY_4: Viral content hooks
  - PRIORITY_5: Ad Library (can't verify performance)
action: Start at top, move down only when needed
confidence: HIGH
source: "Section: My Process For Finding and Creating Hooks"
```

### DR-004: 70-20-10 Allocation
```yaml
rule: INNOVATION_ALLOCATION
trigger: Weekly hook creation
condition:
  - 70% = Core (proven winners, variations)
  - 20% = Emerging (adjacent niche adaptations)
  - 10% = Experimental (completely new ideas)
action: Mathematically proven by Google to maximize returns
confidence: HIGH (Larry Page & Sergey Brin research)
source: "Section: The 70-20-10 Innovation Rule"
```

### DR-005: Awareness Spread
```yaml
rule: AWARENESS_DISTRIBUTION
trigger: Hook set complete
condition:
  - IF 90%_hooks_in_most_aware THEN spread_to_colder_levels()
  - IF uncertain THEN go_broader()
action: "When in doubt, go a little broader. You still capture hot audience + attract cold."
confidence: HIGH
source: "Section: Writing Expansion Hooks"
```

### DR-006: Performance Iteration
```yaml
rule: DATA_DRIVEN_ITERATION
trigger: Weekly performance review
condition:
  - IF hook_in_top_10% THEN create_5+_variations()
  - IF hook_in_bottom_10% THEN never_use_again()
  - IF hook_in_middle THEN test_1_2_variations_only()
action: "Let the data do the teaching"
confidence: HIGH
source: "Section: Testing The Hooks - Author Note"
```

### DR-007: Hook Focus
```yaml
rule: AUDIENCE_NOT_SELF
trigger: Writing any hook
condition:
  - IF hook_about_you THEN rewrite_about_them()
  - IF hook_makes_them_feel_important THEN proceed()
action: "It needed to make them feel important, not me"
confidence: HIGH (Dean Graziosi failure case)
source: "Section: Dean Graziosi's Story"
```

---

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: No Historical Data
**Trigger:** First time creating content, no performance history
**Response:**
- Skip to "First Time Through" checklist
- Collect 50 external hooks from competitors/leaders
- Use all 50 in content
- Build baseline from results
- Quote: "If you're starting out, it's even easier. You just make a bunch with no idea what's gonna happen."

### Exception 2: Niche-Specific Culture
**Trigger:** Operating in niche with specific cultural elements
**Response:**
- Use niche-specific memes and references
- Quote: "Memes or meme-like content attract the largest percentage of your audience"
- Test culture-specific hooks even if they seem narrow

### Exception 3: High Performing Hook Fatigue
**Trigger:** Winning hook performance declining
**Response:**
- Create new variations preserving core structure
- Test visual changes (different person, setting, style)
- Maintain hook type but change specific words
- Never abandon winning hook structure - just refresh execution

### Exception 4: Platform-Specific Requirements
**Trigger:** Different platforms have different constraints
**Response by Platform:**
| Platform | Adaptation |
|----------|------------|
| Twitter | Hook must work in 280 characters alone |
| YouTube | Hook = first 5 seconds (verbal + visual) |
| Email | Hook = Subject line + Preview text |
| Instagram | Hook = First frame + First words |
| Ads | Hook must stop scroll in 0-3 seconds |

### Exception 5: Hook-Content Mismatch
**Trigger:** Audience clicks but doesn't engage with content
**Response:**
- Hook and content must be congruent
- Content must deliver on hook's promise
- If hook promises "5 ways" - deliver exactly 5 ways
- Quote: "The hook dictates the content, and not the other way around"

---

## Part 8: Outputs

| Output | Format | Destination | Frequency |
|--------|--------|-------------|-----------|
| Hook Performance Rankings | Spreadsheet | Marketing Team | Weekly |
| Top 10 Winners Library | Document | Content Team | Weekly update |
| Hook Type Analysis | Report | Strategy | Monthly |
| Awareness Level Distribution | Dashboard | Leadership | Monthly |
| Swipe File Additions | Album + Spreadsheet | Personal/Team | Daily |

### Key Metrics to Track

```
PRIMARY:
├── CTR by Hook (click-through rate)
├── View Retention at 5 seconds
├── Engagement Rate (likes, comments, shares)
└── Conversion Rate by Hook

SECONDARY:
├── Hook Type Performance Distribution
├── Awareness Level Performance
├── Platform-Specific Performance
├── Reuse Success Rate (same hook, new content)
└── Time to Winner (how quickly hooks perform)
```

---

## Part 9: Validation

### Hook Quality Gates

| Gate | Threshold | Action if Failed |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| CTR | >1% | Rewrite hook - not grabbing attention |
| 5-Second Retention | >30% | Strengthen pattern interrupt |
| Engagement vs Views | >2% | Hook promising wrong thing |
| Top 10% Identification | Clear winner exists | More testing needed |

### Process Quality Standards

| Metric | Minimum | Target | Top Performer |
|--------|---------|--------|---------------|
| Hooks Tested/Week | 20 | 50 | 100+ |
| Hook Variations per Ad | 5 | 10 | 20 |
| Swipe File Growth/Week | 10 | 25 | 50 |
| Time on Hooks vs Content | 50% | 80% | 90% |

| Situation | Escalate To | Timeline |
|-----------|-------------|----------|
| All hooks underperforming | Marketing Lead | Same day |

| Competitor hook significantly outperforming | Competitive Analysis | Immediately |
| Winning hook suddenly stops working | Creative Team | Same day |
| Platform algorithm change detected | Platform Specialist | Within hours |

## Appendix B: Hook Writing Templates

### The Mirror Question Template
```
"Have you ever [universal but private situation]?"

Examples:
- "Have you ever looked in the mirror and thought 'I should be further ahead by now?'"
- "Have you ever wondered why some people seem to have it all figured out?"
```

### The Number Shock Template
```
"[Specific impressive number] [metric/timeframe]... [explanation or story]"

Examples:
- "$4,664 per month in recurring revenue... That's what Kyle..."
- "One in every 250 businesses does over 10 million dollars a year..."
- "I've been in business for 13 years. I've sold 9 companies."
```

### The Confession Template
```
"I have a confession... [vulnerable truth]"

Example:
- "I have a confession... Which is I am sick and tired of seeing people who have never run a business before teaching other people how to grow businesses."
```

### The Conditional Pain Template
```
"If you're [situation], you're [doing it wrong]"

Example:
- "If you're working all the time and your business isn't growing, you're working on the wrong sh*t."
```

### The Real Quick Template
```
"Real quick [request/question]..."

Examples:
- "Real quick question... Can I have your email address?"
- "Real quick. The reason for this ad is because..."
```

### The Banana Pattern Interrupt
```
[Unusual visual action] + "You might be wondering why I just [action]... And the reason is because [connect to value]"

Example:
- "You might be wondering why I just caught a banana... And the reason why is because the amount of value I'm going to give you in the next 30 seconds is bananas..."
```

### The Rumor Template
```
"The rumors are true..." [no context, pure curiosity]
```

### The That's Weird Template
```
"That's weird... [observation that creates curiosity]"

Example:
- "That's weird... I don't see your name on the invite list?"
```

## Appendix C: Hooks Checklist

### First Time Through
- [ ] Look at top-performing ads or content of other people
- [ ] Isolate the hooks (first sentence, first visual)
- [ ] Write down your favorite 50
- [ ] Use all of them in ads and content
- [ ] Document results

### Every Time After (Weekly)
- [ ] Look at top 10% performers (top 5 hooks)
- [ ] Make 70% of next batch using those top 5 hooks
- [ ] Make 20% doing permutations (visual + word changes)
- [ ] Make 10% completely different hooks (new research)

### Good Hooks Contain
- [ ] Some way to catch attention (call out)
- [ ] Some implication of value if they consume it

### Variety Checklist (Same Topic, Different Formats)
- [ ] Conditional version: "If you're a [avatar], this will get you [result]"
- [ ] Label version: "[Avatars] I have a gift for you"
- [ ] Question version: "Would you rather [bad option] or [good option]?"
- [ ] Command version: "Watch this if you want to [result]"
- [ ] Statement version: "The top 1% of [avatars] follow these rules..."
- [ ] List version: "[Number] ways [avatars] get [result] without [obstacle]"
- [ ] Story version: "All of a sudden, [dramatic event]..."

        description: "How many hooks to produce (default: 50)"

        format: "markdown"
        schema:

            - "70% Core Hooks (variations of winners)"
            - "20% Emerging Hooks (adapted from other niches)"
            - "10% Experimental Hooks (new ideas)"
      - type: "hook_distribution"
        format: "yaml"
        content: "Breakdown by type and awareness level"

    decision_rules:
      - id: "DR-W001"
        rule: "70-20-10 split: 70% proven variations, 20% adjacent adaptations, 10% experiments"
      - id: "DR-W002"
        rule: "If 90% hooks in 'Most Aware' bucket, spread to colder levels"
      - id: "DR-W003"
        rule: "When in doubt, go broader"

        pattern: "Real quick [question/request]..."

      rumor:
        pattern: "The rumors are true..."
        example: "The rumors are true..."

      thats_weird:
        pattern: "That's weird... [curiosity-creating observation]"
        example: "That's weird... I don't see your name on the invite list?"

      banana_interrupt:
        pattern: "[Unusual action] + You might be wondering why I just [action]... because [value connection]"
        example: "You might be wondering why I just caught a banana... And the reason why is because the amount of value I'm going to give you in the next 30 seconds is bananas"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # HOOK TESTER
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  hook_tester:
    name: "Hook Tester"
    description: "Manages hook testing, collects data, and identifies winners"
    cognitive_type: "Execution + Analysis"

    capabilities:
      - "Set up A/B tests for hooks"
      - "Track performance metrics"
      - "Identify top and bottom performers"
      - "Calculate statistical significance"
      - "Recommend next iterations"

    inputs:
      - type: "hooks"
        description: "Hooks to test"
      - type: "content_type"
        description: "Ad, short content, long content, or email"
      - type: "platform"
        description: "Where to test"
      - type: "budget"
        description: "Testing budget (for ads)"
      - type: "success_metrics"
        description: "What to measure (CTR, views, engagement)"

    outputs:
      - type: "performance_report"
        format: "dashboard"
        metrics:
          - "CTR by hook"
          - "Engagement rate"
          - "5-second retention"
          - "Cost per result"
      - type: "winner_identification"
        format: "ranked_list"
        content: "Top 10% and Bottom 10% clearly identified"
      - type: "iteration_recommendations"
        format: "action_items"
        content: "What to test next based on patterns"

    decision_rules:
      - id: "DR-T001"
        rule: "Test 10 hooks per ad, 3-4 per long content"
      - id: "DR-T002"
        rule: "Top 10% = create 5+ variations"
      - id: "DR-T003"
        rule: "Bottom 10% = never use again"
      - id: "DR-T004"
        rule: "Middle performers = test 1-2 variations only"
      - id: "DR-T005"
        rule: "Let the data do the teaching - no opinions"

    testing_ratios:
      paid_ads:
        hooks_per_piece: 10
        reason: "Highest stakes, need most data"
      short_content:
        approach: "Reuse winning tweets as shorts"
        reason: "Cross-platform validation"
      long_content:
        hooks_per_piece: 3-4
        reason: "Team picks best in post"
      emails:
        approach: "Active split tests every send"
        reason: "Document winners separately"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # SWIPE FILE CURATOR
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  swipe_curator:
    name: "Swipe File Curator"
    description: "Maintains organized library of hooks with performance data"
    cognitive_type: "Curation + Organization"

    capabilities:
      - "Organize hooks by multiple dimensions"
      - "Update performance data"
      - "Remove underperformers"
      - "Surface relevant hooks for new projects"
      - "Track hook reuse success"

    inputs:
      - type: "new_hooks"
        description: "Hooks to add to library"
      - type: "performance_data"
        description: "Updated metrics for existing hooks"
      - type: "query"
        description: "What kind of hooks are needed"

    outputs:
      - type: "organized_library"
        format: "database"
        dimensions:
          - "By Type (8 categories)"
          - "By Awareness Level (5 levels)"
          - "By Platform"
          - "By Performance Tier"
          - "By Date"
      - type: "recommendations"
        format: "curated_list"
        content: "Best hooks for specific query"

    organization_schema:
      by_type:
        - labels
        - questions_yes
        - questions_open
        - conditionals
        - commands
        - statements
        - lists
        - narratives
        - exclamations
      by_awareness:
        - level_5_most_aware
        - level_4_product_aware
        - level_3_solution_aware
        - level_2_problem_aware
        - level_1_unaware
      by_platform:
        - youtube_long
        - youtube_shorts
        - instagram
        - twitter
        - facebook_ads
        - email
        - linkedin
      by_performance:
        - top_10_percent
        - middle_tier
        - bottom_10_percent_archived

# =============================================================================
# EXECUTOR MATRIX
# =============================================================================

executor_matrix:
  phases:
    research:
      steps:
        - step: "Competitor Analysis"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["ad_library_scraper", "social_analytics"]

        - step: "Hook Extraction"
          executor: "Hybrid"
          automation_potential: "MEDIUM"
          tools: ["text_extraction", "human_judgment"]

        - step: "Categorization"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["classification_model"]

        - step: "Pattern Analysis"
          executor: "Human"
          automation_potential: "LOW"
          tools: ["analytics_dashboard"]

    creation:
      steps:
        - step: "70% Core Variations"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["llm_variation_generator"]

        - step: "20% Adaptation"
          executor: "Hybrid"
          automation_potential: "MEDIUM"
          tools: ["llm_with_human_review"]

        - step: "10% Experimental"
          executor: "Human"
          automation_potential: "LOW"
          tools: ["creative_brainstorm"]

        - step: "Quality Review"
          executor: "Human"
          automation_potential: "LOW"
          tools: ["checklist_validation"]

    testing:
      steps:
        - step: "Test Setup"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["ad_platform_api", "content_scheduler"]

        - step: "Data Collection"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["analytics_integration"]

        - step: "Performance Analysis"
          executor: "Hybrid"
          automation_potential: "MEDIUM"
          tools: ["statistical_analysis", "human_insight"]

        - step: "Winner Identification"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["ranking_algorithm"]

    iteration:
      steps:
        - step: "Top 10% Expansion"
          executor: "Hybrid"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["variation_generator"]

        - step: "Bottom 10% Removal"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["library_management"]

        - step: "Library Update"
          executor: "Worker"
          automation_potential: "HIGH"
          tools: ["database_operations"]

# =============================================================================
# QUALITY GATES
# =============================================================================

quality_gates:
  hook_writing:
    gate_1:
      name: "Structure Check"
      criteria:
        - "Hook has clear Call Out element"
        - "Hook has Condition for Value"
        - "Hook type is identifiable"
        - "Awareness level is appropriate"
      pass_threshold: "All 4 criteria met"

    gate_2:
      name: "Distribution Check"
      criteria:
        - "70-20-10 split maintained"
        - "Not >90% in single awareness level"
        - "Multiple hook types represented"
      pass_threshold: "All criteria met"

    gate_3:
      name: "Focus Check"
      criteria:
        - "Hook is about THEM, not about YOU"
        - "No ego-driven introductions"
        - "Value promise is clear"
      pass_threshold: "All criteria met"

  testing:
    gate_1:
      name: "Volume Check"
      criteria:
        - "Minimum hooks per content type met"
        - "Ads: 10 hooks, Long: 3-4 hooks"
      pass_threshold: "Minimum volume achieved"

    gate_2:
      name: "Data Quality Check"
      criteria:
        - "Sufficient impressions for significance"
        - "All hooks tracked properly"
        - "Metrics captured accurately"
      pass_threshold: "Statistical validity confirmed"

    gate_3:
      name: "Iteration Check"
      criteria:
        - "Top 10% identified"
        - "Bottom 10% marked for removal"
        - "Next batch planned with 70-20-10"
      pass_threshold: "Iteration plan complete"

  performance:
    thresholds:
      ctr:
        poor: "<0.5%"
        acceptable: "0.5-1%"
        good: "1-2%"
        excellent: ">2%"

      five_second_retention:
        poor: "<20%"
        acceptable: "20-30%"
        good: "30-50%"
        excellent: ">50%"

      engagement_rate:
        poor: "<1%"
        acceptable: "1-2%"
        good: "2-5%"
        excellent: ">5%"

# =============================================================================
# WORKFLOWS
# =============================================================================

workflows:
  weekly_hook_creation:
    trigger: "Every Friday (Ad Day)"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        name: "Review Previous Winners"
        agent: "swipe_curator"
        action: "Surface top 5 hooks from last week"
        output: "Top hooks for variation"

      - step: 2
        name: "Research New Sources"
        agent: "hook_researcher"

        output: "Fresh hook inspiration"

      - step: 3
        name: "Create Hook Set"
        agent: "hook_writer"
        action: "Write 50 hooks following 70-20-10"
        output: "50 categorized hooks"

      - step: 4
        name: "Quality Review"
        agent: "human"
        action: "Review hooks against quality gates"
        output: "Approved hook set"

      - step: 5
        name: "Test Setup"
        agent: "hook_tester"
        action: "Configure tests for new hooks"
        output: "Tests running"

    expected_output:
      hooks: 50
      time: "2-3 hours"
      quality: "All gates passed"

  hook_performance_review:
    trigger: "Weekly (Monday)"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        name: "Collect Data"
        agent: "hook_tester"
        action: "Pull all performance metrics"
        output: "Performance report"

      - step: 2
        name: "Rank Hooks"
        agent: "hook_tester"
        action: "Identify top 10% and bottom 10%"
        output: "Ranked list"

      - step: 3
        name: "Update Library"
        agent: "swipe_curator"
        action: "Add winners, archive losers"
        output: "Updated swipe file"

      - step: 4
        name: "Plan Next Batch"
        agent: "hook_writer"
        action: "Prepare 70-20-10 plan based on learnings"
        output: "Next week's strategy"

    expected_output:
      insights: "Clear winners and losers identified"
      library_update: "Swipe file current"
      next_plan: "70-20-10 split ready"

  first_time_setup:
    trigger: "New user/project"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        name: "External Research"
        agent: "hook_researcher"
        action: "Collect 50 hooks from top performers"
        output: "Initial hook library"

      - step: 2
        name: "Use All 50"
        agent: "hook_writer"
        action: "Create content using all collected hooks"
        output: "First batch of content"

      - step: 3
        name: "Test Everything"
        agent: "hook_tester"
        action: "Run all hooks, collect baseline data"
        output: "Performance baseline"

      - step: 4
        name: "Establish 70-20-10"
        agent: "hook_tester"
        action: "Identify top 10% for core bucket"
        output: "Ready for weekly cycle"

    expected_output:

      baseline: "Performance data established"
      framework: "70-20-10 ready to execute"

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/landing-page-sop.md

# Landing Page SOP

> **Source:** Checklist LP - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Create landing pages that remove every reason NOT to buy. A landing page doesn't sell - it removes all objections and friction from the decision process.

**Core Equation (Value Equation applied to LP):**
```
Value = (Dream Outcome × Perceived Likelihood) / (Time Delay × Effort & Sacrifice)

Landing Page Elements Attack Each Variable:
├── Dream Outcome ↑: Headlines, benefícios, cases
├── Probabilidade Percebida ↑: Prova social, garantias, autoridade
├── Atraso Temporal ↓: Promessas de velocidade, vitórias rápidas
└── Esforço & Sacrifício ↓: UX simples, suporte visível, checkout fácil
```

**Business Impact:** "Uma landing page que converte 5% com tráfego qualificado vale mais que uma que converte 10% com tráfego lixo." The page can literally be the difference between bankruptcy and financial freedom.

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Creating new landing pages for lead capture
- Optimizing existing landing pages
- Building sales pages for offers
- Any page designed for single-action conversion

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- General website pages (about, contact, etc.)
- Content/blog pages
- Multi-product catalog pages
- Non-conversion focused pages

### Business Types
- Any business with online offers
- Lead magnet capture pages
- High-ticket and low-ticket sales
- B2B and B2C

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Offer Definition | Single, clear offer defined | One page = one offer = one decision |
| Avatar Profile | Target customer deeply understood | Language, pains, desires documented |
| Proof Assets | Testimonials, cases, results available | Numerical results preferred |
| Authority Elements | Creator credentials established | Photo, story, quantifiable wins |
| Technical Stack | Hosting, tracking, checkout ready | PageSpeed >90, SSL, payment processor |
| Copy Framework | Benefits (not features) articulated | Each feature → emotional benefit |

---

## Part 4: Core Framework (Value Equation Applied to Landing Page)

### Value Equation Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    VALUE EQUATION FOR LANDING PAGES                         │
├───────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ NUMERATOR (INCREASE)          │ DENOMINATOR (DECREASE)                      │
├───────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Dream Outcome ↑               │ Time Delay ↓                                │
│ • Headline: resultado específico│ • Timeframe promises                      │
│ • Benefícios com checkmarks   │ • Quick wins highlighted                    │
│ • Cases com resultados numéricos│ • Same-day access messaging              │
├───────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Perceived Likelihood ↑        │ Effort & Sacrifice ↓                        │
│ • Prova social imediata       │ • Mobile-first design                       │
│ • Subheadline de credibilidade│ • Minimal form fields                       │
│ • Garantias destacadas        │ • Checkout simplificado                     │
│ • Autoridade do criador       │ • Suporte visível                           │
└───────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The 10 Phases Framework

```
Phase 1: Above the Fold (0-3 segundos)
Phase 2: Experiência Móvel (60%+ do tráfego)
Phase 3: Estrutura de Persuasão
Phase 4: Qualificação e Objeções
Phase 5: Estrutura de Valor
Phase 6: Autoridade e Confiança
Phase 7: Conversão e Checkout
Phase 8: Otimização e Monitoramento
Phase 9: Suporte e Recuperação
Phase 10: Compliance e Proteção
```

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### PHASE 1: ABOVE THE FOLD (0-3 SEGUNDOS)

#### Step 1.1: Headline Magnética
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create headline using structure "Como [RESULTADO ESPECÍFICO] em [TIMEFRAME] sem [DOR PRIMÁRIA]" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis (crafting compelling promise) |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires human creativity |
| **Executor** | Human (copywriter) |
| **Precondition** | Avatar pains and desires documented |
| **Output** | Headline that makes visitor think "como assim?" or "isso é possível?" |
| **Guardrails** | Teste Obrigatório: Leia em voz alta - se não rolar natural, está errada |
| **Decision Rule** | Must be first thing visible, largest font on page |

**Benchmark:** Deve fazer o visitante pensar "como assim?" ou "isso é possível?"

#### Step 1.2: Subheadline de Credibilidade
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create subheadline using formula "O [MECANISMO] usado por [NÚMERO] [AVATAR] para [RESULTADO COMPROVADO]" |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Proof metrics available (number of users, results) |
| **Output** | Subheadline increasing Perceived Likelihood |
| **Guardrails** | Red Flag: Se parece com jargão de vendedor, refaça |
| **Decision Rule** | Fonte 60% menor que headline, diretamente abaixo |

#### Step 1.3: CTA Principal
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create benefit-oriented CTA button |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception (customer psychology) |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Template-based |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Desired outcome clearly defined |
| **Output** | CTA orientado a benefício ("Quero 30 Clientes em 90 Dias") vs. ação ("Comprar") |
| **Guardrails** | Design: Mínimo 200px largura mobile, contraste 3:1, cor que "grita" |
| **Decision Rule** | Within above-the-fold, visível sem scroll. Hack: Use seta (→) - aumenta CTR 12-26% |

#### Step 1.4: Prova Social Imediata
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Display immediate trust indicators |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis (selecting best proof) |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Real metrics available |
| **Output** | Format: "⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ X+ Alunos \| Y% Satisfação \| Resultados em Z dias" |
| **Guardrails** | Números reais vs. estimativas - sempre números reais |
| **Decision Rule** | Logo abaixo do CTA ou integrada ao header |

#### Step 1.5: Indicador de Urgência
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Add real urgency element |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Timer automation |
| **Executor** | Worker (technical) + Human (strategy) |
| **Precondition** | Real urgency exists (not fake) |
| **Output** | Timer regressivo, vagas limitadas, or bônus expirando |
| **Guardrails** | CRÍTICO: Deve ser 100% real - falsa escassez destrói trust de longo prazo |
| **Decision Rule** | Próximo ao CTA ou em barra fixa no topo. Cor vermelha ou laranja |

---

### PHASE 2: EXPERIÊNCIA MÓVEL (60%+ DO TRÁFEGO)

#### Step 2.1: Velocidade de Carregamento
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Optimize page load speed |
| **Cognitive Type** | Technical execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Hosting and CDN configured |
| **Output** | Google PageSpeed Insights score >90, load <3 segundos no mobile em conexão 3G |
| **Guardrails** | Otimizações: Imagens comprimidas, CDN, lazy loading |
| **Decision Rule** | Teste com dados móveis reais, não só simuladores |

#### Step 2.2: Layout Responsivo
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Ensure mobile-friendly design |
| **Cognitive Type** | Design execution |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Design system established |
| **Output** | Texto legível sem zoom (mínimo 16px), botões mínimo 44px altura |
| **Guardrails** | Elementos não "grudados", fácil navegação com polegar |
| **Decision Rule** | Teste em dispositivos reais, não só simuladores |

#### Step 2.3: Formulários Otimizados
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Minimize form friction |
| **Cognitive Type** | UX optimization |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Form requirements defined |
| **Output** | Campos: Mínimo absoluto necessário (nome + email para lead magnet) |
| **Guardrails** | Input type correto (email, telefone, número), autopreenchimento ativado |
| **Decision Rule** | Validação real-time, não apenas no submit |

---

### PHASE 3: ESTRUTURA DE PERSUASÃO

#### Step 3.1: Hierarquia Visual
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Establish clear visual flow |
| **Cognitive Type** | Design analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Content elements ready |
| **Output** | Fluxo: Headline → Subheadline → VSL/Imagem → Benefícios → CTA |
| **Guardrails** | Tamanhos decrescentes, elementos importantes com contraste, white space entre seções |
| **Decision Rule** | Test: Can user understand offer in 5 seconds? |

#### Step 3.2: VSL ou Imagem Hero
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Add video sales letter or hero image |
| **Cognitive Type** | Content strategy |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Video or transformation mockup ready |
| **Output** | VSL: 8-15 min cold traffic, 15-45 min warm traffic. Thumbnail com play button óbvio + texto de benefício |
| **Guardrails** | Alternativa: Mockup do resultado/transformação |
| **Decision Rule** | Centralizado, 16:9, responsivo |

#### Step 3.3: Bullets de Benefícios
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Create benefit bullets (NOT features) |
| **Cognitive Type** | Copywriting |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Features documented with emotional benefits |
| **Output** | Fórmula: "✓ [RESULTADO] para que você possa [BENEFÍCIO EMOCIONAL]" |
| **Guardrails** | Quantidade: 5-7 bullets máximo (mais dilui impacto) |
| **Decision Rule** | Cada bullet deve fazer o prospect pensar "preciso disso". Design: Checkmarks verdes, espaçamento generoso |

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Above the Fold Completeness
```yaml
rule: ABOVE_FOLD_CHECK
trigger: Page review
condition:
  - IF headline_visible == false THEN "FAIL"
  - IF subheadline_visible == false THEN "FAIL"
  - IF cta_visible == false THEN "FAIL"
  - IF proof_visible == false THEN "WARNING"
  - IF urgency_visible == false THEN "WARNING"
action: All 5 elements must be visible without scroll
confidence: HIGH (Source: Phase 1)
```

### DR-002: Headline Quality Test
```yaml
rule: HEADLINE_NATURAL_TEST
trigger: Headline draft complete
condition:
  - IF read_aloud_feels_natural == false THEN "REVISE"
  - IF visitor_thinks_how_possible == false THEN "REVISE"
  - IF looks_like_sales_jargon == true THEN "REVISE"
action: Read aloud test mandatory
confidence: HIGH (Source: 1.1, 1.2)
```

### DR-003: Mobile First
```yaml
rule: MOBILE_PERFORMANCE
trigger: Page deployment
condition:
  - IF load_time > 3_seconds THEN "FAIL"
  - IF pagespeed_score < 90 THEN "WARNING"
  - IF text_size < 16px THEN "FAIL"
  - IF button_height < 44px THEN "FAIL"
action: Fix mobile issues before launching
confidence: HIGH (Source: Phase 2)
```

### DR-004: Benefit vs Feature
```yaml
rule: BENEFIT_NOT_FEATURE
trigger: Bullet copy review
condition:
  - IF bullet_is_feature THEN transform_to_benefit()
  - IF missing_emotional_benefit THEN add_emotional_benefit()
  - IF bullets > 7 THEN reduce_to_7()
action: Apply formula "✓ [RESULTADO] para que você possa [BENEFÍCIO EMOCIONAL]"
confidence: HIGH (Source: 3.3, Erro Fatal #1)
```

### DR-005: Single Offer Rule
```yaml
rule: ONE_PAGE_ONE_OFFER
trigger: Page structure review
condition:
  - IF offers_count > 1 THEN "FAIL - Erro Fatal #2"
action: One landing page = one offer = one decision
rationale: "Confused mind says no. Excited mind says yes."
confidence: HIGH (Source: Erro Fatal #2)
```

### DR-006: Guarantee Strength
```yaml
rule: GUARANTEE_QUALITY
trigger: Guarantee section review
condition:
  - IF guarantee_text == "Satisfação garantida" THEN "WEAK - Erro Fatal #3"
  - IF guarantee == null THEN "CRITICAL - Erro Fatal #3"
  - IF guarantee_is_specific == true THEN "PASS"
action: Create specific, conditional, even "unfair" guarantee
confidence: HIGH (Source: 5.3, Erro Fatal #3)
```

### DR-007: Price Context
```yaml
rule: PRICE_WITH_CONTEXT
trigger: Price reveal
condition:
  - IF value_shown_before_price == false THEN "FAIL - Erro Fatal #4"
  - IF comparisons_absent == true THEN "WARNING"
  - IF guarantee_absent == true THEN "WARNING"
action: Always show value → comparisons → price → guarantee → urgency
confidence: HIGH (Source: Erro Fatal #4)
```

### DR-008: Copy Specificity
```yaml
rule: AVOID_GENERIC_COPY
trigger: Copy review
condition:
  - IF contains_generic_phrases == true THEN "FAIL - Erro Fatal #5"
action: Use exact language your avatar uses
test: "Does this sound like it was written by someone FROM the niche?"
generic_red_flags:
  - "Transforme sua vida"
  - "Alcance seus sonhos"
  - "Método comprovado"
confidence: HIGH (Source: Erro Fatal #5)
```

### DR-009: Urgency Authenticity
```yaml
rule: REAL_URGENCY_ONLY
trigger: Urgency element review
condition:
  - IF urgency_is_fake == true THEN "REMOVE - destroys long-term trust"
  - IF urgency_is_real == true THEN "PASS"
action: Only use real timers, real limited slots, real expiring bonuses
confidence: HIGH (Source: 1.5)
```

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: Warm Traffic Pages
**Trigger:** Audience already knows you
**Adjustment:**
- VSL can be longer (15-45 min vs 8-15 min for cold)
- Higher conversion benchmarks (>8% vs >3% cold)
- Can reduce proof elements
- Can be more direct with offer

### Exception 2: Lead Magnet vs Sales Page
**Trigger:** Free offer capture
**Adjustment:**
- Form fields: Minimum (name + email only)
- No price comparison needed
- Guarantee = quality of free content
- Exit-intent: Different free asset

### Exception 3: High-Ticket Offers
**Trigger:** Price >R$5,000
**Adjustment:**
- Add application step (qualification)
- More authority elements needed
- More cases required
- May need sales call CTA instead of direct purchase

### Exception 4: Technical/B2B Audience
**Trigger:** Sophisticated buyer
**Adjustment:**
- More specific claims
- More detailed proof
- Less emotional, more logical
- ROI-focused copy

### Exception 5: Regulated Industries
**Trigger:** Health, finance, legal
**Adjustment:**
- Extensive disclaimers mandatory
- Claims must be verified
- Legal review required
- May need compliance approval

## Appendix A: The 5 Fatal Errors

### Erro Fatal #1: Vender Recursos em Vez de Resultados
**O Que Vejo:** "10 módulos + 50 templates + grupo no Facebook"
**Por Que Mata:** Ninguém compra brocas, compram buracos.
**A Correção:** Para cada feature, complete: "...para que você possa [RESULTADO EMOCIONAL]"

**Exemplo:**
- ❌ "Acesso ao grupo VIP no Facebook"
- ✅ "Rede de networking com outros donos de agência faturando 6-7 dígitos para que você nunca mais se sinta isolado construindo seu império"

### Erro Fatal #2: Múltiplas Ofertas na Mesma Página
**O Que Vejo:** "Curso básico por R$297 OU curso avançado por R$997 OU consultoria por R$5000"
**Por Que Mata:** Paradoxo da escolha. Quanto mais opções, menor a conversão.
**A Correção:** Uma landing page para cada oferta.
**Regra Hormozi:** "Confused mind says no. Excited mind says yes."

### Erro Fatal #3: Garantia Fraca ou Inexistente
**O Que Vejo:** "Satisfação garantida" ou pior: nenhuma garantia.
**Por Que Mata:** Sem reversão de risco, a Probabilidade Percebida permanece baixa.
**A Correção:** Garantia específica, condicional e até "unfair":
```
GARANTIA TRIPLA "VITÓRIA CERTA":
✓ Implemente por 21 dias. Sem resultados? Dinheiro de volta.
✓ Não ficar satisfeito por qualquer motivo? Dinheiro de volta.
✓ Aplicar tudo e não ter ROI positivo? Devolvemos 2X seu investimento.
```

### Erro Fatal #4: Preço Sem Contexto
**O Que Vejo:** "Investimento: R$997" - solto, sem ancoragem.
**Por Que Mata:** Preço sem contexto é sempre "caro".
**A Correção:** Sequência matadora:
1. Mostre o stack de valor (R$15.000 total)
2. Compare com alternativas (consultor cobra R$10k)
3. Apresente seu preço (apenas R$1.997)
4. Reforce com garantia (sem risco)
5. Adicione urgência (apenas hoje)

### Erro Fatal #5: Copy Genérico de Nicho
**O Que Vejo:** "Transforme sua vida", "Alcance seus sonhos", "Método comprovado"
**Por Que Mata:** Linguagem genérica não ressoa com ninguém.
**A Correção:** Use a linguagem EXATA que seu avatar usa.

**Exemplo Real (Academia):**
- ❌ Genérico: "Aumente sua receita"
- ✅ Específico: "Pare de brigar por sócio com mensalidade de R$49 quando você pode ter lista de espera cobrando R$149"
