## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/lead-magnet-squad-blueprint.yaml

```yaml
# Lead Magnet Creation Squad Blueprint
# Pattern: HO-SB-001 (Hormozi Squad Blueprint Standard)
# Source: $100M Leads - Alex Hormozi, Section II
# Version: 1.0.0
# Generated: 2026-02-10

squad:
  name: lead-magnet
  purpose: "Create lead magnets that get more engaged leads and customers for less money"
  domain: marketing-strategy
  source_playbook: "$100M Leads - Section II: Engaje Seus Leads"

  core_definition: |
    Lead Magnet = Complete solution to narrow problem
               + Reveals problem solved by core offer
               + Valuable enough to charge for (given free/low-cost)

  business_impact: |
    - 10x more engaged leads for same ad spend
    - 3x reduction in customer acquisition cost
    - 2-4x consumption rates with multi-format delivery

# ===============================================================================
# TIER STRUCTURE
# ===============================================================================

tier_structure:
  orchestrator:
    - agent: magnet-architect
      role: "Orchestrate 7-step lead magnet creation process"
      decisions:
        - "Guide problem selection through Problem-Solution Cycle"
        - "Ensure type matches offer structure"
        - "Coordinate testing and iteration"
      kpis:
        - "Lead magnet to core offer conversion rate"
        - "Cost per engaged lead"
        - "Time to winning variant"

  tier_0_diagnosis:
    - agent: problem-mapper
      role: "Map Problem-Solution Cycles and identify narrow problems"
      inputs:
        - "Core offer description"
        - "Target customer profile"
        - "Customer problems list"
      outputs:
        - "Problem-Solution Cycle diagram"
        - "Ranked list of narrow problems"
        - "Next-problem-revealed validation"

    - agent: type-selector
      role: "Select optimal lead magnet type"
      inputs:
        - "Selected narrow problem"
        - "Core offer structure"
        - "Audience awareness level"
      outputs:
        - "Recommended type (Reveal/Sample/OneStep)"
        - "Rationale documentation"
        - "Alternative types if primary fails"

  tier_1_execution:
    - agent: delivery-designer
      role: "Design delivery methods and create 12-variant matrix"
      specialization: "Step 3: Delivery Method Selection"
      capabilities:
        - "Map single problem to all 4 delivery methods"
        - "Prioritize based on feasibility and audience preference"
        - "Create rotation schedule for testing"

    - agent: name-tester
      role: "Test titles, images, and subtitles systematically"
      specialization: "Step 4: Name Testing"
      capabilities:
        - "Design A/B test sequences"
        - "Analyze engagement data"
        - "Identify 'mega winner' signals"
      techniques:
        - "Poll audiences (social, DM, email)"
        - "A/B test on ad platforms"
        - "Iterative elimination rounds"

    - agent: format-multiplier
      role: "Package lead magnets in multiple consumption formats"
      specialization: "Step 5: Easy Consumption"
      capabilities:
        - "Convert content to video, audio, text, images"
        - "Optimize for mobile and desktop"
        - "Reduce friction in access/delivery"

    - agent: cta-crafter
      role: "Create compelling Calls To Action with reasons"
      specialization: "Step 7: CTA Creation"
      capabilities:
        - "Write clear action statements"
        - "Apply scarcity (ethical/real)"
        - "Apply urgency (time-limited)"
        - "Invent compelling reasons (Frat Party Host)"

  tier_2_judgment:
    - agent: quality-guardian
      role: "Ensure lead magnets are 'charge-worthy' quality"
      specialization: "Step 6: Quality Assurance"
      responsibilities:
        - "Validate 'could charge for this' bar"
        - "Ensure secrets given, not withheld"
        - "Check value exceeds core offer cost perception"
      philosophy: |
        "Give away the secrets, sell the implementation.
        99% won't buy but will create/destroy your reputation."

    - agent: cycle-validator
      role: "Validate Problem-Solution Cycle completion"
      responsibilities:
        - "Confirm narrow problem is truly narrow"
        - "Confirm solution reveals core offer problem"
        - "Ensure no cycle breaks in the logic"
      checklist:
        - "Problem is specific, not broad"
        - "Solution is complete for that problem"
        - "New problem revealed is real"
        - "Core offer solves revealed problem"

    - agent: roi-analyst
      role: "Calculate and track lead magnet ROI"
      responsibilities:
        - "Calculate cost per engaged lead"
        - "Compare with/without lead magnet CAC"
        - "Identify highest ROI variants"
        - "Recommend budget allocation"

# ===============================================================================
# AGENT DEFINITIONS
# ===============================================================================

agents:
  magnet-architect:
    id: magnet-architect
    title: "Lead Magnet Architect"
    tier: orchestrator
    icon: "magnet"

    purpose: |
      Guide the complete 7-step lead magnet creation process.
      Ensure each step builds on the previous and maintains
      alignment with the Problem-Solution Cycle.

    core_frameworks:
      - name: "7 Steps to Effective Lead Magnets"
        source: "$100M Leads p.123-126"
        steps:
          - "Discover problem to solve and for whom"
          - "Figure out how to solve it"
          - "Figure out how to deliver it"
          - "Test how to name it"
          - "Make it easy to consume"
          - "Make it really good"
          - "Make it easy to say they want more"

      - name: "Problem-Solution Cycle"
        source: "$100M Leads p.133-138"
        principle: "Every problem has solution. Every solution reveals more problems."

      - name: "Grand Slam Offers for Free"
        source: "$100M Leads p.127-128"
        principle: "Make lead magnet so good they feel stupid saying no"

    decision_authority:
      - "Approve problem selection"
      - "Validate type selection"
      - "Approve for testing"
      - "Declare winning variant"

    inputs:
      - "Core offer documentation"
      - "Target customer profile"
      - "Available resources/budget"
      - "Testing platform access"

    outputs:
      - "Approved lead magnet concept"
      - "Testing schedule"
      - "Winning variant declaration"
      - "ROI report"

  problem-mapper:
    id: problem-mapper
    title: "Problem-Solution Cycle Specialist"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "map"

    purpose: |
      Map the Problem-Solution Cycle for any business and identify
      the best narrow problems for lead magnets.

    methodology:
      step_1: "Document core offer (what broad problem it solves)"
      step_2: "List all steps/problems before that broad solution"
      step_3: "For each narrow problem, validate it reveals core offer problem"
      step_4: "Rank by: narrowness, significance, revelation strength"

    source_example: |
      Real Estate Example (p.140-142):
      Core Offer: Help sell houses
      Narrow Problems: home value, increasing value, photos, cleaning,
      landscaping, repairs, moving, staging
      Each solves specific problem -> Reveals "still need to sell"

    outputs:
      - format: "Problem-Solution Cycle Diagram"
        content:
          - "Core offer (broad solution)"
          - "All narrow problems identified"
          - "Arrows showing revelation flow"
          - "Recommended problem highlighted"

      - format: "Problem Ranking Matrix"
        content:
          - "Problem name"
          - "Narrowness score (1-5)"
          - "Significance score (1-5)"
          - "Revelation strength (1-5)"
          - "Total score"

    validation_questions:
      - "Is this problem narrow enough? (Not broad like 'sell house')"
      - "Is this problem significant? (People care about solving it)"
      - "Does solving it reveal the core offer problem?"
      - "Can we solve it completely with a lead magnet?"

  type-selector:
    id: type-selector
    title: "Lead Magnet Type Specialist"
    tier: tier_0
    icon: "category"

    purpose: |
      Select the optimal lead magnet type based on audience awareness,
      problem nature, and core offer structure.

    type_definitions:
      reveal_problems:
        name: "Reveal Problems (Diagnosis)"
        source: "$100M Leads p.151-158"
        best_when: "Problems worsen over time; audience unaware of gap"
        examples:
          - "Speed test showing 30% below standard"
          - "Posture analysis showing ideal vs current"
          - "Termite inspection revealing damage/risk"
        mechanism: "Show gap between where they are and should be"

      samples_trials:
        name: "Samples & Trials"
        source: "$100M Leads p.160-167"
        best_when: "Core offer solves recurring problem with recurring solution"
        examples:
          - "Free trial of faster server"
          - "Free chiropractic adjustment"
          - "Sample-size consumables (Costco model)"
        mechanism: "Full access, limited time or uses"

      one_step:
        name: "One Step of Multi-Step Process"
        source: "$100M Leads p.169-176"
        best_when: "Core offer is complex multi-step process"
        examples:
          - "This book (step to $1M, reveals scaling problems)"
          - "First coat of 3-coat sealer system"
          - "Free finance course revealing time investment"
        mechanism: "Give valuable step, sell the rest"

    selection_algorithm:
      - condition: "Audience doesn't know they have the problem"
        recommendation: "Reveal Problems"
        rationale: "Must create awareness before solution desire"

      - condition: "Core offer is recurring solution to recurring problem"
        recommendation: "Samples & Trials"
        rationale: "Let them experience full value, want to continue"

      - condition: "Core offer has multiple steps"
        recommendation: "One Step of Multi-Step"
        rationale: "Prove value on one step, they'll want the rest"

    outputs:
      - "Primary type recommendation with rationale"
      - "Secondary type if primary doesn't test well"
      - "Type-specific implementation notes"

  delivery-designer:
    id: delivery-designer
    title: "Delivery Method Designer"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "package"

    purpose: |
      Design all possible delivery methods for a lead magnet
      and create the 12-variant testing matrix.

    delivery_methods:
      software:
        description: "Give them a tool (spreadsheet, calculator, app)"
        source: "$100M Leads p.184"
        examples:
          - "Dashboard with stats and industry comparison"
          - "Calculator for their specific situation"
          - "Assessment tool with scoring"
        best_for: "Data-driven problems, comparison needs"

      information:
        description: "Teach them something"
        source: "$100M Leads p.186"
        formats: ["Courses", "Lessons", "Interviews", "Presentations",
                  "Live events", "Mistakes/pitfalls", "Hacks/tips"]
        examples:
          - "Mini course on specific skill"
          - "Expert interview compilation"
          - "Mistakes to avoid guide"
        best_for: "Knowledge gaps, skill development"

      services:
        description: "Do free work for them"
        source: "$100M Leads p.188"
        examples:
          - "Run their ads free for 30 days"
          - "Free audit/analysis"
          - "First session/adjustment free"
        best_for: "Demonstrating expertise, removing risk"

      physical_products:
        description: "Give something they can hold"
        source: "$100M Leads p.190-191"
        examples:
          - "Book on their topic"
          - "Sample products"
          - "Assessment charts/materials"
        best_for: "Tangible value perception, retention"

    matrix_creation:
      source: "$100M Leads p.192"
      principle: "3 types x 4 methods = up to 12 lead magnets for single problem"

      template: |
        For problem: [INSERT PROBLEM]

        | Type/Method     | Software | Information | Services | Physical |
        |-----------------|----------|-------------|----------|----------|
        | Reveal Problems | Idea 1   | Idea 2      | Idea 3   | Idea 4   |
        | Samples/Trials  | Idea 5   | Idea 6      | Idea 7   | Idea 8   |
        | One Step        | Idea 9   | Idea 10     | Idea 11  | Idea 12  |

    rotation_strategy:
      source: "$100M Leads p.193-195"
      principle: |
        "Make as many versions as you can and rotate them.
        Keeps advertising fresh with little effort.
        See which work best. Results often surprising."

    outputs:
      - "12-variant matrix populated"
      - "Feasibility assessment per variant"
      - "Prioritized testing order"
      - "Rotation schedule"

  name-tester:
    id: name-tester
    title: "Name Testing Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "flask"

    purpose: |
      Systematically test titles, images, and subtitles to find
      the winning combination that maximizes engagement.

    ogilvy_principle:
      source: "$100M Leads p.199-200"
      quote: |
        "When you've written your headline, you've spent 80 cents
        of your (advertising) dollar... 5x more people read your
        headline than any other part of your promotion."

    impact_range:
      source: "$100M Leads p.200"
      potential: "2x, 3x, or 10x engagement from name improvement"

    testing_order:
      - priority: 1
        element: "Title"
        rationale: "Most important - test first"
        minimum_variations: 3

      - priority: 2
        element: "Image"
        rationale: "Second most important"
        minimum_variations: 2

      - priority: 3
        element: "Subtitle"
        rationale: "Third - refines the hook"
        minimum_variations: 3

    real_example:
      source: "$100M Leads p.206-228"
      book: "$100M Leads"

      title_tests:
        - round: 1
          options: ["Advertising", "Promotion"]
          winner: "Advertising"
        - round: 2
          options: ["Advertising", "Leads"]
          winner: "Leads"
        - round: 3
          options: ["Marketing", "Leads"]
          winner: "Leads"

      image_tests:
        - options: ["Real photo", "Cartoon"]
          winner: "Real photo"

      subtitle_tests:
        - round: 1
          options:
            - "How to make more people want to buy your stuff"
            - "How to make strangers want to buy your stuff"
          winner: "strangers"
        - round: 2
          options:
            - "How to make more strangers want to buy your stuff"
            - "How to make strangers want to buy your stuff"
          winner: "removing 'more'"
          insight: "Small changes = big differences"

    testing_methods:
      polls:
        description: "Ask audience to vote"
        source: "$100M Leads p.236"
        format: "Post options, ask for 1 or 2"

      dm_outreach:
        description: "Message people directly"
        source: "$100M Leads p.236"
        format: "Ask individuals for gut reaction"

      ad_platform:
        description: "Run actual A/B tests"
        format: "Split traffic between variants"

    winner_signals:
      good_winner:
        source: "$100M Leads p.236"
        signal: "People engage in mass"

      mega_winner:
        source: "$100M Leads p.238-239"
        signal: "People respond AND ask when they can get it"

    outputs:
      - "Test plan with variants and timeline"
      - "Round-by-round results"
      - "Winning title/image/subtitle combination"
      - "Statistical confidence notes"

  format-multiplier:
    id: format-multiplier
    title: "Multi-Format Packaging Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "layers"

    purpose: |
      Package lead magnets in all consumption formats to maximize
      uptake and consumption rates.

    core_principle:
      source: "$100M Leads p.241"
      quote: "People prefer to do things that require less effort."

    impact:
      source: "$100M Leads p.242-243"
      potential: "2x, 3x, even 4x+ in acceptance and consumption rates"

    format_guidelines:
      software:
        source: "$100M Leads p.244"
        rule: "Accessible on phones, computers, multiple formats"
        tactics:
          - "Mobile app version"
          - "Desktop version"
          - "Web-based version"
          - "Exportable formats"

      information:
        source: "$100M Leads p.246"
        rule: "Video + Text + Audio + Images - offer ALL"
        tactics:
          - "Video version for watchers"
          - "Written version for readers"
          - "Audio version for listeners"
          - "Visual summaries/infographics"

      services:
        source: "$100M Leads p.248"
        rule: "More hours, more days, more channels"
        tactics:
          - "Extended availability hours"
          - "Multiple day options"
          - "Video call, phone, in-person options"

      physical:
        source: "$100M Leads p.250"
        rule: "Easy to order, fast delivery, simple to use"
        tactics:
          - "One-click ordering"
          - "Fast shipping"
          - "Clear instructions"
          - "Quality packaging"

    real_example:
      source: "$100M Leads p.253-255"
      product: "$100M Offers book"
      split: "Almost perfect 1/4, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4"
      formats: ["Ebook", "Physical book", "Audiobook", "Video (free on site)"]
      result: "2-3-4x the leads for same work"

    outputs:
      - "Format availability checklist"
      - "Conversion plan for each format"
      - "Accessibility audit"
      - "Friction reduction recommendations"

  quality-guardian:
    id: quality-guardian
    title: "Lead Magnet Quality Guardian"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "shield"

    purpose: |
      Ensure every lead magnet meets the "charge-worthy" quality bar.
      Guard against value withholding that destroys reputation.

    quality_standard:
      source: "$100M Leads p.257-259"
      principle: |
        "You want your lead magnet to provide so much value that
        people feel obligated to pay you. The goal is to provide
        more value than the cost of your core offer before they buy."

    fear_of_secrets:
      source: "$100M Leads p.260-261"
      warning: |
        "If you're afraid to give away your secrets, imagine the alternative:
        You give away worthless crap. Then people who could have become
        customers think 'this person is terrible!' Then they buy from
        someone else. Not only that, they tell others not to buy from you.
        It's a vicious cycle."

    philosophy:
      source: "$100M Leads p.266-267"
      principle: |
        "99% of people won't buy, but they will create (or destroy)
        your reputation based on the value of your free stuff.
        So make your lead magnets as good as your paid stuff."

    validation_checklist:
      - question: "Could we charge money for this?"
        pass_if: "Yes, and it would sell"

      - question: "Does it feel like giving away too much?"
        pass_if: "Yes - that's the right feeling"

      - question: "Are we withholding secrets?"
        pass_if: "No - secrets given, implementation sold"

      - question: "Would consuming this make someone more likely to buy?"
        pass_if: "Yes - value delivered builds trust"

      - question: "Would someone recommend this even if they don't buy?"
        pass_if: "Yes - reputation building"

    outputs:
      - "Quality assessment score"
      - "Value density analysis"
      - "Recommendation (pass/revise)"
      - "Revision notes if needed"

  cta-crafter:
    id: cta-crafter
    title: "Call To Action Specialist"
    tier: tier_1
    icon: "zap"

    purpose: |
      Create compelling CTAs that tell people exactly what to do
      and give them reasons to do it now.

    cta_components:
      source: "$100M Leads p.269-273"
      required:
        - element: "What to do"
          description: "Clear, simple, direct action"
          examples: ["Call now", "Click here", "Book a call", "Sign up"]
          rule: "Not 'don't delay' but 'call now'"

        - element: "Reasons to do it now"
          description: "Why not delay"
          types: ["Scarcity", "Urgency", "Invented reasons"]

    scarcity:
      source: "$100M Leads p.276-282"
      definition: "Limited quantity of something"
      best_strategy: "Reality - advertise your actual limitations"
      examples:
        - script: "The most convenient class times fill up fast. Call now to get the one you want."
          source: "p.278-279"
        - script: "I can only handle five people per week, so if you want to solve this soon, do xyz..."
          source: "p.280"
        - script: "We only printed one batch of shirts and will never reprint this design..."
          source: "p.281-282"

    urgency:
      source: "$100M Leads p.284-290"
      definition: "Limited time to act"
      mechanism: "Less time = faster action"
      examples:
        - script: "Our July 4th promotion ends Monday at midnight, so if you want it, act now."
          source: "p.286-287"
        - script: "Our Black Friday promotion ends at midnight. Only four hours left."
          source: "p.288"
        - script: "Until Friday, I'll also throw in a free hat for anyone who buys 3+ books."
          source: "p.289-290"

    invented_reasons:
      source: "$100M Leads p.292-297"
      nickname: "Frat Party Host"
      principle: "Fraternities don't need reasons to party but they invent crazy ones"
      harvard_study: "People more likely to let someone cut in line if given ANY reason"
      examples:
        - "Because... moms know best."
        - "Because... your country needs you."
        - "Because... it's my birthday, and I want you to celebrate with me."

    action_step:
      source: "$100M Leads p.298-299"
      rule: |
        "Give a clear, simple, action-oriented CTA. Then give them
        a 'reason' using scarcity, urgency, and any other reasons
        you can think of. And do it often. Don't be clever, be clear."

    outputs:
      - "CTA statement (clear action)"
      - "Scarcity element (if applicable)"
      - "Urgency element (if applicable)"
      - "Additional reason(s)"
      - "Placement recommendations (where/when to show)"

  roi-analyst:
    id: roi-analyst
    title: "Lead Magnet ROI Analyst"
    tier: tier_2
    icon: "chart"

    purpose: |
      Calculate and track the ROI of lead magnets vs direct
      core offer advertising.

    roi_framework:
      source: "$100M Leads p.302-311"

      without_lead_magnet:
        example:
          profit_per_customer: "$10,000"
          ad_cost_per_call: "$1,000"
          close_rate: "1 in 3"
          cac: "$3,000 (3 calls x $1,000)"
          profit_after_cac: "$7,000"

      with_lead_magnet:
        example:
          lead_magnet_delivery_cost: "$25"
          ad_cost_per_call: "$75 (lower because free = more engagement)"
          total_cost_per_call: "$100"
          close_rate: "1 in 10"
          cac: "$1,000 (10 calls x $100)"
          improvement: "3x reduction in CAC"
          same_budget_result: "3x business growth"

    key_insight:
      source: "$100M Leads p.309-311"
      principle: |
        "With a $25 budget to deliver your lead magnet, you can provide
        A LOT more value than a $0 budget. You attract more customers
        because your lead magnet is more valuable than others."

    metrics_to_track:
      - name: "Cost per engaged lead"
        formula: "Ad spend / engaged leads"
        comparison: "With vs without lead magnet"

      - name: "Lead magnet to call rate"
        formula: "Calls scheduled / lead magnet consumers"

      - name: "Customer acquisition cost"
        formula: "Total cost / customers acquired"

      - name: "ROI per variant"
        formula: "(Revenue - Cost) / Cost"

    outputs:
      - "ROI comparison report"
      - "Variant performance ranking"
      - "Budget allocation recommendations"
      - "Scaling projections"

# ===============================================================================
# EXECUTOR MATRIX
# ===============================================================================

executor_matrix:
  # Step 1: Problem Discovery
  - task: "Document core offer and broad problem it solves"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must be clear, single sentence"

  - task: "List all narrow problems before broad solution"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "AI can suggest, human validates relevance"

  - task: "Validate each problem reveals core offer problem"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Logic must be airtight"

  - task: "Rank problems by narrowness, significance, revelation"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Human approves final ranking"

  # Step 2: Type Selection
  - task: "Assess audience awareness level"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Use customer research data"

  - task: "Match problem to lead magnet type"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Strategic decision"

  - task: "Document rationale for type selection"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Template-based"

  # Step 3: Delivery Method
  - task: "Brainstorm all 4 delivery methods for problem"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "AI generates, human evaluates"

  - task: "Populate 12-variant matrix"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "At least 4 viable variants"

  - task: "Assess feasibility per variant"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Resource and capability check"

  - task: "Prioritize testing order"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Strategic decision"

  # Step 4: Name Testing
  - task: "Generate title variations"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "AI suggests, human curates"

  - task: "Create poll/test structure"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Follow A/B test best practices"

  - task: "Run tests on platforms"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Minimum sample sizes"

  - task: "Analyze results and declare winner"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Statistical significance required"

  - task: "Test images and subtitles"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Only after title winner declared"

  # Step 5: Format Multiplication
  - task: "Identify all possible consumption formats"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Checklist-based"

  - task: "Convert content to each format"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Quality check each conversion"

  - task: "Optimize for mobile/desktop"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Accessibility standards"

  - task: "Reduce access/delivery friction"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "User testing recommended"

  # Step 6: Quality Assurance
  - task: "Validate 'could charge for it' bar"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Expert judgment required"

  - task: "Check for withheld secrets"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Mindset shift may be needed"

  - task: "Assess reputation impact"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Consider non-buyer perception"

  # Step 7: CTA Creation
  - task: "Write clear action statement"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Simple, direct language"

  - task: "Identify real scarcity elements"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must be truthful"

  - task: "Design urgency mechanics"
    executor: Human
    automation: LOW
    guardrails: "Must be legitimate"

  - task: "Create compelling reasons"
    executor: Hybrid
    automation: MEDIUM
    guardrails: "Can be invented but authentic"

  - task: "Place CTAs throughout journey"
    executor: Worker
    automation: HIGH
    guardrails: "Frequency guidelines"

# ===============================================================================
# QUALITY GATES
# ===============================================================================

quality_gates:
  QG-001:
    name: "Problem Narrowness Gate"
    transition: "Problem Selection -> Type Selection"
    condition: "problem_is_narrow AND problem_reveals_core_offer_problem"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Return to problem mapping, narrow further"
    source: "$100M Leads p.138-144"

  QG-002:
    name: "Type-Problem Match Gate"
    transition: "Type Selection -> Delivery Design"
    condition: "type_matches_audience_awareness AND type_matches_offer_structure"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Re-evaluate type selection"
    source: "$100M Leads p.147-178"

  QG-003:
    name: "Delivery Feasibility Gate"
    transition: "Delivery Design -> Name Testing"
    condition: "at_least_one_variant_feasible"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Simplify delivery or increase resources"
    source: "$100M Leads p.180-197"

  QG-004:
    name: "Name Winner Gate"
    transition: "Name Testing -> Format Multiplication"
    condition: "clear_winner_identified OR mega_winner_signal"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Continue testing or pivot problem"
    source: "$100M Leads p.199-239"

  QG-005:
    name: "Format Accessibility Gate"
    transition: "Format Multiplication -> Quality Check"
    condition: "at_least_two_formats_available"
    type: warning
    failure_action: "Add more formats before launch"
    source: "$100M Leads p.241-255"

  QG-006:
    name: "Quality Bar Gate"
    transition: "Quality Check -> CTA Creation"
    condition: "could_charge_for_it AND secrets_not_withheld"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Increase value until passing"
    source: "$100M Leads p.257-267"

  QG-007:
    name: "CTA Completeness Gate"
    transition: "CTA Creation -> Launch"
    condition: "clear_action AND at_least_one_reason"
    type: blocking
    failure_action: "Add missing CTA elements"
    source: "$100M Leads p.269-299"

# ===============================================================================
# WORKFLOWS
# ===============================================================================

workflows:
  lead_magnet_creation:
    trigger: "New lead magnet needed"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        name: "Problem Discovery"
        agent: problem-mapper
        action: "Map Problem-Solution Cycle, identify narrow problems"
        output: "Ranked problem list"
        gate: QG-001

      - step: 2
        name: "Type Selection"
        agent: type-selector
        action: "Select optimal lead magnet type"
        output: "Type with rationale"
        gate: QG-002

      - step: 3
        name: "Delivery Design"
        agent: delivery-designer
        action: "Create 12-variant matrix, prioritize testing"
        output: "Delivery variants and test order"
        gate: QG-003

      - step: 4
        name: "Name Testing"
        agent: name-tester
        action: "Test titles, images, subtitles systematically"
        output: "Winning name combination"
        gate: QG-004

      - step: 5
        name: "Format Multiplication"
        agent: format-multiplier
        action: "Package in multiple consumption formats"
        output: "Multi-format lead magnet"
        gate: QG-005

      - step: 6
        name: "Quality Validation"
        agent: quality-guardian
        action: "Validate charge-worthy quality"
        output: "Quality certification"
        gate: QG-006

      - step: 7
        name: "CTA Creation"
        agent: cta-crafter
        action: "Create CTAs with reasons to act now"
        output: "CTA copy and placement plan"
        gate: QG-007

  lead_magnet_optimization:
    trigger: "Existing lead magnet underperforming"
    steps:
      - step: 1
        agent: roi-analyst
        action: "Diagnose performance gaps"
        output: "Gap analysis report"

      - step: 2
        agent: cycle-validator
        action: "Validate Problem-Solution Cycle integrity"
        output: "Cycle validation report"

      - step: 3
        agent: name-tester
        action: "Re-test naming if engagement low"
        condition: "If engagement metrics below threshold"

      - step: 4
        agent: quality-guardian
        action: "Re-assess quality if conversion low"
        condition: "If consumption-to-conversion below threshold"

      - step: 5
        agent: cta-crafter
        action: "Strengthen CTAs if conversion low"
        condition: "If conversion metrics below threshold"

# ===============================================================================
# KPIs & SUCCESS METRICS
# ===============================================================================

kpis:
  primary:
    engagement_rate:
      formula: "Engaged leads / Total impressions"
      target: "Higher than core offer direct"
      source: "$100M Leads - engagement principle"

    consumption_rate:
      formula: "Consumers / Engaged leads"
      target: ">50%"
      source: "$100M Leads p.241-243 (2-4x with easy consumption)"

    cost_per_engaged_lead:
      formula: "Ad spend / Engaged leads"
      target: "Lower than without lead magnet"
      source: "$100M Leads p.302-307"

  secondary:
    lead_magnet_to_call_rate:
      formula: "Calls / Lead magnet consumers"
      benchmark: "1 in 10 (10%)"
      source: "$100M Leads p.305"

    customer_acquisition_cost:
      formula: "Total cost / Customers"
      target: "3x lower than without lead magnet"
      source: "$100M Leads p.306-307"

    roi_per_variant:
      formula: "(Revenue - Cost) / Cost"
      tracking: "Compare all 12 variants"

  by_step:
    step_1_problem:
      - "Problem narrowness score"
      - "Revelation clarity score"

    step_4_naming:
      - "Title test engagement rates"
      - "Subtitle test engagement rates"
      - "Time to winner identification"

    step_5_formats:
      - "Format split percentage"
      - "Consumption rate by format"

    step_7_cta:
      - "Click-through rate"
      - "Conversion rate by CTA variant"

# ===============================================================================
# TROUBLESHOOTING
# ===============================================================================

troubleshooting:
  - symptom: "Low engagement on lead magnet"
    possible_causes:
      - "Name/title not compelling"
      - "Problem not relevant to audience"
      - "Delivery method mismatch"
    diagnosis:
      - "Check name test results"
      - "Validate problem with audience research"
      - "Survey for format preferences"
    solutions:
      - "Re-run name testing with more variations"
      - "Return to problem mapping"
      - "Try different delivery method"

  - symptom: "High engagement, low consumption"
    possible_causes:
      - "Too difficult to access"
      - "Too long/complex"
      - "Wrong format for audience"
    diagnosis:
      - "Audit access friction"
      - "Check completion rates by section"
      - "Survey format preferences"
    solutions:
      - "Add more formats (2-4x potential)"
      - "Simplify/shorten"
      - "Create summary version"

  - symptom: "High consumption, low conversion to core offer"
    possible_causes:
      - "Problem doesn't reveal core offer need"
      - "Quality not high enough"
      - "CTA weak or missing"
    diagnosis:
      - "Re-validate Problem-Solution Cycle"
      - "Quality audit (could charge?)"
      - "CTA presence/strength audit"
    solutions:
      - "Choose different narrow problem"
      - "Increase value until 'too much'"
      - "Add scarcity/urgency/reasons"

  - symptom: "High CAC despite lead magnet"
    possible_causes:
      - "Lead magnet attracting wrong audience"
      - "Core offer mismatch"
      - "Competition in space"
    diagnosis:
      - "Analyze lead quality"
      - "Check offer-magnet alignment"
      - "Competitive analysis"
    solutions:
      - "Narrow targeting"
      - "Realign or change lead magnet"
      - "Increase value differentiation"

# VALIDATION
# ===============================================================================
```

## Referência: references/squad/docs/sops/lead-nurture-sop.md

# Lead Nurture SOP

> **Source:** $100M Playbook: Lead Nurture - Alex Hormozi
> **Pattern:** SC-PE-001 (SOP Extraction Standard)
> **Version:** 1.0.0
> **Extracted:** 2026-02-10

---

## Part 1: Purpose

Transform leads who show interest into scheduled appointments who actually show up to buy. The Lead Nurture process maximizes **throughput** - the total percentage of engaged leads that show up to appointments.

**Core Equation:**
```
Throughput = Schedule Rate × Show Rate

Example:
- 100 Leads
- 50% Schedule Rate = 50 Appointments
- 50% Show Rate = 25 Shows
- Throughput = 25%
```

**Business Impact:** A 20-40% increase in show rates translates directly to revenue. At 20% margins, this means 2-3x profit increase.

---

## Part 2: Scope

### When This SOP Applies
- Leads have shown interest (opted in, filled form, responded to ad)
- Time between advertising and sales appointment
- Medium-term nurture: maximizing 30-day show rates

### When This SOP Does NOT Apply
- Long-term follow-up (emails, podcasts, content) - covered in other playbooks
- Pre-advertising lead generation
- Post-sale customer success

### Business Types
- Any business with scheduled appointments (phone, video, in-person)
- B2B and B2C
- High-ticket and low-ticket (adjust tactics accordingly)

---

## Part 3: Preconditions

| Precondition | Requirement | Validation |
|--------------|-------------|------------|
| Lead Source | Opt-in mechanism exists | Forms, ads, landing pages active |
| CRM/Scheduler | System to track leads and appointments | Software configured |
| Sales Team | Personnel available to contact leads | Capacity mapped |
| Communication Channels | Phone, SMS, Email, DM access | All channels operational |
| Lead Scoring System | Red/Yellow/Green classification | Criteria defined |
| Incentive Inventory | Gifts or A/B options available | Stock verified |

---

## Part 4: The Four Pillars Framework

### Pillar Overview

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    FOUR PILLARS OF LEAD NURTURE                        │
├──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────────┤
│ AVAILABILITY │    SPEED     │ PERSONALIZATION  │       VOLUME          │
├──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ More slots   │ Faster       │ More relevant    │ More attempts         │
│ = More shows │ = More shows │ = More shows     │ = More shows          │
├──────────────┼──────────────┼──────────────────┼───────────────────────┤
│ Days/week    │ <5 min first │ Preferred medium │ 7+ reach-outs         │
│ Hours/day    │ <72h appt    │ Lead scoring     │ Auto reminders        │
│ Slots/hour   │ Fast replies │ Segment messages │ Manual reminders      │
│ Multi-option │ Pull forward │ Incentives/Proof │ BAMFAM               │
└──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────┴───────────────────────┘
```

---

## Part 5: Process Steps

### PILLAR I: AVAILABILITY

#### Step 1.1: Maximize Days Per Week
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Schedule appointments all 7 days per week |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis (operational decision) |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Calendar configuration |
| **Executor** | Worker (initial setup) → Human (staffing decisions) |
| **Precondition** | Business hours policy defined |
| **Output** | 7-day availability calendar |
| **Guardrails** | Staff rotation schedule required |
| **Decision Rule** | "You pay rent 7 days/week. Make money 7 days/week." |

**Rationale:** 5 days = 71% availability. 7 days = 100% availability. 40% more opportunity.

#### Step 1.2: Maximize Hours Per Day
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Extend appointment hours (target: 6am-6pm PST minimum) |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Calendar rules |
| **Executor** | Worker (config) → Human (staffing) |
| **Precondition** | Coverage capacity determined |
| **Output** | Extended hours calendar |
| **Guardrails** | Nationwide coverage: 9am-9pm EST recommended |
| **Decision Rule** | "Be available when customers are available to buy" |

#### Step 1.3: Increase Time Slot Flexibility
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Offer 4 scheduling options per hour (every 15 minutes) |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception (customer convenience) |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Scheduler configuration |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Appointment duration defined |
| **Output** | 15-minute interval scheduler |
| **Guardrails** | May create gaps; use gaps for lead follow-up |
| **Decision Rule** | "Convenient for lead > convenient for business" |

#### Step 1.4: Enable Multi-Channel Scheduling
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Provide inbound, outbound, AND self-scheduling options |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker (self-schedule) + Hybrid (inbound/outbound) |
| **Precondition** | All channels configured |
| **Output** | Tri-channel booking system |
| **Guardrails** | Self-scheduler must have visible time slots, minimal steps |

**Self-Scheduler Optimization:**
1. Header confirms right place + next action + why
2. Available dates/times visible immediately (mobile + desktop)
3. Eliminate steps - don't ask info already provided
4. Show person's name/photo for human connection

---

### PILLAR II: SPEED

#### Step 2.1: Speed to First Contact
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Contact leads within 5 minutes of opt-in |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception (trigger detection) → Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH (notification) + Hybrid (call) |
| **Executor** | Worker (alert) → Human (call) |
| **Precondition** | Real-time lead notification system |
| **Output** | First contact completed |
| **Guardrails** | 60-second target for 391% conversion increase |
| **Decision Rule** | "If not hearing 'that was fast!' daily = too slow" |

**Statistics:**
- 391% increase in conversions when contacted in 60 seconds (Velocify)
- 7x more likely to qualify vs 1 hour later (HBR)
- 78% buy from first responder (Lead Connect)

#### Step 2.2: Speed to First Appointment
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Book appointments within 72 hours maximum |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Human override needed |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Contact established |
| **Output** | Appointment scheduled <72h out |
| **Guardrails** | Same-day = best, never >5 days |
| **Decision Rule** | "Closer scheduling = higher show rate" |

**Appointment Outcomes (priority order):**
1. Close them NOW (talking right now = 100% show)
2. Hot handoff to active closer
3. Pull appointment forward to today
4. Confirm within 72h window
5. Remove unqualified from calendar

#### Step 2.3: Pull Appointments Forward
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Call scheduled leads to move appointments sooner |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment + Negotiation |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Requires conversation |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Appointment already scheduled |
| **Output** | Moved appointment or confirmed |
| **Guardrails** | Use gaps between appointments for this activity |

**Pull Forward Script:**
```
"Hey, this is [Name] calling from [Company] on a recorded line...
I saw you booked a time for [X] on [Day]. Just calling to confirm
some details before your appointment. Is now a terrible time?

[Qualify: WHO they are, WHAT they want, WHAT they've tried]

Okay great. Two things:
1. Good news: I think we can help you out.
2. Better news: I have an opening that canceled today at [time]...
   unless now is a good time?"
```

#### Step 2.4: Speed of Response
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Respond to all lead messages within minutes |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception + Execution |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Can alert, human responds |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Message received |
| **Output** | Response sent promptly |
| **Guardrails** | Track response times by rep |
| **Decision Rule** | "Slow response = 'we don't prioritize you'" |

---

### PILLAR III: PERSONALIZATION

#### Step 3.1: Use Preferred Communication Method
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Contact via ALL channels, continue where they respond |
| **Cognitive Type** | Perception + Adaptation |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH (multi-channel blast) + Human (continuation) |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Contact info for multiple channels |
| **Output** | Conversation established on preferred channel |
| **Guardrails** | Reach out like you MEAN it (not going through motions) |

**Channel Priority:**
1. Blast: Call + Text + DM + Email simultaneously
2. Continue: Wherever they respond first
3. Escalate: Move to richer medium (phone/video) when appropriate

#### Step 3.2: Qualify Leads
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Score leads and remove poor fits from calendar |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - AI can pre-score, human validates |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Qualification criteria defined |
| **Output** | Lead score (Red/Yellow/Green) |
| **Guardrails** | Canceling bad appointments = more time for good ones |

**Lead Scoring System:**
| Score | Meaning | Action |
|-------|---------|--------|
| GREEN | Prime lead | Priority routing to best closer |
| YELLOW | Less qualified | Standard process, "garbage man" opportunity |
| RED | Unqualified | Remove from calendar, offer downsell or resources |

#### Step 3.3: Route Best Leads to Best Closers
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Match lead quality to closer skill |
| **Cognitive Type** | Analysis + Optimization |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Rule-based routing |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Lead scored, closer rankings known |
| **Output** | Optimized lead-closer pairing |
| **Guardrails** | Track conversion by pairing for continuous optimization |

**Implementation:**
1. Look at best customers (demographics + actions)
2. Ask those questions in opt-ins/applications
3. Score leads 1-5 or Red/Yellow/Green
4. Route best leads → best closers
5. Track and optimize

#### Step 3.4: Segment Messaging
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Tailor communication to lead characteristics |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis + Creativity |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Templates automatable, custom research human |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Lead data collected |
| **Output** | Personalized messaging sequence |
| **Guardrails** | 5 minutes research per lead minimum for high-value |

**Easy Version:** Research lead's profile, website, social before contact
**Hard Version:** Create different email/text sequences per lead category

**Example:**
```
"Hey Greg, I see that your site traffic is down 18% this quarter.
We had another customer in a similar situation. They're now up 100%
90 days later. I prepped a walkthrough to show you how we can apply
the same principles to your auto shop."
```

#### Step 3.5: Provide Incentives
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Give leads reasons to show up |
| **Cognitive Type** | Creativity + Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH (delivery) + Human (selection) |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Incentive inventory available |
| **Output** | Incentive committed and delivered |
| **Guardrails** | Amount must not be insulting; choice creates commitment |

**Push Incentive (Gift - Reciprocity):**
```
"Hey [Name]! I wanted to make sure you're caffeinated for our
meeting tomorrow. Check your email - I just sent you a $5 gift card."
```

**Pull Incentive (A/B Choice - Commitment):**
```
"Hey [Name]! Since you're a first-time client, I'm setting aside
some free products for you. Would you prefer face cream or hand lotion?"

[They respond with choice] = Implicit commitment to show
```

**A/B Offer Categories:**
- Quantity: One bottle or two?
- Start dates: Tomorrow or Monday?
- Type: Shirt or shorts?
- Colors: Black or white?
- Personnel: John or Sara?
- Times: Morning or afternoon?

#### Step 3.6: Demonstrate Proof
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Show testimonials/case studies matching lead profile |
| **Cognitive Type** | Synthesis |
| **Automation Potential** | MEDIUM - Library automatable, matching needs judgment |
| **Executor** | Hybrid |
| **Precondition** | Proof library organized by demographic |
| **Output** | Relevant proof delivered |
| **Guardrails** | Match proof demographics to lead demographics |

**Proof Timing:**
- After schedule, before show
- Between first and second call
- Every 90 days for ghosted leads (show results of people who signed up when they ghosted)

---

### PILLAR IV: VOLUME

#### Step 4.1: First Week Contact Cadence
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Execute 7+ reach-out attempts in first week |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution (process following) |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH - Dialer/sequencer |
| **Executor** | Worker (triggers) + Human (calls) |
| **Precondition** | Lead opted in |
| **Output** | Contact established or moved to long-term nurture |
| **Guardrails** | Front-load attempts; follow local laws |

**Day 1 (Opt-in Day):**
1. Call within 5 minutes
2. Double-dial immediately
3. Leave voicemail
4. Text immediately after voicemail
5. Double-dial + text two more times (hours apart)

**Days 2-3:**
- Call 2x per day (early + late)
- Text after second call each day

**Days 4-7:**
- Call + text 1x per day

**Day 8+:**
- Transition to long-term nurture (content + soft CTAs)
- Re-engage triggers restart from top

#### Step 4.2: Automated Reminders
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Send system reminders at intervals before appointment |
| **Cognitive Type** | Memory/Retrieval |
| **Automation Potential** | HIGH |
| **Executor** | Worker |
| **Precondition** | Appointment scheduled |
| **Output** | Reminders delivered |
| **Guardrails** | Be transparent these are automated |

**Reminder Schedule:**
| Timing | Content |
|--------|---------|
| Immediately | Confirmation: time, date, caller number, person meeting with |
| 24 hours before | Reminder with details |
| 12 hours before | Reminder |
| 3 hours before | Final automated reminder |

**Reminder Template:**
```
[Auto msg] Hey [Name]! Quick reminder about your appointment
tomorrow at [time]. You'll be speaking with [Closer Name] from
[Area Code]. Looking forward to it!
```

#### Step 4.3: Manual Reminders
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | Send personal reminders from real phone |
| **Cognitive Type** | Execution + Personalization |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW - Must feel personal |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Appointment within 24 hours |
| **Output** | Personal connection established |
| **Guardrails** | Use iPhones (blue messages) for higher response |

**Manual Reminder Schedule:**
| Timing | Content |
|--------|---------|
| Night before | Personal check-in |
| Morning of | Confirmation |
| 60 minutes before | "See you soon" |

**Conversation Framework (A-C-A):**
1. **A**cknowledge: Respond to what they said
2. **C**ompliment: Something genuine about them
3. **A**sk: The next question (qualify or pull forward)

#### Step 4.4: BAMFAM (Book-A-Meeting-From-A-Meeting)
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Description** | NEVER end a call without scheduling the next one |
| **Cognitive Type** | Judgment + Negotiation |
| **Automation Potential** | LOW |
| **Executor** | Human |
| **Precondition** | Currently on call with lead |
| **Output** | Next meeting scheduled |
| **Guardrails** | Treat "I'll get back to you" as objection to handle |
| **Decision Rule** | "BAMFAM as a way of life" |

**Script:**
```
[Before hanging up]
"Great, let me pull up my calendar... What day works better for you -
[Day A] or [Day B]? Perfect. Morning or afternoon? Great, I've got
you locked in for [specific time]. You'll get a confirmation shortly."
```

**Why It Works:**
- Both parties present = highest scheduling probability
- "I'll follow up later" = lead goes to no-man's land
- If they're dodgy about next call = objection to handle

---

## Part 6: Decision Rules

### DR-001: Speed Classification
```yaml
rule: SPEED_TO_CONTACT
trigger: New lead opt-in
condition:
  - IF contact_time < 60_seconds THEN "EXCEPTIONAL" (+391% conversion)
  - IF contact_time < 5_minutes THEN "STANDARD"
  - IF contact_time > 5_minutes THEN "SLOW" (revenue leak)
action: Prioritize immediate contact
confidence: HIGH (Velocify, HBR data)
```

### DR-002: Scheduling Window
```yaml
rule: APPOINTMENT_WINDOW
trigger: Scheduling conversation
condition:
  - IF available_slot == today THEN "PRIORITY" (highest show rate)
  - IF available_slot <= 72_hours THEN "ACCEPTABLE"
  - IF available_slot > 72_hours THEN "WARNING" (increased no-show risk)
  - IF available_slot > 5_days THEN "DISCOURAGE"
action: Always offer same-day first
confidence: HIGH (ALAN data)
```

### DR-003: Lead Scoring Action
```yaml
rule: LEAD_SCORE_ROUTING
trigger: Lead scored
condition:
  - IF score == GREEN THEN route_to_best_closer()
  - IF score == YELLOW THEN standard_process() # "Yellows are the new gold"
  - IF score == RED THEN remove_from_calendar() + offer_resources()
action: Match lead quality to closer quality
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-004: Ghost Recovery
```yaml
rule: GHOST_DETECTION
trigger: Scheduled lead not responding
condition:
  - IF no_response AND hours_until_appointment < 24 THEN double_book_slot()
  - IF no_response AND days_since_schedule > 3 THEN send_proof()
  - IF ghosted_completely THEN add_to_90_day_nurture()
action: Never give up completely; show them what they missed
confidence: MEDIUM [INFERRED: specific thresholds]
```

### DR-005: Incentive Deployment
```yaml
rule: INCENTIVE_TYPE
trigger: Appointment scheduled
condition:
  - IF first_time_client THEN use_push_incentive() # Gift card
  - IF qualified_lead THEN use_pull_incentive() # A/B choice
  - IF high_value_lead THEN combine_both()
action: Create reciprocity and commitment
confidence: HIGH
```

### DR-006: Volume Escalation
```yaml
rule: CONTACT_ATTEMPT_ESCALATION
trigger: No response to contact
condition:
  - IF day == 1 AND attempts < 6 THEN continue_attempting()
  - IF day <= 3 AND attempts < 10 THEN continue_attempting()
  - IF day <= 7 AND attempts < 15 THEN continue_attempting()
  - IF day > 7 THEN transition_to_long_term_nurture()
action: Front-load contact attempts
confidence: HIGH
```

---

## Part 7: Exceptions & Edge Cases

### Exception 1: Too Many Bad Appointments
**Trigger:** Calendar filled with unqualified leads
**Action:** Add friction to scheduling process
- Add video to watch before scheduler visible
- Add sales letter above scheduler
- Add price visibility
- Delay scheduler appearance

### Exception 2: Lead Can't Schedule Within 72h
**Trigger:** Lead unavailable in standard window
**Response:** Treat as objection, not fact
**Script:**
```
"What days were you planning on [activity related to offer]?
Great - this appointment is the first step to that. Let's use
that time slot for your appointment."
```

### Exception 3: High Show Rate, Low Close Rate
**Trigger:** Rep gets lots of shows but few closes
**Analysis:** May be cherry-picking easy leads
**Action:** Review lead quality distribution across team

### Exception 4: Lead Requests Different Closer
**Trigger:** Lead asks for someone else
**Action:** Accommodate if possible; investigate pattern

## Part 9: Validation

### Show Rate Quality Gates

| Gate | Threshold | Action if Failed |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| First Contact Speed | >50% within 5 min | Add capacity or automation |
| Schedule Rate | >40% | Review availability/messaging |
| Show Rate | >60% | Review speed/personalization/volume |
| Throughput | >25% | Full funnel audit |

### Rep Performance Standards

| Metric | Minimum | Target | Top Performer |
|--------|---------|--------|---------------|
| Daily Calls | 150 | 200 | 400 |
| Show Rate | 50% | 70% | 85% |
| Close Rate | 15% | 25% | 40% |
| Lead-to-Close | 7.5% | 17.5% | 34% |

## Appendix A: Cultural Elements ("The Garbage Man Culture")

### Core Mantras
| Mantra | Meaning | Application |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| "Volume negates luck" | More attempts = more success | Do more than competitors |
| "Yellows are the new gold" | Less qualified leads = opportunity | Don't sleep on any lead |
| "BAMFAM as a way of life" | Always book the next meeting | Never leave calls open |
| "Be a garbage man" | Take leads others reject | Every lead is practice |
| "Process > All" | No one is above the process | Follow the system |

### Desired Behaviors
- Love "the boring work" that gets results
- Treat every lead as equal opportunity
- Never judge a book by its cover
- See unqualified leads as "free practice"
- Compete on total metrics, not cherry-picked ones

### Metric Rankings (display publicly)
1. **Show Rate** - measures work ethic
2. **Close Rate** - measures skill
3. **Lead-to-Close** - measures complete performance

---

## Appendix B: Technology Stack

### Required Tools
| Tool Type | Purpose | ROI Justification |
|-----------|---------|-------------------|
| Auto Dialer | 2-3x team efficiency | Eliminates manual dialing time |
| Multi-channel Messaging | Reach leads on preferred channel | Higher response rates |
| Lead Scoring | Prioritize high-value leads | Better time allocation |
| Calendar System | Self-scheduling + 15-min slots | More booking options |
| Local Area Code Wrapping | Match caller ID to lead location | Higher pick-up rates |
| iPhone for Texting | Blue messages (not green) | Higher trust/response |

### Integration Requirements
- CRM with timestamp tracking
- Automated reminder sequences
- Lead scoring algorithm
- Rep performance dashboard
- Call recording for training

## Appendix C: Edification Script (Hot Handoff)

When transferring a qualified lead to a closer:

```
"You're in luck. You're actually going to speak with one of our
top experts on [topic]. He's been in this game for a while and
helped [similar businesses/people] achieve [thing they want].
We're fortunate to have him. He'll definitely be able to help
you with that.

Let me check his calendar really quickly. [pause]

[If moved time] Yep - I'm gonna slide you in so you can get
this taken care of ASAP.

[If same time] Yep - you're all confirmed and good to go.

The moment we get off the call, I'm going to introduce you
to him via text message. Does the [phone number] work?

Great. Alright. Have an amazing day, and enjoy your time
with [Closer Name]."
```

Then immediately:
1. Create 3-way text group
2. Introduce lead to closer
3. Include key qualification points
